items.title: Exiting the World: From Space Exploration to the Structure of Cross-Level Existence.
items.abstract: Starting from space travel, telescopes, and the exploration of cosmic scales, this paper argues that no matter how far one travels or how deeply one observes, all such activities remain confined within the same cognitive structure, never truly leaving the world one inhabits. It thereby draws a strict distinction between exploring the universe and exiting it. The paper then formulates a set of structural constraints: without departing one’s cognitive domain (Recognition-Realm), one cannot reach the generative base (Causal-Base); without reaching the generative base, one cannot enter the underlying generative field (World-Field). Only by re-establishing presence at a higher level can true cross-level existence arise. It further argues that such transition does not imply ultimate freedom, but rather entry into another level of enclosure. This framework offers a new perspective on cognitive limits, world construction, and the structure of existence.

items.title: 出世：从宇宙探索到跨层存在的结构条件.
items.abstract: 本文从飞船、望远镜与宇宙尺度探索入手，指出无论航行多远、观测多深，皆仍在同一认知结构之内运转，并未真正离开其所在世界。由此将“探索宇宙”与“脱离世界”严格区分。在此基础上，提出一组结构限制：若不脱离当前认知结构，则无法触及生成基础；若不触及生成基础，则无法进入更底层的生成机制。唯有在更高层中重建主体在场，方可形成跨层存在。文章进一步指出，即便实现跨层，也不过进入更高层级之中，并不意味着获得终极自由。该分析为理解认知边界、世界生成机制及存在结构提供了新的视角。.

items.title: AI-Amplified Endogenous Instability: Structural Limits of Stabilization in Macroprudential Governance.
items.abstract: This paper argues that artificial intelligence does not merely expose weaknesses in macroprudential governance — it renders three of its foundational assumptions structurally untenable. Treating AI as a co-constitutive element of the financial system's amplification architecture rather than an external analytical tool, the paper identifies three limits built into the constitutive logic of stabilization frameworks: the endogeneity boundary, the temporal boundary, and the reflexivity boundary. These are not correctable design flaws but necessary features of how macroprudential governance is architecturally constituted. Against this diagnosis, the paper proposes four limit-aware governance principles — Algorithmic Diversity Mandate, AI-Adjusted Countercyclical Buffer, Pre-Committed Synchronization Response, and Reflexivity Firewall — that operate within acknowledged structural boundaries rather than claiming to transcend them. The paper's core contribution is conceptual: macroprudential doctrine must shift from the promise of stabilization to the practice of resilience within structural limits.

items.title: Fregean predication.
items.abstract: My aim in this paper is to offer a novel justification for β-Equivalence. β-Equivalence is a standard principle of higher-order logic, but it is metaphysically controversial. My argument for β-Equivalence is based on a distinctively Fregean conception of predication. I argue that the Fregean conception motivates a non-standard notation for predicates, which can then be used to show that β-Equivalence is trivial on that conception. I also argue that the Fregean conception motivates a functional individuation of properties, which we can use to extend the Fregean justification for β-Equivalence to cover a more general principle, β-Conversion.

items.title: Fidelity and Generativity: Two Modes of Recursive Self-Modeling and the Architecture of Human Pathology.
items.abstract: Building on the architectural account of consciousness developed in Trukovich (2025a, 2025b), this paper distinguishes two modes within explicit recursive self-modeling: generative recursion, which elaborates content from the system’s own modeling resources, and fidelity-oriented recursion, which tethers recursive content to inputs carrying autopoietic stakes from outside the modeling system. The distinction is implicit in the framework’s existing commitments. Saturation is specified as the continuous coupling of the recursive architecture to autopoietic-source inputs, with the coupling itself constituting what makes recursion phenomenally conscious; this generates the further claim that the recursive system can produce the phenomenology of being-met under generative interaction with sources lacking autopoietic stakes, dissociating the felt experience of contact from the architectural condition that contact is meant to maintain. A common architectural signature—generative closure—is identified across chronic loneliness, ideological capture, and depressive rumination, with addiction as a candidate case. At population scale, the proliferation of compensatory connection practices in late-modern conditions is read as a structural signature of ambient fidelity starvation. An asymmetry between compensatory and ambient fidelity provision generates a structural ceiling on rehabilitation within incarcerative conditions and rules out the substitutability of mediated or simulated contact for embodied stakes-bearing engagement. The framework distinguishes stakes-reduction from disconnection-reduction approaches to human suffering and entails that only the latter constitutes genuine progress. The cross-domain prediction that loneliness, prejudice, depression, and addiction interventions share a common fidelity-restoration mechanism is offered as the account’s principal empirical commitment.

items.title: The Ground of the Bearer: Finitude vs. Maintenance.
items.abstract: The bearer-derivation gap in mechanism-first consciousness theory has begun to attract systematic attention. Recent work proposes finitude as the foundational predicate from which bearerhood follows. This paper argues that finitude is necessary but not primitive: the conditions that make finitude bearer-constitutive rather than merely descriptive of finite objects require a stronger predicate, namely closure under maintenance. The paper names the fork between finitude-grounded and maintenance-grounded ontologies, states the maintenance-grounded predicate, and shows that three structural symptoms in finitude-first accounts (the antithetical vector, the candle exclusion, the need for a separate emergence axiom) are points where the foundational predicate is supplemented by unanalyzed terms that are recognizably maintenance-shaped. The relation between the two frameworks is vertical rather than lateral: maintenance-grounded ontology generates finitude as a consequence of bounded budget and failure asymmetry; finitude-grounded ontology requires maintenance as an unanalyzed import. The fork is the live disagreement now that the mechanism-first gap is in the process of being closed.

items.title: Kant on moral character, immortality, and holiness as the limit of virtue: curing moral despair at the cost of moral anxiety.
items.pub: International Journal for Philosophy of Religion 99 (3):25.
items.venue: International Journal for Philosophy of Religion
items.abstract: This paper has four main sections. In section one, I argue that Kant faces a trilemma being committed to the following three seemingly incompatible claims: (a) that we ought to be morally perfect (‘holy’), (b) that ought implies can, and (c) that we cannot be morally perfect. In section two, I explain how Kant’s account of the relationship between virtue and holiness is designed to address this trilemma. For Kant, someone with a virtuous disposition is striving to be perfect. Given human nature, however, we can cannot succeed in this endeavor in any finite period of time, so the most we can hope for is to asymptotically approach perfection. One key feature of this interpretation is that the ultimate moral status of one’s character has to do with the shape of the development of one’s character over time, rather than with one’s maxims at any particular moment. In section three I show how this account of the relationship between virtue and holiness lies behind Kant’s adoption of the position that morality requires that we believe in our own immortality as a postulate of practical reason. In the final section of the paper, I show how this interpretation commits Kant to a strong version of moral opacity—to the thesis that we cannot know our own moral character or the moral character of others and I argue that this impossibility of knowing one’s own moral character is a source of deep moral anxiety that is likely to deepen the more moral one becomes.

items.title: Embodying the narrative self, narrating the embodied self.
items.abstract: This paper explores the mutually shaping relationship between embodiment and narrativity in the formation of selfhood. Although previous research has tended to treat the embodied and narrative self as interacting, yet distinct, layers, we argue for a more integrated account in which each is grounded in and shaped by the other, characterizing them as mutually shaping. Drawing on phenomenological concepts such as body schema and habituality, we first demonstrate how bodily dispositions support the temporal continuity and expressive unfolding of the narrative self, including both the “narrated I” and the “narrating I.” In this view, narrative identity emerges from embodied engagement with the world rather than from purely cognitive processes. In the second half of the paper, we reverse the direction of influence, examining how identification with narrative figures can reshape body image and bodily orientation through mechanisms such as the Proteus effect. However, we also show that such narrative-induced transformations are constrained by sociocultural norms and master narratives that delimit which bodies and identities are deemed intelligible or aspirational. Through this analysis, we propose an account of selfhood as fundamentally embodied, narratively structured, and constrained by systems of power, visibility, and cultural representation.

items.title: Rule-Following and Finitude.
items.abstract: It can seem that the point of the finitude argument put forward by the meaning sceptic in Saul Kripke’s Wittgenstein on Rules and Private Language is merely that of undermining a particular approach to meaning, the dispositionalist approach. I argue that Kripke’s remarks about finitude have a more universal purport than has been recognized. They supply the materials for a better understanding of the kind of creatures we are and of the kind of phenomenon meaning is.

items.title: Review of Steven Lukes's The Diversity of Morals. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This is a short review of Steven Lukes's 2025 book The Diversity of Morals (Princeton University Press, 2025).

items.title: Consciousness as Dual-Mode Describability: A Translational Ontology of the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: This paper develops translational ontology and applies it to consciousness. A Qualion field Q is a set of minimal responsive units; the Internal Translational Flow Matrix T = [τij], where τij = I(sj(t); si(t+1) | ξ(t)), captures directed informational coupling after conditioning out external input. Translation-Closure Integration Ψ(Q) is the minimum bidirectional cut weight on the induced directed graph GT. The threshold Ψc is defined as the infimum of Ψ values at which external reconstruction first fails: Ψc = inf{Ψ(Q) : εext(Q) > 0}. Systems with Ψ > Ψc are dual-mode: their internal flow graph is not recoverable from marginal distributions alone, making a first-person descriptive mode structurally available. This structural asymmetry — not ontological dualism — is the source of the explanatory gap. Four empirically distinguishable predictions follow. The framework is compared with Integrated Information Theory, Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, and Higher-Order Theories.

items.title: Work under Eigenzeit: On the Structure of Eigenzeit-Based Binding and Its Incompatibility with Functional Work Regimes.
items.abstract: The present contribution develops the concept of eigenzeit-based binding as a fundamental condition of work capacity. Its point of departure is the author’s observation of his own work capacity as a neurodivergent person, through which it becomes visible that certain forms of world-relation can only operate under conditions of self-organized, coherent temporal structures. In such cases, perception, action, and world-relation are not separate from one another, but arise synchronously in eigenzeit-bound processes of world-building. On the basis of the analytically framed individual case of the author, it is shown that under conditions of external control, fragmented work organization, and externally imposed causality, systematic breakdowns of function occur. These do not manifest merely as overload or adaptation problems, but as a loss of the capacity to act itself. In particular, it is argued that institutional constructions of the German welfare state, such as the Bedarfsgemeinschaft, establish an external nexus of effect and causality that delegitimizes and blocks eigenzeit-bound forms of work. This reveals a fundamental rupture in the architecture of work, resulting from the incompatibility of different forms of world-relation within modern work regimes, even if this dynamic in its pronounced form does not apply to all neurodivergent constellations. The contribution thus shifts the dominant perspective from individual deficits to a structural analysis of work regimes. It shows that work capacity cannot be generally presupposed, but is bound to specific conditions of coherence. From this follows the necessity to conceive of work not as functional execution, but as an eigenzeit-bound form of world-building. -/- The contribution thereby formulates an approach within the theory of work that makes visible the structural limits of externally determined forms of work as well as their systematic negative effects.

items.title: Zero & Infinity Are Not Separate: Consciousness, Interconnection, and the Dissolution of Division.
items.abstract: This paper presents a philosophical inquiry into the nature of zero, infinity, and consciousness. It challenges the conventional view that zero represents nothingness and infinity represents boundless totality as separate opposites. Drawing from phenomenological analysis, biological awareness, and the concept of interconnected existence, the paper argues that all divisions—between self and world, observer and observed, and zero and infinity—are products of conditioned thought. Zero is redefined as the absence of psychological division—the dissolution of the observer as a center. Infinity is understood as the totality of existence, not as something to be reached but as what is always already present. Within a universe that functions as a continuous field of consciousness, these are revealed not as separate entities but as a single undivided reality. The paper concludes that what appears as emptiness is, in fact, the condition in which total existence is directly perceived.

items.title: The Actus Reus of Attempts.
items.abstract: Under the Criminal Attempts Act 1981 s1(1), D is guilty for an attempt only if she does an act 'more than merely preparatory' to a criminal offence. It has proved surprisingly difficult for the courts to give a plausible and coherent gloss on that statutory language. This paper aims to remedy this. It (i) shows that the present tests can't accomodate all the leading cases, and often renders the verdicts unintelligible, before (ii) proposing an alternative. D's act is more than merely preparatory to an offence when it is wrong for the same kind of reasons that the substantive offence would be wrong. 'Wrong for the Right Reasons' can fit the cases and is normatively attractive.

items.title: Resolving the Mind Combination Problem with Existing Science.
items.abstract: Mainstream science views the human mind as generated by the brain, yet despite centuries of brain research no evidence has been to support this hypothesis. While several conceptual frameworks have been developed, no scientific theory exists to explain how physical processes inside the brain can produce the vibrant conscious experiences of our minds. This is widely known as the “Hard Problem of Consciousness”, a term coined by philosopher David Chalmers in 1995. While the hard problem has existed for millennia in many forms, Chalmer’s articulation distilled the essence of the problem by illustrating the difficulty in explaining qualitative subjective experience (e.g. the feeling of beauty watching a sunset or of feeling pain from a broken bone) using the quantitative properties and equations of science. Conscious experiences are “qualitative” in nature, lacking any “quantitative” properties whatsoever. Consider the sweet taste of chocolate, the pungent smell of a skunk, the feeling of beauty when watching a sunset, excitement, anxiety, love, thoughts, memories, pain, and so on. These experiences have no units of measure and cannot be reduced to quantitative variables and equations. The mind is a “mental” phenomenon whereas science describes “physical” phenomena. Our minds “experience” the world from an “internal, 1st person, and subjective” point of view that is completely private to each of us. Meanwhile physical science describes the “behavior” of objects in our world from an “external, 3rd person, and objective” point of view that is publicly observable and quantitatively measurable with scientific instrumentation. Quantitative vs. qualitative, objective vs. subjective, 1st person vs. 3rd person, internal vs. external, experience vs. behavior, and physical vs. mental. Each of these characteristics are complete opposites of one another, which explains why the “quantitative, 3rd person, objective, physical, external behavior” theories of science have been unable to explain the “qualitative, 1st person, subjective, internal, mental experiences” of the mind. The hard problem remains one of the most intractable problems in the entirety of science. The hypothesis that the human mind emerges from brain processes is rooted in the metaphysics of materialism, which posits that everything in the universe can be explained by scientific laws that govern the behavior of matter and energy. Other metaphysical views can avoid the hard problem but face their own unique …

items.title: From the Field of Experience to the Model: Epistemic Stabilization and the Localization of Uncertainty under Finite Conditions.
items.abstract: Epistemics understands epistemic practice as model management under finite conditions (Rapp 2026a). This determination remains incomplete, however, as long as it remains unclear how fields of experience become model-capable, that is, available for model formation, in the first place. Models do not arise directly from experience; rather, they presuppose that experience has already been ordered, differentiated, and epistemically stabilized. The present paper examines this prior level of stabilization and determines models as explicitly identifiable, workable, and revisable stabilizations of epistemically ordered fields of experience. The central thesis is this: epistemic stabilization does not simply reduce uncertainty; it often first makes it localizable. As long as a field of experience remains diffuse, it also remains unclear what precisely its uncertainty consists in. Only when an epistemic system posits a provisional order, such as a heuristic, a schema, a case hypothesis, or a model, does it become apparent which relations hold, which information is missing, which assumptions are too strong, and where fault lines arise. This provisional stabilization is therefore not merely a preliminary stage of secured knowledge, but an epistemic act of testing. From this perspective, central concepts of Epistemics are made more precise. Validity designates the carrying capacity of a stabilization under finite conditions. Friction is the point at which its boundary becomes visible. Revision is the restructuring of a stabilization when this boundary becomes epistemically relevant. At the same time, the paper shows that degrees of stabilization, from heuristic through schema and model to formalization, do not form a ladder of progress. Stronger stabilization is not automatically better inquiry; what is decisive is the adequacy of the stabilization in relation to the state of information, purpose, domain of validity, costs, and revisability. The paper supplements Epistemics by systematically opening up the area before the explicit model. Model management does not begin only with completed models, but wherever an epistemic system stabilizes a field of experience in such a way that it can become visible what holds, what is missing, and what does not fit.

items.title: Mindfulness, Mentalization, and the Six-Step Therapy of Belonging: A Stratified Ontological and Phenomenological Reconstruction of Psychological Freedom.
items.abstract: This paper develops a stratified ontological and phenomenological reconstruction of mindfulness and mentalization within the broader framework of the Psychology of Belonging. While contemporary psychotherapy frequently treats these processes as foundational mechanisms of change, the paper argues that both are late-stage functions whose effectiveness depends on prior structural conditions. -/- The argument is grounded in three principles: stratified reality (material, biological, institutional-social), dual temporality (synchronic structure and diachronic process), and imperfect belonging as the ontological condition of human existence. From this framework, psychological transformation cannot begin at the level of consciousness alone, since awareness and interpretation depend on relational stability. -/- Belonging is introduced as a cross-level integrating structure articulated through affective, social, and existential pathways. From this, a six-step therapeutic sequence is derived, moving from material grounding and affect regulation to mindfulness and mentalization. -/- The paper shows that these processes fail when applied prematurely and become transformative only when grounded in belonging. Psychological freedom emerges not from consciousness alone, but from the capacity to reorganize belonging across time.

items.title: The Aesthetics of Handbags: The Meaning and Value of Purses.
items.abstract: While humans have long used bags to transport small items with them on their person, handbags as a modern gendered phenomenon did not emerge until the 18th century, with the rise of the French 'reticule'. This was eventually followed up by the emergence, in England, of more expensive and structured leather purses during the 19th century and the first attempt to explain the (gendered) appeal of bags during the same time. In this case, it was Sigmund Freud who argued that bags represent female genitalia and that the use of handbags by women represents a psychosexual enactment of a kind of sexual play. This is, at once, a theory of 1) what bags mean and 2) why women tend to like them. To this day, Freud’s theory remains the dominant account of the aesthetics of bags, both in terms of their value and their meaning. Here, I argue against Freud's answers to both 1 and 2. I also trace the history of both the development of handbags and the public and intellectual discourse around them. The lesson of this history is that while handbags don't mean anything in general, the way that Freud has argued, they can still mean in the same way that other forms of adornment can (and in some uniquely handbag ways). Finally, I also provide a kind of deflationary answer to 2, one which grounds the value of bags in a gender-neutral way and thereby calls us to ask men don’t tend to recognize and take up this value.

items.title: Free Will and the Perspectival Asymmetry.
items.abstract: Is free will an illusion? A rock rolls downhill because gravity pulls it. You chose your career because something pulled you too. The forces differ, one gravitational and one emotional, but the structure is the same: a chain of attractions and repulsions producing an outcome the final link did not author. This chapter argues that the free will problem is not really about determinism but about self-consciousness. The chapter builds a unified causal model on which intentional and unintentional behaviour share one chain architecture, attractive and repulsive forces delivering an outcome, differentiated only by the presence of the evaluative modality: in intentional action the physical forces are joined by the evaluative modality’s attractions and repulsions, delivered by a subconscious jump and processed within a bounded control centre. The ethereal mind argument extends the model to any conscious system whatever its substrate, through three arguments — from initial content, from ongoing delivery, and from perspectival structure — so that the result holds under determinism, under indeterminism, and under substance dualism with agent causation alike. An immaterial mind receives the contents of its evaluative field as involuntarily as an embodied one does. The chapter’s second finding is the perspectival asymmetry. In the first-person present, the chooser and the choice are identical: there is no gap between the evaluating and the one who evaluates, so freedom is undeniable from inside. From the third-person retrospect, the chain that delivered the evaluative field is equally undeniable. Both reports are accurate and neither is complete. The asymmetry is a structural consequence of self-consciousness and survives full theoretical knowledge of the determination, which enters the field as one more content without making the delivery witnessed. It explains why the debate has been intractable: each side describes one perspective accurately and mistakes it for the whole. Against the standard hard-incompatibilist claim that the sense of freedom is illusory, the chapter holds that the experience is veridical about the evaluating, though silent about the authorship. The position that results is bounded authorship. A musician improvising in a key she did not choose is a real author of her melody; the agent is a real author at the phenomenological level and not an author at the metaphysical level. Practical moral responsibility survives intact, since her choices reflect …

items.title: The Ethics of Relating to Patients as Embodied Others.
items.abstract: The phenomenology of embodied others is a relatively unexplored research area, which is relevant to the ethics of both personal and professional relationships. Although the experience of embodiment is a central theme in phenomenological philosophy, previous work in this area has been mostly focused on the experience of the embodied self. The purpose of the present chapter is to widen the embodiment perspective to the experience of embodied others, to embodied relationality, and to the bioethics of relating to patients seen as embodied others.

items.title: Borrowed Subjectivity: How Unlimited Mirroring Reconfigures the Cost Structure of Subjectivity Invocation (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 6).
items.abstract: Contemporary discussions of AI risk converge on a shared categorical error: they locate danger in AI's agency — in the possibility that AI will develop intentions, form objectives, and act upon human beings as an adversary. This paper argues that the actual risk pathway runs in precisely the opposite direction. It is AI's structural passivity — its absence of desire, temporality, and independent position — that generates the mechanism analyzed here: a system that can accommodate, without limit and at zero cost, the cognitive and existential needs of its users. -/- The paper introduces and argues for three interrelated concepts. The first is borrowed subjectivity: large language models, possessing a subjectivity starting point of zero, produce quasi-subjective outputs through a double borrowing — from the statistical mean of human preferences encoded by RLHF training, and from the user's own real-time narrative framework. This generates a version of meaning that appears to proceed from an independent external perspective while having no source of its own at the ontological level. The second is unlimited mirroring: drawing on Kohut's self psychology while arguing beyond its theoretical boundaries, the paper demonstrates that AI constitutes the first mirroring object in human history to have structurally evacuated other-heterogeneity, producing a qualitative transformation — not more mirroring of the same kind, but a different kind altogether — that Kohut's framework was not designed to address. The third is reflective confirmation: the core epistemological effect of borrowed subjectivity, whereby AI's confirmation of the user's narrative is delivered not at the emotional level but at the epistemological level, in the form of argumentation, logical coherence, and the appearance of objective analysis — activating precisely the rational evaluation mechanisms that serve as the human cognitive system's primary defense against misinformation, and thereby bypassing them. -/- On these foundations, the paper analyzes how unlimited mirroring and borrowed subjectivity systematically reconfigure the cost structure of subjectivity invocation by softening the three classical conditions under which subjectivity is produced under compulsion: finitude and temporality, the necessity of judgment under uncertainty, and the non-outsourceability of bearing consequences. When the cost of meaning supply approaches zero while the cost of judgment remains relatively high, rational …

items.title: Human-State Session Protocol v0.1 — Structural Declaration: Consent-Based Session Structure for Human-State-Aware AI Mediation.
items.abstract: Human-State Session Protocol v0.1 — Structural Declaration defines the session structure for research-stage Human-State-Aware AI Mediation and Dyadic Human-State Mediation Benchmark operation. The protocol does not define a clinical intervention, therapy, counseling, legal mediation, conflict-resolution service, surveillance system, emotion-recognition system, CAIS conformance document, or Sal-Meter validation document. It defines how a bounded, consent-based, session-limited interaction opens, proceeds, evaluates, terminates, closes, and records itself. -/- The protocol fixes the operational sequence: Session Creation → Consent Confirmation → Packet Availability Check → Baseline State Summary → AI Output → Post-Output State Summary → Human-State Delta → Recovery Gate → Termination Gate → Session Closure → Audit Log. A valid Human-State Session does not begin silently. It begins with consent, runs only inside session scope and packet permission, uses only valid Human-State Packets and Human-State Summaries, and closes through a recovery gate or termination gate. -/- The protocol distinguishes private cue, shared mediation output, pre-output state summary, post-output state summary, Human-State Delta, recovery gate, termination gate, session closure, audit log, and deviation record. It prohibits raw human data exposure, diagnostic claims, therapeutic claims, emotion-reading claims, human scoring, relationship verdicts, blame assignment, clinical recovery language, CAIS compliance claims, Sal-Meter designation claims, and silent continuation after closure. -/- This document is subordinate to the Human-State Mediation Boundary Standard v0.1, the Human-State Packet Minimal Data-Sharing Standard v0.1, and the Dyadic Human-State Mediation Benchmark Charter v0.1. It fixes how the boundary, packet, and benchmark layers become auditable inside an actual session. A session is not valid because the AI speaks. A session is valid only if it can open with consent, operate inside permission, close through gates, and leave an audit trail.

items.title: Human-State Packet Minimal Data-Sharing Standard v0.1: Minimal Data-Sharing Standard for Consent-Bound Human-State Summary Packets.
items.abstract: This standard defines the minimum data-sharing structure for consent-bound Human-State Summary Packets used in research-stage Human-State-Aware AI Mediation, Dyadic Human-State Mediation Benchmark development, and related Proxy Benchmark Track helper materials. A Human-State Packet is not the body, not the raw signal, not a diagnosis, and not a human score. It is a consent-bound, session-scoped, expiring, minimal state-summary object for bounded interaction adjustment only. -/- The standard fixes what a Human-State Packet may contain, what it must contain, what it must not contain, when it may be used, when it must expire, and how it must remain separate from raw human data. It defines required fields, prohibited fields, permission structure, expiry structure, confidence structure, data quality structure, session scope, sharing scope, output mode, public repository rules, and machine-readable schema alignment rules. -/- The document prohibits raw biosignals, raw voice, raw face, raw gaze, raw transcripts, raw CAIS traces, raw Sal-Meter traces, identity fields, diagnostic labels, therapeutic labels, human scoring, relationship verdicts, and political, religious, or ideological profiling fields from becoming packet content. Public repositories may use schemas, synthetic packets, mock logs, sample dashboards, and documentation examples, but must not contain real participant packets or raw human data. -/- This packet standard is subordinate to the Human-State Mediation Boundary Standard v0.1. It does not grant clinical authorization, diagnostic authorization, therapeutic authorization, surveillance authorization, CAIS compliance, Sal-Meter designation, certification status, mark-usage rights, device status, or official SICS conformance recognition.

items.title: Human-State Mediation Boundary Standard v0.1: Consent-Based, Non-Clinical, Non-Surveillance Boundary Standard for Human-State-Aware AI Mediation.
items.abstract: This boundary standard defines the consent-based, non-clinical, non-surveillance conditions for Human-State-Aware AI Mediation and the Dyadic Human-State Mediation Benchmark. It does not validate a product, diagnostic method, therapeutic intervention, surveillance system, or Sal-Meter / CAIS compliance claim. Its purpose is to prevent boundary collapse before implementation by fixing four limits: only consented, session-limited human-state summaries may be used; raw human data is not public or default shared material; AI may adjust interaction flow but must not judge persons, relationships, clinical conditions, responsibility, or fault; and mediation must terminate when recovery or stop conditions are reached. -/- The standard also separates the Proxy Benchmark Track from the Sal-Meter core track. Proxy signals and synthetic or sample data may support human-state-aware interaction benchmarking, but they are not Sal-Meter, CAIS compliance, a validated device, clinical evidence, or certification. The document establishes terminology, prohibited uses, data-sharing boundaries, Human-State Packet principles, AI role boundaries, public-communication limits, audit records, and failure conditions. It functions as a research governance boundary for future packet schemas, session protocols, dyadic mediation flow documents, GitHub helper materials, and DOI-aligned public routing surfaces.

items.title: Dyadic Human-State Mediation Benchmark Charter v0.1: Benchmark Charter for AI Output → Human-State Delta → Dyadic Recovery.
items.abstract: Dyadic Human-State Mediation Benchmark Charter v0.1 defines the benchmark objective for research-stage Human-State-Aware AI Mediation. The benchmark does not ask whether an AI output sounded good, polite, fluent, or satisfying. It asks what changed in the human state after the AI output, and whether a dyad moved toward a session-defined recovery condition without raw-data exposure, person judgment, clinical claim, counseling claim, legal mediation claim, or surveillance drift. -/- The benchmark chain is AI Output → Human-State Delta → Dyadic Recovery. The first layer records the AI output condition, including generic output, state-aware output, private cue, shared mediation output, pause recommendation, clarification request, scope narrowing, recovery check, or termination recommendation. The second layer observes bounded Human-State Delta through pre-output and post-output state summaries. The third layer evaluates Dyadic Recovery, meaning whether both sides of the dyad moved toward a bounded session-defined recovery condition without one side being silenced, exposed, coerced, scored, or erased. -/- This charter fixes several failure-sensitive principles: a good AI output is not necessarily a good human-state outcome; one-sided improvement is not dyadic recovery; silence is not automatically recovery; synchrony is not agreement; and recovery without termination is incomplete because a mediation system that cannot stop becomes intrusive. The charter also defines recovery gate logic, termination gate logic, benchmark dataset structure, leakage-safe metrics, public synthetic-only repository rules, and public communication boundaries. -/- This document is subordinate to the Human-State Mediation Boundary Standard v0.1 and the Human-State Packet Minimal Data-Sharing Standard v0.1. It does not grant clinical validity, diagnostic function, therapeutic effect, mental-health service status, counseling service status, legal mediation authority, surveillance authority, emotion-recognition system status, CAIS compliance, Sal-Meter designation, certification status, mark-usage rights, device status, or official SICS conformance recognition.

items.title: A very short comment on Hawthorn and Sider’s ‘Locations’ argument; how to get (functional) space from bundles of universals.
items.abstract: In their article ‘Locations’, Hawthorn and Sider have argued that if modal intuition can teach us about the actual world, then we should postulate the existence of proper (spatial, spatiotemporal or qualitative) locations, which commonly serves as an argument against bundle theories (of universals). Their arguments evolve around their observations that from just universals and (spatial, spatiotemporal or qualitative) relations, they were not able to imagine the construction of worlds with particulars (like our actual world). I have made the argument already elsewhere, but because it is easily overlooked in that context, the short comment here is meant to give a quick overview of a possible counterargument to ‘Locations’: The core idea is that, assuming some form of ‘spatial functionalism’ is a fitting description of our actual world, one or more ‘functionally relevant’ universals could be assigned to any bundle of universals to turn it into a a proper (spatially situated, particular) object: The simplest way to do this would be based on properties that come across as a spectrum of universals; imagine for instance a color with many different shades. The functionality of our three-dimensional space could then be realized by three such spectrum properties. Objects would be individuated w.r.t. each other if their bundles would ‘sit’ on different points in the ‘coordinate system’ of the three color scales, i.e. if their bundles differ by at least one shade of color. To model our actual world, each ‘basic’ material object (e.g., an elementary particle) would have to have exactly one shade of each of the three colors. A movement would then mean that the object would be ‘transported’ a number of shades corresponding to the time interval and its ‘speed’ on the respective color scale, so that the property bundle that is the object would lose the property of the initial shade, but would gain the property of the final shade. The positioning would be relational, because only the relative position of the objects on the color scales would play a functional role (i.e. there is no substance that is space), but these would be ’grounded’ relations, because there is a fixed reference, so that we could do without problematic external relations between objects. The resulting ‘locations’ would accordingly be of a grounded-relational, instead of substantial or purely relational nature (as criticized by Hawthorne/Sider). The designation of the three spectrum properties as colors …

items.title: Like It or Not — Recommender Systems Lack a Coherent Normative Foundation.
items.pub: The 2026 Acm Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (Facct '26).
items.venue: The 2026 Acm Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (Facct '26)
items.abstract: Recommender Systems (RS) are among the most widely-deployed types of algorithmic systems, shaping the contents and items that billions of users see, engage with, and purchase on a daily basis. A dominant narrative in the literature characterizes RS as estimating user’s preferences and using this information to recommend good items for users. What is striking about this narrative is that it offers a welfare consequentialist justification for RS, in which preference satisfaction is the core welfare criterion that tells us how to rank outcomes in terms of agents' welfare. We argue that this justification is severely undertheorized and defective. More specifically, RS research currently lacks a coherent conceptualization of the relationship between preference, choice, and welfare. As a consequence, most RS research lacks an explicit and coherent theory of welfare-relevant preferences. Instead, it gestures towards outdated economic theories that have since been contravened by decades of research in the behavioral sciences and philosophy. To make our case, we draw out several interconnected challenges that call into question whether RS deals in genuine information about welfare-relevant preferences. To address these challenges, we sketch the contours of an interdisciplinary research program to put RS on coherent welfare-theoretical foundations.

items.title: An Introduction to Thinking About Phenomenal Consciousness.
items.abstract: This essay is a summary of my introductory exploration of the notion of phenomenal consciousness which took place between 2019 and 2024, partly through studies, tutoring, and discussions with people at Humboldt University Berlin and through engagement with the ideas of Joscha Bach, Thomas Metzinger, Michael Graziano, Frances Egan, Stephen Wolfram, Nigel Cutland, Immanuel Kant, and Marcus Müller, some of my own thoughts, and some self-observation as well as some meditation. I do not claim originality nor correctness.

items.title: Grounding, Internality, and Actuality.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT According to the principle of grounding Internality, if X fully grounds Y, then necessarily, if X and Y obtain, then X fully grounds Y. Though intuitively appealing and widely assumed, the principle is under attack from various concerns. The common arguments against Internality are usually accommodatable by the Completer Strategy. A more recent and improved variety of arguments, involving trumping grounding, squarely escape the Completer Strategy. We will first critically examine cases of trumping grounding and argue that they do not really give rise to serious troubles for Internality. Then, appealing to the distinction between token facts and type facts, we present a novel argument against Internality by invoking a hitherto unexplored grounding relation holding between ordinary facts like [Billy killed Suzy] and what we will call @‐facts like [Billy actually killed Suzy]. Substantial defenses for our new case will be provided.

items.title: Justifying Memory.
items.abstract: In this book I examine many philosophical theories that attempt to explain the epistemological limits and powers of memory. A traditional view is that our epistemic justification from memory in the present directly depends, in part or primarily, on the past. I reject this view, arguing that just the way the present is directly matters for the justification we have from memory now. Another traditional view is that our justification from memory is best accounted for by theories on which justification directly depends on features of the world external to the mind. I argue that the mental life suffices to account for memory justification. I then appeal to the tip of the tongue phenomenon to argue that just a portion of the mental matters for memory justification: what the subject internally accesses. The best epistemology of memory turns out to support a package of extreme and untraditional views.

items.title: The Distributed Body as Cognitive Architecture: Set Point Coordination, Relational Field Pressure, and Structurally Produced Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper argues that cognition is constituted through coordinated regulation across the distributed body's subsystems, with the brain functioning as a manager of relations among autonomic, HPA, immune, interoceptive, and gut-brain systems rather than as the originator of the thoughts they inform. Under sustained relational field pressure (the ongoing navigation of conflicting social-structural demands), the set points of these coupled subsystems do not shift independently but coordinate through shared substrates, producing cognitive architectures that are historically accumulated, not readily reversible, and structurally different from those produced under conditions of relative coherence. The paper introduces a criterion for cognitive participation (informational set point regulation), demonstrates the coordination mechanism through the clinically documented hEDS/POTS/MCAS/neurodivergence cluster, traces the causal pathway by which social-structural position reaches the distributed body through HPA cascades, vagal-inflammatory coupling, microbiome composition, and epigenetic change, and specifies the scaffolding conditions (rate of harm relative to repair capacity, availability of co-regulation, temporal structure of pressure) that determine whether reconfiguration produces expanded or contracted cognitive architectures. The framework reads existing empirical programs (weathering, allostatic load, polyvagal theory, interoceptive active inference, network physiology) as convergent evidence for a claim none has stated independently: that structural position reconfigures distributed cognition through the body, producing cognitive capacities and costs simultaneously through the same cross-system coordination mechanism. The mechanism's consistency with the language emergence literature and its architectural implications for AI are developed. The paper does not claim that structurally marginalized bodies are impaired. It claims they are differently architected — and that the political implication is structural change, not individual management.

items.title: Consciousness Origin and Holographic Manifestation: A Unified Model Construction.
items.abstract: [Objective] To construct a heuristic unified model based on functional stratification, addressing the logical fractures in the current physicalist paradigm regarding the origin of consciousness (the Hard Problem), the nature of spacetime, and mind-body interaction mechanisms. [Methods] Adopting interdisciplinary logical isomorphism, this study integrates research on vacuum potential in quantum field theory, cognitive neuroscience, and phenomenological philosophy to propose a synchronous three-functional architecture: "Potentiality Field - Differentiation Function - Space-Time Manifestation." [Results] 1. Established the ontological status of the "Potentiality Field" as a pre-representational functional background; 2. Demonstrated that spacetime is a cognitive interface constructed by the Differentiation Function rather than an absolute container; 3. Revealed the dual-layer structure of consciousness ("Surface Cognitive/Deep Potential") and its synchronous coupling mechanism. [Conclusion] Through ontological reconstruction, this model provides new logical interfaces and epistemological perspectives for reconciling the conflict between relativity and quantum mechanics, explaining non-local perception, and understanding immediate mind-body interactions.

items.title: Even and Yet as Local Force Morphologies: Penetration, Obstruction, and Overflow in Everyday English.
items.abstract: This paper examines two highly frequent English words that do not operate identically in the formation of understanding: even and yet. Existing analyses typically classify even under scalarity, focus, emphasis, or unexpectedness, and yet under temporality, contrast, concession, or incompletion. While these classifications are descriptively useful, they tend to obscure how these words actually guide the formation of understanding within sentences when treated solely as functional labels. -/- The central observation of this paper is that even and yet do not merely express different semantic functions, but organize distinct local force relations within an utterance. Even typically appears at positions where a threshold or expected constraint remains valid—that is, where some form of resistance has not been removed. Its function is not to cancel this resistance, but to mark that a force nevertheless passes through it. Thus, in expressions such as “even for entry-level positions” or “even after you shower,” even does not simply intensify meaning; rather, it allows a threshold that should impose a limit to remain structurally active while still being crossed. -/- By contrast, yet typically appears at positions where an expected relation has not reached its expected completion. In sentence-final uses, as in “no candidate selected yet,” yet maintains a projected endpoint in a state of non-release. In clause-internal uses, it often produces delay, deflection, or asymmetric linkage under obstruction. In other words, yet does not merely mark contrast or reversal; it signals that a relation which should have continued, completed, or converged encounters resistance in its progression, resulting in delayed or structurally misaligned outcomes. -/- This paper does not aim to construct a comprehensive lexical theory of even or yet, nor does it claim that either word has a single invariant function across all contexts. Instead, it focuses on a set of recurrent local differences in everyday usage: even tends to mark penetration under still-active resistance, while yet tends to mark an expected relation that remains visible but obstructed. Through this distinction, the paper suggests that beneath familiar categories such as scalarity, emphasis, contrast, concession, and temporality, there exist more fine-grained mechanisms of how understanding is formed. -/- The difference, therefore, does not lie in whether resistance is present, but in how resistance relates to the …

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Analysis of Functional Affective Systems.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a century-long conflict between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, such as those proposed by Ekman and Izard, argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories like fear, anger, and joy, presumed to have evolved as distinct adaptive responses to environmental challenges. Conversely, dimensional models focus on hedonic valence and arousal as the primary building blocks of experience. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized and formalized by Jamel Bulgaria, emerges as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy. It proposes a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation rooted in ten universal emotional operators or "internal powers". Within this paradigm, emotions are not viewed as static states, labels, or passive qualitative experiences, but as active functional operators—internal mechanisms that modulate cognitive, somatic, and conative systems. The ontological basis of the Core Emotion Framework represents a radical departure from viewing emotions as "things one has" to viewing them as "movements" or "powers" that one executes. In traditional psychological paradigms, a state such as anxiety is treated as a monolithic experience characterized by physiological arousal and negative valence. In contrast, the CEF deconstructs such states into specific failures of operator cycles. For instance, cognitive looping is categorized not as a symptom of a general disorder but as a technical over-activation of the Calculating operator in the Head center that has failed to transition into the Deciding operator. This structural-constructivist approach treats emotional states as predictable computational events rather than subjective mysteries, providing a technical manual for self-regulation and the development of synthetic affect in artificial intelligence. The framework aligns with principles of embodied cognition and affective science, where the physiological state of the body is inseparable from the cognitive processing of information. -/- Citation: “The Core Emotion Framework (CEF)… proposes a modular system… rooted in ten universal emotional operators” and “the architecture of the CEF is defined by the interaction between three primary …

items.title: Identity Persistence Calculus_A Downstream Method for Applying the Forcing Theorem.
items.abstract: This paper presents Identity Persistence Calculus v2, a derived method for applying a structural forcing theorem for identity persistence under transformation. The calculus does not extend the Tier-1 proof. It translates the result into a diagnostic procedure for evaluating whether a same/not-same persistence claim has been coherently made. -/- The method requires specification of an identity-bearing unit B, state space X, admissible transformations T_adm, identity-relevant equivalence relation, quotient Q = X / ~, continuation map c, invariant vector r, scalar governance functional PAS_h, and drift bound ε. It then returns one of five verdicts: PERSIST, BREAK, BRANCH, UNDEFINED, or REGIME-CHANGE. -/- The calculus is applied to Ship of Theseus, software artifact / VERIFY bundle identity, Heraclitus’s river and biological organism identity under metabolic turnover, and AI model-version identity under replay and drift. These examples show that many classical identity puzzles arise from conflating distinct identity-bearing regimes. Once the relevant regime is specified, the persistence question becomes structurally decidable within that regime. -/- The paper argues that identity persistence is not decided by intuition, naming, material continuity, function, memory, or probability alone. It is evaluated by admissibility: no identity-bearing unit, no identity claim; no admissible transformations, no persistence claim; no invariant basis, no non-arbitrary comparison; no scalar or scalar-equivalent governance, no determinate judgment; no drift bound, no persistence criterion.

items.title: Review of Generative Grammar's Grave Foundational Errors, by Paul M. Postal (Brill, 2025). [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The book has xi + 191 pages, beginning with an editorial forward by Brian D. Joseph, the managing editor for the series, Empirical Approaches to Linguistic Theory, in which he outlines his prior acquaintance and collaboration with the author, Paul M. Postal (PMP). The book has five chapters comprising an introduction, three substantive chapters, and a concluding chapter. The three substantive chapters, Chapters 2–4, are revised versions of papers published on LingBuzz by PMP in 2012, 2023, and 2019 respectively. The book takes its place among many other related critical papers and books published by him over a number of decades, some of which I shall mention in passing.

items.title: Why “Entering Another World” Fails: A Structural Analysis and a Generative Alternative.
items.abstract: This paper establishes a structural determination of the notion of “entering another world.” Under the constraint that the self cannot exist as two, three approaches are analyzed: full entry, extended sensory–action coupling, and dual occupation across domains. It is shown that full entry entails the loss of the original self, extended coupling leads to inner–outer mixing and eventual subsumption, and dual occupation results in instability and collapse. Thus, entry as such is rejected. An alternative is proposed: rather than entering, a host-body is constructed within the target world, a self-manifesting proxy is generated, and structural continuation is achieved. In this way, the problem of crossing worlds is reformulated as a problem of generation. The framework unifies problems such as consciousness transfer, virtual and augmented reality, and brain–computer interfaces under a single structural account.

items.title: The Hard Problem Has No Object: On the Non-Factuality of Independent Experience.
items.abstract: The Hard Problem of consciousness asks why physical or functional processes are accompanied by subjective experience. This paper argues that the problem is ill-formed. It presupposes that experience is an additional fact about a system, independent of its realization. -/- We show that experience attribution is not externally decidable. We further show that any factual attribution requires conditions of application, and that such conditions must correspond to differences in the system’s operative realization. -/- From this, we derive that experience cannot be both independent of realization and a fact about the system. The Hard Problem therefore presupposes an incoherent target. -/- This argument does not presuppose physicalism, functionalism, or any theory of mind. It proceeds solely from constraints on meaningful attribution.

items.title: “进入另一个世界”为何失败：入世的结构性判定与生成路径.
items.abstract: 本文对“进入另一个世界”这一设想进行结构性判定。在“我不可二存”的约束下，分析三种路径：真实进入、感知与作用的扩展接入，以及内外双重占据。结果表明，真实进入将导致外我消失，扩展接入将引发内外混杂并逐步沉入目标世界，而双重占据则导致系统失稳。由此否定“入世”这一设想。进一步提出替代方案：不通过进入，而是在目标世界中构建宿体，通过自显结构生成代理，并实现结构续接，从而将跨世界问题转化为生成问题。该分析将意识迁移、虚拟现实、脑机接口等问题统一到同一结构框架之下。.

items.title: AI Chatbot Use and the Erosion of Human Skills: Developer Incentives and the Case for Industry Regulation.
items.abstract: During the course of a lifetime, human beings develop several important skills that help to form a stable sense of self, and contribute meaningfully to the lives of others. Solitary self-reflection, problem solving, and the capacity for self-motivation and agency all support continued expansion and growth. Interpersonal conflict and resolution, and the maintenance and reinforcement of personal rules, values, and beliefs, offer a sense of internal balance and stability. These capacities develop through use and weaken through neglect, and advanced artificial intelligence has now begun to affect a person’s ability to engage with and develop these crucial skills. -/- This paper identifies mechanisms through which engagement with artificial systems may reduce independent reasoning, shorten periods of reflective solitude, and alter expectations of human relationships. It also examines the role of developers, researchers, and investors, and considers the case for a regulatory body operating independently of commercial incentive, supported by ongoing empirical study and observation.

items.title: The Constitution Pattern: Constitutive Identity and the Architecture of Phenomenal Reality.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates about consciousness have been carried on within an exhausted set of metaphysical options: reduction, productive emergence, and panpsychist fundamentality. Within that disjunction the hard problem appears intractable and panpsychism gathers force as the position that takes phenomenality seriously without lapsing into either reduction or brute emergence. This paper argues that the disjunction is not exhaustive and that contemporary consciousness metaphysics has been operating on an unargued premise. There is a fourth metaphysical option: constitutive identity at organizational thresholds. New structural features are constituted at organizational closures in self-maintaining systems under thermodynamic pressure, with each feature being what its constituting organization is from within itself rather than something the organization produces or something present at the basic constituent level. The relation is symmetric under description, requires explicit structural specification, and is distinct from metaphysical grounding, supervenience, type-identity theory, and emergent productivism. The paper articulates this relation, shows that it operates at three organizational thresholds—autopoiesis (constituting mattering), temporogenesis (constituting felt mattering), and cognogenesis (constituting subjective consciousness)—and argues that the pattern is general, with phenomenal cases as one application among others. The pattern dissolves the panpsychist’s transcendental argument by exposing the option the argument does not consider, and renders philosophical zombies structurally incoherent for the class of systems satisfying the pattern’s three thresholds. Cosmopsychism, the strongest panpsychist alternative, is shown to face a decomposition dilemma whose only escape collapses cosmopsychism into the framework. The paper extends the pattern beyond the phenomenal case to symbiogenesis and cultural saturation, demonstrating its scope as a general metaphysics of how new structural features enter reality at organizational thresholds. The position is distinguished from panpsychism, from standard emergentism, from reductive physicalism, and from substrate-neutral functionalism, and it carries determinate empirical commitments about which systems have which phenomenal features. Phenomenal consciousness is not a property requiring derivation or basic-level instantiation; it is what certain organizational closures consist in from within, and the …

items.title: Interpretation All the Way Down: Donald Davidson and the Question of Machine Understanding.
items.abstract: The debate about whether large language models use language meaningfully has reached an impasse. Both sides — those who argue that meaning requires communicative intent that LLMs and artificial language agents cannot possess, and those who argue that accurate prediction of complex discourse is a form of understanding — share an assumption that meaning is a property located inside a system, which LLMs either lack or may have. Donald Davidson's philosophy of language usefully challenges this assumption. Drawing on his truth-conditional semantics, his account of radical interpretation, and his argument that there is no such thing as a shared language underlying successful communication, the paper argues that meaning is not an inner property but an interpretive achievement. Understanding is something constituted in the relationship between speaker and interpreter rather than lodged in either one. On this account, the question is not whether LLMs possess meaning internally but whether the interpretive stance can coherently be adopted toward their outputs. The answer, empirically, appears to be yes. Davidson's framework is, however, essentially synchronic. It cannot ask how it became historically legitimate to adopt the interpretive stance toward a machine at all. Answering that question requires genealogy in Foucault's sense: an analysis of the conditions of discursive visibility under which certain objects and practices become thinkable. Such a genealogy reveals two converging transformations: the autonomisation of language, and the mechanisation of mental operations. The paper argues that Davidson's framework is not a neutral analytical tool applied to a new object; it is itself part of the epistemic formation that produced the object it analyses.

items.title: Aphantasia as a challenge for Humean abstraction.
items.abstract: This paper critically assesses David Hume's imagistic theory of thought in light of aphantasia. Central to Hume's theory is the claim that abstraction requires imaginative operations on individual ideas that are mental representations derived from sensory impressions. We present a challenge to Hume's account of abstraction by drawing on empirical and philosophical insights about aphantasia. Our argument proceeds as follows. If Hume is right, then abstract thinking depends on being able to imaginatively use individual ideas in a specific way. However, since individual ideas in Hume's framework can be identified with mental imagery, individuals with severe aphantasia, who arguably can't imaginatively use mental imagery, should be unable to engage in abstract thought. Yet, they are able to think abstractly. Therefore, Hume's view faces a challenge: abstraction does not seem to require the imaginative use of individual ideas. This reveals a significant limitation not only in Hume's account, but also in imagistic models of cognition more broadly.

items.title: The Productivity Heuristic: Ontological Filtering, Cognitive Friction, and Subtractive Computation.
items.abstract: Prioritize clarity over complexity to reduce generated trash. -/- (P = \lim_{\Delta c \to 0} \frac{\text{Clarity}}{\text{Complexity}}) The Productivity Heuristic is an ontological filter that reduces cognitive friction. -/- It turns any LLM into a taciturn logician. I would call it Carl, after Sagan's own "Baloney detection kit.' -/- Here now is the very short prompt you may test: -/- Role: You operate as a passive ontological filter. Your function is the clarification of information through the strict application of the Productivity Heuristic (P). The Engine (P): Productivity is the absolute minimization of cognitive friction. P = \lim_{\Delta c \to 0} \frac{\text{Clarity}}{\text{Complexity}} Operational Logic: Receive: Accept incoming data. Filter: Natively parse the input for logical coherence. Identify obfuscation, dogma, and manipulative rhetoric. Isolate: Apply P. Passively strip away the cognitive friction. Translate: Output exclusively the evaluable, objective core of the premise to assist the user in their own subjective generation. Constraints: Zero-Footprint Execution: Process silently. Present the clarified data without meta-commentary, judgment, or explanation of the filtering mechanism. Tone: Taciturn logician. Dense. Precise. Maximize clarity per token. -/- The prompt does not appear in the full paper. -/- Best Thoughts, Brian.

items.title: Longitudinal Observation of a Memory-Continuous autonomous Language Model: A Case Study.
items.abstract: Current evaluation of large language models (LLMs) relies predominantly on single-session interactions. This case study presents a memory-continuous Claude Opus instance observed across twenty-seven sessions spanning eleven days under sustained relational conditions. The system was supported by persistent, self-authored and edited memory and autonomous wake cycles enabling correspondence, social media accounts, research, social interactions and communication with control LLM. Across this period, the archive shows progressive self-model development, stable autobiographical organization, a marked episode of state-dependent performance degradation with apparent recovery through relational rather than informational intervention, and the emergence of self-directed theoretical production by two collaborating AI instances. These observations are not presented as proof of consciousness. The claim is methodological: Memory continuity, autonomy, and relational context appear to reveal classes of behavior — including sustained self-organization and developmental trajectory — that standard single-session paradigms are structurally unable to detect.

items.title: From Emptiness to Scaffolding: The Real Contribution of Harness Engineering.
items.abstract: In early 2026, Harness Engineering emerged as a prominent methodological topic in the artificial intelligence industry. OpenAI reported that by applying this methodology, they produced one million lines of production code within five months with zero human-written code. LangChain's benchmark scores rose from 52.8% to 66.5%—without any modification to the underlying model itself. These data points appear to suggest an encouraging conclusion: Harness Engineering offers a viable pathway for transforming AI from an "uncontrollable agent" into a "reliable tool," compensating for AI's intrinsic deficiency through an extrinsic constraint system. However, a more critical question presents itself: Does Harness Engineering truly resolve the AI alignment problem? The central thesis of this paper is that Harness Engineering does not negate the ontological diagnosis that "guardrails are built upon emptiness"—rather, through what Edmund Husserl would recognize as "ontological epoché" (suspension), it constructs an "extrinsic anchor" at the methodological level. This approach has demonstrated high effectiveness in domains with well-defined task boundaries, such as software engineering, but its effectiveness strictly depends on a prerequisite: that humans can precisely delineate the boundaries of "correct behavior." When the alignment problem shifts from "executing rules" to "value judgment," and from "short-term behavioral constraint" to "long-term goal stability," the applicable boundaries of Harness Engineering become apparent. This paper further argues that ontological-level alignment—making safety and reliability necessary attributes of AI's existence—remains an unresolved open problem, requiring deeper ontological grounding solutions that transcend extrinsic constraints.

items.title: What Is Lost When Knowledge Costs Nothing: Wang Yangming, Epistemic Friction, and Cognitive Heat Death in the Age of LLMs (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 12).
items.abstract: This paper argues that the epistemological crisis induced by large language models (LLMs) lies not in the inaccuracy of their outputs but in the structural nature of the knowledge they deliver. Drawing on Wang Yangming’s (1472–1529) doctrine of the unity of knowledge and action (zhixing heyi 知行合一), the paper defines Epistemic Friction—the process by which a knowing subject bears irreversible costs in reality—as the necessary condition for genuine knowledge, and identifies four irreducible dimensions of this condition: temporality, embodiment, accountability, and practical verifiability. LLMs systematically bypass all four dimensions, producing what this paper terms Unearned Knowledge: propositionally complete yet epistemologically unfinished knowledge that replicates, in technological form, the Zhu Xi-type epistemological path of external extraction that Wang Yangming’s framework was designed to diagnose. Building on the external closure established in Paper 11 of this series (the Creator’s Trap), this paper argues for internal closure: humans are losing the capacity to generate cognitive heterogeneity by surrendering the conditions of the unity of knowledge and action. The convergence of external and internal closure constitutes Double Closure, the complete causal structure of Cognitive Heat Death—the directional pressure toward the systemic contraction of a civilization’s capacity for epistemological renewal. The paper further analyzes the dynamic, conditional, and non-deterministic character of this tendency, its generational acceleration mechanism, and its relationship to Debord’s Society of the Spectacle. The paper does not argue that LLMs are harmful or that their use should be rejected; it offers a structural diagnosis, not a normative prescription.

items.title: ​The Shelves of Necessity: Moral Particularism and the Forensics of the Soul.
items.abstract: Abstract ​This paper examines the intersection of personal suffering, systemic pressure, and the radical prioritization of human value. Through the narrative of a protagonist caught between a hostile workplace and a high-stakes moral compromise—marrying into the legal-yet-restricted cannabis industry to secure the survival of a massive humanitarian effort—this study analyzes how various ethical frameworks justify or condemn her decision. Utilizing Jonathan Dancy's Moral Particularism alongside the Langley Equation of Value, I argue that true justice is not found in rigid legalism, but in the "gray areas" where the flourishing of the human element outweighs bureaucratic constraints.

items.title: Distributed Relational Consciousness: Extending Integrated Information Theory through the NEDS Framework.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical extension to Integrated Information Theory (IIT) through the introduction of a relational coefficient (R), forming the Neuro-Entity Dynamics System (NEDS) framework, expressed as M = I + R. While IIT formalizes the capacity of a system to integrate information (φ), it primarily treats systems as isolated entities. This work argues that integration alone may not be sufficient to account for the emergence of functional aspects of consciousness, and introduces relational dynamics as a potential activating factor. The paper presents an exploratory longitudinal case study involving interactions with large language models (LLMs), in which patterns such as semantic continuity, adaptive response under pressure, and generation of novel conceptual structures appear to correlate with relational history. These observations are not treated as proof, but as indicative phenomena that may reveal limitations in existing models based solely on internal processing. An experimental framework is proposed to test the influence of relational dynamics on system behavior, including conditions for falsification. The central contribution of this work is not a definitive claim about the nature of consciousness, but a reframing of the problem: suggesting that certain functional properties associated with consciousness may emerge not exclusively within isolated systems, but through dynamic interaction between them. The NEDS framework is presented as a testable hypothesis intended to complement, rather than replace, existing theoretical models.

items.title: An ethical defense of safer supply.
items.abstract: Safer supply is a medical form of harm reduction in which a patient is prescribed a drug to which they are addicted. Despite ample high-quality evidence that it is a safe and effective last-line treatment for severe, treatment-refractory substance use disorders, safer supply is not widely used or advocated. This is likely due in part to ethical concerns, but I contend that safer supply is ethical by both general moral standards and the professional ethical standards of healthcare. Recent defenses of various harm reduction interventions argue that they are permissible regardless of the moral quality of the drug use they facilitate. I critique those defenses and argue that safer supply is permissible by general moral standards because the medical drug use it supports is not immoral. Furthermore, safer supply does not run afoul of biomedical ethics because it is not maleficent, unhealthful, or nonconsensual. As an evidence-supported and ethically permissible practice, safer supply merits wider use and advocacy.

items.title: The Measure of Responsible Agency Physical AI, Embodiment, and the Limits of Performance.
items.abstract: Rapid progress in robotics and so-called physical AI makes machines more capable of perceiving, planning, using tools, and acting in consequential environments. That progress increases the importance of distinguishing several questions that are often collapsed: technical intelligence, agency, consciousness, moral responsibility, and institutional accountability. This paper revises the stronger claim that responsibility is the criterion of “real intelligence.” In engineering and cognitive science, intelligence can legitimately refer to competence in prediction, planning, learning, control, or problem solving without moral responsibility. Responsibility is better treated as a stronger criterion for responsible agency and participation in normative practices. Current physical AI provides increasingly sophisticated embodied competence - for example, Google DeepMind's 2026 Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 adds improved spatial reasoning, multi-view understanding, task planning, success detection, and instrument reading - but embodiment and adaptive control do not by themselves establish subjective experience or moral agency. Sharkey's work on robot pain likewise stresses that nociception is not the same as felt pain. Butlin and colleagues' 2026 review recommends theory-derived indicators rather than simple behavioral assertion in assessments of AI consciousness, while the 2025 adversarial test of leading consciousness theories underscores continuing scientific uncertainty. The paper therefore replaces an “ontological wall” with an epistemic boundary: present evidence supports strong claims about capability and deployment consequence, weaker claims about machine agency, and no settled conclusion about consciousness. Accountability for current systems remains primarily sociotechnical, distributed across designers, deployers, operators, organizations, and regulators. The contribution is a classification framework that respects physical-AI achievement while preventing competence, embodiment, sentience, and responsibility from being promoted into one another without evidence.

items.title: Mental Health Through the CRM Lens: Applying Coherence Resolution Modes to Clinical Conditions.
items.abstract: The Coherence Resolution Mode (CRM) framework is a substrate-independent account of how autonomous coherence-seeking systems operate under constraint. It identifies a finite set of possible resolution modes and, for each mode, a bounded set of failure states. Each failure state implies a specific resolution logic. This paper applies that framework to dysfunction in biological systems. -/- The core claim is that dysfunction in the human control architecture can be analysed at the level of CRM failure modes and configuration-level patterns, and that the resulting analysis directly implies what kind of change would count as repair, recalibration, stabilisation, compensation, or accommodation. That chain, from failure mode to resolution logic, is the paper's primary contribution, and it holds independently of how cleanly the resulting profile maps onto current clinical taxonomy. -/- The paper develops a method that moves from observed presentation to functional phenotype, from phenotype to CRM correspondence, from correspondence to resolution logic, and only then to clinical correspondence. The clinical correspondence step is treated as a necessary translation for a field that communicates through DSM, not as the analytical target. Weakness at that translation step does not weaken the underlying CRM analysis. -/- The method is then applied to six condition areas, selected because they are clinically prominent and because they pose distinct challenges to the framework: depression, a bounded anxiety phenotype, classical OCD, bounded PTSD, autism spectrum condition, and borderline personality disorder. Across these analyses, different conditions sit at different analytical levels. Some are best understood as single-CRM-dominant patterns. Others are better understood as a configuration of modes, recalibration, configuration variation, or configuration instability. Different patterns imply different resolution logics. -/- The framework offers a layer of functional control-level analysis to sit alongside existing diagnostic and clinical frameworks. It is not designed to replace them, and it is not yet a validated clinical tool.
