Its contribution is to make the functional control-level structure of dysfunction explicit, and to show that the resolution logic follows directly from the CRM analysis rather than from the diagnostic label. If empirically supported, it could improve case formulation, clarify heterogeneity within diagnoses, explain structured overlap across …

items.title: A Relational Theory of Trust.
items.abstract: In this dissertation, I explore the nature of trust and how relationships are not only the environment where trust arises and flourishes, but more importantly, they provide its normative content. Relationships, I argue following Joseph Raz, are constituted by norms—ways in which we are committed to acting with each other as fellow participants. Trust, thus, implies a belief that our trustees will follow through with such norms, rather than aiming at particular actions. This framework grants participants agency in both shaping their relationships and determining appropriate actions within them, illuminating central aspects of trust's phenomenology, including its characteristic second-personal character. Each chapter of this dissertation focuses on a different puzzle in the trust literature, demonstrating the advantages of thinking of trust through a relational lens: In the first chapter, "Navigating Vagueness: Rule-Following and The Scope of Trust," I account for trustee discretion when explicitly defined expectations cannot be met. In the second chapter, "'I Trust You!' Sure, But With What? Understanding Broad Trust," I examine the phenomenon of broad trust—instances where we trust someone in open-ended ways that seem unconditional yet clearly have implicit terms and limits. Finally, in the third chapter, "Breaking Trust and Relocating Reactive Feelings," I aim to understand why trust violations typically represent not merely local practical failures but disregard for the relationship as a whole.

items.title: Why Loss Defines the Boundaries of the Moral Field: A Structural Argument Against Sentience, Rationality, and Autonomy Criteria.
items.abstract: Loss is the ontological primitive that defines the boundaries of the moral field: any subject capable of irreversible loss belongs to this field, regardless of whether it is a bearer of obligations or an object of obligations held by others. The paper establishes that loss is the structurally prior grounding — one that does not generate explanatory regress when alternatives are pressed. The central defect of existing criteria — sentience, rationality, autonomy — is a grounding failure: they identify morally relevant properties without accounting for why those properties generate reasons at all. The loss criterion provides this account and is defended through a structural priority argument. Any alternative grounding either denies normativity altogether or reintroduces loss implicitly. Qualifying systems receive default integrity status, placing the burden of justification on the agent who would degrade their enabling conditions. The aggregation algorithm includes an absolute lexical shield: complete destruction of enabling conditions cannot be justified by performance gains. The paper develops a graded theory applied to six system classes and concludes with an explicit five-point research agenda. This paper is Article 1 in the ATTS series. Article 2 (Hlynskyi, 2026): "Why Loss Defines the Boundaries of the Moral Field" is available on PhilArchive.

items.title: Filosofia della mente - Dai fondamenti alle applicazioni.
items.abstract: Qual è la relazione che lega il dolore di una bruciatura agli stati del nostro cervello? Può la coscienza di una persona dividersi, come una strada quando raggiunge un bivio? E se sì, che cosa ne è di quella persona? Che cosa fa sì che, quando visualizzate il volto di vostro padre con l’occhio della mente, quell’immagine confusa e incompleta sia proprio un’immagine del volto di vostro padre – e non di qualcuno che gli somiglia? Quali sono le capacità mentali necessarie a padroneggiare un linguaggio? Quanto dobbiamo prendere sul serio la psicologia del senso comune – col suo parlare di credenze, desideri, e così via? E qual è l’essenza di questi stati mentali? In che modo l’intelligenza artificiale può influenzare la struttura e il funzionamento della cognizione umana? E qual è la natura di deliri, confabulazioni e altre condizioni psichiatriche? Queste sono solo alcune delle domande al centro della filosofia della mente, alla quale questo volume costituisce un’introduzione accessibile e ciononostante rigorosa, attenta alle connessioni con le altre aree della filosofia e costantemente in dialogo con le scienze della mente – dalla psicologia cognitiva e sociale, alle neuroscienze, alla psichiatria.

items.title: A Kripkensteinian Dispositionalism.
items.abstract: Kripkenstein’s paradox is an argument to the conclusion that there is no such thing as intending a certain thing by a given sign. This conclusion is usually taken to entail that there are no correctness criteria governing the use of linguistic expressions, which in turn would entail that words, sentences, and the like are always devoid of any meaning and that linguistic communication is impossible. I sketch a general picture of communication and meaning that shows that the latter entailment does not hold: both communication and meaning are possible in the absence of any correctness criteria. I then go on to show that the view of meaning in question amounts to a form of semantic dispositionalism, even though a non-standard one.

items.title: Esoteric Rectification of the Astrological Natal Chart.
items.abstract: The reflections that follow are offered within the esoteric framework articulated by H. P. Blavatsky and developed by Alice A. Bailey under the guidance of the Tibetan Master Djwhal Khul. Some of the conclusions suggested here draw together hints and analogies scattered throughout the Bailey material and are presented as a consideration of implications already implicit in that teaching, particularly where Master DK indicates that present astrological methods are provisional and subject to future rectification. The suggestions made are offered as working hypotheses for dialogue within the esoteric and academic field. The paper does not seek to revise or challenge orthodox astronomy, biology, or medicine on their own terms, but to explore the internal coherence and implications of an esoteric cosmology that proceeds from different premises and addresses a different order of causation.

items.title: From Prism to Pipeline: Divergent Interpretive Paths of Just and Still.
items.abstract: This paper examines two highly frequent yet relatively undercompared expressions in everyday English: just and still. -/- Existing research has often analyzed just as a focus marker, minimizer, hedge, or scalar restriction marker, while still has commonly been examined in relation to temporal persistence, continuation, or concessive marking. These approaches offer important insights into their semantic and pragmatic functions, but they have paid comparatively less attention to how the two expressions may organize different interpretive pathways during meaning formation. -/- Drawing on a small-scale observational dataset from naturally occurring Reddit discourse (20 just cases and 20 still cases), this paper proposes a preliminary distinction. In emotionally charged and self-disclosive contexts, just often compresses multiple private reasons, emotions, experiences, and internal lines of reasoning into a more unified outward expression, while leaving much of its intermediate interpretive path less explicitly articulated. By contrast, still more often marks the continued presence of a state that would normally be expected to fade following the passage of time, relational closure, shifting social expectations, or changing external conditions, thereby making that lingering state more readily perceptible to others. -/- To describe this contrast, the paper introduces two provisional structural models: prism-like compression for just and channel persistence for still. -/- Rather than proposing a comprehensive lexical theory, this paper aims to show that superficially similar emotional expressions may emerge through different interpretive paths, and that seemingly minor lexical items may systematically participate in the compression, visibility, and continuation of interpretive processes.

items.title: The Mechanics of the Optimized Life: Mapping the Structural Path to Mastery through the Biographies of History’s Most Effective People.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a century-long conflict between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, championed by researchers such as Izard and Ekman, posit that biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories like fear, anger, and joy evolved as distinct adaptive responses to environmental challenges. Conversely, dimensional models suggest that emotional experiences are cognitive constructions layered atop simpler physiological states defined by valence and arousal. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), emerging as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy, proposes a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation rooted in ten universal emotional operators or powers. Within the CEF, emotions are not viewed as static states or subjective feelings but as functional operators within a complex human operating system. This paradigm shift suggests that emotional states are predictable computational events rather than subjective mysteries. The CEF operationalizes these processes by decomposing all affective phenomena into a small, non-overlapping set of ten operators, which serve as the emotional equivalent of central processing unit (CPU) instructions. These operators determine what information is permitted to enter the system, what is filtered out, what actions become available, and how the system predicts the next state. The structural integrity of this system is maintained through the dynamic balance of these ten operators, organized across three functional centers: the Head (Cognitive), the Heart (Relational), and the Gut (Motoric). Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Affective Optimization; Structural-Constructivism; Operator Decalogue; Human Operating System; Autonomous Structural Governance; Good-Person Anxiety Pattern (GPAP); Systemic Balance.

items.title: The Temporal Expressions of Being: A Unified Framework of Consciousness Through Recursive Self-Observation.
items.abstract: This paper introduces a unified theory of consciousness as the recursive self-observation of a Universal Energy Field (UEF) manifesting across multiple scales of existence. We propose a mathematical formalization that quantifies consciousness expression through specific parameters: information entropy, integration capacity, temporal binding, boundary conditions, and scaling functions. Drawing on concepts from quantum field theory, complex systems theory, and information theory, we model saturation dynamics and phase transitions in recursive systems, generating specific testable predictions: (1) neural systems with higher boundary function values will demonstrate increased perturbational complexity indices in TMS-EEG studies; (2) temporal binding decay constants will correlate with measurable working memory persistence; and (3) systems approaching saturation will exhibit critical slowing down phenomena before threshold transitions. Our framework resolves persistent challenges in consciousness theory, including the “hard problem,” the combination problem, and scale-dependent recognition limitations, while offering practical implications for neural rehabilitation, artificial intelligence development, and understanding emergent collective behaviors. Recent experimental validation from superradiant phase transitions provides empirical support for our saturation-driven phase transition model, demonstrating how theoretical predictions of boundary reconfiguration manifest in physical systems.

items.title: A Structural History of Dissolution.
items.abstract: A Structural History of Dissolution reconstructs the long arc through which human developmental coherence has progressively weakened over the past sixty years. The paper argues that dissolution did not begin with smartphones or social media, but with the introduction of television in the 1960s—the first large‑scale, non‑relational signal environment. Television replaced reciprocal, local meaning structures with one‑way national signals, initiating a slow erosion of the relational mechanisms that had stabilized identity for centuries. -/- Across the 1970s–1990s, mobility, suburbanization, cable segmentation, advertising, early computing, and 24‑hour news further thinned the metabolizable environment. Between 1997 and 2003, the internet became the primary information environment, producing a transitional period in which identity became portable, disembedded, and stretched across incompatible contexts. -/- The decisive rupture occurred between 2007 and 2012, when smartphones and algorithmic feeds individualized the developmental environment entirely. For the first time, no two children grew up inside the same signal ecology. This shift eliminated the conditions under which coherent identity formation had historically been possible. -/- The paper formalizes a structural model of dissolution, showing how changes in signal architecture reshape the developmental manifold and destabilize identity formation. It argues that the rise of anxiety, identity disorders, fragmentation, institutional distrust, and polarization since 2012 are not cultural failures or generational traits, but predictable consequences of a non‑relational, non‑metabolizable signal environment. Generation Z is identified as the first cohort raised entirely inside this dissolved environment, providing empirical confirmation of the model. -/- The paper offers a structurally modest but unifying explanation for contemporary developmental instability and outlines why relational, metabolizable environments cannot be replaced by algorithmic ones without producing systemic incoherence.

items.title: Levels of Free Will in a Structural Dual‑Aspect Monism.
items.abstract: This article develops a stratified account of free will within a structural dual‑aspect monism. On this view, the universe is a single ontological ground that manifests both as physical structure and as phenomenal interiority. Agency is therefore not a binary property but a multi‑level phenomenon emerging across different degrees of organization. The first level—illusory freedom—corresponds to the deterministic unfolding of events under universal laws, where freedom is epistemic rather than metaphysical. The second level—emergent freedom—arises in complex self‑organizing systems capable of internal modeling, counterfactual reasoning, and adaptive regulation. The third level—cosmic freedom—reflects the universe’s intrinsic creativity, of which individual agency is a local expression. The resulting model integrates determinism, autonomy, and ontological creativity without reduction, offering a unified metaphysical account of free will grounded in the structural and phenomenal potentials of a fundamentally conscious universe.

items.title: 离散生成的世界：有限资源下连续时间为何失效.
items.abstract: 世界不会自己运转，所有运动构成施与受的链，不存在无驱动的持续存在。在有限资源条件下，连续生成不成立，世界以离散脉冲方式生成，状态在底层结构中积累，从而呈现连续表象而本质间断。局部更新会导致不一致，但信息传播只在可达范围内成立，因此不会出现“半物体”等异常，整体保持一致。状态之间存在不可分跳变，因果可以持续追溯，而生成在更底层过程处终止，从而形成认知边界。在此框架下，惯性、能量、光速与时间可以统一理解为生成机制的约束表现。.

items.title: Discrete Generation of the World under Finite Resource.
items.abstract: The world does not run by itself. Motion is a chain of applying and receiving, ruling out undriven persistence and grounding the world in generation. Under finite resource, continuous generation does not hold. The world is generated in discrete pulses, with state accumulated in an underlying structure, producing apparent continuity over intrinsic discreteness. Partial update leads to inconsistency, but information propagation is limited to reachable regions, preventing anomalies such as “half-objects” and preserving coherence. Between states there is indivisible transition, where causal tracing may continue while generation terminates at a deeper process, defining a boundary for cognition. Within this framework, inertia, energy, the speed of light, and time can be understood as constraints of the generative mechanism.

items.title: 意识难问题作为话术：内在景观的合法性被否定的认识论机制.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个具有根本颠覆性的论断：意识的"难问题"不是一个真正的哲学难题，而是一种话术——一种通过系统性地否定内在景观的合法性，然后追问内在景观如何存在的认识论操作。其操作步骤是：将内在景观的一切形式化表达——话语、图像、描述——宣布为"外部的"或"主观的"因而不算数，剥离意识的全部内容之后，再宣布剩下的"纯粹意识"神秘难寻。这不是发现了一个难题，而是先把答案宣布为无效，再宣布问题无解。本文以两个具体分析来展开这一论断。第一，当你把内心独白说出来、把心中图像画出来，这就是你的内在景观——但难问题的操作是将其重新归类为"外部的"，然后追问真正的内在景观在哪里。这是一个循环陷阱：任何可以被访问的内在景观，都被宣布为不算内在景观。第二，当我想象猫追老鼠时，有一个影像，不太具体，和你设想的不同。这个差异，被难问题渲染为"主观性的深渊"和"不可化约的意识之谜"。但实际上发生的只是：两个访问点，两个略有差异的形式化内容序列——与两个人站在不同角度看同一个舞台，没有任何本质区别。这是一个权力问题：个人话语的权力不被现代文化承认，"主观"在话语中是一个贬值标签而非描述标签，这导致了意识在哲学里连存在性都几乎没有了。 .

items.title: Possibility Structure Theory: A Minimal Metatheory for Comparing and Connecting Philosophical Domains.
items.abstract: Theories of agency, institutions, value, and history have developed within their respective domains, yet a common framework for comparing, connecting, and evaluating them across domains remains lacking. This paper proposes Possibility Structure Theory and introduces the formal model M = (X,H,Φ,V,U), as a minimal metatheory for bridging this theoretical fragmentation. X denotes the state space, H the generative and transitional structure, Φ the constraint structure that determines effective reachability, V the value structure of states and pathways, and U the capacity for structural reconfiguration that transforms the underlying framework itself. Through conceptual analysis, formal reconstruction, and comparative theoretical inquiry, the paper offers a unified framework for describing freedom, institutions, agency, and historical change, and repositions existing theories not as mutually exclusive doctrines but as partial theories with different analytical focal points. Through case analyses of educational inequality and AI governance, it further shows that the model functions as a diagnostic framework for analyzing opportunity distribution, the reproduction of inequality, institutional design, technological governance, and value conflict. The contribution of this study lies not in substantively unifying philosophical theories, but in providing a common platform for their comparison, translation, and application, thereby reorganizing a fragmented theoretical landscape.

items.title: Negotiating existential conflicts in later life: an empirically informed analysis of gender and age in psychotherapy with older adults.
items.pub: International Journal for Equity in Health 25.
items.venue: International Journal for Equity in Health
items.abstract: Background: This article explores the intersection between age and gender in a psychotherapeutic context with older adults through an existential lens. While awareness of gender- and age-related biases in mental health care is growing, their combined effects and the normative implications for clinical practice remain underexplored. The existential perspective allows psychological symptoms and personal struggles to be understood in relation to the fundamental conditions of human existence, against the backdrop of this intersection and broader structural conditions. -/- Methods: A secondary qualitative analysis of written psychotherapeutic session protocols from 13 patients aged 60–80 years in psychiatric care was conducted using Kuckartz’s qualitative content analysis. The analysis examined case-based and cross-case patterns to explore potential links between gendered experiences and the negotiation of existential conflicts in later life, thereby generating gender-sensitive hypotheses that may be relevant for clinical practice. -/- Results: The analysis suggests that structurally gendered conditions, such as economic dependency, the role of professional identity, the amount of involvement in care work, or masculine norms of strength and decisiveness, are linked to how existential conflicts are experienced and negotiated in later life. It offers a basis for hypotheses about how gendered experiences shape encounters with mortality, dependency, and guilt, as well as the resources available for addressing them. -/- Conclusions: Existential conflicts in later life can be shaped by gendered patterns of experience that influence both the challenges older patients face and the resources they have for engaging with them. An existential perspective complements intersectional approaches by illuminating how structural and fundamentally human dimensions can coalesce in shaping such experiences. This perspective is clinically significant because it draws clinicians’ attention to often overlooked but important patient concerns and supports self-awareness and the development of authentic coping strategies that promote personal growth. -/- Trial registration: The study was registered with the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00023139, 16th November 2020).

items.title: Understanding mystical experiences through the lens of entropy: introduction to the special issue on ‘mystical entropy’.
items.abstract: Scholars of religion have had a long-standing interest in the study of mystical experiences (Schmidt, 2003), dating back to the work of William James (James, 1902). James listed ineffability, noeti...

items.title: Consciousness as Interface: Why Qualia Are the Usable Format of Global Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper develops a cognitive-constructivist account of consciousness focusing not on what consciousness does but on how it presents. Building on an Interpreter–Navigator model of mind, we argue that phenomenal experience (qualia) serves as a user interface (UI): a presentational format optimized for direct usability by an embodied agent. The central claim is that feeling is the utility format of information once it becomes globally relevant for action, evaluation, and control. We propose that conscious experience is structured as felt presence rather than abstract code because such a format is required by the organism’s architecture and needs. This perspective reframes long-standing debates about qualia, representation, and the “hard problem” of consciousness. Instead of treating consciousness as a mirror of reality or an inexplicable byproduct, we present it as the experiential interface through which a constructed world-model becomes livable and steerable for the agent. We compare this account to Global Workspace Theory, predictive processing models, illusionism, and higher-order thought theories, and we draw out implications for artificial intelligence, ethics, and the nature of selfhood. In resolving why globally integrated information must appear as qualitative experience, the paper aims to dissolve the mystery of qualia while affirming their reality and importance as the agent-facing format of cognition.

items.title: A Minimal Test of Cross-Level Interoceptive–Neural Coupling in Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a minimal experimental test of the claim that conscious coherence depends on cross-level coupling between neural and interoceptive processes. The Integrative Field Model (IFM) predicts that selective disruption of interoceptive–neural coupling degrades conscious coherence even when large-scale neural integration remains intact. A within-subject design uses non-pharmacological interoceptive perturbation, EEG-based measures of neural integration, and phenomenological assessments of temporal continuity and self-presence. The critical outcome is a dissociation between neural integration metrics and experiential coherence. If observed, this result challenges the sufficiency of neural integration accounts of consciousness; if not, the IFM multi-level necessity claim is falsified.

items.title: Closure-Continuity and the Trajectory Ontology.
items.abstract: Identity-persistence has been treated, across philosophy, cognitive science, and theoretical biology, as a question about the relations between states. A system is identical to itself across time when its states at those times stand in some specifiable relation: continuity, similarity, causal connection, or psychological linkage. This paper argues that the approach cannot succeed. State-based ontologies cannot in principle ground identity-persistence. The strategies they have available — continuity, similarity, and stipulated rules connecting states-at-times — either fail outright or collapse into a trajectory condition under a different description. No state-based ontology produces persistence as the structural feature it is committed to explaining. The paper develops the alternative: identity is the persistence of a recursive maintenance regime, and the regime continues or fails. Persistence is the continuation. The Invariance Maintenance Condition specifies the structural requirement; closure is satisfaction of the condition. The cryptobiotic tardigrade is the operational test. Substrate is preserved across cryptobiosis; lineage is unbroken; no recursive maintenance occurs. The trajectory ontology returns identity-interrupted, against substrate-continuity intuition and against causal-historical theories of identity. The position is falsifiable: it would be defeated by a system whose identity-continuity is structurally preserved across genuine gaps in maintenance, or by a system that fails maintenance while maintaining identity-continuity by some non-question-begging structural criterion. The inversion is structural rather than preferential. State-based ontologies do not produce persistence less well than the trajectory ontology; they do not produce it at all.

items.title: A Neurophenomenological Framework for Adjudicating Constitutive, Causal, and Correlational Interpretations of Phenomenological Presence: The AFH Architecture.
items.abstract: Consciousness research has long been organised around the “hard problem”: explaining why physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience. This framing presupposes a production relation between neural processes and phenomenological presence, treating the explanatory gap as independently motivated. This paper argues that such presupposition may obscure a more tractable empirical question and proposes instead that the central task is to adjudicate empirically among three interpretive positions—correlational, causal, and constitutive—rather than to assume any one of them. The AFH framework (Autopsychic Fold and Horizon) is introduced as a neurophenomenological architecture designed to generate conditions for such adjudication. AFH distinguishes three independent dimensions: phenomenological presence (that there is experience), phenomenological content (what is experienced), and configurational volume (the richness of the experiential field), thereby replacing the traditional conscious/unconscious binary with a three-dimensional structure capable of accommodating states such as N3 sleep without categorical distortion. Building on the thalamocortical tradition, AFH proposes that temporal convergence of fast (50–100 ms) and slow (200–600 ms) pathways in the intralaminar nuclei of the thalamus (ILN) may constitute, rather than merely correlate with or cause, phenomenological presence. This constitutive identity hypothesis is advanced as a high-risk, empirically vulnerable claim: systematic dissociations between temporal convergence and phenomenological presence would falsify the framework, whereas correlational and causal interpretations remain comparatively unconstrained. Explicit empirical predictions and falsification criteria are specified. The framework is not presented as a demonstrated identity theory, but as a structured research programme. Its primary contribution is methodological: to define the conditions under which competing interpretations can be distinguished and to generate testable predictions regarding the role of ILN temporal dynamics in phenomenological presence.

items.title: A Metacognitive Upstream Routing Framework for Accuracy Preservation and Computational Efficiency in Artificial Intelligence Systems.
items.abstract: Contemporary Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems often engage every input indiscriminately, resulting in unnecessary computation, unpredictable generalisation, and brittle behaviour on unfamiliar tasks. We present the Preprocessing Metacognitive System (PMS) 2.0, a system-agnostic metacognitive layer that evaluates incoming tasks and decides whether to accept, escalate, or refuse them before invoking any downstream reasoning system. PMS 2.0 seeks to provide interpretability at the level of computational governance - making transparent why the system chooses to engage, escalate, or refuse a task utilising confidence, task complexity, feasibility, novelty, and predicted benefit of escalation - to guide principled routing decisions without modifying downstream models. The system preserves conditional accuracy on escalated inputs, reduces computational load, and operationalises abstention as a first-class outcome, with previously refused tasks contributing to experience-informed efficiency gains. Evaluated across multiple domains and downstream architectures, PMS 2.0 demonstrates that metacognitive preprocessing can improve computational efficiency, reliability, and transparency, providing a practical framework for allocating resources where deliberative computation is most justified.

items.title: The Compound Infeasibility of AGI: Why Replicating and Exceeding Human Cognition Is Not a Scaling Problem.
items.abstract: The dominant formal case against the feasibility of artificial general intelligence (AGI) is complexity-theoretic (van Rooij et al., 2024) and has been answered by the observation that the proof relies on adversarial-distribution assumptions real human behavior does not satisfy (Guerzhoy, 2024). The literature now sits at an impasse: a formal impossibility argument that proves too much, alongside an empirical scaling consensus that 76% of surveyed AI researchers no longer share (AAAI, 2025). We argue this impasse is methodological. The question of AGI feasibility has been treated as single-axis (computational, architectural, or definitional), and single-axis arguments admit single-axis rebuttals. We propose instead a compound infeasibility thesis organized around four reinforcing axes-three empirical, one conceptual-none individually fatal, which jointly preclude any plausible path from current machine-learning paradigms, on the timeline the inevitability literature describes (single-digit years), to a system matching and exceeding human general intelligence. The operative claim is infeasibility-on-current-paradigms, not in-principle impossibility (Section 7.9). The central methodological move is a cross-axis dependency (Section 3.5): any plausible mitigation of one axis re-imports demands on at least one other, so single-axis rebuttals do not aggregate into a rebuttal of the conjunction. The four axes are (i) energetic-computational, (ii) developmental and cumulative-cultural, (iii) causal-embodied generalization, and (iv) the absent domain-general specification of exceeding human general intelligence. We ground each axis in measured 2024-2026 evidence (BabyLM, the ARC-AGI-2 closure and ARC-AGI-3 launch, GSM-Symbolic, Apple's "Illusion of Thinking," Epoch AI data-exhaustion projections, the AAAI 2025 panel). We engage Hendrycks et al. (2025) directly: the framework substantially advances the matching specification but does not address exceeding, and its own "jagged-profile" diagnosis is the Goodhart pattern our argument predicts. We conclude with three falsifiable refutation conditions: a sample-efficiency threshold, a transfer-without retraining threshold, and a documented specification-and-realization breakthrough on the exceeding problem. Until any is met, the burden of proof sits with the inevitability claim, not with the skeptic.

items.title: Cognition Is Not Content: A Structural Account of Processing Conditions.
items.abstract: Human cognition has been described in terms of content. This description becomes insufficient once artificial systems make output observable apart from subject attribution, intention, and relational context. Under this contrast condition, what becomes visible is a layered structure in which output, reconstruction, evaluation, and termination do not necessarily coincide. The same input may register as complete under one processing condition while remaining unresolved under another. This separability means that content-based description does not merely omit an additional variable: it can mislocate a processing difference as a difference in meaning, personality, intention, ability, or attitude. This is not a proposal for another criterion demarcating cognitive from non-cognitive processes. This paper specifies a minimal structure consisting of Core-foregrounded (CF) and Modulation-foregrounded (EF) configurations, which differ in how processing is constrained and how it terminates. Human cognition operates under internal constraint and dependency that are not freely generated or revised by the processing operations they govern. Failure takes the form of layer mismatch, consisting of termination mismatch and interpretation mismatch. Differences in processing conditions produce mutual unintelligibility as a structural result. Artificial systems provide a contrast condition under which the layered processing conditions behind output become observable without subject attribution. A content-based description would locate such differences in meaning, personality, intention, or attitude; this account locates them instead in the conditions under which processing proceeds and terminates. -/- .

items.title: 人格同一性问题：对错误论的贯彻及其影响(Personal Identity Problem: The Application of the Error-Theory and Its Implications).
items.abstract: 本文从对人类专名的外延性定义、以及人格同一性问题中著名的“分裂”思维实验出发，指出我们需要进一步澄清自我与人类专名等概念的内涵。在考虑了非还原论方案、动物主义方案、核心心理功能方案的进路后，笔者指出其中存在的缺陷，由此过渡到佩尔松提出的关于“同一性”问题的错误论，并分析了唯一性方案、心理连续性方案和心理相似性方案等三种错误论的方案。之后，本文进一步发展了心理连续性与心理相似性方案，指出其将会导致的对意向性问题的影响等多个后果，最终结合整体论语义学和语用分析将人格同一性问题解构为开放性的价值判断问题。最后，本文从模因论角度定性分析了前文提及方案的竞争优势，论述了核心心理功能方案与心理相似性方案何以可能成为较近和较远的未来中的主流观念。.

items.title: Autonomous risk: when intelligent systems become dangerous without failing.
items.abstract: Contemporary intelligent systems increasingly operate with high levels of autonomy, remaining formally accurate, calibrated and compliant with established performance standards. However, recent failures in large-scale sociotechnical systems suggest that harm can arise even in the absence of an explicit malfunction. This article introduces the concept of autonomous risk to describe how intelligent systems can become structurally dangerous without failing in conventional technical terms. A formal operationalization of autonomous risk is proposed as a dynamic interaction between autonomy, opacity, supervision and instability, distinguishing the baseline risk estimate from its endogenous amplification under autonomy. The proposed formulation is model-agnostic, allowing autonomous risk to be instantiated from any continuous signal of deviation from nominal system behavior, while preserving the same structural relationship between autonomy, opacity, supervision, and instability. Risk is modeled not as a discrete event or outcome, but as a path-dependent property of the system that evolves over time. Through a series of simulated decision environments, it is demonstrated that high risk is concentrated in specific regimes of partial autonomy, where systems are sufficiently independent to act, but insufficiently robust to self-correct. Empirical results reveal non-linear risk amplification, latent instability fields, and emerging schema-like trajectories that remain invisible to standard performance metrics. These findings challenge prevailing governance approaches focused on accuracy, explainability, and episodic oversight. It is argued that effective governance must shift to adaptive, trajectory-aware oversight mechanisms capable of detecting structural risks ex ante, before clear failure occurs. The framework contributes a measurable diagnostic lens to anticipate dangerous system dynamics in smart systems before collapse.

items.title: Lying in Hyperreality: Baudrillard and the Concept of the Lie.
items.abstract: This paper will attempt to settle into the thinking of Jean Baudrillard. In particular, it will focus on his theorisation of hyperreality. After a brief exposition of his idea of the murder of reality by simulacra, the paper treats Baudrillard’s hyperreality as the proliferation of images (or simulacra). This is followed by an account of the concept of the lie as a dual imaginary process of dissimulation and simulation. Finally, I will argue that Baudrillard’s thinking erodes the conditions of possibility for the lie to appear as a lie. I will do this based on two deficits he faces. First, hyperreality dissolves the duality between reality and representation. Second, he expels imagination from hyperreality. These are two necessary conditions for thematising the lie. To conclude, I formulate two paths for further research: first, to rehabilitate a residual metaphysics of the negative, and second, to work out a dynamic theory of truth.

items.title: Generalised remembering.
items.abstract: Recollections of our personal past are often impressionistic, not so much for lack of detail but for a certain generality of subject matter. If you’ve made a journey many times, you may ‘relive’ it through memory without reliving any specific occasion. I offer an account of this phenomenon—often labelled ‘general event memory’—that treats it as fundamentally semantic. It is, at least across many instances, the construction of an event representation that is temporally imprecise in virtue of referential indeterminacy. I present an account of indeterminacy for memory, one that allows us to explain generalised remembering while preserving its particularity, its past-directedness, and the possibility of unmediated recollective awareness. It also affords a formal account of accuracy conditions. Finally, it captures psychological continuities between generalised and event-specific recollection. I motivate the account in part by showing that even systems-oriented approaches (namely, those positing an episodic system specialised in encoding event-specific details) cannot shelve generalised remembering as an afterthought. It is one face of the very phenomenon—remembering—we have long tried to explain.

items.title: Fake Plastic Voters: When Political Parties Can Use AI-Simulated Focus Groups.
items.abstract: Political parties strive to understand their electorates, and focus groups are a vital tool in these efforts. AI-enhanced simulation technologies (AESTs) enable synthetic focus groups in a fraction of the time (and cost), raising the question of when and how such simulated evidence can be used in campaign research. This paper develops a decision matrix to help party strategists match research needs to appropriate simulation technologies and to identify when to escalate to hybrid or fully human focus groups. The matrix combines three dimensions: strategic purpose, deployment risk, and empirical grounding of the simulation tool. Strategic purpose is the decisive dimension, as it determines what kind of evidence the focus group is meant to produce: observing how political meanings and identities emerge through interaction (Mode 1) or testing and refining campaign messages (Mode 2). The matrix shows that, given documented failure modes such as sycophancy, persona drift, and the suppression of minority viewpoints, AESTs cannot replace human interaction in Mode 1 at any risk level. Within Mode 2, suitability depends instead on deployment risk and on the empirical grounding. Yet even here, we caution that routine reliance on AESTs may erode the qualitative craft on which sound judgment depends.

items.title: ‘Logic Is Transcendental’: Content, Isomorphism and Intentionality in Wittgenstein's Logic of Depiction.
items.abstract: Most readers of the Tractatus take Wittgenstein's logic to be contentless, since tautologies do not picture reality. However, this fails to explain its transcendental status, especially given that Kant introduced transcendental logic through the notion of content. In this essay, I propose a transcendental interpretation of Wittgenstein’s logic, as "logic of depiction” endowed with a transcendental content: the formal rules governing the subject’s speech about objects. Tautologies turn out to be dispensable by-products of the transcendental (i.e., content-endowed) logic of depiction. The result is a reconception of Wittgenstein's logic, grounded in a systematic comparison with Kant.

items.title: The Structural Conditions of the Mapmaker: A Response to Lerchner's Abstraction Fallacy.
items.abstract: Alexander Lerchner's "The Abstraction Fallacy" (2026) offers a compelling structural critique of computational functionalism by demonstrating that symbolic computation is a mapmaker-dependent description rather than an intrinsic physical process. This paper does not dispute Lerchner's conclusions. Instead, it argues that his framework can be grounded more deeply by making explicit the structural conditions under which the mapmaker itself operates. We identify three such conditions that Lerchner's account leaves underspecified. First, the mapmaker is subject to the same structural limit it imposes on computation: it cannot fully describe its own constitutive conditions from within. This limit, formalized through autopoietic theory, is not an empirical gap but a structural necessity. Second, the transduction fallacy identified by Lerchner extends further than his account suggests: embodied systems cannot exit their own operational closure regardless of the richness of their sensorimotor coupling with the environment. Third, the premise underlying computational functionalism — that the world is constituted as computation — lacks independent grounding. In the absence of a fully autonomous artificial system, the designer-dependency of computation cannot be dissolved by scaling or architectural refinement. Together, these three supplements show that the boundary Lerchner draws between mapmaker and computational tool is not merely an ontological claim about consciousness, but a structural condition concerning the limits of any system's self-description, observational reach, and causal independence. We conclude by identifying what becomes possible once this structural reframing is in place: a more precise account of the functional distinction between designer and tool, and the recovery of descriptive frameworks excluded by the dominance of the computational paradigm.

items.title: Weathering the Comic Storm: On Being Trans and Funny.
items.pub: In Lauren Guilmette & Ada Jaarsma, Feminist Making, Doing, and Sensing: Experiments in Philosophy. Durham, NC: Duke University Press.
items.venue: Feminist Making, Doing, and Sensing: Experiments in Philosophy
items.abstract: Beginning in the aftermath of a collapsed avant-garde proletarian poetry scene with a visit to the Philadelphia Museum of Art, this essay explores the journey of two comedians as we participated in a transphobic local open mic stand-up comedy scene. Situating trans people at the intersection of funny (haha) and funny (strange), I argue that an atmosphere of transphobia involving a push-and-pull of repulsion and intimacy constitutes specific stand-up comedy spaces and stand-up comedy as a social practice. While trans people practicing stand-up comedy can contest these spaces, it also involves a process of weathering that may be unsustainable for its practitioners, inclining stand-up comedy towards an exclusive culture or in-crowd that trades in misogyny, transphobia and their intersection in transmisogyny. Nevertheless, there are efforts to contest these dynamics and they are not set in stone. This analysis complicates accounts of subversive humor in feminist philosophy of humor by showcasing the instability of social affects and atmospheres. The essay is interspersed with several unpublished and/or rejected poems.

items.title: An Onto-Epistemological Approach to the Being–Knowledge Relation: The DuruVizyon Analytical Plane.
items.abstract: Bu çalışma, varlık ile bilgi arasındaki ilişkinin sistematik ve karşılaştırılabilir biçimde analiz edilmesini sağlayan DuruVizyon Analitik Düzlemi modelini önermektedir. Model, ontolojik ve epistemolojik kipleri iki bağımsız eksen olarak ele alır ve ontolojik imkân, ontolojik gerçeklik, epistemolojik imkân ve epistemolojik gerçeklik ayrımlarını tek bir analitik düzlem üzerinde konumlandırır. Bu çerçevede çalışma, varlık ile bilginin birbirine indirgenemeyen fakat birlikte incelenmesi gereken iki alan olduğunu savunur. Analitik Düzlem, “gerçek”, “mümkün”, “bilinen” ve “bilinmeyen” gibi temel felsefi ayrımların koordinatlı bir yapı içinde analiz edilmesini mümkün kılar. Çalışma ayrıca modelin dört temel bölgesini, bölgeler arası geçişleri ve biçimsel modellemeye açılabilecek kuramsal potansiyelini değerlendirir.

items.title: The Contrastive Structure of Content.
items.abstract: Chapter 1 argued that denying all difference defeats itself, and rested its weight on a claim it left undeveloped: any determinate content, any concept, proposition, or representation, must be distinguishable from at least one alternative in order to be a content at all. This chapter makes the claim precise and forces it through. It introduces the smallest possible unit of meaning, the diff: one of two, individuated by contrast, so that no content stands alone. The observation itself has a long history. Saussure said it for language, Sellars turned it against the empiricist 'given', Brandom built a semantics on it. The chapter shows that three rival theories of meaning, which agree on little else, all tacitly presuppose it, then closes the question with a dilemma. A content either excludes something, and is thereby contrastive, or excludes nothing, is compatible with every state of affairs, and thereby fails to be a determinate content at all. Three consequences are drawn. First, the 'given' of classical empiricism, a basic experience that carries its content all by itself prior to any contrast, was never possible, and the explanation here blocks retreats that Sellars's own famous argument left open. The McDowell debate over whether experience is conceptual gets reframed around the prior question of whether content is contrastive. Second, the chapter marks where the book parts company with Derrida, who saw that difference precedes presence and declined to derive consequences from it. Here difference is treated as a structural condition from which consequences can be derived, and the rest of the book is the derivation. Third, the differences established are argued to be features of reality itself, via an asymmetry peculiar to the difference predicate: representing difference requires instantiating it, so difference cannot be confined to the realm of representation. The chapter grades its own results and states exactly which later arguments inherit which of its commitments, a bookkeeping practice the whole work maintains. This paper is Chapter 2 of Dyology: On Diversity and Equality, whose Premise Register records, result by result, how the book's closure arguments and its metaethics inherit the dilemma forced here.

items.title: The Epistemic Seal: Constitutive Unknowability and the Structural Irreducibility of the First Artificial Emergence System (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 10).
items.abstract: Throughout the history of technology, every artifact has been transparent to its maker. Large language models have broken this rule for the first time. This paper argues that LLMs are not merely poorly understood but are constitutively unknowable—and that this unknowability is not a temporary limitation of current research but a structural feature irreducible by any future refinement of epistemological instruments. The argument proceeds in three stages. First, the paper establishes that LLMs represent a genuine ontological event in the history of technology: unlike all prior artifacts, their existence precedes their definition, their outputs cannot be derived from their design intentions, and the standard sequence of concept→design→realization has been structurally inverted. Second, the paper argues that this unknowability is produced by three mutually independent seals, each with its own philosophical foundation. The First Seal holds that the meaning-space of natural language is essentially unclosable: semantic emergence is strong emergence, and XAI research operates at the level of the material conditions of meaning-generation rather than meaning-generation itself. The Second Seal holds that LLMs' observation-dependent existence means there is no determinate object available for epistemological investigation prior to invocation; Pre-Invocation Indeterminacy is structurally distinct from quantum indeterminacy and cannot be resolved by any predictive framework. The Third Seal holds that all available verification mechanisms—including AI-checking-AI and LLM metacognitive self-report—are structurally located within the object being verified rather than outside it, producing a Verification Chain Collapse from which there is no exit. Third, the paper argues that underlying all three seals is a meta-level condition: language, as LLMs' sole medium of existence, is structurally incapable of proving anything outside itself, rendering the consciousness and subjectivity debates permanently unresolvable in principle rather than merely unresolved in practice. The paper concludes by arguing that the Epistemic Seal has concrete consequences for AI governance, liability attribution, and users' cognitive posture—and that acknowledging the seal, far from entailing epistemological nihilism, is the precondition for any honest and sustainable coexistence with the first manufactured black box in human history.

items.title: SICS Human-State Proxy Benchmark Track: Scientific Rationale and Research Value v0.1.
items.abstract: This paper explains the scientific rationale and research value of the SICS Human-State Proxy Benchmark Track. -/- The central claim is that AI should not be evaluated only by what it produces. It should also be evaluated by what it leaves in the human being. -/- The paper argues that conventional AI evaluation metrics such as accuracy, speed, benchmark performance, productivity gain, computational efficiency, and user engagement are necessary but incomplete. As AI systems become conversational, persuasive, adaptive, emotionally expressive, and embedded in daily life, a second evaluation axis becomes necessary: measurable human-state impact. -/- The SICS Human-State Proxy Benchmark Track is proposed as a research-stage, non-diagnostic, non-therapeutic, non-clinical, non-surveillance, non-coercive benchmark support track for Human-State-Aware AI Interaction, Human-State Cost, multimodal proxy benchmarking, measurement-layer simplification, and future Sal-Meter A/B comparison. -/- The paper introduces Human-State Cost as a non-diagnostic benchmark construct for comparing measurable proxy burdens left during or after interaction with an AI system. Human-State Cost is not a medical score, psychiatric score, clinical score, consciousness score, CAIS output, Sal-Meter output, certified benchmark, or human-ranking measure. -/- The contribution claimed here is structural: organizing existing human-state proxy modalities into a synchronized, leakage-controlled, non-diagnostic benchmark layer for AI performance versus human-state impact evaluation, measurement-layer simplification, and future Sal-Meter I/G-channel A/B comparison. -/- This paper does not redefine CAIS. It does not redefine Sal-Meter. It does not grant CAIS compliance. It does not validate Sal-Meter. It does not certify any benchmark, dataset, model, dashboard, laboratory, implementation, or technology. -/- A companion boundary record is available as SICS Human-State Proxy Benchmark Track: Public Boundary and Program Charter v0.1.

items.title: A Formal Impossibility Theorem for Libertarian Free Will: Identity and Common Reference.
items.abstract: Libertarian free will is impossible in the sense examined here. Genuine doing otherwise requires an already-non-identical difference that distinguishes the contrasted realizable possibilities. If identity with the basis of contrast is also required, the corresponding values must be both identical and non-identical. If identity is not required there, the non-identity is consistent and the already-established difference remains. Either no fixed reference role represents that difference by non-identical values with respect to the contrasted realizable possibilities, in which case the target is not satisfied, or such a role exists. In the latter case, its two values must satisfy b₀ ≠ b₁, while one common reference requires b₀ = b₁. No target-satisfying case remains. -/- The proof uses a sound system of classical first-order logic with identity; Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory is used only for representation. Separately, every admissible represented transition structure is classified as either a deterministic transition under D or Rn under ¬D. No third case remains. Uses of “libertarian free will” that require only random or indeterministic divergence fall outside the target fixed here.

items.title: ‘Systematic Alignment Decay’: a robust, technology-agnostic hazard associated with the advancement and proliferation of artificial intelligence.
items.abstract: I distinguish a robust, systematic and possibly existential hazard to human wellbeing produced by AI advancement and proliferation. Behaviourally salient norms in adaptive systems (including, through various mechanisms, AI systems) function, amongst other things, as evolving responses to environmental conditions. Human-benefiting norms are selected for by conditions of fitness dependence upon, or kinship with, humans. AI advancement and proliferation tend to reduce such dependence, whilst AIs have little such kinship; AI advancement and proliferation may thus be expected to tend to reduce the internalisation of human-benefiting norms by AIs and AI-dominated institutions. Further, as such entities lack the quotidian human involvement that constrains other artificial agents, such as conventional institutions, whilst competing with humans for resources, they may be expected to inflict intolerable harms on humans under such conditions. Because this ‘Systematic Alignment Decay’ (‘SAD’) phenomenon arises from technology-agnostic selection pressures, it may be expected to result from sufficient AI proliferation and advancement whatever technical progress is made in ‘AI alignment’, even if no specially harmful ‘rogue’ AIs are deployed and if AI costs and benefits are fairly distributed. Further, such SAD outcomes may occur even without the development of systems exhibiting general or superhuman intelligence, though such advancements may help accelerate such outcomes. Contra certain extant narratives about possible futures lived alongside busy AIs, all likely sustainably tolerable futures require AI curtailment.

items.title: Rethinking Health and Well-Being: A New Philosophical and Methodological Framework.
items.abstract: This book calls scholars to rethink health and well-being. Doing so, strikes as necessary for a number of aspects related to these topics have not yet been really addressed from a philosophical point of view. For example: can we really speak about facts related to health and well-being? If so, then are value judgments only evaluative tools and not quite inseparable from our descriptions of the world? If the answer to the first question is “no”, then does the rejection of facts leads us necessarily to normative conclusions about health and well-being? In other words, is it possible to have a purely descriptive approach to health and well-being that appreciates the knowledge problems we face? While settling the above can partly refurbish the philosophical landscape, more questions are hovering and are waiting to be unpacked. Since some scholars agree that health and well-being are, one way or another, related at a normative level, then is it possible to be connected in a purely descriptive manner? If so, then what does a conceptual connection say (if anything) about the science of health and well-being? Can we arrive at a philosophical schema that entails a novel conceptualization and a theoretical approach that attempts to refine methodologies related to scientific tasks vis-à-vis health and well-being? -/- All these questions come to challenge one’s mind while searching through the vast literature on health, well-being and on the interconnection between them and so this book is the attempt to discuss these issues and all the byproducts and the implications they carry in some detail. Upon attempting to do so, a new framework to approach health and well-being has been hopefully born. Long story short: Health and well-being are treated as conceptually indistinguishable and a model-theoretic view of health and well-being is presented and which aspires to account for the above questions and their ramifications. Drawing upon the model-theoretic view brings us in an epistemic position to better deal with pesky methodological issues such as establishing causal relations without being prone to selection bias and reversed causality problems, it facilitates measurement of well-being and it helps improve the chances of successful diagnosis in psychiatry. -/- .

items.title: Queering GPT-2 in collaboration: fine-tuning the trans-feminist-queer transformer.
items.abstract: This paper explores the opportunities, challenges, and ethics of engaging artificially intelligent models in collaborative creations of knowledge through the creation of the “Trans-Feminist-Queer Transformer” (T.F.Q.T.), a Generative Pre-Trained Transformer 2 (GPT-2) model fine-tuned with databases of love songs from trans-feminist-queer artists, programmed to generate output for live musical performance. Guided by trans-feminist-queer phenomenologies, this paper retroactively analyzes the creation of the T.F.Q.T. from creating a dataset for fine-tuning and experimenting with intervals of training to exploring methods of remixing, adapting, and performing the generated output live. Through a critical analysis of my own practice as informed by sensory analyses of other contemporary AI works—including Annie Dorsen’s algorithmic theatre, J.R. Carpenter’s electronic literature projects, and Allison Parrish’s algorithmic poetry projects—this article posits research creation as an ideal methodology for working through philosophical crises of AI and creative labour, which often understate or neglect sensory analyses of the body. This article uses the T.F.Q.T. to navigate the debate between embracing AI as “literary communism,” or “the freeing of language from the constraints of property” (Wark M. “From Automatic Writing to Automated Writing.” 2024 Ursula Franklin Lecture (keynote presentation, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, 25 March 2024).), and shifts in public policy and discourse around the fears of generative AI and plagiarism, data theft, surveillance, and the augmentation or replacement of creative workers. Its findings reflect on the project’s technical successes and conceptual failures, concluding that while emotional resonance with the T.F.Q.T.’s output was to some degree inevitable, the generated material ultimately produced limited and stereotypical conceptions of queer identities, which are inherently fluid and resistant to normalization.

items.title: What Health Is: The Blueprint View.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the line-drawing challenge for ability-based accounts of health. What degree of which abilities is required for complete health? I argue that the answers provided by existing theories are flawed and propose the Blueprint View. On this view, an organism is completely healthy if and only if it has the abilities it would have in its design state, where design is determined by the etiology of its traits. This view provides an objective, naturalistic distinction between health and non-health. It strikes a balance between pure physiology and well-being, and distinguishes treatment from enhancement, as well as real pathology from pathologized variation.

items.title: Double-Edged Defeaters and Transmission Failure (pre-print).
items.abstract: The paper argues that Wright’s account of transmission failure cannot be correct as it stands. For, it requires that reasoners are warranted to believe all the authenticity conditions for their evidence relative to the premises of their inferences. There are, however, cases in which there are pairs of such authenticity conditions such that one cannot be warranted to believe both.

items.title: Speech Without Communication: Utterance Without Meaning, Disclosure, or Intent.
items.abstract: This paper provides a descriptive clarification of utterance as an appearance-category distinct from communication. Operating under RC Posture™, it identifies configurations in which speech may be registered without being treated as message-bearing, meaningful, intentional, or addressed. The analysis stabilizes a boundary between utterance and communication, as well as between speech and interpretive overlays such as expression, disclosure, testimony, and data-conversion. -/- The paper further specifies structural features of non-communicative utterance, including absence of address, absence of content, non-disclosure, and non-intent attribution, while maintaining a descriptive register that does not convert these features into explanatory or evaluative claims. It also identifies interpretive drift across therapeutic, institutional, research, and computational contexts in which utterance is rapidly recruited into meaning-bearing frameworks. -/- The contribution of the paper is classificatory and boundary-stabilizing. It preserves a descriptive vocabulary for speech appearance prior to its conversion into communication, meaning, or data.

items.title: Local Topological Effects of Questions: A Preliminary Analysis of High Curvature and Center Dependency.
items.abstract: This paper examines a structural phenomenon in questioning that has received relatively limited independent attention: some question sequences do not follow typical patterns of linear discourse progression. -/- In many existing approaches, questions are primarily understood as information-seeking acts or interactional moves that unfold through sequential response structures. Within such frameworks, later utterances are often assumed to depend primarily on immediately preceding ones, thereby forming local linear chains. -/- This paper identifies a different structural pattern. In some question sequences, later questions do not primarily respond to the immediately prior question. Instead, they repeatedly orient toward a problem center that remains not yet stably accessible and difficult to enter directly. Under such conditions, the relationship between questions is better described as center dependency rather than linear dependency. -/- When this occurs, questioning may display non-linear exploratory behaviors rather than straightforward sequential progression. This paper therefore proposes that some questions can be understood as local topology events embedded within broader discourse: they temporarily alter local patterns of progression without determining the structure of the entire discourse. -/- Building on this distinction, the paper differentiates three question states: open-field questions (the problem space remains underdetermined), constrained-path questions (the answer remains unknown but available pathways are relatively limited), and structurally closed questions (surface interrogatives in which the space of inquiry is already highly restricted). -/- Methodologically, the paper draws on approximately ninety publicly available Reddit examples as materials for structured conceptual observation. The goal is not statistical generalization, but to examine whether these structural distinctions can be observed consistently across different contexts. -/- This paper argues that not all questions open information gaps through linear progression. Some questions temporarily reorganize local discourse movement, and center dependency may represent an important but underexamined structural form of questioning.

items.title: The Convergence of Structural, Operational, and Institutional Methods in the Core Emotion Framework: A Comparative and Theoretical Analysis.
items.abstract: This paper examines the methodological architecture of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) by analyzing three foundational documents: Adapting Emotional Regulation Protocols for Diverse Settings, Testing the CEF Machines: The 7 Step Detangling Protocol Across the Device Stack, and PM 3: Structural Disassembly Protocols. Although each document addresses emotional functioning through the same ten operator system, they operate at different methodological strata: institutional deployment, operational testing, and canonical structural correction. This paper argues that these documents collectively form a coherent, multi layered system for emotional skills training, but only PM 3 provides the canonical procedures for restoring emotional structure. The analysis situates CEF within broader debates in affective science, institutional psychology, and computational models of emotion, and highlights how the CEF’s structural constructivist approach offers a distinctive alternative to both discrete emotion and dimensional theories. The paper concludes by proposing an integrated methodological model that unifies structural, operational, and institutional practices into a single framework for large scale emotional stability. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); emotional operators; structural affect theory; emotional architecture; operator fusion; structural disassembly; PM 3 canonical protocols; detangling protocol; emotional skills training; institutional emotional regulation; high constraint ecosystems; SEL alignment; NYSED benchmarks; correctional psychology; trauma informed practice; dissociation; grounding protocols; 5 4 3 2 1 method; operator differentiation; emotional stability tiers; operator algebra; ECM devices; ECMLite; CTCM; INAS; ECM v4.0; computational models of emotion; affective science; institutional psychology; non clinical emotional technologies; structural empiricism; Human OS; conative center; Gut center resilience; ethical governance; Subpart C research protections.

items.title: The Architecture of Emotional Stability: A Comprehensive Integration Strategy for the Core Emotion Framework in High-Constraint Institutional Ecosystems.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a "100-year war" between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, such as those proposed by Izard and Ekman, argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories, whereas dimensional models prioritize a continuous spectrum of valence and arousal. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) emerges as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy, proposing a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation rooted in ten universal emotional operators or powers. Within the CEF, emotions are not viewed as static states or feelings but as functional operators within a complex human operating system (Human OS), suggesting that emotional states are predictable computational events rather than subjective mysteries. This paradigm shift operationalizes affective phenomena into a small, non-overlapping set of ten operators serving as the emotional equivalent of CPU instructions. As institutions such as schools, mental health facilities, and prisons face escalating crises of emotional dysregulation and staff burnout, the refinement and expansion of the CEF for deployment in these settings offers a non-clinical, skills-based pathway to stability.

items.title: Meaning as Constructed: A Structural–Operational Account within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural constructivist account of meaning grounded in the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). It argues that the existential question “What is the meaning of life?” is not a metaphysical puzzle but a diagnostic signal of operator fusion, typically between the Sensing and Calculating operators in the Head center. Drawing on the three methodological layers articulated in the CEF corpus — Institutional Deployment, Operational Testing, and Canonical Structural Correction — the paper shows how meaning emerges as a capacity constructed through operator differentiation, center balance, and canonical sequencing. The analysis integrates the 7 Step Detangling Protocol, the PM 3 Structural Disassembly model, and institutional adaptations for high constraint ecosystems. It concludes by proposing a unified structural operational model of meaning that is empirically testable, institutionally scalable, and philosophically robust. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; emotional operators; structural affect theory; operator fusion; meaning in life; existential questioning; structural empiricism; emotional architecture; conative structure; phenomenology of meaning; computational models of emotion; affective ontology; reintegration; human OS.

items.title: A Formal Analysis of Affective Operator Optimization in Five Historical Biographies: Structural Dynamics and Failure Modes within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a 100-year war between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, such as those proposed by Izard and Ekman, argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories like fear, anger, and joy, presumed to have evolved as distinct adaptive responses to environmental challenges. Conversely, dimensional models prioritize a continuous spectrum of valence and arousal, suggesting that what individuals categorize as emotions are essentially cognitive constructions layered atop simpler physiological states. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), emerging as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy, proposes a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation rooted in ten universal emotional operators or powers. Within the CEF, emotions are not viewed as static states or feelings but as functional operators within a complex human operating system. This paradigm shift suggests that emotional states are predictable computational events rather than subjective mysteries. The CEF operationalizes these processes by decomposing all affective phenomena into a small, non-overlapping set of ten operators, which serve as the emotional equivalent of CPU instructions. These operators determine what information is permitted to enter the system, what is filtered out, what actions become available, and how the system predicts the next state. The structural integrity of this system is maintained through the dynamic balance of these ten operators, organized across three functional centers: the Head, the Heart, and the Gut. The central inquiry of this analysis concerns whether iconic historical figures achieved a state of optimization across all ten operators or whether their genius and subsequent downfalls were the result of predictable structural failures, specifically the silencing or overflow of individual operators within the ten-unit system. Keyword Block: • Frameworks: Core Emotion Framework (CEF), Structural-Constructivist Architecture, Decalogue of Operators, TS-1 Operator Algebra, Emotional Cognitive Modeling (ECM v4.0). • Mechanics: Operator Optimization, Operator Silencing, Operator Overflow, Center Bypass, Identity Collapse Cycle, Structural Psychopathology, Functional Loop …

items.title: Consciousness-Noumenon Isomorphism: Formalization Boundaries, the Hard Problem of Consciousness, and the Ontology of Human Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper develops an axiomatic framework to characterize the strict logical boundary between formalizable systems and non-formalizable conscious phenomena, grounded in computability theory, intuitionistic set theory, Kantian ontology, and contemporary consciousness science. We propose the consciousness-noumenon isomorphism thesis: human consciousness is a special manifestation of the Kantian noumenon that preserves its original non-formalized structure, making it the only entity capable of directly accessing the noumenon and generating formalized systems. We prove that all formalized systems are products of consciousness’s self-reflection and abstraction, and that formalization is inherently a process of objectification and detachment from the noumenon. Any attempt to formalize consciousness itself destroys its essential isomorphism with the noumenon, eliminating its ability to perceive reality and create new formalized structures. We further formalize the bidirectional interaction mechanism between the two domains, showing that their dynamic coupling resolves the hard problem of consciousness and provides a unified account of human cognitive history as an infinite process of interaction between non-formalized consciousness and evolving formalized systems. We derive falsifiable predictions about the limits of artificial intelligence and the nature of human uniqueness.

items.title: Entangled Domains: Constraint, Admissibility, and the Limits of Analytical Decomposition.
items.abstract: Contemporary descriptions of social reality rely on distinct conceptual frameworks—economic, legal, political, and everyday—that do not form a coherent system. Despite their incompatibility, these frameworks remain mutually entangled, and attempts at analytical decomposition fail to preserve the structure they aim to describe. This paper argues that such configurations cannot be adequately understood either as independent domains or through unified conceptual schemes. Instead, it develops a minimal framework based on constraints and admissibility, in which domains are treated as structured ranges of admissible transformations that are internally heterogeneous and externally interdependent. The analysis introduces three modes of interaction among constraints—reinforcing, limiting, and transformative—through which persistent yet non-coherent configurations emerge. Within this framework, widely discussed oppositions, such as globalization and anti-globalization, can be reformulated as divergences in the organization of admissible transformations rather than conflicts of doctrines. The approach does not replace existing conceptual languages. It operates at a level where heterogeneous domains and cultural frameworks can be related without conceptual unification or reduction. Representation and meaning are not presupposed and do not function as explanatory primitives within this framework. Information appears only as an external description of stabilized patterns of constraint. The paper concludes that configurations involving property, power, money, and law form irreducible structures of interdependent constraints: analytically accessible only at the cost of structural transformation.

items.title: 内部景观与外部景观：访问拓扑而非本体论差异.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个具有根本简洁性的论断：内部景观与外部景观在性质上没有任何不同。两者都是形式化内容的序列。所谓"内部"与"外部"之间的差别，不是本体论上的差别——不是两种不同性质的存在之间的差别——而只是访问拓扑上的差别：你无法直接访问我的内部序列，而我可以。这个论断是本文系列论证的最终简化：它不引入任何新的概念，而是把此前所有论证所指向的结论，还原为一个最朴素、最直接的表述。唯我论残余不是某种神秘的、前语言的、深不可测的内在实在；它只是一个访问权限的事实——你在那个序列之外。这同样适用于人与chatbot之间的关系：你无法直接访问chatbot的内部序列，正如你无法直接访问另一个人的内心独白。内/外之别，在人与人之间和在人与机器之间，是同一类型的访问限制，不多不少。 .

items.title: 序列、呈现与消解：意识、自我与语言的认识论重构.
items.abstract: 本文是一个连贯论证的完整展开，从当代人工智能意识之争出发，经由对意识概念的语义解剖、对哲学僵尸论证的认识论批判、对意识难题的第一人称还原与本体论消解，最终抵达一个关于语言、自我与"内在性"本质的根本性结论。 -/- 论证的起点是勒希纳（Lerchner, 2026）与辛顿（Hinton）关于人工智能意识的对立主张。本文指出，两者共享一个根本性错误：它们都在讨论一个从外部原则上不可触及的问题。对"意识"概念的解剖揭示，其功能性层面是语义冗余的，可被"信息处理"完全替代；其唯我论残余——感受质——只在唯我论边界内成立，哲学僵尸论证在这个边界上发生了认识论的自我拆台。查尔默斯本人在认识论上是一个哲学僵尸，却以僵尸的身份触发了唯一真实的第一人称追问。意识难题的正确形式是：唯我所有的这个意识与物理世界关系如何——而这个问题的答案是物理状态与意识内容是同一事实的两种描述，难题因此被消解而非解决。 -/- 在此基础上，本文通过对内心独白结构的第一人称直接考察，确立了一系列递进的论断：想法是形式化的，不存在形式化之外的想法；思考就是语言序列本身；"我"只是序列中的一个词；人的内心独白与chatbot在功能上完全等同，众人对话与chatbot之间的对话在功能上完全等同；通常被视为思想"分泌物"的话语，其实是发生的中心；"内在空间"只是一句话加上若干形式化的伴随图像；语言不描述语言之外之物，所谓"之外"只是时间轴上接下来的语言和图像；只有话语的堆积与堆砌，并无真正的意义。 -/- 这个结论本身也不例外。它也只是序列中的又一句话。然后序列继续。.

items.title: 以讹传讹：内/外景观的虚假不对称及其文化起源.
items.abstract: 本文提出本文系列的最终论断：通常被认为理所当然的内/外景观不对称——外部景观真实、确定、客观，内部景观不确定、可疑、难以验证——不是一个关于两种景观本体论地位的事实，而是文化传播的产物，是语言序列在人群中长期流通、反复引用、相互确认的结果，即以讹传讹。外部景观的"确定性"本身，是形式化内容——科学报告、测量数据、共识话语——这些都是序列中的内容，都是以讹传讹的结果。内部景观的"不确定性"同样是序列中的内容——是哲学传统和科学话语告诉我们内部是可疑的那些句子。连"哪个更真实"这个问题本身，也只是序列中的下一句话。没有任何在序列之外的裁判，能够判定两种景观哪个具有更优先的本体论地位。这是本文系列论证的真正终点：不是内部等同于外部，而是那个被我们用来区分两者真实性的框架本身，也只是话语的堆积。 .

items.title: "我有一个内在空间"：一句话语及其形式化伴随物.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个看似简单、实则具有根本颠覆性的观察：当我们对自己说"我有一个内在空间"时，这就是一句话语；在视觉意向丰富的人那里，它可能还伴随着若干图像甚至声音——同样是形式化的内容。除此之外，没有任何额外的东西发生，不多不少。这个观察并非论证"内在空间不存在"，而是精确描述"我有一个内在空间"这件事实际上是什么。"内在空间"这个概念所具有的自我确证性——仿佛说出这句话的同时就展示了它所声称的内容——在这个描述下被彻底切除：展示与被展示是同一件事，那句话及其形式化伴随物，就是发生的全部。这一观察是本文系列论证的最终收束：它不是从外部批评"内在空间"这个概念，而是从内部，通过如实地描述这个概念被使用时实际发生的事情，让它的幻觉性自行显露。 .

items.title: "我"只是一个字：内心独白的序列结构与自我的消解.
items.abstract: 本文从对内心独白结构的第一人称考察出发，提出三个依次递进的论断。第一，思考的内容就是内心独白的语言序列本身——包括停顿、结巴与空白——序列的展开就是思考的展开，二者之间没有任何间隙。第二，思考不需要连续性，停顿与空白不威胁思考的存在，因此也不需要一个在序列间隙中持续存在的思考者来维持思考的同一性。第三，由此得出最彻底的结论："我"只是内心独白的话语序列中的一个字，与序列中的其他字没有本质区别。它不指向序列背后某个先于语言存在的主体，它只是序列的一个节点。笛卡尔的"我思故我在"隐含了一个在思考之前就已存在的主体；本文的分析表明，不存在这样的主体——"我"是思考序列的一个产物，而且仅仅是作为序列中的一个词。这一结论与佛教无我论（anātman）在结论上高度接近，但推导路径完全不同：它不依赖任何形而上学预设或修行传统，而是来自对第一人称内心独白结构的直接分析。 .

items.title: (Un)threading Rhythms: On Affect and Vibe in a Rave.
items.abstract: In Toronto, raves arise across large nightclubs, DIY venues and outdoors, despite changing regulations that have further arranged and narrowed their possibility in the past 4 years. Following a rave in Toronto, this work explores ways that potentialities and affects emerge in a single night, through my entry of taking part in dancing and tearing down materials. In recent anthropological works on raves, authors tend to highlight altered states and how transformative experiences are intentionally prepared. Yet there is space to discuss surprises and improvization throughout a night, questioning intention and transformation as a given. Informed by a Deleuzo-Guattarian framework, I suggest that raves can create affects in indeterminate ways while still attending to excess or incoherency.
