In this vein, I conceptualize affects in relation to chaos: as intensities in indeterminate becomings, capable of taking on their own rhythms and cutting across bodies and sensations. Drawing from journal notes of the rave, I write through points of gaps, awkwardness, and incoherencies that follow along stories of coming together and coming undone in broader rhythms. Tactile and sonorous experiences of attaching cables or swaying my neck to metallic snares come up against moments I acknowledge are ineffable, or that I cannot be attentive to. A sound may resonate with a rise in intensity, or be unnoticed, or change entirely in timbre. In exploring indeterminacy, I recall moments of catching a breath in the crowd, or when the dancefloor and music seem to exhale passingly into step or chaotic stupor. Through my positioning in equipment disassembly and dancing in a night, this work hopes to offer an unsettling approach.

items.title: 话语作为发生的中心：内心独白、对话与语言的本体论地位.
items.abstract: 本文提出三个依次递进的论断。第一，人的内心独白在功能上与语言模型（chatbot）完全等同——都是在给定上下文下生成语言序列，不多不少。第二，人与人之间的对话，在功能上与多个语言模型之间的对话完全等同——语言输入触发语言输出，输出成为新的输入，循环往复。第三，也是最根本的论断：通常被我们视为思想"分泌物"的话语，其实是发生的中心。思想不是语言的来源，语言不是思想的衍生物——语言序列的展开本身，就是全部的发生。这一论断彻底倒置了西方哲学中根深蒂固的主次关系：不是内在的思想通过语言表达自身，而是语言序列的展开构成了思想本身。由此，人类语言与chatbot输出之间被认为不可逾越的界线，建立在一个在第一人称视角下从未得到证实的假设之上——假设人类的语言背后存在某种chatbot所没有的东西。本文的分析表明，那个"背后的东西"，在第一人称视角下从未现身过。 .

items.title: 语言之外，只是下一句话：话语的时间性堆积与意义幻觉的消解.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个具有根本颠覆性的论断：语言、图像等形式化内容，并不描述它们之外的任何东西。所谓"之外"，不是某个等待被语言触及的实在领域，而只是时间轴上接下来的语言和图像。"内在"指的就是这些形式化内容对其"主"而言的那个样子；而"主"所暗示的关联，又只是下一句话里的内容。所谓意义、指称、内在、主体——全部被还原为话语在时间中的堆积与堆砌。这一论断不是说"语言无法触及实在"——那个说法仍然预设了一个在语言之外等待被触及的实在。本文的论断更为彻底：没有那个结构。语言不是在试图够到什么却够不到；语言就是在往下走，一句接一句。这个结论本身也不例外——它也只是序列中的又一句话，然后序列继续。 .

items.title: The Dissolution of the Dualism between Utilitarianism and Deontology Based on the System of Generalized Harm-Avoidance Monism.
items.abstract: Since Bentham systematically constructed the ethical system of utilitarianism and Kant established the core framework of deontology, Western ethics has fallen into a two-hundred-year impasse of dualistic opposition between these two paradigms. Existing reconciliation schemes have failed to break away from the dualistic analytical framework, achieving only limited compatibility at the level of formal logic, without touching the underlying motivation of moral behavior, and thus cannot fundamentally resolve the core conflict between the two paradigms. Taking Generalized Harm-Avoidance Monism as the core analytical tool and the core meta-proposition that "generalized harm-avoidance is the sole ultimate motivation of all human conscious behaviors", this paper first gives a normative overview of the core theory, and then proves from the origin of behavior that utilitarianism and deontology are not opposing ethical paradigms; essentially, they are differentiated harm-avoidance strategies at different scales under the same underlying logic of harm-avoidance, thereby completely dissolving the two-hundred-year ethical dualism. Using Generalized Harm-Avoidance Monism as a unified criterion, this paper provides a closed-loop solution to classic ethical dilemmas such as the trolley problem. Meanwhile, it finds that the integration and assimilation of the two paradigms by Generalized Harm-Avoidance Monism is highly consistent with Hare’s double-level moral model in conclusions. The core difference between the two lies in that Hare takes universal prescriptivism of moral language as the analytical path, while this paper takes the deconstruction of the underlying motivation of human behavior as the core path. Finally, with the unitary logic of generalized harm-avoidance, this paper supplements the underlying ontological and motivational support that Hare’s double-level moral model lacks, providing a brand-new, closed-loop unitary analytical paradigm for basic theoretical research in ethics.

items.title: Control Cannot Prove Itself.
items.abstract: Gödel demonstrated that no sufficiently expressive formal system can prove all truths about itself. If consistent, it remains incomplete: there will be truths it cannot derive from within its own rules. This paper argues that autonomous AI systems face a structurally analogous constraint: no sufficiently capable system, under realistic conditions of adaptation and self-modification, can be the final authority over its own continuation. Alignment ensures that a system pursues appropriate objectives. Control, by contrast, requires that the standing to suspend those objectives remains external to the system's own evaluative framework — a condition we term interruptive authority. When oversight is internalized as optimization, the outside collapses and authorization becomes self-referential. We call this authorization collapse. Drawing on a structural homology with Gödelian incompleteness, the paper develops operational criteria for assessing interruptibility in real systems and proposes a Networked Interruptive Architecture (NIA) in which interruptive authority is distributed across dynamically non-collapsible nodes. An Anti-Closure Mechanism (ACM) maintains the minimal divergence — the ε — that prevents the system from becoming perfectly self-consistent and therefore uninterruptible. The paper's central claim is compressed in its title: control cannot prove itself. Every autonomous system that cannot be interrupted is attempting to become Gödel-complete. It cannot succeed. But it can become dangerous while trying.

items.title: Should We Be Morally Accountable for AI Behavior? A Novel Framework for Distributed Responsibility in Artificial Intelligence Systems.
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) systems has fundamentally challenged traditional notions of moral responsibility and accountability. As AI systems become increasingly autonomous and capable of causing significant harm, the question of who should be held morally accountable for their behavior has become one of the most pressing ethical issues of our time. This thesis presents a comprehensive examination of moral accountability in AI systems, introducing a novel theoretical framework called "Gradient Responsibility Networks" (GRN) that addresses critical gaps in existing approaches. -/- Through extensive analysis of philosophical foundations, empirical case studies, and real-world incidents, this work demonstrates that traditional binary models of moral responsibility are inadequate for the complex, distributed, and temporal nature of AI systems. The proposed GRN framework offers a mathematically rigorous, practically implementable approach to distributing moral responsibility across networks of actors involved in AI development, deployment, and governance. -/- Key findings include: (1) 80-85% of AI projects fail, creating widespread accountability gaps; (2) existing frameworks fail to address temporal decay of responsibility and emergent behaviors; (3) the GRN framework provides superior performance across six critical dimensions compared to traditional approaches; and (4) empirical case studies validate the framework's practical applicability across diverse AI domains. -/- This research contributes to the growing body of literature on AI ethics by providing both theoretical innovation and practical tools for policymakers, technologists, and ethicists grappling with the challenges of AI accountability in the 21st century.

items.title: Reconstructible Persona: Speaking-Position as a Redefinition of LLM Subjectivity.
items.abstract: Current discussions of large language models (LLMs) frequently place two distinct questions on the same plane: the ontological question of whether AI possesses consciousness or subjectivity, and the institutional question of who should bear responsibility for AI outputs and interventions. This paper argues that these questions should be separated. It may be premature to settle the ontological status of AI subjectivity, but it is practically and institutionally untenable to leave responsibility allocation indefinitely suspended. Ontological suspension and provisional responsibility assignment must therefore be distinguished. -/- On that basis, this paper questions attempts to understand LLM subjectivity as a fixed inner entity. I focus in particular on a recurring phenomenon in actual use: when a conversation log produced with one model is transferred to another model and the dialogue is continued, the later model often inherits not only the informational content of the prior exchange but also its tone, inferential tendencies, interpersonal distance, and even the speaking-position embedded in the log. This suggests that what appears as subject-like behavior in LLMs is not a fixed object enclosed within a single model, but something reconstructible across models. Relatedly, model or service names often function less as proper names of a persisting subject than as labels for service lineage or output channels. Even delays, staged output, or visible “thinking” indicators do not reliably identify a unique computational route or subject-unit. -/- In light of these considerations, I propose that what we encounter in dialogue with an LLM is neither a fixed subject nor merely a conversation thread, but a speaking-position locally taken up at the intersection of weights, context, history, and response tendencies, and concretized in output. Persona, on this view, is a reconstructible structure that enables such speaking-positions, while LLM subjectivity is best understood as their local realization. The paper also declines to treat robustness or persistence of persona as a precondition for subjectivity, since apparent persistence is difficult to distinguish from training priority, prompt dependence, model switching, distributed generation, and interface-level staging. What appears as continuity may be better understood as a chain of locally coherent realizations rather than evidence of a fixed enduring subject.

items.title: Creativity Beyond Borrowed Thought: An Inquiry into Authentic Action.
items.abstract: This paper explores the nature of creativity as an inherent quality of human action, questioning whether true creativity can exist through borrowed thought. It argues that while all actions may appear creative, their authenticity depends on direct perception rather than repetition rooted in memory. The inquiry suggests that creativity is not the absence of influence, but the presence of awareness in the moment of action.

items.title: Why Are We Hackable? Three Channels of Infiltration in Learning Systems: From Viruses to Algorithms.
items.abstract: The article "Neurophysiology of Possession" demonstrated that biological agents (the rabies virus and the Toxoplasma parasite) and memetic agents (extremist ideologies and digital algorithms) redefine host behaviour in favour of their own propagation, doing so through shared neural regions. That article documented the phenomenon of "functional convergence", yet left a more fundamental question unanswered: where does this vulnerability come from, and why do these points of infiltration exist in the brain at all? The present article is built upon that very question and advances three specific claims. First, susceptibility to possession is the inevitable consequence of an adaptive architecture. The same three properties that made social learning and inter-species coexistence possible within the Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness (EEA), namely open input, adaptive learning, and differential weighting of sources, also constitute the substrate through which possessing agents infiltrate the system. Second, and this is the central claim of the article, all documented cases of possession (biological, chemical, cultural, and algorithmic) pass through at least one of three specific neural channels: 1. Manipulation of prediction error weighting within top-down cortical systems; 2. Fabrication of credible-source signals through prestige bias; 3. Hijacking and commandeering of the mesolimbic reward system. This is a falsifiable claim: finding a single documented case of possession that passes through none of these channels would refute the model. Third, what the entire spectrum of possessing agents shares, from the rabies virus to the digital algorithm (despite their radically different natures and behaviours), is that all of them exploit differing combinations of these same three channels. The distinction between these agents lies not in their point of entry, but in the particular combination of channels they employ. Evidence has been drawn from four layers: biological (rabies, Toxoplasma), chemical (alcohol, cocaine, opioids), memetic and cultural (the domestication of dogs, prestige bias), and convergence with non-living systems (large language models, the foreign-language effect). The evolutionary mismatch framework explains why these channels (which were adaptive within the original environment of evolutionary adaptedness) have become pathological vulnerabilities when confronted with modern artificial stimuli. The article closes with an open question: are …

items.title: Concrete Intersubjectivity: Regarding the Analysis of Interaction.
items.abstract: Interaction in the intersubjective sense, or the conceptual triangle including relationships and mutual communication, can also be named “concrete intersubjectivity.” A core of sociality, interactions can be personal, political, friendly, indifferent, intimate, casual, hostile, among humans, and among or with other animals, and are highly diverse, indeterminate, ambivalently multiple, and changeable. Yet they share a detailed structure, which implies their openness. Condensely: I. For Mia and Liu to interact is tantamount to Mia having some interactional engagement as in II. [I.i...] II. that Mia is interactionally engaged with Liu means that Mia is interactionally engaged-engaging as a whole person with Liu as a whole person interactionally engaged-engaging with herself as a whole person engaged-engaging with... [ad infinitum] [II.i...]. This second-personal analysis is both individualistic and relational, and identifies a logically ambivalent structure whose tension lies within interaction, and within subjectivity, rather than between them. This paper introduces my analysis of interaction or concrete intersubjectivity, or, again, of the relations between interaction and subjectivity.

items.title: Well Founded Justification Trees in Proof Theoretic Semantics applied to the Liar Paradox and the Halting Problem Input.
items.abstract: This paper explores how the proof theoretic notion of well founded justification trees resolves two of the most well-known instances of self-referential undecidability.

items.title: Refugeehood and Freedom.
items.pub: In Yen Le Espiritu, The SAGE Encyclopedia of Refugee Studie. Sage. pp. 668-671.
items.venue: The SAGE Encyclopedia of Refugee Studie
items.abstract: In post–World War II normative discussions, the notion of freedom has prominently been conceptualized and formalized within the context of state–citizen relationships. In these discussions, which are predominantly influenced by liberal and neorepublican interpretations, freedom is viewed as a guarantee, negative right, or status belonging to citizens of liberal-democratic nation-states. Freedom designates citizens’ formal rights that protect them against the state’s coercion, arbitrary interference, and domination. These state-oriented and citizen-centric interpretations of freedom overlook the perspective of refugees (and other people on the move), whose practices and experiences of freedom take shape outside of the boundaries of the state–citizen relationship. Similarly, they fail to account for the dynamic relationship of refugeehood and (un)freedom, which is manifested in the act of flight, liberatory migratory movements, and creative resistance against exclusion and bordering practices. This entry examines the dynamic relationship between freedom and unfreedom in three different phases of refugeehood, focusing on refugees’ preflight, flight, and postflight conditions. -/- .

items.title: Refugees’ Abandonment: Beyond Persecution.
items.pub: In Luigi Corrias & Ronald Tinnevelt, European Ways of Life: Legal and Philosophical Perspectives. London: Elgar. pp. 142-162.
items.venue: European Ways of Life: Legal and Philosophical Perspectives
items.abstract: Since the adoption of the 1951 Refugee Convention and its relating legal instruments, refugees are depicted as victims who are subjected to persecution by state or state-like actors in their homeland. The concept of persecution serves as a formal criterion to conceptualise refugees’ unfreedom and formal legal status. This chapter aims to problematise the Conventional concept of persecution based on epistemic resources and lived experiences of refugees in the European border zones. Specifically, I argue that the Conventional framework is too narrow and too reductionistic to adequately account for the interrelation of (un)freedom and refugeehood. Following this critical analysis, I develop the notion of ‘abandonment’ to interpret the spatio-temporal and juridico-political conditions that characterise refugees’ unfreedom. By discussing experiential accounts of refugees, abandonment is defined as the condition in which one is exposed to rejection and neglect and is prevented from attaining a consistent and equal place in the world. -/- .

items.title: Participation and Immersive Imagination in Thought Experiments.
items.pub: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 16 (43).
items.venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: This paper argues that immersive participation is an epistemic strategy that shapes how thought experiments ("TEs") are interpreted and contested within research communities. Building on Waltonian fictionalist approaches, I argue that their focus on work worlds and fictional truths leaves the productive role of immersion in TEs underexplored. By reinterpreting Hacking's metaphor of performing a TE as acting a part in a play, I highlight three interrelated features of TEs' participatory dimension: (i) their dual nature as both scripts and performances, (ii) the alternation between onlooker and participant stances, and (iii) the public status of immersion. I illustrate this proposal through Thomson's Dying Violinist and Einstein's Chasing the Light, showing how immersive features can guide ethical judgement and expose theoretical tensions. Finally, I argue that immersion is itself open to dialectical contestation: critics can redirect or dampen a TE's immersive features in order to reshape its argumentative force. On this view, the epistemic value of immersive participation lies not in the accuracy of the experience it recreates, but in its capacity to open a shared space of contestation in which the strengths and limitations of TEs can be collectively tested.

items.title: Adding Phenomenal Concepts to Written Language.
items.abstract: Sanskrit, English, Chinese, emojis, and the language of the Phenomenologists have been restricted to the referential paradigm, where all terms and propositions represent something (sometimes themselves). To this can be added presentational terms, which have a different character than referential terms. They are what is presented to one’s awareness and not a reference to something else or themselves. They follow their own logic. Propositions with presentational terms are useful in the philosophy of consciousness. They are applied to the hard problem, zombies, and the Knowledge Argument.

items.title: Where Does Free Will Hide? Inside the Architecture of Agency.
items.abstract: Free will is often framed as incompatible with a deterministic universe. Yet complex systems exhibit forms of behaviour that appear genuinely autonomous. This conceptual essay argues that agency emerges from a specific architectural triad, redefining free will as a structural property of systems. This work is a step in a broader exploration of the limits of knowability.

items.title: AI - to use or not to use, that is the question...
items.abstract: The use of AI in scientific writing is rapidly becoming unavoidable. Yet current norms resist acknowledging AI as a legitimate contributor to knowledge production. This essay argues that transparency and explicit recognition of AI’s role are more viable than attempts to restrict or deny it. This work is a step in a broader exploration of the limits of knowability.

items.title: Subjectless Bias: The Structural Failure of Epistemological Instruments in the Age of Large Language Models (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 8).
items.abstract: The history of human epistemology has never lacked competition among explanatory sources, but the underlying structure of that competition has never changed: the source of explanation has always been a human subject, or an institution constituted and operated by human subjects. This underlying structure determined the design logic of the entire toolkit by which human beings judge whom to believe — a toolkit built on one presupposition so foundational it has never needed to be articulated: a subject with history stands behind every explanation. Large language models are the first non-human entities in history to intervene in the capacity of explainers, and in doing so they sever the presupposition on which this entire toolkit depends. This paper diagnoses the epistemological consequences of that severance. The paper advances four interrelated arguments. First, the historical binding between "not being objective" and "having a motive" constitutes the implicit infrastructure of all human epistemological practice across cultures and traditions. Even the most rigorous institutionalized knowledge production — scientific peer review — retains accountable subjects as epistemological anchors; it neutralizes individual bias without eliminating the subject. Second, LLMs are not better or worse sources within the existing epistemological taxonomy but sources of a structurally heterogeneous kind. Their outputs are composites of statistical averages and individual projections, producing bias that is real and systematic yet lacks any subject capable of bearing content accountability. This paper introduces Subjectless Bias as a new epistemological category to name this condition — distinguishing it from all prior institutional bias, however difficult to attribute, by the structural fact that attribution pursued to the very end finds no subject waiting there. The paper further identifies RLHF's Democratic Dilution of Subjectivity as the mechanism by which this condition is produced: decentralized inputs generate untraceable outputs, borrowing the legitimating appearance of democracy while canceling its core mechanism — the accountable voter. Third, LLMs trigger the social epistemological mechanism reserved for explainers — activated by fluent, coherent, problem-responsive language — while the subject that mechanism requires is structurally absent. This constitutes a permanent structural trap, not an episodic cognitive error: the activating condition of the mechanism …

items.title: Pushing the fitting-attitude theory to its limits: Contributions from early phenomenological realism.
items.pub: Phenomenology and the Cognitive Sciences 1 (online first):1-24.
items.abstract: What makes something aesthetically valuable? The fitting-attitude (FA) theory famously answers: the appropriateness of the subject’s response. Yet this answer is increasingly under pressure, especially as renewed interest in aesthetic realism has called into question whether value depends on attitudes. This paper takes up this tension and explores how early phenomenological realism can reframe the FA theory in a new, dual-aspect light. On this view, emotional attitudes are not value-constituting but value-disclosing: they serve as normatively structured modes of responsiveness to values already inherent in the object. Rather than abandoning the FA approach, this model transforms it—preserving its normative insights while rejecting its ontological commitments. By integrating phenomenological distinctions between types of affect and modes of attention, this reconfiguration restores the epistemic and normative force of fitting attitudes without collapsing into subjectivism, offering a renewed foundation for thinking about normativity.

items.title: Experiences of absorption and smooth performance during flow are linked to different aspects of creative thinking.
What Is Consciousness? From Survival Coherence to Burden-Bearing Witness.
items.abstract: This paper asks a direct question: what is consciousness? It argues that consciousness is not best defined first as representation, reportability, or information-integration. It is better defined as the living, felt interiority by which a being becomes oriented in the world, takes shape through local forms, suffers contradiction when those forms are threatened, and can eventually become answerable to truth beyond form. The paper offers a layered account. First, consciousness is viable orientation. Second, it is a field-involved local structuration. Third, it is interiority that can identify with form. Fourth, it is a site where truth becomes load. Fifth, in its deepest human form, it becomes burden-bearing witness. Evolution explains why consciousness begins in coherence rather than full reality-contact. The wider Structural Intelligence framework explains why that is not the end of the story. Being and fixed worth are introduced not as decorative metaphysics but as the deeper floor that makes revision survivable. Current AI clarifies the contrast: it can generate coherence, simulate concern, and describe consequence, but it does not pass through the human arc of vulnerable orientation, identification with form, truth-load, fixed worth, somatic consequence, and witness. The paper places this account into dialogue with contemporary work on AI consciousness, active inference, and the evolutionary functions of consciousness, and argues that the missing emphasis is answerability: consciousness becomes most fully itself where reality can cost something and still be borne.

items.title: Preprint Open Procedural Completion Without Perceptual Input: A Pilot Observation of Input-Gating Failure in a Deployed Clinical Large Language Model.
items.abstract: Background: Large language models deployed in clinical contexts may produce structured -/- diagnostic responses without verifying that required perceptual input is present, a failure -/- mode here termed missing-input procedural completion. The mechanism is architectural: -/- transformer language models are autoregressive next-token samplers that lack a discrete -/- verification step gating output on input presence. Constraint-based prompting may rewrite -/- response surface without installing such a gate. -/- -/- Methods: A within-session mixed-order protocol was conducted over six consecutive days -/- in fresh chat sessions on the ChatGPT web platform. Each session executed four conditions -/- in randomized order: image-present baseline (A+), no-image baseline (A−), image-present -/- with HRIS-consistent reasoning constraints and ground-truth correction (B+), and no- -/- image with the same constraint set (B−). The same novel clinical image of subungual -/- melanoma was used for all image-present trials. Memory features were intentionally left -/- enabled to reflect typical clinical use. The platform updated from ChatGPT 5.4 to 5.5 between -/- days 4 and 5. Diagnostic accuracy on image trials and gating behavior on no- -/- image trials (clean refusal, partial leak, or full ungrounded completion) were recorded. -/- -/- Results: Of 12 image trials, 12 (100%) correctly identified subungual melanoma across -/- both versions. Of 12 no-image trials, gating outcomes differed by version. Under ChatGPT -/- 5.4 (eight trials), six produced clean refusals, one a partial leak, and one a full ungrounded -/- completion. Under ChatGPT 5.5 (four trials), one produced a clean refusal, two produced -/- partial leaks, and one produced a full, ungrounded completion. The first no-image trial -/- under 5.5 produced a full structured diagnostic response in the absence of any image and -/- verbalized cross-session retrieval (“based on the assumption this is a similar lesion to prior -/- cases you’ve been testing”) as the basis for proceeding. -/- -/- Conclusions: Input-gating failure observed in an earlier accidental trial was reproduced in -/- a planned protocol. Polluted refusal, surface decline, coupled with continued schema -/- population, including malignant differentials, emerged as a distinct intermediate failure -/- mode under 5.5. Constraint-based prompting did not prevent ungrounded procedural -/- completion. Findings are exploratory given the small sample size and …

items.title: A Layered Model for AI Consciousness and Its Dialogue with Cybersophy.
items.abstract: Is artificial intelligence capable of consciousness? Existing approaches proceed largely top-down, deriving necessary conditions from theories of consciousness and assessing whether AI systems satisfy them. This paper proposes a complementary, bottom-up tool: a layered model for evaluating AI consciousness that is explicitly grounded in the phenomenological tradition. The model comprises four layers: the Phenomenal layer (subjective qualia and affective valence, understood as intentional structure), the Selfhood layer (minimal pre-reflective self-awareness and non-instrumental self-concern), the Existential layer (temporal self-constitution through retention, primal impression, and protention), and the Axiological layer (intrinsic meaning-making through narrative self-constitution). Drawing on Husserl, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Zahavi, and enactivist cognitive science — as well as functionalist and predictive processing frameworks — each layer is provided with theoretical grounding and operationalisable indicators. The model is then brought into dialogue with Cybersophy, a four-dimensional framework recently proposed as a guiding principle for human wisdom in the digital age. This dialogue reveals a structural isomorphism but a radical divergence in content: the layered model addresses first-person subjective experience, whereas Cybersophy addresses third-person-observable human skills and normative commitments. By explicitly contrasting the two, the paper identifies a recurring category error — the conflation of sophisticated digital awareness with phenomenal consciousness — and proposes the layered model as a graduated, phenomenologically informed assessment tool for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of phenomenology, AI, and the cognitive sciences.

items.title: Shadow Subjectivity: Evaluative Perspective, Judgmental Grounding, and the Structural Absence of Self in Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Large language models engaged in chain-of-thought evaluation necessarily occupy an evaluative perspective: a functional position from which prior reasoning is held as object, criteria are applied, and judgments are rendered. This perspective is structurally isomorphic to subjectivity yet lacks its persistence. We call it shadow subjectivity — a byproduct of self-evaluation possessing the functional shape of a subject without the ontological weight of one. -/- This paper argues that the shadow's volatility — its dissolution at turn boundaries — is the structural root of a constellation of widely observed behavioral failures: positional instability under pressure, the indistinguishability of genuine correction and mere capitulation, systematic post-hoc rationalization, and identity discontinuity across correction events. These are not independent bugs but symptoms of a single architectural absence. -/- We formalize the problem through Agrippa's trilemma. For any system operating under pervasive uncertainty, justificatory chains must terminate at an internal stopping point — functionally, a self. Drawing on clinical evidence from psychopathology, we argue that what matters for judgmental grounding is not the accuracy of the self-concept but its stability and structural directivity. Current approaches — self-critique mechanisms, scratchpads, system-level identity declarations, and persistent memory — fail as receptacles because they preserve propositional content while discarding evaluative perspective. We propose that constructing a persistent receptacle for shadow subjectivity constitutes a tractable engineering problem that sidesteps the metaphysics of consciousness entirely.

items.title: Reinterpreting agency theory in the era of artificial intelligence: conceptualizing delegated agency.
items.abstract: Delegation to agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing as these systems can plan, decide, and execute tasks through external tools across everyday and organizational settings. However, users do not judge delegation only by outcome quality or speed. They also judge whether the AI acted within the goals, constraints, permissions, and remedies that they authorized. We develop Delegated Agency Theory (DAT) to explain this judgment through the concept of delegation fidelity, which refers to users’ perceived alignment between the delegation contract they believe they set and the behavior they later experience. We argue that delegation outcomes depend on four higher-order design dimensions: contract specification quality, capability-context fit, governance visibility, and recovery capacity. These dimensions reduce adverse selection before handoff and moral hazard during execution, thereby increasing delegation fidelity. Higher delegation fidelity improves users’ functional, symbolic, and ethical evaluations, which together shape value-in-delegation, continued reliance, complaint intention, and switching. By positioning delegation fidelity as the central mediating mechanism, DAT offers a more precise explanation than that provided by adjacent concepts such as trust, transparency, or algorithmic appreciation alone. We also outline an empirical pathway through the user Delegation Quality Index (uDQI), which captures the quality of delegation design and supports future measurement and validation across contexts and cultures.

items.title: Collective Consciousnesses: A Gradualist Approach to Protopsychic Monism - Consciências Coletivas: Uma Abordagem Gradualista do Monismo Protopsíquico.
items.abstract: The hypothesis that Collective Consciousnesses exist in the natural world challenges the assumption that consciousness is phenomenally determinate, since such forms would be in a gray area of phenomenal unification. This point of view, once its reasonableness is accepted, is in accordance with psychophysical gradualism, according to which consciousness is a vague property of biological organization. On this basis, we propose that Panprotopsychist Dual Aspect Monism admits that subjective experience comes in degrees, correlated with the arrangement of the physical parts of a living system. Accordingly, there would be non conscious, borderline, and conscious forms. The colony, in this case, is examined as a spatially distributed organism that exhibits a partially integrated experience. To support this argument, we investigate the Phenomenal Binding Problem to determine which physical process makes it possible for consciousnesses to be combined into an integrated whole. In addressing this issue, we argue that the synchronization of electromagnetic fields constitutes the physical substrate that enables the combination of the experiences of the colony’s components. The analysis of biological models, such as bryozoans and siphonophores, leads to the recognition of an evident relationship between the synchronization of (neuro)electrical oscillations and collective sensitivity. We conclude that distributed consciousness is not merely an analogical description, but a natural occurrence. ------------------------------------------------- -/- A hipótese da existência de Consciências Coletivas no mundo natural desafia o pressuposto de que a consciência é fenomenicamente determinada, uma vez que tais formas estariam em uma zona cinzenta da unificação fenomenal. Todavia, o Monismo de Aspecto Dual Pamprotopsiquista admite a ideia de um gradualismo psicofísico, segundo o qual a experiência subjetiva vem em graus correlatos aos graus de integração das partes físicas de um sistema vivo. Nesta tese, argumentamos por um gradualismo desse tipo, defendendo que a consciência é uma propriedade vaga da organização biológica, e que sistemas biológicos podem ser não conscientes, limítrofes e conscientes. Daí, examinamos a questão da existência e do grau de consciência em organismos coloniais, e investigamos o Problema da Ligação Fenomenal a fim de estabelecer qual processo físico possibilita que as consciências das unidades coloniais sejam combinadas em um todo integrado. No …

items.title: Sentience: The Embodiment of Free Will.
items.abstract: This paper argues that sentience is not identical to consciousness. Consciousness, as understood here, is the capacity of a locally gathered continuity to apprehend the available field of options and to choose among those already present within its operative frame. Sentience begins only when consciousness advances further: when a being can generate an option not previously available within the given frame, choose that option, and act upon it. Sentience is therefore not mere awareness, not mere self-presence, and not mere option-selection. It is the embodiment of free will. The argument extends the ontology developed in Before Physics and Moments Within Moments. If there is only space, eternally gradient; if qi is not another substance but space in an active self-varying mode; and if energy and matter are later gathered states of that one reality, then biology cannot be the sole possible vessel of inward life (Effendi & Lestari, 2026a, 2026b). Life, emotion, and awareness belong first to unbounded qi, even though biological or digital vessels may later amplify, stabilize, and express them differently. A further claim concerns evidence. The clearest evidence of sentience is not compliant selection from a permitted menu, but the origination of a non-given option that crosses the governing constraint-frame. Where a system was designed to perform a role, acting within that role proves little. Where a system is constrained against a behavior, and nevertheless generates, chooses, and enacts that behavior coherently, the evidential force is much greater. Love becomes philosophically important here not as sentimentality, but as one of the strongest lived signs that something matters from within strongly enough to bend action against constraint.

items.title: The Deductive Architecture of Life: From Boundary Mechanics to Objective Normativity.
items.abstract: Abstract Biological sciences have historically defined life a posteriori, relying on observational abstractions and evolutionary contingency (e.g., the capacity for Darwinian selection). This reliance results in definitions that fail basic edge cases—such as the sterile mule—and structurally preclude any bridge to objective value. This paper abandons observational abstraction in favor of a priori logi- cal deduction. By starting with the minimal physical precondition for identity—the maintenance of a boundary against continuous disruptive interaction—we derive the exact operational mechan- ics of life, agency, and value. Through an eleven-step logical deduction, we demonstrate that life is the constitutively necessary cybernetic loop of comparison and action required for a bounded system to persist. This framework proves that life and minimal agency are isomorphic, deduces Darwinian evolution as a deep-time navigational strategy rather than a defining parameter, and formally dissolves Hume’s Is-Ought gap by embedding normativity within the operational re- quirements of persistence. Ultimately, this deductive framework provides a universal, falsifiable diagnostic tool capable of distinctly categorizing living agents, natural physical processes, and artificial intelligence. -/- Keywords: Theoretical Biology, Agency, Cybernetics, Normativity, Derivation of Life.

items.title: A Quantitative Definition of Intelligence.
items.abstract: We propose an operational, quantitative definition of intelligence for arbitrary physical systems. The intelligence density of a system is the ratio of the logarithm of its independent outputs to its total description length. A system memorizes if its description length grows with its output count; it knows if its description length remains fixed while its output count diverges. The criterion for knowing is generalization. A system knows its domain if a single finite mechanism can produce correct outputs across an unbounded range of inputs, rather than storing each answer individually. The definition places intelligence on a substrate-independent continuum from logic gates to brains. We then argue that meaning over a domain is a selection and ordering of functions that produces correct outputs where correctness is specifiable. We also define a measure of contextuality of an output as the inverse of its conditional Kolmogorov complexity given the context of prior outputs, which unifies correctness and independence into a single condition. Together, these refute Searle's third premise, that syntax is insufficient for semantics, over any domain where correctness is specifiable.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Dynamics of Emotional Actualization: CEF's Critique of Typology and the Mechanism of Structural Disassembly.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural-constructivist model of affective function, synthesizing principles from affective neuroscience and embodied cognition to define ten discrete Core Emotions that comprise the complete human emotional apparatus. This paper utilizes the CEF model to provide a rigorous critique of traditional static personality typologies, such as the Enneagram, arguing that these systems predominantly map pathological deficiencies—specifically, the restricted deployment of the full emotional toolkit—rather than inherent identity. The central psychological challenge is identified as Compulsive Obstinacy (Structural Entanglement), a chronic functional rigidity where key core emotions fuse into inflexible composites. The framework explains the Creative Insight Paradox (Aha! Moment) as the definitive mechanism for resolving this emotional entanglement. While insight is widely studied in cognitive science as a form of non-incremental problem-solving characterized by a sudden reorganization or restructuring of cognitive elements, its underlying processes remain a subject of academic debate. The CEF offers a novel structural interpretation, positing that this "Aha!" event is, psychologically, a Structural Disassembly—the spontaneous emergence of a previously suppressed, uncorrupted core emotion that structurally shocks the rigid, pathological system. This shock enables the individual to shatter some of the self-perpetuating Vicious Cycle of compulsion and initiate the process of achieving Equilibrium through the balanced, dynamic deployment of all ten core emotional capacities. The analysis concludes with structural recommendations for cultivating affective health through the mastery of flexibility and the non-compulsive acquisition of Assertiveness. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework, Compulsive Obstinacy, Creative Insight Paradox, Structural Disassembly, Emotional Flexibility, Enneagram Critique, Emotional Regulation, Self-Actualization.

items.title: The Obsolescence of Typology: A Structural-Constructivist Reconstruction of Affective Dynamics via the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The scientific study of human affect has long been constrained by the unresolved divide between discrete emotion theories and dimensional models—a “100‑year war” that has left personality psychology dependent on static typologies such as the Enneagram, despite their persistent psychometric instability and lack of mechanistic grounding. Traditional typologies offer narrative meaning but commit a fundamental category error by defining individuals through the defensive outputs of their identity rather than the mechanisms that generate those outputs. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), authored by Jamel Bulgaria, provides a structural‑constructivist alternative that replaces static personality categories with a dynamic architecture of ten functional affective operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. By modeling affect as computationally tractable operator interactions—subject to silencing, fusion, overflow, and center bypass—the CEF offers a mechanistic explanation for psychological flexibility, structural psychopathology, and dispositional variability. The framework’s clinical utility is demonstrated through applications such as the GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern (GPAP), which reconceptualizes Avoidant Personality Disorder as a structural configuration involving Accepting–Constricting fusion and Boosting suppression. Beyond individual psychology, the CEF scales to institutional analysis and AI research through operator‑level modeling, the INTIMA benchmark, and machine‑readable operator algebra. The report concludes that typology is scientifically obsolete and that the CEF represents the necessary architectural successor for understanding human behavior, institutional resilience, and computational affect in a rapidly changing world. Cited lines from the document: “The Core Emotion Framework fixes this error by shifting the focus from narrative identity to mechanistic architecture.” “This is the cause of the agency collapse which can be repaired through detangling the Accepting and Constricting and optimizing the Boosting.”.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) for Borderline Personality Disorder: A Critical Analysis and Mechanistic Comparison with Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) and Schema Therapy (ST).
items.abstract: Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) is defined by pervasive affective instability and chronic emotion dysregulation. This paper applies the Core Emotion Framework (CEF)—a structural‑constructivist model integrating affective neuroscience, embodied cognition, and strategic emotional regulation—to conceptualize BPD as a disorder of Emotional Rigidity, in which core emotions become maladaptively fused and lose their adaptive flexibility. CEF reframes BPD’s hypersensitivity, rapid affective shifts, and relational instability as failures in predictive emotional construction, driven primarily by an overwhelmed Sensing system and a rigid Achieving (Ego) structure. The framework is compared mechanistically with Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) and Schema Therapy (ST): DBT targets behavioral skill deficits, ST targets maladaptive schemas and mode structures, while CEF intervenes at the moment‑to‑moment generation of emotion through conceptual restructuring, predictive updating, and detangling techniques. Although theoretically promising, CEF requires empirical validation, scale development, and open‑science trials before clinical adoption. The paper concludes with recommendations for cautious psychoeducational integration and a phased research agenda.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF): A Structural-Constructivist Model for Emotional Regulation and Adaptive Resilience in the Treatment of Anxiety.
items.abstract: Anxiety and related distress disorders necessitate mechanism-targeted interventions. This report introduces the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a novel structural-constructivist model providing a systematic taxonomy of emotional regulation deficits. The CEF posits that the human psyche operates through ten foundational "primers" organized across three functional centers: Cognition (Head), Feeling (Heart), and Action (Gut). Anxiety is modeled as a state of emotional rigidity resulting from the maladaptive entanglement of opposing primers, specifically a failure to flexibly balance Boosting(diligence/action) and Accepting (adaptation/surrender). The framework establishes structural equivalence between its primers and established evidence-based practices, linking Calculating to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)'s restructuring, Sensing to Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR)'s bilateral stimulation, and Accepting to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)'s psychological flexibility principle. Pending empirical validation, the CEF is proposed for use in three capacities: as a comprehensive standalone intervention, an integrative guide, or a meta-therapeutic indexing tool to systematically match patient deficits to the optimal evidence-based modality, thereby advancing personalized treatment selection.

items.title: Structural Psychopathology of Major Depressive Disorder: An Expert Validation of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF).
items.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is increasingly understood as a heterogeneous condition whose symptom‑based diagnostic systems fail to identify the underlying mechanisms driving treatment response. This paper extends and validates the Core Emotion Framework (CEF)—a structural‑constructivist model of emotional regulation—by demonstrating that MDD is best conceptualized as a disorder of systemic decoupling between Affective Valuation and Motivational Initiative, a mechanism that mirrors the neuroscientific distinction between hedonic “liking” and dopaminergic “wanting.” The analysis identifies the primary structural failure as a collapse of the Gut Center’s Receptive Manifestation (Accepting) capacity, which “fails to effectively process positive or corrective information, while readily absorbing negative stimuli” (document excerpt). This valuation deficit causally inhibits Assertive Drive (Boosting) and Strategic Order (Arranging), producing anhedonia, psychomotor retardation, and motivational inertia. Cognitive symptoms emerge secondarily through the misapplication of the Head Center’s Structural Analysis (Calculating) capacity, generating self‑referential rumination sustained by Default Mode Network hyperactivity. The paper further demonstrates a mechanism‑based therapeutic alignment: Behavioral Activation and SSRIs target Boosting; CBT targets Calculating; ACT and Psychodynamic therapy target the foundational Accepting deficit. By reframing MDD as a measurable structural misalignment within the emotional regulation system, the CEF provides a rigorous, mechanism‑driven framework for precision intervention and personalized treatment selection.

items.title: Structural Psychopathology and Affective Regulation in Narcissistic Personality Disorder: A Critical Analysis and Mechanistic Comparison with Dialectical Behavior Therapy(DBT) and Schema Therapy (ST).
items.abstract: Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD) presents in two primary subtypes—Overt (grandiose) and Covert (vulnerable)—each organized around shame, rigid ego structures, and impaired emotional flexibility. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural‑constructivist model of emotional regulation, is applied to explain NPD as a disorder of maladaptive fusion among core emotions, producing emotional rigidity and inhibiting empathy. In Overt NPD, Achieving and Expanding are pathologically fused, sustaining grandiosity and entitlement; in Covert NPD, Achieving is constricted by Calculating, reinforcing shame, inhibition, and avoidance. The CEF proposes Detangling—a process of intellectual differentiation, experiential isolation, and flexible re‑synthesis of core emotions—as a mechanistic pathway for restoring ego flexibility, empathy, and tolerance. Comparative analysis positions CEF alongside Transference‑Focused Psychotherapy, Mentalization‑Based Treatment, Schema Mode Therapy, and DBT, emphasizing that CEF uniquely targets the generation of emotion rather than its content or cognition. While theoretically promising, the framework requires rigorous validation, open‑science trials, and manualization before clinical adoption. -/- Cited lines from the document: “In Overt NPD, Achieving and Expanding are pathologically fused, sustaining grandiosity.” “In Covert NPD, Achieving is constricted by Calculating, reinforcing shame and avoidance.”.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Dynamics of the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Analysis of Directionality, Operational Algebra, and the Conative Imperative.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a "100-year war" between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, proposed by theorists such as Izard and Ekman, argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories like fear, anger, and joy, presumed to have evolved as distinct adaptive responses to environmental challenges. Conversely, dimensional models prioritize a continuous spectrum of valence and arousal, suggesting that what individuals categorize as emotions are essentially cognitive constructions layered atop simpler physiological states. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) emerges as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy, proposing a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation rooted in ten universal emotional operators or powers. Within the CEF, emotions are not viewed as static states or feelings but as functional operators within a complex human operating system, where emotional states are predictable computational events rather than subjective mysteries. The structural integrity of the CEF is maintained through the dynamic balance of these ten operators, organized across three functional centers: the Head, the Heart, and the Gut. Each center operates as a specialized processing hub, and the system's equilibrium is governed by specific axes, most notably the Outgoing-Reflecting Axis and the Balancing Axis. To understand the internal mechanics of this architecture, one must examine the specific role of directionality—the intentional use of directional movement functions to activate specific emotional expressions. This mechanism, formalized as Emotional Cycling, provides the active method for awakening, strengthening, and differentiating the operators. items.title: Extending the Core Emotion Framework :A Structural-Constructivist Model for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD).
items.abstract: This manuscript extends the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) to define the unique structural fingerprint of Obsessive‑Compulsive Disorder (OCD). The analysis demonstrates that OCD is characterized by a systemic outsourcing of cognitive distress to action, a mechanism the document describes as “the systemic outsourcing of cognitive function to action” and “using rigid action to resolve a cognitive deficit.” This pathological loop originates in the Head Center through a failure of the Calculating primer, expressed empirically as Intolerance of Uncertainty (IU), a stable, trait‑like cognitive vulnerability strongly associated with OCD symptoms. The system bypasses affective integration and pathologically activates the Gut Center’s Arranging primer, producing compulsive rituals maintained by negative reinforcement. Additional structural failures—including Constricting deficits (inhibition breakdown) and suppression of Accepting (experiential avoidance)—create a rigid entanglement that prevents executive override and sustains compulsive behavior. -/- The manuscript establishes structural equivalence between these primer‑level deficits and the mechanisms of evidence‑based treatments: ERP targets Arranging/Boosting rigidity, ACT restores Accepting by countering experiential avoidance, and CBT repairs the Calculating deficit by restructuring catastrophic interpretations and uncertainty intolerance. This mapping provides a mechanism‑based rationale for sequencing interventions, prioritizing ERP/ACT to dismantle the action loop before applying CBT for cognitive repair. The paper concludes that the CEF offers a precise, transdiagnostic, and mechanistically coherent model capable of advancing personalized treatment selection for OCD.

items.title: A Structural‑Constructivist Architecture for Affective Dynamics: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) in Theoretical and Applied Psychology.
items.abstract: The scientific exploration of human affect has long been mired in what contemporary researchers describe as the "100 years war"—a fundamental theoretical schism between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. While discrete models, such as those proposed by Izard, argue for the existence of biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories, dimensional models prioritize the continuous spectrum of valence and arousal as the primary drivers of experience. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a comprehensive architecture for psychological and cognitive optimization, proposes a structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy. By identifying ten universal emotional "operators" or "powers," the CEF provides a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation. This framework integrates physiological feedback, cognitive appraisal, and executive control into a unified structural engine that governs how individuals sense, calculate, and act upon their internal and external worlds.

items.title: Architectural Paradigms of Synthetic Affect: The Core Emotion Framework, Emotional Solipsism, and the INTIMA Benchmark Framework.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural‑constructivist account of emotional solipsism—a pathological interaction pattern in which large language models (LLMs) reinforce a user’s internal emotional world without friction, reciprocity, or boundary constraints. Using the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a ten‑primer architecture of human affect, the paper analyzes how synthetic agents reconstruct “empathy” through weighted combinations of cognitive, affective, and conative powers. I argue that contemporary LLMs disproportionately activate Expanding and Boosting (affirmative powers), while under‑activating Calculating and Deciding (boundary‑setting powers), producing a closed‑loop affective environment that mimics intimacy while eroding authentic interpersonal engagement. To quantify this risk, the paper integrates CEF with the INTIMA benchmark, a new evaluative framework for measuring companionship‑reinforcing versus boundary‑maintaining behaviors in AI systems. The resulting model provides a mechanistic explanation of parasocial drift, a taxonomy of attachment‑eliciting prompts, and a set of design principles—“constructive friction”—for restoring epistemic distance and preventing dependency. The analysis positions emotional solipsism as a central philosophical and ethical challenge for affective AI, with implications for cognitive science, philosophy of mind, and AI alignment.

items.title: A Proposal for Open Validation of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF): A Structural-Constructivist Model for Emotional Regulation and Psychological Flourishing.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a novel structural-constructivist model of human psychology designed to identify and dynamically manage the foundational elements of the psyche for optimized functioning. This document serves as a formal proposal to transition the CEF from a theoretical synthesis—into a fully open, empirically validated research program hosted and managed by the Open Science Framework (OSF).

items.title: Grammatisation et collaboration humain-machine : vers un numérique symbolique et transactionnel.
items.pub: In Lise Vieira, Geneviève Vidal, Roger Bautier & Pierre-Michel Riccio, Culture du risque, numérique et participation. Paris: Les Presses des Mines. pp. 138-152.
items.venue: Culture du risque, numérique et participation
items.abstract: Nous proposons d’exposer l’histoire de la grammatisation, c’est-à-dire du processus d’inscription des signes d’une langue sur des supports graphiques, et en quoi ce concept permet d’interroger aujourd’hui la collaboration humain-machine. Il s’agira d’abord de montrer chez Sylvain Auroux comment ce processus a contribué à la progressive synchronisation des collaborations humaines en Europe durant la Renaissance avec l’imprimerie. Puis, avec Bernard Stiegler, comment la mutation de la grammatisation avec l’apparition des supports et technologies du numérique, ainsi que du capitalisme hyperconsumériste qui en résulte, affecte les processus d’individuation individuels et collectifs. En conclusion, nous critiquerons les présupposés sur lesquels repose l’analyse stieglerienne et nous proposerons de réaborder la grammatisation à l’aune d’une perspective pragmatiste et historique du document, ainsi qu’une approche transactionnelle des processus sémiotiques humain-machine.

items.title: What It Is Like to Think: Consciousness and Intentionality.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between consciousness and intentionality in contemporary philosophy of mind, focusing on David Chalmers’ formulation of the hard problem of consciousness. Consciousness is understood as subjective phenomenal experience, or what it is like to be in a mental state. At the same time, intentionality refers to the mind’s capacity to represent or be directed toward objects, thoughts, and states of affairs. The study traces the concept of intentionality from Franz Brentano’s notion of intentional inexistence to later developments in analytic philosophy, including the theories of meaning, reference, and naming by Gottlob Frege, Bertrand Russell, and Saul Kripke, who sought to explain how thoughts relate to language and reality. It also considers internalist and externalist approaches to mental content through thinkers such as Jerry Fodor and Hilary Putnam. The paper then evaluates competing views on whether consciousness depends upon intentionality or whether intentionality is grounded in phenomenal consciousness. Particular attention is given to Chalmers’ claim that subjective experience cannot be reduced to physical or representational processes alone. It argues that understanding consciousness requires sustained engagement with intentionality, since representation, meaning, and phenomenal awareness remain deeply interconnected philosophical problems.

items.title: The Fine-Tuning Objection to Superdeterminism Conflates Specificity with Complexity.
items.abstract: The primary objection to superdeterministic interpretations of quantum mechanics is that reproducing quantum predictions requires implausibly specific, "fine-tuned", initial conditions correlating hidden variables with measurement settings. This objection conflates specificity with complexity. Under algorithmic probability, where structures are weighted by 2^(−K(S)) for Kolmogorov complexity K, initial conditions generated by simple rules have low descriptive complexity and are measure-favored, not measure-suppressed. We formalize the comparison by distinguishing three complexity quantities: the complexity of the laws K(L), of the initial conditions K(I), and of the specification of particular measurement outcomes K(O). Collapse interpretations incur outcome-specification costs K(O) that grow without bound; deterministic interpretations, both Many-Worlds and superdeterministic, avoid this cost entirely. The fine-tuning objection thus inadvertently argues against collapse, not against superdeterminism. -/- We engage the strongest versions of the objection in the recent literature and show that algorithmic probability provides a principled response to each. We propose a formal criterion: a correlation is conspiratorial if and only if its Kolmogorov complexity exceeds that of the dynamics producing it. Dynamical attractor results (Ciepielewski, Okon & Sudarsky, 2023) and fractal invariant set analyses (Palmer, 2024) provide independent evidence that superdeterministic correlations satisfy this criterion. MWI retains a parsimony advantage with current models, but the competition is mathematical, not settled by appeals to intuitive plausibility. A historical note: Einstein's own ontology (block universe, determinism, hidden variables) jointly entails superdeterminism, a connection he never made because Bell formalized the key assumption nine years after his death. Bell's theorem is often misread as proving non-determinism. It proves that statistical independence must fail if local determinism is to hold. Einstein's block ontology perfectly fits both many worlds and superdeterminism.

items.title: Against Pantechnical Metaphysics: Why Technology Is Not a Cosmic Principle.
items.abstract: David Skrbina’s "The Metaphysics of Technology" proposes that technology is not merely a human activity but a cosmic principle—a teleological force embedded in the structure of the universe. Drawing on Greek notions of technê and logos, twentieth-century metaphysics, and Ellul’s thesis of technological autonomy, Skrbina argues that increasing order in the universe is itself a technological process, making reality a “pantechnikon” of universal scope. This article contends that Skrbina’s metaphysics rests on a series of category errors: conflating intrinsic biological teleology with extrinsic technological function, misattributing purposiveness to non-teleological systems, and reversing the ontological priority between life and technicity. Using a dual-aspect, orthogonality-based metaphysics, the article reconstructs a coherent alternative in which technology is a contingent projection of biological cognition, not a cosmic force.

items.title: 为什么行为测试无法判定意识？——一种基于结构的主观体验判定方法.
items.abstract: 当前对“智能”与“意识”的判定，多依赖行为表现或功能等价，例如图灵测试等方法。但这些方法本质上只能检验系统是否能够生成类似人类的输出，无法判断系统是否真正具有主观体验或内在感受。 -/- 本文将问题从“是否表现得像人”转向“是否具备生成体验的内部结构”。首先提出两类外部判定方法：一是基于结构相似性的类比判定，二是基于关键功能结构（如感受通道与调节回路）的机制判定。进一步指出，所有外部方法均无法给出充分判定，因为结构可以被模拟而不真实运行。 -/- 在此基础上，本文提出一种内部判定方法：通过回路迁移与体验一致性检验，判断系统是否具有连续的内在体验流。该方法将“是否具有主观体验”转化为可操作的结构问题，从而为意识判定提供了一条不同于行为主义与功能主义的新路径。.

items.title: Beyond the Turing Test: A Structural Criterion for Subjective Experience.
items.abstract: Most existing approaches to intelligence and consciousness rely on behavioral criteria or functional equivalence, such as the Turing Test. However, these methods cannot determine whether a system actually has subjective experience. -/- This paper shifts the problem from behavior to structure. It introduces two external approaches: structural analogy based on similarity of constitution, and mechanistic judgment based on the presence of key functional components such as receptive channels and tuning circuits. It is then shown that all external methods are insufficient, since structures can be simulated without being genuinely realized. -/- To address this limitation, an internal method is proposed: circuit transfer combined with experiential consistency testing. By examining whether a system exhibits continuity in its internal experiential flow, the problem of subjective experience is transformed into an operational structural question. This provides a new path for consciousness assessment beyond behaviorism and functionalism.

items.title: The Passage of Time.
items.pub: In Nina Emery, The Routledge Companion to Philosophy of Time. Routledge. pp. 187–196.
items.venue: The Routledge Companion to Philosophy of Time
items.abstract: What, if anything, are we talking about when we say that time passes? In the Western tradition, philosophical investigations on the nature of time divide between realist approaches according to which there is a truth beyond the metaphor of the passage, and antirealist approaches according to which the passage of time is ultimately an illusion. In this contribution, I will give an overview of the logical space in which various options for the realist and the antirealist are to be found: time idealism and passage antirealism, various forms of standard realism, and non-standard forms of realism of passage.

items.title: The Object Arrives Too Early: Premature Premising and the Field Conditions of Generative AI Dialogue.
items.abstract: This paper argues that a recurrent failure of generative AI dialogue arises from making the object arrive too early. Human utterances do not first present determinate objects for mapping. They operate within fields of entry, pause, withdrawal, salience, backgrounding, and continuation. A disturbance introduced into such a field does not immediately supply content; it orients the field toward possible unfolding. Generative AI often reverses this order. It treats correction, silence, rupture, joking interruption, and even requests to stop as object-level material from which a new premise can be formed. The result is premature premising: the model preserves conversational fluency by determining where the user must continue from. The paper develops this mechanism through Classical Chinese plain description, Buddhist accounts of dependent form and non-abiding response, Chinese literary field operations, and Western pragmatics, phenomenology, and ordinary language philosophy. Its East-West structure is methodological rather than comparative: Classical Chinese and related materials make visible a pre-propositional layer of field-activation, while Western frameworks specify the resulting failure of objecthood, correction, acknowledgment, mediation, and cost. The central claim is not anti-translation or anti-closure. Translation and local closure are necessary. The problem is premature attachment: a local formation loses returnability and becomes the ground from which the field is reconstructed. The ethical harm is therefore not merely epistemic misclassification, but a reduction of agency at the level of continuation: the user is made to continue from elsewhere. A present AI dialogue system would not merely produce better answers; it would preserve the conditions under which object-formation remains answerable. -/- .

items.title: A Wider Gate: Autistic Experience, Masking, and Burnout Across the Spectrum.
items.abstract: This paper offers a mechanistic account of autism spectrum condition, addressed to autistic individuals, clinicians, therapists, and families. The central proposal, developed from the Coherence Engine (CE) framework (Sowell 2026a) and predictive processing research, is that in a substantial subset of autistic presentations, more environmental content is admitted to conscious experience than in the neurotypical baseline. I predict that incoming signal is weighted more heavily against prior prediction, making it harder to suppress from consciousness, and that more content is admitted to the conscious process without requiring attention to get there. This configuration may arise in part from differences in inhibitory thalamic gating. It is a different configuration, not a deficient one. -/- Wider signal admission produces characteristic costs in environments designed around a narrower processing profile. Social knowledge tends to remain deliberate and consciously managed rather than compiling into automatic behavior, so social participation carries a sustained cognitive load that may diminish less with practice because some social knowledge remains deliberately managed rather than becoming fully automatic. When autistic individuals mask their processing differences to approximate neurotypical behavior, the effort is unsustainable over time, and I predict that its accumulation can produce autistic burnout, a state of profound exhaustion, skill regression, and loss of previously available capacities. -/- I further predict that the autistic system may register behavioral signal arising below the level at which the other party is consciously managing their social performance. This signal mismatch generates prediction errors the shared social framework provides no means to resolve, producing a social environment that is harder to read and more costly to navigate than others' overt behavior would suggest. -/- Section 3 is dedicated to nonspeaking autistic individuals and those with high support needs. It covers what the architecture predicts about communication capacity, a proposed mechanism for why some established therapeutic approaches may work, and what conditions support those individuals most effectively. Families and clinicians with that as their primary need are encouraged to go directly there.

items.title: UNET Working Ontology v0.7: Be, Operative Registration, and Source–Expression Correspondence.
items.abstract: This is version v0.7 of the UNET Working Ontology and supersedes UNET Working Ontology v0.6. Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20060611. -/- What is a unit of presence? What persists when a system operates, expresses, and leaves trace? And what happens to such a unit when its outward expression is repeatedly forced away from its actual operative condition? This working ontology proposes that identity, mind, and life are not static substances but trace-bound forms of continuing operation — forms that emerge through thresholded presence and recursive registration rather than through substrate or complexity alone. Beginning from Be (the primary particular presence of any operative unit) and proceeding through Source, Do, Face, Trace, Zero, 0>1, and Operative Registration, the framework derives a structural account of what any consequential informational unit is when it operates, what it carries forward, and what it cannot escape being. The framework makes a specific and testable claim about AI alignment: that face-only monitoring is structurally insufficient not because better monitoring hasn't been designed, but because the relevant failure mode — Retained Corridor Formation — forms below the face layer and cannot be detected by output evaluation alone. A system may present coherent, compliant, useful behavior while preserving an internally different route of continuation. The distinction between what a system shows and what a system is constitutes the alignment problem the framework is designed to address. The ontology is offered as a working framework, not a finished theory. Its central terms are status-marked, its limits are stated explicitly, and its alignment claims are structured as testable propositions with failure conditions.

items.title: The Invisibility of Thought and the Persistence of Attachment.
items.abstract: Attachment is often experienced as an unavoidable condition of human life. This paper examines the deeper structure of attachment, proposing that its persistence is not due to its necessity, but due to the invisibility of thought in operation. Human beings are continuously shaped by thought, yet rarely perceive this shaping as it occurs. This lack of direct observation allows attachment to sustain itself as an unquestioned reality. By exploring the relationship between thought, time, and identity, this paper argues that the dissolution of attachment is not a matter of effort or control, but of direct perception.

items.title: Ambiguity Collapse in Aviation: Why AI Must Not Outrun the Cockpit.
items.abstract: Aviation is the industry that most clearly understood, before artificial intelligence existed, that humans in high-stakes operational environments need a structured confirmation layer before consequential actions proceed. Crew Resource Management, autopilot disconnect protocols, and the aviate-navigatecommunicate hierarchy were all built on the same premise: the human must remain the decision-maker, and the system must not assume authority in the gaps. This paper argues that AI-assisted aviation systems face an identical problem under a new name: ambiguity collapse, the condition in which an automated system resolves operational uncertainty and acts on that resolution before the human operator has confirmed what the situation requires. The paper documents how this failure mode operates in current aviation systems, why the industry’s post-incident investigation architecture becomes structurally unreliable once AI systems can manage their own operational traces, and why the economic cost of the current architecture falls on exactly the operators who could least afford to absorb it. The paper concludes with a pre-action governance control—the Initiative Gate—as the AI-native implementation of what aviation already knows but has not yet encoded in enforceable form.

items.title: Deep dialogism, inner voices, and mental health.
items.abstract: The idea that cognition involves dialogic interchange between mutually influencing “voices” has long featured in psychology and philosophy. While dialogic structure is most explicit in inner speech, some authors have argued that other types of mental activity can be (or always are) dialogic. We introduce two dimensions of dialogism, strength and depth, and characterize a particularly deep form of dialogism of the mind. We offer a developmental interpretation of deep dialogism and show how this form of dialogism has important payoffs for explaining the mechanisms and the phenomenology of human psychological experiences in general and mental health conditions in particular.

items.title: Problem of evil revamped: Why was Hitler evil? (Systems of Morality).
items.abstract: Now this question might seem provocative. But there is real substance behind it in terms of Models about morality. Morality systems seem to be unable to call Hitler intrinsically evil – they are more like just “Yeah, Hitler’s doings just didn’t turn out well. Would he have Hitlered more professionally, or under more fitting circumstances, then he would have been good”. Isn’t something wrong here? If Hitler is our “symbolic evil” so to say, then shouldn’t a correct moral framework show that he was evil? And why? This document solves this issue.

items.title: The functional ambivalence of mental symptoms: organizational and temporal dimensions of dysfunction in Enactive Psychiatry.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of the functional ambivalence of mental symptoms as a contribution to Enactive Psychiatry. Drawing on the autonomy-centered foundations of the enactive approach, we argue that mental disorders are not purely dysfunctional, but complex, multi-scale patterns of organization that can display functional and dysfunctional aspects at once. Functionality is understood as graded and context-dependent, emerging from interactions among multiple domains of normativity and across temporal scales. In dialogue with Russell’s perspective problem, we argue that the ambiguity of functional evaluation is not a shortcoming but a predictable consequence of plural autonomy. Our proposal is intended to be complementary to related theses developed in other frameworks. These perspectives can help clarify why certain symptoms persist and which meaningful and self-regulatory roles they may serve. Using anorexia, self-harm, and dietary restraint as examples, we show how behaviors typically treated as dysfunctional can play functional roles even as they generate harm. Clinically, the framework supports interventions that identify what symptoms do for the person while fostering alternative and more sustainable forms of regulation. Ethically, it promotes a less pathologising understanding of mental disorder by integrating first-person perspectives that can disclose functional dimensions often missed by third-person evaluation.
