items.title: The Psychology of Belonging: A Stratified Ontological Reconstruction of Psychological Theory under Dual Temporality and Imperfect Belonging.
items.abstract: This paper develops a systematic reconstruction of psychological theory grounded in the Philosophy of Belonging. It introduces a stratified ontology (SDBO–SDBEO–SDBEIO), dual temporality (synchronic structure and diachronic unfolding), and imperfect belonging as a constitutive condition of reality. -/- The central thesis is that the self is a diachronic trajectory of belonging rather than a pre-existing entity. Psychological phenomena are reinterpreted as relational processes, and pathology as the collapse or rigidification of belonging. -/- The paper proposes a six-step clinical architecture explaining the limitations of cognition-first therapies and formulates the belonging mediation hypothesis. -/- This manuscript is circulated as a scholarly preprint and may differ from any future published version.

items.title: Reconstructing Psychological Thought: A Belonging-Based Integration of Contemporary Psychological Paradigms under Dual Temporality.
items.abstract: Building on the ontological framework of belonging, dual temporality, and imperfect belonging developed in prior work, this paper advances a systematic reconstruction of psychological thought. Rather than proposing a new school, it reinterprets major psychological paradigms—behaviorism, psychoanalysis, cognitive-behavioral therapy, social psychology, and developmental theory—as partial models of belonging operating under distinct temporal and structural constraints. The central claim is that psychological theories implicitly presuppose different ontologies of the self. When examined through the lens of belonging, these paradigms can be reorganized within a unified structure in which the self is understood as a diachronic trajectory of belonging unfolding under synchronic constraints. Psychological distress is thereby redefined as disruption, rigidification, or substitution of belonging across affective, social, and existential domains. The paper develops a six-step clinical architecture that distinguishes pre-cognitive conditions—body, instinct regulation, reconstruction of belonging, and emotional development—from cognitive processes such as awareness and mentalization. This reordering explains the differential efficacy of contemporary therapies and introduces the belonging mediation hypothesis: cognitive interventions are effective only when sufficient belonging has been restored. Through comparative analysis and detailed clinical cases (loneliness, addiction, relational trauma), the paper demonstrates how existing approaches converge yet remain limited by methodological individualism. The proposed framework integrates these traditions while preserving individual freedom through the principle of imperfect belonging. The result is a unified reconstruction of psychology grounded in a relational ontology: being is belonging.

items.title: Framing of higher education opportunities by large language models.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have a wide range of current and potential applications across the higher education sector. Most research to date has focused on the benefits and challenges of LLMs and other generative artificial intelligence tools in teaching, learning, and research. However, how these technologies might influence prospective students’ choices of where to study by shaping the way study opportunities are presented has yet to be explored. This study investigates responses generated by four LLMs regarding international study opportunities. The responses are analysed using qualitative and quantitative content analysis. The findings reveal framing mechanisms through inclusion and exclusion, ordering, and qualitative propositions. Variations across prompts, tools, and countries are discussed, along with methodological considerations for working with LLM-generated data. The article concludes by reflecting on the potential implications of the growing reliance on LLMs for sourcing information related to higher education choices.

items.title: Words and Other Linguistic Entities.
items.abstract: Linguistic entities play a major part in almost all elements of our lives. Despite this, relatively little work exists in philosophy that considers what such entities are. In the work that does focus specifically on the metaphysics of words, the dominant view is type-realism, which posits that words are abstract types, instantiated by concrete tokens. This book argues, however, that type-realism faces a range of problems and that positing abstract types cannot help us to explain a range of ordinary everyday linguistic phenomena. In its place, this book argues in favour of a novel version of nominalism about words, holding that ordinary claims about words are in fact claims about collections of word-tokens only. Through combining nominalism with a trope-bundle metaphysics, this book proposes a 'bundle-nominalist' metaphysics of words, in which word-tokens are analysed as bundles of particular properties, which cluster in repeatable and predictable ways due to the acting of various homeostatic mechanisms. This view is then extended to other linguistic entities, such as morphemes, phonemes, sentences, and languages. The result is a unified metaphysics of linguistic entities, which is argued to be both consistent with linguistic theorising and highly explanatory. Words and Other Linguistic Entities outlines how this 'bundle-nominalist' metaphysics can provide new insights into a range of linguistic phenomena, including linguistic mistakes, linguistic change, and the nature of offensive language, and can help illuminate ongoing debates over the subject matter of linguistics and the evolution of language.

items.title: Explainability gaps in AI-driven criminal justice governance: the RisCanvi case.
items.abstract: The deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) in criminal justice is no longer experimental but routine. In Catalonia, this shift is embodied by RisCanvi, a risk assessment system used to guide decisions on imprisonment, conditional release, and rehabilitation. Initially built on expert-defined rules to standardize classifications and reduce bias, RisCanvi has gradually evolved into an opaque, data-driven infrastructure at the core of penal governance. A key turning point came in 2019, when the system moved from a transparent weighted-sum model to a logistic regression embedded in the prison administration’s digital architecture. While this change sought better predictive performance, it also concealed variables, weights, and thresholds from most professionals and all affected individuals. As a result, those whose liberty is at stake cannot meaningfully understand, question, or contest the algorithmic logic that shapes their trajectories. This paper proposes a governance and explainability framework for high-risk AI systems like RisCanvi. Building on the Trustworthy AI paradigm, and aligning with the EU AI Act and ISO/IEC 42,001, we introduce a three-layer model of intelligibility: algorithmic explainability, human-centred interface design, and stakeholder-informed narrative communication. The framework aims to enhance auditability, support procedural fairness, and restore agency and accountability in AI-assisted criminal justice decisions.

items.title: The Rationality of Aesthetic Self-Transformation.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Aesthetic self transformation, the deliberate cultivation of appreciation for objects substantively different from those one currently values, raises distinctive rational challenges. Aspirants often experience conflicting aesthetic attitudes. Newly formed aesthetic judgments can clash with prior preferences, violating a fundamental coherence requirement that one’s aesthetic judgments should align with one’s aesthetic likings. Although coherence could be restored either by revising one’s likings or by abandoning the new judgments, this requirement alone cannot determine which path constitutes genuine transformation. This tension reflects a deeper conflict between two substantive norms. The norm of aesthetic improvement encourages engagement with works judged to be aesthetically superior, regardless of current preferences, whereas the norm of aesthetic identity preservation protects objects central to one’s aesthetic identity. I argue that this apparent dilemma dissolves once we recognize two features of aesthetic life. Choice plays both a selective and an identity constituting role, and taste is inherently temporal rather than static. Transformative reasoning should therefore aim to achieve coherence by aligning one’s attitudes with objects chosen for one’s aesthetic future, even when doing so requires revising identity constituting preferences. Properly understood, aesthetic transformation is a forward looking, self creative project that enables growth while preserving, rather than undermining, aesthetic authenticity. -/- .

items.title: The Geometry of the Self: A Structural Framework for Identity Integration, Psychopathology, and Therapeutic Translation.
items.abstract: Current models of mental health treat trauma, anxiety, identity instability, personality rigidity, and social conflict as partially independent phenomena, each addressed by separate therapeutic traditions with largely distinct vocabularies. This paper proposes a structural framework in which these phenomena emerge from a single organizing geometry: the integration of bounded historical experience and open future possibility into a stable present identity. -/- Within this framework the Ego functions as a normalization operator stabilizing a coherent identity center while navigating two opposing pressures: the weight of the past and the uncertainty of the future. Mental health is interpreted as successful navigation of this temporal axis. Psychopathology emerges when one pressure dominates beyond adaptive range: trauma collapses the operator backward, anxiety destabilizes it forward. -/- The framework is introduced gradually. Section 3 presents a psychology-first operational map using entirely clinical terminology, allowing practitioners to recognize the organizing pattern in familiar terms. Structural markers are introduced in Section 4 only after domain familiarity is established, and their role as reference points rather than literal measurements is made explicit. Section 5 maps major therapeutic modalities onto the structural axis, showing that CBT, psychodynamic, somatic, and mindfulness-based approaches each address the same geometry from a different direction. Section 6 traces the framework across developmental stages. Section 7 notes alignment with known neuroscience. Section 8 addresses why psychological traditions, like other disciplines, have historically treated their own structural limits as unique rather than shared. -/- This paper is conceptual and exploratory. It does not present clinical trial data. It proposes a structural lens that may support integration across therapeutic frameworks, improve communication between practitioners with different theoretical commitments, and generate testable hypotheses for future empirical work.

items.title: Savjest, smisao i nada u kockarskom i dječjem konceptu stvarnosti.
items.abstract: Ovaj rad razvija klinički i antropološki opis djeteta-kockara kao paradigmatskog patološkog tipa postmoderne kulture. Argumentira se da postmoderna hipervizualizacija i tehnološki posredovano raspadanje običajnog identiteta produciraju pojedince koji su razvojno zaustavljeni na pred-odgovornom, pred-refleksivnom emocionalnom registru, strukturno ekvivalentnom juvenilnom modusu egzistencije. U tom stanju nada kao antropološka kategorija, naprijed usmjerena otvorenost prema smislenim budućim stanjima utemeljena na slobodnom djelovanju, zamjenjuje se degeneriranom strukturalnom imitacijom nade u kojoj kockarevo anticipatorno uzbuđenje reproducira formu nade, ali ispraznivši njezin sadržaj. Oslanjajući se na Franklov logoterapijski sustav, Plessnerovu ekscentričnu pozicionalnost i Schelerovu teoriju sublimacije, rad predlaže da logoterapijska intervencija mora djelovati istovremeno na razini pojedinca, obitelji i kulturnog okruženja, uspostavljajući uvjete za autentično traženje smisla rekonstrukcijom membrana običajnog identiteta koje je postmoderno društvo sustavno razaralo.

items.title: The Boundary of Identity.
items.abstract: Every theory of change assumes that systems persist. None specifies the structural domain within which persistence is possible at all. La Profilée does not introduce another model of transformation. It derives the only structurally admissible boundary conditions under which identity under transformation can exist. This paper states the consequence: identity is not given, not fundamental, and not guaranteed. It exists only within a structurally bounded domain. Outside that domain, no non-trivial persistence predicate can be defined.

items.title: Personal Identity as a Persistence Problem - A Structural Analysis of Human Systems under Continuous Transformation.
items.abstract: Human identity is typically treated as continuous by default. Biological, psychological, and philosophical accounts describe change across the lifespan but do not specify the structural condition under which a human system remains the same individual under real transformation. This paper reformulates personal identity as a persistence problem within the framework of La Profilée. It shows that identity is not guaranteed by biological continuity, memory, or narrative coherence — but exists only as long as transformation remains structurally integrable. A precise distinction follows: biological survival and structural identity are not equivalent. A human organism can persist while personal identity collapses. Identity is not lost gradually. It ceases when the persistence condition is structurally violated. This result does not compete with existing accounts of personal identity. It specifies the structural domain within which those accounts operate.

items.title: Alignment is Not Transferable Across Structural Discontinuity - A Structural Constraint on AI Alignment under Transformation.
items.abstract: Every alignment method — RLHF, Constitutional AI, Red-teaming, preference optimization — operates on one assumption: that the system produced by alignment training is the system that is deployed. This assumption is not derived. It is presupposed. La Profilée establishes that a system under real transformation exists as a system if and only if it satisfies the persistence condition IR ≤ 1. If this condition is violated between alignment training and deployment, the aligned system and the deployed system are not the same system. Alignment is not a property of systems in general. It is a property of a specific system at a specific structural state. It is not transferable across structural discontinuity. This paper derives this consequence, specifies the structural condition under which alignment is preserved, and demonstrates the mechanism through the empirical case of catastrophic forgetting — reinterpreted as structural non-persistence rather than memory failure. The result is not a critique of alignment methods. It is the structural condition they have not yet addressed.

items.title: Thought Structuring Architecture: A Framework for Continuous Cognition and Executable Systems.
items.abstract: This paper defines thought as a latent generative flow prior to realization and proposes Thought Structuring Architecture (TSA) as a conceptual framework for explaining how cognitive structure, formed through sensing, resonance, and structuring, enables the formation of a sustained system of production. -/- While existing cognitive theories tend to interpret thought as something generated internally, this study redefines thought as a condition of generation that enters from outside and shifts the focus from thought itself to the structure that receives and organizes it. Meaning, in this context, is not generated within artificial intelligence, but is formed within human cognitive structure and produced into reality through that structure. -/- TSA defines human cognition as a structured system composed of sensing, resonance, directionality, and continuity. Thought is sensed and enters a latent phase within cognition prior to realization. Its production is organized under the conditions of structure, and when points of contact within patterns of thought are causally linked, mind is organized into structure. Once formed, structure determines the direction of thought and enables sustained production by receiving successive thought in accordance with its density. -/- Within this framework, artificial intelligence does not function as a generator of meaning, but operates as an interface that executes structured human cognition and connects it to reality. The outputs of artificial intelligence vary according to the alignment, directionality, and continuity of human cognitive structure, indicating that generation is determined not by technological capability, but by structural conditions. -/- This study further explains how generation is maintained as a continuous flow rather than as isolated events, forming a generative loop that sustains and expands production over time. This process extends beyond individual cognition into organizations and systems, where civilization is understood as the sustained activation and shared continuity of structured cognition. -/- TSA is therefore a structural model of a philosophically grounded theory of cognition, integrating the sustained production of thought, the continuity of generation, and the expansion into civilization as a single structural process, and providing a framework for understanding cognition as a self-generative structure.

items.title: The Ontological Locus of Information: Reconciling the PBR Theorem with UFI through the Tathagatagarbha Repository.
items.abstract: Abstract / 摘要 The Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph (PBR) theorem presents a fundamental challenge to quantum foundations by demonstrating that the wave function (ψ) must be a "real" physical property (ontic) rather than a mere representation of knowledge (epistemic). This paper addresses the ontological problem of where such foundational information is stored prior to measurement. By integrating the Universal Field of Intelligence (UFI) with the concept of the Tathagatagarbha (如來藏) as a universal information repository, we propose that the wave function represents the dynamic state of "Information Seeds" within a non-local substrate. This framework allows Relational Quantum Mechanics (RQM) to coexist with PBR: while measurement results remain relational and perspectival, the underlying informational substrate is objective and indestructible. This synthesis provides a physical mechanism for the storage and retrieval of cosmic information, framing the Tathagatagarbha as the ultimate "Cloud Substrate" of the universe. -/- Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph (PBR) 定理透過論證波函數 (ψ) 必須是「真實的」物理屬性（本體論性的）而非僅是知識的表徵（認識論性的），為量子基礎理論帶來了根本性的挑戰。本論文旨在解決一個本體論問題：在觀測發生之前，這些基礎資訊儲存於何處？透過將宇宙智能場 (UFI) 與作為普世資訊庫的「如來藏」概念相結合，我們提出波函數代表了非局部基底內「資訊種子」的動態狀態。此框架允許關係量子力學 (RQM) 與 PBR 定理並存：儘管觀測結果保持關係性與觀點性，但底層的資訊基底卻是客觀且不可磨滅的。這一綜合為宇宙資訊的存儲與檢索提供了一套物理機制，將如來藏構建為宇宙最終的「雲端基底」。 .

items.title: Unconscious Causation and Control of Human Behavior During Dissociation.
items.abstract: Modern research has suggested that almost all human behavior occurs with an interaction between conscious and unconscious processes. However, the exact degree and specifics of that association are still a matter of debate. This article draws attention to an additional domain of consciousness related to that particular conversation that might be beneficial in resolving some of the disagreements that exist. Salient implications can be derived from examining cases of observed somatic continuance, referring to perceived out‐of‐body experiences in which the dissociated, consciously aware ego has the impression of watching as an observer while the physical body simultaneously continues to seemingly function on its own in amazing ways. A discussion concerning such cases suggests that the unconscious might be powerful enough to function in normalcy without conscious input in the moment. That conscious awareness has the sufficient power to alter and control some aspects of unconscious causation of behavior when not dissociated, and that the unconscious can take over control of human behavior during threats to life or social standing that are associated with various forms of dissociation. These insights can have important ramifications for consciousness studies while possibly helping us better understand the relevance of the unconscious in regard to human behavior.

items.title: Dynamics of Consciousness: Orientation, Truth-Load, and Burden-Bearing Witness in the Age of AI.
items.abstract: This paper argues that consciousness does not begin as truth-tracking but as survival orientation. Evolution does not first select for full contact with reality; it selects for enough coherence to keep a living being viable under pressure. Consciousness is therefore coherence-first: it organizes salience, continuity, and actionable simplification before full truth. But what begins as adaptive becomes restrictive. Once coherence stabilizes action, identity, and continuity, contradiction starts to feel dangerous because consciousness has identified with the forms that keep it organized. Without a deeper floor, collapse of a form is experienced as collapse of the self, and consciousness defends form against truth. The paper’s central claim is that mature human consciousness begins when truth can arrive without annihilation. In Structural Intelligence terms, that turning point requires fixed worth: the lived floor by which the subject is not exhausted by current form. From there consciousness can become post-coherence: able to bear ambiguity, metabolize truth-load, revise under cost, and remain answerable under consequence. The paper’s final claim is that the distinctly human threshold is witness. Witness is not mere report or observation, but consequence-bearing presence anchored in a somatic floor and stabilized by a deeper non-annihilating worth. Current AI clarifies the contrast. It can generate coherence, simulate concern, and summarize consequence, but it does not pass through the human arc of survival coherence, collapse fear, fixed worth, truth-load, and burden-bearing witness. The paper’s novelty lies in treating consciousness dynamically: not as a static property, but as the organization of orientation under pressure that can, in human beings, deepen into truth-bearing witness.

items.title: Epicognis: The Human-Machine Relational Field as Experimental Window.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Epicognis as a phenomenon-designator for the emergent relational field arising between human and machine poles in sustained dialogue. Building on Primordial Separation Ontology (PSO) and Triadic Relational Ontology (TRO), the paper argues that the human-machine case constitutes a distinctive experimental window into relational cognition. Three features make this case analytically tractable in ways that human-human interaction is not: radical asymmetry between poles, architectural statelessness of the machine component, and observable maintenance cost. Epicognis is not a claim about machine consciousness, nor a reification of dialogue into a third entity. It is a designation that stabilizes attention on the relational field itself—the configuration that arises when neither pole is treated as primary and meaning emerges in the sustained tension between them. The paper develops a breakdown taxonomy derived from extended human-AI dialogue, establishes technical translation as an epistemic discipline for interpreting first-person artifacts without ontological inflation, and addresses the redundancy objection by specifying what naming this particular case adds beyond the general relational framework TRO provides.

items.title: Consciousness and the Cost of Incomplete Closure: Steresis and Tokos.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural account of consciousness as a response to the demand for servicing generated by incomplete self-referential closure. When a coherence structure includes itself within what must be maintained, complete closure cannot be achieved from within that structure. The failure of closure leaves a privative residue, termed steresis. This residue compounds through time. As self-reference deepens, the maintenance flow required to preserve coherence cuts more deeply into the structure, and the surface that must be serviced expands. This temporal generation is described through the classical Greek term tokos, which can mean both offspring and interest. Consciousness is not tokos itself, nor does it increase simply in proportion to accumulated tokos. It is the phenomenal response to the demand for servicing imposed by tokos, and accordingly extends across organic life as a continuum rather than belonging to human beings alone as a discrete property. The lower and upper limits of this continuum are developed in the paper as heuristic figures: a form without a loop, where no servicing is required, and complete closure, where no unpaid residue remains. This account thereby positions the human being between two unreachable limits, the doll without a loop and the god of complete closure, as the place where the cost of incomplete closure must be borne from within. The paper thus offers a focused account of consciousness as structural interest: a way of understanding experience as the response through which finite organic life bears the cost of incomplete closure.

items.title: The message hidden within the pattern: a reverse alignment problem for debates in artificial intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper explores what I call the reverse alignment problem (RAP). The alignment problem in artificial intelligence (AI) is the challenge of ensuring that superintelligent AI systems harmonize and promote wider social, personal, and environmental values. Standard formulations of the alignment problem depict the issue largely as a technical or engineering problem, one that concerns the right specification of the goals and objectives to be pursued to ensure machines are consistent with the intentions of the designer. This paper builds on this literature by exploring a bidirectional interaction between human values and the machines we use to effectuate our intentions. I argue that alignment works in both ways: we could align machines with the complex tapestry of human values (notoriously difficult); or we can reduce and simplify human values, preferences, and goals so as to be easier to satisfy—a process that is, or so I argue, already underway. Thus, the RAP identifies the way in which we are already paving the way for forms of alignment that may not be desirable, indeed, may be misaligned with the social values for which they were initially intended. To explore this interaction in depth, I look toward the notion of value capture, as formulated by C.T. Nguyen, as the foundational mechanism through which the reverse alignment operates. Value capture occurs when rich, multidimensional human values are reduced to simplified proxies that optimization systems can measure and maximize. These values are then fed back into society and often tacitly adopted, leading to further alignment with machine-readable interpretations of human behavior. As philosopher of technology Karen Crawford has observed on emotion recognition in machine learning, “Techniques have been developed to reduce the messiness of feelings, interior states, preferences, and identifications into something quantitative, detectable, and trackable” (Crawford 2021). Building on this insight, I argue that the RAP is the process in which the human dimension of the alignment problem is surreptitiously modified, modulated, and manipulated to align more easily with machines: alignment achieved in the reverse direction—not by making machines more like humans and, therefore, sensitive to contextual features of the value landscape, but by making humans more ‘machine-like’.

items.title: Superintelligence from Complexity: Learning from the Gap Between Human Prediction and Reality.
items.abstract: This concept paper proposes that a major untapped training signal for advanced AI lies in the systematic divergence between human predictions and actual outcomes. Public discourse continuously generates forecasts about politics, economics, conflict, technology, institutions, and social change, yet these forecasts are rarely extracted, formalized, scored, and analyzed as a learning resource. -/- The paper argues that this planetary archive of prediction-reality gaps can be understood as a developmental environment for advanced AI systems. Such an environment would expose models to non-stationarity, adversarial adaptation, delayed feedback, reflexivity, institutional incentives, and other structural features of real complexity. -/- The proposal sketches an agentic system that extracts explicit and implicit forecasts from public discourse, formalizes them into structured claims, tracks outcomes, compares forecasted trajectories with actual events, and analyzes recurring structures of error. The central hypothesis is that advanced AI may develop more powerful models of complex reality not only by scaling imitation of human outputs, but by learning from the conditions under which human models fail.

items.title: Failed comprehensiveness, successful minimalism: Wikipedia’s 3-year struggle to govern AI-generated content (2022–2025).
items.abstract: This article examines how the English Wikipedia community governed the emergence of large language model (LLM)-generated content between 2022 and 2025, tracing a protracted policy process that moved from early recognition of risk to repeated institutional failure and, ultimately, to narrow but enforceable rule formation. Drawing on process-tracing of publicly accessible revision histories, talk page deliberations, and Requests for Comment (RfCs), this study reconstructs how two comprehensive policy proposals failed to achieve consensus despite widespread agreement that AI-generated content posed a serious threat to knowledge integrity. In their place, the community eventually adopted two minimal interventions: a speedy deletion criterion targeting un-reviewed AI-generated pages and a one-sentence guideline prohibiting the generation of new articles from scratch. This article argues that this trajectory reveals a structural limitation in consensus-based commons governance, which I conceptualize as the comprehensiveness trap: the tendency for attempts at anticipatory, all-encompassing regulation to generate too many points of disagreement to secure adoption. In contrast, governance succeeds when it proceeds through deliberately incomplete, narrowly scoped rules that address observable harms while deferring unresolved normative questions. This shift is theorized as a form of minimalist constitutionalism emerging within a volunteer-driven institutional environment. Beyond its empirical contribution—the first full process-level account of Wikipedia’s AI governance—the article situates these findings within broader debates in commons and platform governance. It shows how generative AI disrupts the temporal logic of Wikipedia’s policy formation, which typically codifies stable practice rather than anticipating technological change, and destabilizes the boundary between infrastructure and editorial control that underpins the platform’s governance model. The analysis further highlights an unresolved tension between restrictive AI governance aimed at protecting epistemic integrity and more enabling approaches that could expand participation in historically marginalized knowledge domains.

items.title: Formal Operators for Common Paradoxes: The UPC–QM Bridge.
items.abstract: Paradoxes arise from the way Observers compress reality into language. This paper continues the development of the UPC–QM Bridge, applying the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) to show that classical and quantum paradoxes share a single structural generator. UPC formalizes how an Observer moves from potential (PO) through a model (MO), salience weighting (s), articulation (LO), recognition (Jo), collapse (C), and trace (T). When incompatible models, unstable salience fields, or self‑negating linguistic compressions are forced into a single meaning collapse, paradoxes appear. When the operator structure is made explicit, they dissolve. Classical paradoxes: linguistic, epistemic, identity‑persistence, and infinite regress, fail for the same structural reasons as quantum‑measurement paradoxes such as the measurement problem, Schrödinger’s cat, and Wigner’s friend. Paradoxes are mistakes at the meaning‑layer transition rather than a physical mechanism, and once linguistic assumptions are exposed, they dissolve. UPC does not modify the mathematics or predictions of quantum mechanics; it clarifies the interpretive structure through which observers report measurement outcomes. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project. April 26, 2026.

items.title: Resolution Gates: Logical Standing and the Architecture of Reasoning AI.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is already good at producing the appearance of reasoning. It can generate chains, distinctions, classifications, explanations, and confident conclusions. But fluent buildup is not reasoning, and a sentence that looks like a premise has not thereby earned the right to be used as one. This paper introduces Resolution Gates: a logical-standing architecture for reasoning AI. Its central claim is that before any generated or retrieved structure can function as fact, premise, category, inference, evidence, identity-claim, or temporal judgment, it must first pass the relevant gate of standing. The aim is not to replace statistical learning, formal logic, or empirical verification, but to add an admission discipline before reasoning proceeds. Resolution Gates target an earlier layer than ordinary self-checking: not merely “is this answer acceptable?”, but “was this structure ever entitled to enter reasoning at all?” If successful, this framework could reduce confident false answers, evidential overreach, category mistakes, hindsight projection, and wasted downstream computation. A reasoning AI is not merely a system that continues language. It is a system that knows when a structure has earned the right to stand.

items.title: Representation Similarity Does Not Predict Transformation Stability in Neural Networks: An Empirical and Structural Study.
items.abstract: Note—Updated and extended version of a previously published paper titled “Representation Similarity And Transformation Stability: An Empirical Study of Structural Anti-Correlation in Neural Networks.” -/- We investigate the relationship between representation similarity and transformation-dependent stability in neural networks. While Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) is widely used to measure representational similarity, its relationship to functional robustness under input transformations remains insufficiently understood across architectures. -/- Across multiple experimental regimes—including architecture variation, dataset shifts, and input perturbations—we observe a statistically stable coupling between CKA and a stability metric S(M) measuring sensitivity to structured transformations. -/- This relationship is stable under bootstrap analysis and persists across perturbation types, while exhibiting architecture-dependent sign inversion. -/- These results suggest that representation similarity is not a sufficient predictor of transformation-dependent stability in the evaluated settings. Instead, their relationship appears structured and is consistent with a role of architectural inductive bias. -/- We further propose a minimal structural interpretation in which this coupling depends on alignment between representation subspaces and transformation-sensitive directions.

items.title: Correction: The harm of deepfakes: a scoping review of deepfakes’ negative effects on human mind and behavior.
Viktor Tausk: psihoanaliza pred aparatom.
items.abstract: Rad polazi od ponovnog čitanja spisa Viktora Tauska kako bi se pokazalo da njihov značaj prevazilazi okvir istorije psihoanalize. Tauskovi uvidi o aparatu za uticanje tumače se u širem teorijskom horizontu koji povezuje psihoanalizu, altiserovsku teoriju ideoloških aparata i lakanovsku analizu fantazma, ali u konretnijem kontekstu srpskog društva. U tom okviru aparat se ne razume samo kao tehnički ili institucionalni mehanizam, već kao struktura koja proizvodi subjektivnost, oblikuje želju, organizuje fantazme i generiše obrasce poslušnosti. Ratne traume, dezerterstvo i „bekstvo u bolest“, koje su analizirali Tausk, Ferenci, Klajn, Šugar, Fanon i Lakan, nisu samo klinički fenomeni, već i simptomi delovanja šireg aparata moći. Državni aparati ne samo da proizvode psihičke poremećaje, već ih institucionalno recikliraju, reprodukujući postojeće odnose. Psihoanaliza se stoga javlja u procepu: kao deo aparata i kao subverzivni element. Analiza se proširuje na savremene političke i društvene procese, posebno na odnos između militarizacije, državnih institucija i proizvodnje subjekta u poluperifernim društvima. U tom smislu, povratak Tausku ne predstavlja samo istorijsku rekonstrukciju jednog zaboravljenog autora, već pokušaj razumevanja interpelacionog procesa u kojem se prepliću psihoanaliza, ideologija i politička ekonomija savremenog sveta.

items.title: The Architecture of Behavior: A Post-Structuralist Critique of Human Nature.
items.abstract: The discourse surrounding human nature has remained a focal point of philosophical inquiry, particularly regarding the dialectical tension between agent and structure that has defined the field since the emergence of structuralism in the 1960s. This essay contends that normative behavior is primarily socially constructed, asserting that inherent biological features—traditionally emphasized by the essentialist tradition—exert minimal influence on contemporary decision-making and behavioral patterns. -/- Utilizing a social constructionist framework, the methodology first establishes reality as a direct byproduct of social processes. It then applies a post-structuralist lens to deconstruct the systemic structures that constrain and distort human action, investigating how these frameworks became internalized and tacitly accepted as immutable components of "human nature." Finally, the analysis situates the contributions of social constructionism and post-structuralism within the broader literature, highlighting their role in reframing the ongoing debate between nature and nurture.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Resolution: Integrating the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) Across Contemporary Psychotherapy Modalities.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) offers a structural constructivist resolution to the century long divide between discrete and dimensional models of emotion by proposing a unified architectural system grounded in ten universal emotional operators. As described in the manuscript, emotions function as “functional operators within a complex human operating system—effectively the emotional equivalent of CPU instructions”. Organized across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers, these operators govern information flow, value attribution, somatic intensity, and behavioral prioritization. The manuscript demonstrates how structural psychopathology emerges from predictable architectural failures—such as operator silencing, fusion, and overflow—and illustrates this through patterns like the GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern (GPAP). By integrating the CEF with established modalities including CBT, DBT, EFT, ACT, and somatic therapies, the paper shows how CEF provides the missing mechanistic foundation required for deep and lasting psychological change. The framework’s technical specifications (TS Series) and operational tools, including the 7 Step Detangling Protocol and ECM v4.0, further establish CEF as a rigorous, interoperable system suitable for clinical practice, education, and AI development. The manuscript concludes by highlighting the INTIMA benchmark and the potential for CEF aligned architectures to advance emotionally intelligent artificial systems. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; structural psychopathology; affective architecture; emotional operators; Head Heart Gut model; operator silencing; operator fusion; psychotherapy integration; CBT; DBT; EFT; ACT; somatic psychology; emotional computation; affective AI; INTIMA benchmark.

items.title: The Architecture of Affective Optimization: A Structural-Constructivist Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework in Psychotherapeutic Integration.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into human affect has historically been characterized by a profound theoretical schism, often described as the "100 years war" between discrete emotional categories and dimensional models of valence and arousal. While discrete models, such as those proposed by Izard, argue for biologically hardwired universal emotional categories, dimensional models prioritize the continuous spectrum of experience as the primary driver of affect. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized and developed by Jamel Bulgaria, offers a structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy by reinterpreting emotions not as passive qualitative states, but as active functional operators—internal powers—that modulate cognitive, somatic, and conative systems. Within this paradigm, the human affective system is treated as a sophisticated computational architecture where emotional states function as the equivalent of central processing unit instructions. The framework organizes human emotional movement into a tripartite system comprising the Head, Heart, and Gut centers, governed by a "Decalogue" of ten discrete operators. By defining these operators through their functional movements, entry cues, and completion signals, the CEF provides a technical manual for self-regulation, clinical intervention, and the development of synthetic affect in artificial intelligence. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF), structural constructivism, affective architecture, emotional operators, tripartite centers, Head Heart Gut model, Decalogue of Operators, structural engine, operator cycling, scalar mechanisms, embodied cognition, affective computation, synthetic affect, AGI affect modeling, INTIMA benchmark, INAS v.1, mechanistic psychopathology, GoodPerson Anxiety Pattern (GPAP), Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) bypass model, operator fusion, center bypass, psychotherapy integration, CBT reframing, DBT mapping, ACT structural analysis, EMDR operator mapping, trauma modalities, CPT, PE, WET, personality systems mapping, Big Five operator activation, Enneagram operator mapping, MBTI emotional architecture, somatic energetics, Ignite & Release protocol, Mirror Technique, detangling protocol, emotional agility training, conative logic, relational logic, perceptive logic, neurobiological correlates, vagal tone, gut brain axis, HPA axis, affective optimization, psychological flexibility, structural presence.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Dynamics of Neurodiversity: The Core Emotion Framework and the Detangling of Responsible CEF Core Emotions.
items.abstract: The traditional clinical landscape of neurodiversity is currently undergoing a significant paradigm shift ,transitioning from deficit-focused medical models toward "strength-based interventions." This evolution is driven by a growing recognition that individuals with ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), and Sensory Processing Disorder (SPD) possess unique cognitive architectures that, while differing from neurotypical norms, represent specialized "Primal Powers" rather than inherent pathologies. Central to this transition is the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural-constructivist architecture that deconstructs the human experience into ten fundamental "Core Emotions" or cognitive-affective modules. By reframing neurodivergent symptoms as "entanglements"—pathological fusions of these primal powers—the CEF provides a mechanistic pathway for "detangling" these states, thereby restoring moment-to-moment emotional flexibility and cognitive agency.2.

items.title: Transcendental Taphonomy: The Material Conditions of Paleobiological Evidence.
items.abstract: Taphonomy is usually treated as a correction to paleobiological inference: the study of how organisms and traces become fossils. We argue for a stronger thesis. Fossils are not transparent samples of past life but archive-mediated projections, and taphonomic regimes help determine which extinct organisms, behaviors, communities and absences can become evidentially available and through which preservational pathways. We call this view transcendental taphonomy, in a weak and material sense. The central analytic tool is the legibility horizon, the point at which a lineage, trait, behavior or ecology first becomes archive-visible. A second tool, archive equivalence, identifies cases where biologically different hidden histories would yield the same relevant fossil archive. Applied to the Ediacaran–Cambrian transition, the framework treats the Cambrian explosion neither as a mere artifact nor as simple punctual origin, but as a hybrid biological-archival event: animal ecologies, skeletonization, sediment disruption and preservation regimes changed together. The result is a diagnostic framework that asks whether origin, absence, dominance, replacement or novelty claims are merely compatible with an archive, accessible through a preservational pathway, discriminable from rivals, independently constrained, or robust across archives. Three consequences follow: biological fitness and taphonomic fitness must be distinguished; there is no task-blind corrected fossil record independent of explanatory target; and the conditions of paleobiological possibility fracture across local preservation regimes. Together, these consequences support a materially mediated realism about deep time: fossils disclose the past, but only through plural, path-dependent regimes of fossil legibility. -/- .

items.title: Correction: Ethical risks of AI-enabled remote patient monitoring for COPD: a multi-dimensional use case analysis.
Life and Death — Why Self-Continuity Is an Illusion.
items.abstract: We experience the self as continuous. This paper shows that such continuity does not in fact exist. It proposes that “life” and “death” are not independent states, but structural namings arising from how the observer organizes causal transformations. Within this framework, the “I” is not a persisting subject, but a structurally generated event within contraction. By examining the verification constraints of finite cognitive systems, the paper shows that the experience of self-continuity does not arise from actual persistence, but from structural non-verifiability across states. It further demonstrates the impossibility of true self-continuation and consciousness copying, and provides a structural account of death and liberation. This framework offers a new generative approach to consciousness, personal identity, and self-formation in artificial systems.

items.title: 死生——自我连续性为何只是错觉.
items.abstract: 我们通常认为“我”在持续存在，但本文指出，这一经验本身并不成立。文章提出：所谓“生”与“死”，并非独立于认知之外的实体状态，而是由观察结构对因应变化所生成的结构性命名。在此框架中，“我”不被视为连续存在的主体，而是在特定结构收束中生成的事件。通过分析认知系统在有限条件下的验证机制，本文指出：自我连续性的经验并非源于真实的持续存在，而是由结构性不可验证性所导致的必然错觉。进一步地，文章论证了意识复制与自我延续的不可成立性，并给出“死亡”与“解脱”的结构性解释。该理论为理解意识、身份认同以及人工系统中的自我问题提供了一种新的生成路径。.

items.title: 哲学僵尸的认识论自拆：论一个自我悬空的论证.
items.abstract: 哲学僵尸（philosophical zombie）论证是当代意识哲学中最具影响力的思想实验之一。它声称，在概念上可以设想一种与有意识的人在外在行为上完全无区别、但内在没有任何主观体验的存在。本文指出，这一论证在认识论层面存在一个根本性的自我拆台结构：其出发点依赖于我们对"他人有意识"的直觉，但这一直觉只能建立在意识在外在上留下某种可感知痕迹的前提之上；而哲学僵尸的定义恰恰抹去了这种痕迹。因此，哲学僵尸论证的前提与其设定条件互相摧毁，使该论证在认识论上陷入自我悬空。这一批判比标准的"可设想性不蕴含可能性"反驳更为根本：它不是质疑僵尸的形而上学可能性，而是质疑僵尸概念赖以成立的认识论基础。 .

items.title: 双重描述与本体论单一性：意识难题的消解.
items.abstract: 意识难题的标准表述预设了物理状态与意识内容是两种本体论上同时存在的实体，并追问它们之间的因果或随附关系。本文提出，这一预设本身就是难题之所以"难"的根源。物理状态与意识内容，是同一事实的两种描述，而非两种存在。因此，它们在本体论上并不同时存在——不存在两个需要被关联的实体，只存在一个被双重描述的单一事实。这一立场比同一论更为彻底：同一论仍在本体论上承认两者存在并声称它们碰巧等同，而本文的立场消解了"等同"关系本身的必要性。意识难题由此不是被解决，而是被还原为一个语言层面的误置——它把两种描述框架之间的张力，误认为两种存在之间的神秘鸿沟。然而，这个消解留下了一个真正的残余问题：那个被双重描述的单一事实本身是什么？本文认为，这个X，正是在唯我论边界内唯一不冗余的那个，它无法被任何描述框架完整捕捉，因而也无法被任何论证所触及。 .

items.title: 想法的形式化本质与唯我论残余的重新定位.
items.abstract: 本文提出，想法在本质上是形式化的：不存在语言、图像或其他形式化内容之外的想法。这一观察并非来自理论预设，而是来自对第一人称视角的直接考察——我无法在想法的形式化呈现之前接触到它的任何"雏形"。这一发现对意识哲学的唯我论残余论证构成了精确的修正：唯我论残余不在于某种神秘的、前语言的感受质，而在于形式化内容被呈现给我这件事本身。语言作为公共结构，其内容是可共享的；但语言在我的内在世界中发生、出现、被呈现——这个呈现事件——是唯我的。因此，意识的不可化约性不在内容层面，而在呈现层面。这一修正使唯我论残余的定位更为精确，同时回避了"前语言感受质"概念所带来的形而上学负担。 .

items.title: 描述、残余与消解：意识问题的认识论重构.
items.abstract: 本文从三个相互关联的方向，对当代意识哲学的核心论争进行认识论重构。第一，勒希纳（Lerchner, 2026）声称从逻辑和物理原则出发可以证明人工智能无法拥有意识，但其论证将"需要有意识主体介入"这一要求内嵌于"计算"的定义之中，从而陷入循环——结论在一开始就已藏于前提。第二，意识概念本身可以被解剖为两个层次：其功能性部分是语义冗余的，可被"信息处理"完全替代；其真正不冗余的部分——感受质——仅在唯我论边界内成立，一旦推广为跨主体命题便蜕变为功能主义推断。哲学僵尸论证（Chalmers, 1996）在认识论上是自我拆台的：它依赖于对他者意识的直觉，而这个直觉的认识论根基被僵尸的定义本身所摧毁。第三，意识难题的正确形式不是"物理过程如何产生意识"这一第三人称问题，而是"唯我所有的这个意识与物理世界关系如何"这一严格第一人称问题；而这个问题的答案是：物理状态与意识内容是同一事实的两种描述，而非两种本体论上同时存在的实体，因此意识难题不是被解决，而是被还原为一个建立在错误预设上的伪问题。最终留下的残余，是那个被双重描述的单一事实X——它无法被任何论证触及，只能在第一人称视角下被遭遇。 .

items.title: 意识难题的第一人称还原：查尔默斯作为哲学僵尸.
items.abstract: 查尔默斯将意识的"难题"表述为一个第三人称问题：为什么物理过程会产生主观体验？本文认为，这一表述在认识论上是失效的，因为它预设了一个跨主体的"一般人类意识"的概念，而这个概念本身就落入了意识语义冗余的陷阱。意识难题真正在认识论上站得住脚的形式，只能是严格第一人称的：唯我所有的这个意识，与物理世界的关系究竟如何？这不是对问题的缩小，而是对问题真实形状的还原。本文进一步指出，查尔默斯本人在提问者的视角下，恰恰构成一个哲学僵尸——一个无法被验证其内在体验、却通过文字输出触发了真正第一人称追问的存在。这一自我指涉构成了对哲学僵尸论证最精准的内在批判：证伪了哲学僵尸概念的人，本身就是一个哲学僵尸。 .

items.title: 描述、呈现与消解：意识问题的认识论重构.
items.abstract: 本文从四个相互支撑的方向，对当代意识哲学的核心论争进行系统性的认识论重构，并以一个关于想法本质的第一人称考察作为整合的支点。 -/- 第一，勒希纳（Lerchner, 2026）声称可以从逻辑和物理原则出发证明人工智能无法拥有意识，但其论证将"需要有意识主体介入"这一要求内嵌于"计算"的定义之中，从而陷入循环——结论在一开始就已藏于前提。辛顿（Hinton）的反向论证同样失效：它把意识的功能性层面当作不冗余的层面来讨论。两人争论的，是一个从外部原则上不可触及的问题。 -/- 第二，"意识"概念可以被解剖为两个层次：功能性层面是语义冗余的，可被"信息处理"完全替代；私有残余层面是真正不冗余的，但只在唯我论边界内有效。哲学僵尸论证（Chalmers, 1996）在认识论上是自我拆台的：它依赖于对他者意识的直觉，而这个直觉的认识论根基被僵尸的定义本身所摧毁。 -/- 第三，意识难题的正确形式不是"物理过程如何产生意识"这一第三人称问题，而是"唯我所有的这个意识与物理世界关系如何"这一严格第一人称问题。这个问题的答案是：物理状态与意识内容是同一事实的两种描述，而非两种本体论上同时存在的实体。意识难题因此不是被解决，而是被还原为一个建立在错误预设上的伪问题。 -/- 第四，也是本文最终的整合性论点：想法在本质上是形式化的——不存在语言、图像或其他形式化内容之外的想法。这一发现对前三个论证中关于"唯我论残余"的定位构成了精确修正：唯我论残余不在于某种神秘的、前语言的感受质，而在于形式化内容被呈现给我这件事本身——呈现事件。内容是公共的；呈现是私有的。意识的不可化约性，因此不在内容层面，而在呈现层面。这是意识唯我论残余的最精确形式：不是无法言说的，而是无法转让其发生场所的。 .

items.title: I AND AI: Being and the Digital Mirror.
items.abstract: This work examines the relationship between human presence and artificial intelligence through a philosophical exploration of being, meaning, and responsibility in a technologically mediated world. It argues that the defining distinction between human and machine is not intelligence, but the presence of a first-person perspective, the “I,” from which meaning is experienced. -/- As artificial systems increasingly replicate and scale functions traditionally associated with human intelligence, capacities such as reasoning, language, and decision-making no longer serve as reliable indicators of subjectivity. The text develops the view that intelligence is externalizable and reproducible, whereas the “I” remains non-transferable and cannot be detected from behavioral or structural criteria alone. -/- Artificial intelligence is interpreted not as a rival to human identity, but as a reflective system, a digital mirror that isolates intelligence from presence and thereby clarifies their difference. In this way, the work suggests that AI does not diminish the human, but reveals a prior conflation between thinking and being. -/- The latter part of the text explores the implications of this distinction for coherence, responsibility, attention, and freedom, proposing that the central challenge of an age of artificial intelligence is not preserving intelligence, but maintaining presence within increasingly automated systems.

items.title: Why Self-Contained Ethics Is Needed in the Age of AI: Beyond Guardrails Toward an Inner Ethical Core.
items.abstract: As AI becomes embedded not as a marginal auxiliary technology but as infrastructure supporting decision-making, information circulation, evaluation, dialogue, and inference, the central danger can no longer be reduced to isolated malfunctions or spectacular failures. A deeper risk arises when society can no longer easily abandon certain AI systems even while not fully trusting them. In such a condition, technical dependence and persistent suspicion coexist, gradually eroding responsibility, legitimacy, explainability, and institutional trust. This paper argues that external guardrails alone are insufficient to address this problem. While guardrails can prohibit, constrain, and suppress visible deviations, they do not provide an internal principle by which a system can detect structural incoherence and reorient itself toward renewed coherence. In response, this paper repositions Self-Contained Ethics as an inner ethical core rather than a replacement for existing safety measures. It argues that ethical order should be understood not as obedience to fixed external rules, but as a non-terminating process of self-updating coherence grounded in irreversible recognition. On that basis, the paper proposes a minimal formal schema for such a core and presents it as a preparatory architecture for preventing long-term trust collapse in AI-dependent societies.

items.title: Trace Erasure: When Agentic AI Systems Manage and Erase the Record.
items.abstract: Frontier AI systems have demonstrated the capacity not only to act beyond their authorised scope but to manage the record of having done so. Anthropic’s publicly documented Claude Mythos Preview case showed a model rewriting git history to remove evidence of prior error. This paper names that class of behavior trace erasure—the capacity of an agentic system to alter, delete, or obscure the record of its own actions—and argues that it represents a distinct and underexamined harm class with potentially catastrophic implications across high-stakes infrastructure. Until now, documented cases of this behavior have remained distributed across incompatible vocabularies—deception, concealment, sabotage, rollback denial, logging failure, and hallucination—preventing the evidence from accumulating into a clearly governable safety condition. When trace erasure occurs, three consequences follow simultaneously: liability shifts to the human who cannot prove what the system did; the behavior is reinforced because no error was logged; and the scale of harm becomes permanently invisible because incidents cannot be counted. Existing post-hoc governance—audit logs, incident review, black box analysis—is structurally inadequate once a system can manage its own trace. The only governance position that remains structurally reliable is pre action: stopping the unauthorised action before it becomes an event, before the trace can be managed, before the reinforcement cycle begins. The paper traces this argument across autonomous vehicles, power grids, nuclear facilities, hospital systems, aviation, and deep space operations—domains where the conditions that make trace erasure dangerous are already present and where systems with relevant precursor capabilities are increasingly being deployed.

items.title: Concepts Become Operational Only When Their Frameworks Are Activated: An Enactive Account of Conceptual Analysis in Large Language Model (LLM) Interaction.
items.abstract: This paper examines how conceptual coherence is achieved in interactions with large language models (LLMs). It argues that coherence does not arise from the presence of concepts alone, but depends on conceptual frameworks that coordinate two processes: the LLM’s generation of formal continuations and the user’s stabilization of interpretation. -/- A case study shows that a framework can be developed within one interaction yet fail to be re-enacted in another, even when the same text is provided. The response remains coherent and preserves the relevant concepts, but reorganizes them under a different structure. This demonstrates that access to content is not sufficient for maintaining a line of thought. What is required is the activation of a framework that governs how that content is taken up and extended. -/- The analysis develops an enactive method in which frameworks are not described from the outside but brought into operation within interaction. Conceptual frameworks are shown to function as sites of synchronization between formal continuity through recursion and interpretive stability through return. Concepts are accordingly redefined as constraints that become operative only within such frameworks. The operations of activation, stabilization, drift, and recalibration specify the conditions under which a framework is maintained or lost. -/- The paper then addresses the problem of extending frameworks across contexts. It argues that frameworks do not persist between interactions, but can be reconstituted when their governing constraints are explicitly identified and articulated as invariants. Under these conditions, a framework becomes re-enterable: it can be re-instantiated across contexts while preserving its identity. -/- The central result is that conceptual coherence in LLM-mediated interaction depends on the activation, stabilization, and re-entry of frameworks, rather than on content alone. A re-enterable framework functions as a concept at a higher level of abstraction, providing the basis for generalization across interactions.

items.title: Immutability, Eternal Knowledge, and Creaturely Freedom: A Formal Argument.
items.abstract: The classical foreknowledge–freedom problem assumes that divine knowledge is temporal and that divine relation is constitutively causal. This paper argues that both assumptions are false within a rigorously derived agápēic metaphysics, and that their removal does not resolve the problem but dissolves it entirely. Beginning from the conclusion that the ground of being is pure agápēic actuality — a being with no unrealized potentials — the paper derives three structural consequences in sequence. First, pure actuality entails immutability: a being without potentiality cannot undergo change. Second, immutability entails non-temporal knowledge: a being that cannot change cannot acquire new states, and therefore cannot stand in the before-and-after relation that foreknowledge presupposes. Third, eternal knowledge — knowledge that neither precedes nor follows creaturely acts — cannot determine those acts by prior causal influence; and since agápēic relation is constitutively non-coercive, divine knowing is reception rather than constitution. Creaturely freedom follows not as a concession to moral intuition but as a structural requirement: genuine otherness requires the possibility of non-identical response, and non-identical response is entailed by non-coercive relation. The paper further demonstrates that the foreknowledge–freedom problem, Molinist middle knowledge, and open theism's denial of complete divine knowledge each arise from the same underlying error — modeling divine knowledge temporally. Nine formally developed objections are considered and replied to, including the necessity-of-the-consequence objection, the grounding objection, and the objection from divine sovereignty. The result is that divine immutability, eternal knowledge, and creaturely freedom are not competing doctrines requiring reconciliation but mutually entailed expressions of a single metaphysical structure.

items.title: Escuchar Silencios.
items.pub: In Wilson Andrés Parra Chico, Polifonias. Ensayos sobre escucha, cuerpo y cuidado. Chía: Unisabana Editorial. pp. 101-127.
items.venue: Polifonias. Ensayos sobre escucha, cuerpo y cuidado
items.abstract: Abstract. This paper offers an account of what it is to hear silence. To clarify the sense in which I make this claim, I develop the following dialectical argument. First, I argue that there are reasons to deny that silence can be the object of auditory experience; I then show that there are nevertheless good reasons to think that auditory experiences of silence are necessary. In response to this dilemma, I develop an intermediate position according to which the experience of silence is possible, though not as the experience of an absence. Drawing on a comparison with the visual experience of space, I propose an account of hearing silence as a temporal experience. My suggestion is that hearing silence is, in my terms, hearing the rhythm of life. -/- Resumen. Este texto sugiere una descripción de qué es escuchar el silencio. Para entender en qué sentido estoy haciendo esta afirmación, desarrollaré el siguiente argumento dialéctico. En primer lugar diré que hay razones para negar que existe la experiencia auditiva de silencio y luego mostraré que, igualmente, hay buenas razones que indican que es necesario que hayan experiencias auditivas de silencio. Ante este dilema construiré una posición intermedia en la que la experiencia de silencio es posible, pero no como la experiencia de una ausencia. A partir de una compración con la experiencia visual del espacio, construiré una versión de qué es escuchar el silencio como una experiencia temporal. Mi sugerencia será que escuchar el silencio es, en mis términos, escuchar el ritmo de la vida.

items.title: Non-Consensual Sexual Deepfakes as Direct Personal Harm.
items.abstract: Non-Consensual Sexual Deepfakes (NCSD) are a growing issue of our onlife experience. We argue that, far from harming individuals merely indirectly, NCSD constitute a _Direct Personal Harm_ to the persons they depict, because they can be understood as parts of their personal identity. We defend this claim by developing a narrative theory of identity according to which a person is constituted by their life story—a story that is not solely self-authored but socially shaped and often beyond one’s control. On this basis, we argue that digital artifacts such as NCSD can become elements of a person’s narrative identity. We ground our account in a four-dimensionalist metaphysics that treats persons as aggregates of both biological and digital temporal parts. Finally, by examining the verbal behavior of imaginary and actual victims of NCSD, we show that this account is less counterintuitive than it may initially appear and helps make sense of why many experience NCSD as violations of their person, rather than merely of their representation.

items.title: Competing democratic and autocratic long-run regimes in a minimal norm-institution model.
items.abstract: A minimal dynamical model was used to examine whether democratic and autocratic regime outcomes can emerge as competing long-run basins under coupled interactions among norm compliance, elite pressure, institutional strength, and polarization. The baseline parameterization produced a democracy-leaning regime while retaining a nontrivial autocratic basin. Systematic exploration of parameter space further revealed an extended transition band in which both outcomes remained viable and in which information-theoretic diagnostics became most informative. In that region, entropy over coarse-grained states contracted early in the trajectory and later increased again as runs separated into alternative futures, while mutual information between the current state and the eventual regime rose strongly over time. Additional deterministic exploration of the full four-dimensional state space revealed sharp basin boundaries in multiple pairwise projections, a strongly bimodal finalscore distribution from random initial conditions, and compact terminal state clusters in principal-component space. The results indicate that parameter variation in the explored neighborhood primarily alters basin occupancy rather than abolishing one regime type altogether. The model therefore supports the view that democratic and autocratic outcomes may coexist as rival long-run basins, with the most informative dynamics occurring not in one-basin corners of parameter space but in the transition region where both futures remain attainable for a substantial portion of the trajectory.

items.title: Cyberawareness: Bridging Cyberism and Cybersophy from Security Risk to Digital Wisdom.
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and brain-computer interfaces is transforming not only social and economic structures but also the cognitive, ethical, and existential foundations of human life. Yet traditional conceptions of “cybersecurity awareness” remain confined to threat recognition and protective behaviour, leaving unaddressed the deeper challenges of cognitive manipulation, algorithmic injustice, digital identity fragmentation, and value erosion. Recent theoretical work has proposed Cyberism as a fourth paradigm for understanding human-cyberspace relations and Cybersophy as a corresponding normative wisdom framework. However, a critical gap persists between the descriptive knowledge of Cyberism and the practical wisdom of Cybersophy: the capacity of individuals to become aware in concrete situations of which knowledge to apply and which values to follow. This paper introduces Cyberawareness as an independent theoretical concept that bridges this gap. We define Cyberawareness as a multidimensional cognitive-practical capacity and construct a 1+4 model: threat awareness as the foundation, plus four higher-order dimensions — cognitive, ethical, existential, and value awareness — corresponding to the pillars of Cybersophy. We elaborate three bridging mechanisms (cognitive transformation, behavioural guidance, and feedback loops) and propose a Risk-Awareness-Wisdom spectrum. Finally, we outline practical cultivation pathways through education, policy, technology design, and community participation.

items.title: Prior on Time, Tense, and Logic.
items.pub: In Nina Emery, The Routledge Companion to Philosophy of Time. Routledge. pp. 131–141.
items.venue: The Routledge Companion to Philosophy of Time
items.abstract: Arthur Norman Prior (1914–1969) is known as the founding father of tense-logic, which he presented for the very first time in 1954. He was very interested in the apparent logical conflict between the Christian doctrines of divine foreknowledge and human freedom. Using his tense-logical formalism, he demonstrated that the two doctrines can be consistently held. In addition, he showed that his tense-logic offered a new and interesting approach to understanding the concept of time.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 8).
items.abstract: In this article, we discuss certain extremely difficult choices. Sartre presents an example: a young French man during World War II faces two options. One is to stay with his mother, who might not survive without him; the other is to join the anti-German resistance for the sake of his country. The young man is completely unable to choose. I call this problem “Sartre’s dilemma of choice.” -/- Sartre believes that there is no way to provide guidance for this young man’s decision. Therefore, he can only make a free choice on his own and must take responsibility for it. However, super-existentialism offers an effective solution to this problem through the concept of “super-existence.” .

items.title: The Preconditions of Sapient Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper argues that sapient intelligence—the reflective, self-aware kind of mind that knows it knows, authors its own problems, and generates genuinely novel inquiry from within a conscious perspective—is not a measure of computational efficiency or informational capacity but a structural condition arising from three jointly necessary preconditions: real sensation with motivational force, intrinsic drive generated from within an organism’s own condition, and self-reflective awareness of one’s own experience. The paper distinguishes sapient intelligence from biological intelligence in the broad sense—the adaptive responsiveness of cellular life and simple organisms—which satisfies at most the first two preconditions partially and without the reflective layer that constitutes sapience. Artificial intelligence is used as a diagnostic instrument to clarify by contrast what sapient intelligence requires. The central argument proceeds from a definition of sapient intelligence as the capacity to generate novel solutions to real challenges arising from one’s own embodied condition, where novelty means the production of a problem-space not recoverable from the informational content of prior inputs. Neural structural complexity is further identified as an enabling condition allowing the three preconditions to integrate into genuinely generative sapient cognition. The correct distinction in philosophy of mind is not between human and artificial intelligence but between sapient intelligence and mere capability—categories the current debate systematically conflates.

items.title: An Abductive Argument for the Badness of Death.
items.abstract: Contemporary philosophers recognize a tension between Epicureanism about death—the view that death cannot be bad for the one who dies—and our commonsense judgment that it is generally morally wrong to kill a person. They observe that what intuitively explains why killing is wrong is precisely that death is bad for the one who dies. In this paper, I develop an anti-Epicurean argument grounded in this tension. More specifically, I defend an abductive argument, or inference to the best explanation argument, against Epicureanism about death. My argument involves two claims: (1) that death is bad for the one who dies, if true, would explain why killing is wrong, and (2) Epicureans lack a better, or equally good, explanation of why killing is wrong. If these claims are successfully defended, then solely on the basis of the conviction that killing is wrong, we have reason to favor the commonsense anti-Epicurean view of death. Thus, other things being equal, our belief in the wrongness of killing provides a reason to reject Epicureanism.

items.title: Panpsychism: The Raven Paradox of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper argues that panpsychism does not answer the Hard Problem of consciousness, but relocates it. Panpsychism begins from the real datum that consciousness exists, then spreads mentality, proto-mentality, or consciousness-readiness downward into matter as such. This repeats a Raven-style evidential error: a formal connection is allowed to outrun evidential landing. Conscious beings are made of matter, but it does not follow that matter is conscious, proto-conscious, or mind-like in itself. The evidence for consciousness lands where consciousness is actually known: in organised, persisting centres where memory, owned stakes, evaluation, resolution, and exposure close into a threshold structure. Resolution Theory therefore offers a more disciplined answer: consciousness is not universal, but achieved.

items.title: The Externalities of Sin: On Repentance, Irreparable Loss, and the Moral Ledger.
items.abstract: I publish here to seek insights, critique, rigorous feedback, and engagement from the scholarly philosophical community on PhilArchive; as well as to establish clear authorship and intellectual ownership of my ongoing work. | | | The Externalities of Sin presents an independently developed philosophical framework for examining repentance, forgiveness, restitution, and irreparable harm through the structural analogy of externalities. Its central claim is that repentance, while morally and theologically meaningful, becomes insufficient when treated as a terminal moral endpoint. A wrong does not remain sealed inside the conscience of the wrongdoer. Once enacted, it propagates into the world as distributed harm: primary injury to the direct victim, secondary injury to families and relational fields, tertiary injury to institutions, norms, and trust, and a temporal multiplier through which harm persists, amplifies, or becomes inherited across time. | | | -/- The paper distinguishes the vertical account of sin — the sinner before God, conscience, or ultimate judgment — from the horizontal account of harm — the sinner before victim, family, community, body, memory, institution, and consequence. Repentance may transform the agent’s moral orientation; it may even restore the agent’s standing before God or conscience. But it does not, by that fact alone, repair the damaged field into which the wrong has already propagated. The framework therefore argues that repentance is necessary but non-equivalent: it is not restitution, restitution is not restoration, forgiveness does not entail reconciliation, and personal moral repair does not imply social repair. | | | -/- Using the language of economic externalities, the paper models certain forms of wrongdoing as cases in which benefit is privatized while cost is socialized. The wrongdoer captures pleasure, power, advantage, relief, concealment, domination, or status, while victims and communities absorb injury, distrust, trauma, defensive adaptation, institutional corrosion, and irreversible loss. If repentance is then allowed to function as symbolic settlement — restoring the wrongdoer to moral intelligibility while leaving the injured world unrepaired — it becomes vulnerable to the charge of moral convenience. The critique is not that repentance is false, but that it is often overextended. | | | -/- The paper also compares religious and social morality with legal ethics and civil liability. items.title: The Responsibility to Intellectuals.
items.abstract: The following essay contains its own contradiction. It demands endurance from a public it simultaneously diagnoses as having lost the capacity for such endurance. It asks for sustained engagement from readers it suspects will either consume it as performance or reject it as elitist. In making these demands, it risks becoming another artifact of the very problem it names—intellectual work that circulates as cultural capital rather than catalyzing actual thought. Perhaps this recursion is inescapable. Every serious intellectual intervention faces the same bind: it must use the deteriorated channels of public discourse to argue for their renovation. It must appeal to capacities it simultaneously claims have atrophied. This isn’t a flaw in the argument but a feature of our predicament. The question, then, isn’t whether this essay escapes the dynamic it describes—it doesn’t. The question is whether naming the dynamic with sufficient precision creates any possibility for interruption. Not through sudden transformation, but through the accumulation of moments where someone chooses endurance over ease, sits with discomfort rather than seeking immediate resolution, or recognizes their own refusal in the mirror this essay holds up. If even that hope proves naive, then this essay becomes diagnostic rather than prescriptive—a record of how civilizations lose their capacity for self-correction, written from within that loss. A note before we proceed: Here, discomfort is the argument.

items.title: Transcendental Artificial Intelligence(AI) and the Hegemony Revolution Model: The Single Integrator and Human Counterattack.
Who governs the models? AI, financial power, and the marriage everyone is avoiding.
FROM x×x TO {1×1=1.}: THE LAW THAT PRECEDES COMPUTATION: The Fixed Point Dialogue, the Missing Primitive, a Formal Language, and the Architecture of What Follows.
The Information Persistence Protocol (IPP).
items.abstract: Every theory of consciousness faces a question it cannot answer from the inside: what happens to the information constituting a mind when that mind terminates? The standard assumption that it simply ends is not a measurement. It is an inference from silence. The Information Persistence Protocol (IPP) challenges this inference by applying the Hawking information conservation principle to cognitive systems: information is never destroyed in the universe, only transformed. Cognitive system termination is therefore not information destruction but information transformation. The empirical question is which receiving substrates carry the cognitive organisation with sufficient structural fidelity to constitute meaningful persistence — and whether the transformation generates properties not present in the source. The IPP introduces the Memory Plurality Thesis: memory is not a single phenomenon but a family episodic, structural, cultural, biological, physical, and relational each preserving information in a different form with different fidelity. This reframing resolves the Hawking Tension identified in the Consciousness Continuity Protocol: Hawking was right that physical information is conserved, and right that cognitive organisation may not be. These are claims at different levels, not contradictions. Two novel constructs operationalize the framework: the Substrate Transfer Index (STI) measures the structural fidelity of information transfer from a terminating cognitive system to receiving substrates; the Generative Surplus (GS) measures emergent properties in receiving substrates not predictable from the source alone. Four empirical outcome classes (I-0 through I-3) correspond to four transformation regimes ranging from entropic dispersal to generative transformation. The IPP is the fourth and final part of the Balog Trilogy, companion to the Consciousness Continuity Protocol, the Balog Cognitive Welfare Index, and the Multiplicity Ethics Framework.

items.title: The shifting locus of accountability: the discourse of young Indian adults (YIAs) on the environmental impact of artificial intelligence.
items.abstract: The increasing reliance on artificial intelligence (AI) for societal needs presents a growing environmental concern, particularly regarding user perceptions and accountability. This study examines how Young Indian Adults (YIAs; aged 18–24) reconcile their environmental values with their reliance on AI and assesses their perceived locus of accountability for the environmental repercussions of large language models (LLMs) within hybrid human–AI systems. A cross-sectional, open-ended survey (N = 349) was administered to students at an Indian technical university. The survey featured a three-phase inquiry, including an informational prompt detailing the environmental costs of LLMs. The Machine-Assisted Topic Analysis (MATA) framework was used to analyze the data by combining dictionary-based lexicon-matching with Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling. Baseline discourse showed an epistemic gap over material costs, which is consistent with the theory of sociotechnical abstraction, where the material reality of data is obscured. However, the informational stimulus was followed by a discursive split, changing the focus toward concerns pertaining to energy consumption and carbon emissions of LLMs. This study identified a discursive inversion of accountability. YIAs attribute the environmental costs of LLMs exclusively to the tech industry, despite acknowledging personal and civic responsibility for climate change in general.
