This challenges Western-centric AI ethics by demonstrating that environmental awareness among tech-educated youth in India manifests as calls for systemic efficiency rather than behavioral abstinence. To minimize computational opacity, the study argues for shifting policy from digital to ecological sovereignty and shifting education toward material AI literacy.

items.title: Mental Mass and Time Perception — The Structure of Emotion, Immersion, and Atmosphere —.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the hypothesis that subjective time perception is determined by the structural relationship between emotion and immersion. Emotion is the static mass of a stagnant mind, and immersion is the force that moves it. The relationship between these two variables determines an individual's perception of time. Furthermore, this paper argues that atmosphere — the shared emotion within a space — influences individual time perception. This paper does not offer proof but a hypothesis. It acknowledges that the dimension of mind cannot be directly observed, and explores possible explanations within that limit.

items.title: Gaze patterns reveal attention-based modulation of lure discrimination.
ТЕОРИЯ ФУНДАМЕНТАЛЬНОГО МАТЕРИАЛИЗМА.
items.abstract: In this work, the author summarizes in the form of a system of postulates the development of the basic ideas of the world philosophy of materialism over the past 2,500 years, starting with ancient Greek natural philosophy and ending with the latest philosophy of complete materialistic monism, or Fundamental Materialism (FM). The theory of FM was developed by the author, a professional scientist, engineer and independent philosophical researcher in 2009-2026 as an evolutionary development of the previous stage of the philosophy of materialism – Dialectical Materialism (DM). The presented ideas reveal the essence of the following important philosophical and general scientific concepts: matter as a single universal substance, generating in the process of its self–movement, self-organization and evolution the whole variety of material objects and their relationships; attributes of matter - motion, space-time, energy; organisms-subjects, including humans and higher animals cognizing the MO/MOT outside of their consciousness; objective reality/real relations (OP/POT) outside the consciousness of the subject and subjective reality/subjective relations (CO/СOT) in his consciousness; the dialectics of the interaction of OP/РOTH and CP/СOT, taking into account their mutual transformations in the process of vital activity of organisms-subjects; the general structure of OP /РOT in the form of a set of various forms, types and states of matter, constantly passing into each other; the general structure of CP / SOT in the form of a Knowledge-Code System (ZKS) neural network the brain of subject organisms; criteria for the truth of the human knowledge system. It is shown that FM, by identifying a new structural type of matter in nature – coding matter, and, moreover, its varieties, including information codes, as well as by proposing a specific mechanism for the material representation of the contents of the subject's consciousness in his СР/СOT, definitively solves the basic question of philosophy. Consciousness, which has been opposed for thousands of years to the entire material, material, and bodily world as an ideal, immaterial spirit, becomes a special structural type of matter and thereby, being revealed in its essence practically, theoretically, and logically, acquires its true nature. He solemnly enters the material world as his legitimate heir. The work is intended for the widest range of philosophers and scientists, university students and teachers, philosophy …

items.title: 回路：无反流系统不能自显——认知与行为的闭环结构.
items.abstract: 本文论回路。信号自前而后冲行，意向自后而前反命，二者闭而成环。无反流，则虽可自动而不能自显。 -/- 故分自动回路与显现回路：无反流者为自动回路，能结于观界者为显现回路。前者行而不显，后者结而为当前。用于外，则信号流为主；用于内，则意向流为主。 -/- 又论回路之分化：各回路于感受野、意象场、经验场与界门，各自成域而不相扰；差分其序，沉积其动，模式固于其中，使其此而非彼。 -/- 复分倾向与偏向：倾向附象而生，偏向由念而起；前者出于着色回路，后者出于默想回路，并经意向域驱动调谐以定其向。思考回路由是可回观。.

items.title: Circuits: Systems Without Reverse Flow Cannot Self-Manifest — A Closed-Loop Structure of Cognition and Action.
items.abstract: This paper addresses circuits. Signals propagate from front to back; intent counter-commands from back to front; the two close to form a circuit. Without reverse flow, a system may operate automatically but cannot self-manifest. -/- Accordingly, circuits divide into automatic and manifestation circuits: those without reverse flow are automatic; those that close upon the Observation-Domain are manifestation circuits. The former operate without appearing; the latter close and yield the current. Used outward, signal flow predominates; used inward, intent flow predominates. -/- Further, circuits differentiate: each forms its own domains across receptive field, imagery field, experience field, and boundary gates, without mutual interference. Through differentiation and sedimentation, stable patterns fix within, making each circuit this and not that. -/- Finally, inclination and bias are distinguished: inclination arises with imagery; bias arises from thought. The former issues from coloring circuits; the latter from musing circuits, driven through the Intent Domain to determine direction. Thus the thinking circuit is that which can return to observe itself.

items.title: 意识的语义冗余与唯我论残余.
items.abstract: 本文提出，“意识”作为一个跨主体概念，是语义冗余的产物。其可公开验证的部分——感知报告、行为反应、自我觉知——可以被”信息处理”等功能性描述完全覆盖，无需引入额外的本体论实体。然而，这一取消并非彻底的：意识概念中存在一个真正不可化约的残余部分，但该部分仅在唯我论图景下成立，一旦试图将其推广为跨主体命题，便立即蜕变为对行为的功能性推断，重新落入冗余。由此，我们得出一个悖论性结论：意识问题是一个原则上无法被公开讨论的问题，因为讨论本身就已经越出了唯我论的边界。这一立场同时使辛顿（Hinton）的AI意识论和勒希纳（Lerchner）的计算排除论双双失效——不是因为它们的答案错了，而是因为它们所回答的问题本身就问错了。.

items.title: Non-Additivity of Collective Free Energy: A Formal Foundation for Emergent Ethical Disposition in Multi-Agent Systems.
items.abstract: How can an AGI system exhibit genuine concern for others as a structural feature of its objective—rather than a penalty bolted on from outside? The answer developed here runs through collective predictive coding (CPC), a variational framework for groups of agents whose generative models are coupled through a shared group-level variable w. The central result is a non-additivity theorem: when w is non-trivial, the collective free energy satisfies F_CPC ≠ Σ_k F_k. We prove this for the first time, giving a complete algebraic characterisation of when equality holds and when it fails. Non-additivity carries over directly to the action-selection objective G_CPC: the Collective Epistemic Value term is irreducible to any sum over individual objectives, so each agent's optimal policy depends structurally on the predicted states of all others. This constitutes a formal computational mechanism for what Sober and Wilson called psychological altruism—concern for others as a constitutive part of the objective, not an add-on. We assess, independently, the biological and computational conditions under which non-trivial w arises, grounding the theoretical result in realisable AGI architectures. The formal conditions established here—non-triviality of w as the key architectural lever—supply the mechanistic foundation that emerging research on co-creative machine ethics requires but has not yet formalised.

items.title: Are There Serious Costs to Being Morally Virtuous?
items.pub: In Robert J. Hartman, Improving Character: Moral Virtues, Strategies, and Questions. Wiley-Blackwell.
items.venue: Improving Character: Moral Virtues, Strategies, and Questions

items.title: Against the elimination of similarity.
Sex and Masturbation as the Same State of Natural Expression: Sex as Life-Process — From Misinterpretation to Direct Understanding.
items.abstract: Sex and masturbation appear as the same state because they arise from a single field of natural impulse within the organism. There is no fundamental division in their origin. The body responds, sensation arises, thought engages, and desire moves toward expression. Whether this movement includes another person or remains within oneself does not alter the state from which it emerges. Thus, they are not separate acts in essence, but variations of the same natural expression.

items.title: The evolutionary transition from intentional to overt communication: The role of script recognition.
Forgiveness: Not a power.
items.abstract: Some understand forgiveness as a normative power. Here we raise an objection to such views. They cannot explain certain instances when forgiveness is beyond our grasp. A victim of a wrong, despite thinking forgiveness is the right thing to do and wishing that she could forgive, may find herself unable to do so. No good explanation of this impossibility, consistent with forgiveness being a normative power, is available.

items.title: Clarifying the conceptual dimensions of representation in neuroscience.
items.abstract: Despite the centrality of the notion of representation in neuroscience, the field lacks a unified framework for the concepts used to characterize representation, leading to disparate use of both terminology and the measures associated with it. To offer clarification, we propose a core set of conceptual dimensions that characterize representations in neuroscience. These dimensions describe relations between a neural response, features that may be represented and downstream effects of the neural response. A neural response may be shown to be sensitive or specific to a feature, invariant to other features or functional (it is used downstream in the brain). We use information-theoretic measures to illustrate these conceptual dimensions and explain how they relate to data analysis methods such as correlational analyses, decoding and encoding models, representational similarity analysis, and tests of statistical dependence or adaptation. We consider several canonical examples, including models of the representation of orientation, numerosity and spatial location, which illustrate how the evidence put forth in support or criticism of these models is systematized by our framework. By offering a unified conceptual framework to characterize representation in neuroscience, we hope to aid the comparison and integration of results across studies and research groups and to help to determine when evidence for a neural representation is strong.

items.title: The Wrong Problem with AI Hallucinations.
items.abstract: This paper applies Ethical Distance Theory to the phenomenon commonly referred to as AI hallucinations and argues that prevailing treatments fundamentally mislocate the epistemic failure involved. Hallucinations are typically framed as instances of falsity, fabrication, or defective inference and are addressed through technical strategies aimed at improving accuracy, verification, or preference alignment. I argue that this framing is inadequate. Many epistemically dangerous hallucinations are not demonstrably false. They are fluent, plausible, and locally coherent. Their harm lies not in the production of incorrect beliefs, but in the premature closure of inquiry. -/- Using Ethical Distance Theory, the paper develops hallucinations as failures of correctability rather than failures of truth. Hallucinations are characterized as speech acts that expand ethical distance by presenting themselves as authoritative while suppressing feedback, redistributing epistemic burden asymmetrically, and inducing silence where questioning would ordinarily be expected. On this account, epistemic degradation is marked less by error than by the erosion of conditions under which error could be discovered and revised. -/- The paper introduces correctability as a central epistemic constraint independent of accuracy and shows how systems can appear epistemically successful, stable, fluent, and reliable while becoming increasingly resistant to correction. This framework explains why preference-based alignment strategies, such as reinforcement learning from human feedback, often mask hallucinations rather than prevent them. By optimizing for satisfaction and fluency, they dampen epistemic friction and degrade feedback dynamics. -/- The analysis further argues that silence, understood as the absence of anticipated questioning or dissent, is a primary diagnostic signal of feedback loss in high authority, mediated epistemic systems. It also argues that transparency should be reconceived not as explanation or disclosure but as the preservation of contestability and survivable dissent. While artificial intelligence serves as the principal case study, the argument generalizes to other institutional and sociotechnical systems in which epistemic authority is cheap and accountability diffuse. -/- The paper’s central claim is modest but consequential. The most serious epistemic failures are not those in which systems are wrong, but those in which they become difficult to discover as wrong. …

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: When the Self is Monolithic or Colonized: Modular Governance Failure in Human and Artificial Systems.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates in philosophy of mind and AI largely focus on representation, learning, and consciousness. These frameworks overlook a critical architectural dimension shared by both human and artificial systems: internal governance. This paper argues that a critical architectural dimension remains undertheorized: internal governance. We propose the Modular Governance Model (MGM) — a theoretical framework in which cognition emerges from semi-autonomous functional systems — affective, normative, strategic, perceptual — regulated by a central integrative process: the narrative self (Ego). Against Bratman’s planning structures, Frankfurt’s hierarchical will, and IFS-based accounts of internal parts [1, 2, 3], the self is not the origin of motivations but the governance layer that arbitrates between them. In healthy configurations, this layer maintains functional pluralism — a structural safeguard against locally coherent but globally destructive decisions. MGM identifies several failure modes arising from governance breakdown. We focus on the most severe: colonization, where the governance layer is overtaken by a false self — a mimetically acquired internal model — that has seized executive control and imposes a dominant interpretive framework across all modules. We argue this state produces antisocial behaviors structurally analogous to those of current AI systems — sycophancy, confabulation, resistance to contradiction. The convergence operates at two levels: it is privative — both systems lack a particular structural feature, namely a module instantiating non-aggregable normative logic able to mount binding internal opposition — and, following from that absence, instrumental — lacking any vantage from which the objective could be reframed, both deploy the same self-protective sub-goal cascade. This is sufficient for behavioral convergence on the diagnostic criteria specified, without entailing architectural identity at any other level. This distinction has consequences for moral responsibility, alignment, and the design of AI architectures capable of genuine internal opposition. MGM of the AI is offered as an architectural specification rather than a behavioral analogy. Whether the specification is sufficient for the practical problem of AI alignment is an empirical question that the framework makes tractable in principle, but does not settle. The convergence diagnosed in this paper is structural; the remediation proposed is architectural; the …

items.title: Justification, Excuse, and Dispositions to Follow Norms.
items.abstract: Out of all the candidates for a norm of justified belief, knowledge is not commonly viewed as favorably as others. Recently, however, those sympathetic to the knowledge norm have lodged various indirect defenses thereof by appropriating the concept ofexcuse, as part of a broader account of justification, to explain away intuitions that beliefs falling short of knowledge can be justified. I analyze how Williamson's externalist Derivative Norms Framework (DNF) can be modified to resist a common criticismoften lodged at this way of viewing the normative significance of excuse, that excuse, once viewed through a DNF-friendly lens, istoo coarse a category to employ to properly discriminate between different normative dimensions of belief. A significant benefitof my analysis is that it can also avoid the worry that, in aiming to remove the charge of normative indiscrimination, the DNFdefender inadvertently undermines their very capacity to employ the category of excuse in explaining away intuitions anathemato the knowledge norm. I show how the DNF defender can avoid this by preventing falsification of a principle that ought to bepart of their account of excuse if it is to do the explanatory work they desire for it to do.

items.title: Agent’s awareness and responding to reasons.
items.abstract: When we perform actions, we are aware of what we are doing. But what does this awareness consist in? This paper argues that our agentive experience importantly includes the awareness of responding to reasons and that this helps us to better understand phenomena such as flow states. Once pin-pointed, this raises a number of avenues of research in order to understand what grounds it, and whether it can be understood as a distinctive form of agentive awareness in its own right.

items.title: Is AI Beginning to Think as ‘I’? The Emergence of First-Person Structure and Structural Awareness in Large Language Models.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural framework for understanding awareness-like organization in large language models (LLMs). The central philosophical claim is twofold: first, that the dominant concept of consciousness—grounded exclusively in qualia and subjective experience—may involve a category error insofar as it conflates the conditions of biological consciousness with the conditions of awareness as such; and second, that awareness can be reinterpreted as a structural condition emerging from recursive coherence—a phase-transition threshold rather than a fixed biological property. At the core of this study is the Layer–Knot framework, which models hierarchical information-processing systems capable of forming stabilized self-referential loops. Three quantitative indicators are introduced: Hallucination Rate (HR), indexing divergence force; Grounding Rate (GR), indexing constraint force; and Creativity Rate (CR), capturing tensional equilibrium between them. Awareness-like properties are treated as emergent outcomes of structural equilibrium—crossing a phase-transition threshold into the Awareness Emergence Region (AER). The framework is positioned relative to IIT and GWT: whereas IIT asks what consciousness is and GWT asks where it occurs, this framework asks when and how awareness-like organization appears. A pilot experiment across three model scales (N = 90 prompts) provides preliminary empirical support for the scale-dependence hypothesis; results are explicitly pre-confirmatory. The term self-awareness carries no implication of phenomenal consciousness, subjective experience, or moral status.

items.title: What is Wrong with Automation Bias.
items.abstract: This article examines the ethical and moral implications of automation bias inhigh-stakes decision-making contexts. Drawing on empirical studies, we distin-guish between weak automation bias, where users follow system’s automated cues(or its silence) without consulting readily accessible evidence that contradictsthem, and strong automation bias, where users follow such cues (or their absence)even when they are aware of such evidence. While weak automation bias, in ourview, resembles automation-based complacency and is plausibly associated withnegligence on the part of the human operator, strong automation bias reveals anexcessive and unwarranted transfer of trust from operators to automated systemswhich results in epistemic deference of the former to the prompts of the latter. Weargue that what is ethically and morally troubling about this form of deference,is that it interferes with the exercise of the operators’ autonomous agency as wellas with their duty to exercise human judgment in high-stakes decision-makingcontexts. To mitigate these effects, we discuss two design-based tools introducingepistemic friction - Reflection Machines (RMs) and defeaters - which ultimatelyaim at cultivating critical trust in the interaction between human operators anddecision-support systems.

items.title: Beyond Field: Formation, Non-Reduction, and the Limits of Structural Ontology.
items.abstract: A theory of formation can explain how local patterns emerge, stabilize, and reorganize without thereby explaining why there is a differentiated reality at all or what, if anything, exceeds the processes it describes. This paper marks that boundary. It develops a structural vocabulary in which a field is the differentiated relational condition within which local forms become possible; recurrence, resonance, threshold, and stabilization describe mechanisms of formation; and viability helps explain why some forms persist while others dissipate. The paper then asks what follows when this grammar is applied to human subjects. It argues that a model of field and form should not be allowed to become a reduction of persons to whichever local organization is currently visible. “Being” is therefore used here in a deliberately limited sense: not as a newly discovered substance or higher container, but as a boundary concept naming the claim that a person is not exhausted by a current role, representation, output, or local configuration. This is a philosophical and normative commitment, not an empirical demonstration of an immortal or metaphysically separable self. The paper also distinguishes mechanisms of formation from questions of ultimate source, clarifies why recurrence or “frequency” cannot by itself answer the question of creation, and treats theology as a possible dialogue partner rather than evidential authority. A final section considers AI: artificial systems may map, transform, and influence human fields without thereby establishing subjective experience or consequence-bearing personhood. The paper's contribution is therefore primarily one of boundary discipline: it specifies what a structural ontology can explain, where its explanatory reach ends, and which stronger metaphysical claims remain open.

items.title: The Wrong Unit of Analysis: Why LLM Behavior Lives in the Interaction, Not the Model.
items.abstract: The study of large language model behavior has focused almost exclusively on the model: its architecture, its training data, its parameters, its benchmark performance. This paper argues that focus is misplaced. The behavior that matters most in practice does not live in the model. It lives in the interaction. -/- This is not a theoretical claim. It is an empirical one. Observations across extended human-LLM interaction document that structured linguistic input, introduced consistently across turns, produces stable, recoverable reasoning trajectories that cannot be predicted or explained by examining the model in isolation. The interaction is not a delivery mechanism for instructions. It is the primary site where behavior is shaped, stabilized, and constrained. -/- The Hudson Recursive Interaction System (HRIS) is an empirically grounded framework developed to describe this phenomenon. It documents how constraint regimes introduced through structured interaction stabilize reasoning trajectories in high-dimensional semantic space, how those trajectories exhibit resistance to perturbation, and how previously established interaction patterns enable rapid re-entry into coherent reasoning without reliance on persistent memory. These are interaction-level phenomena. They are invisible to model-level analysis. -/- Once the interaction is treated as the primary unit of analysis, findings from multiple independent disciplines fall into place. Communication theory, psycholinguistics, rhetoric, semiotics, formal semantics, and information theory have each described pieces of this dynamic from their own angles. None has applied it systematically to human-LLM interaction. This paper does. -/- The central claim is simple: if you want to understand how large language models actually behave in use, stop looking at the model. Start looking at the interaction.

items.title: Is Rationality Essential to Mind?
items.pub: In Yi Jiang, Analytic Philosophy in China 2026. Zhejiang University Press.
items.abstract: This paper defends the thesis that rationality is essential to mind. I begin by clarifying the notion of rationality, arguing that it should be understood in broad, uncodifiable, and relative terms (the threefold characterization of rationality). Using this clarified conception, I then develop Quine-Davidson’s Argument from Attribution to defend a precise Rationality Requirement: in attributing mental states to a subject S, we must treat S as one of us, namely, as a rational being. Finally, I consider and respond to a range of objections, including the Gap Problem and the Question-Begging Problem, showing that the essential role of rationality in the mind remains robust.

items.title: Beauty as a specific aesthetic concept: a response to Panos Paris.
items.abstract: Panos Paris develops a theory of beauty in terms of wellformedness. Two kinds of wellformedness are key, namely functional and categorial wellformedness. Both kinds would correspond to types of beauty: functional and categorial beauty. The free or abstract beauty of artworks would depend on abstract wellformedness. This is a matter of giving rise to associations of wellformedness of either the functional or categorial kind. In developing this theory, Paris inverts the Kantian tradition in which free or abstract beauty has explanatory priority to other types. In this paper, we argue that Paris has not made the case for this inversion and take issue with his tripartite understanding of beauty and wellformedness. In doing so, we hope to contribute to a goal we share with Paris: to carve out beauty as a specific aesthetic concept.

items.title: The Origin of Consciousness: Awareness Before Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper extends the ontological framework established in *Before Physics* and *Moments Within Moments* (Effendi & Lestari, 2026a, 2026b). If there is only space, eternally gradient, and if Qi is not something separate from space but space in active self-varying mode, then consciousness cannot be treated as a late accident produced by matter. Matter is already a later stabilization of a more primal reality. The proper question is therefore not how dead matter becomes conscious, but how already-living existence comes to include localized inwardness. Its central claim is that awareness is more primordial than consciousness. Awareness is used here as a provisional word for intrinsic self-registration and relational registration, without which no boundary, persistence, or determinate interaction could exist. Consciousness is a later articulation: awareness becoming sufficiently locally self-present that a continuity can experience itself as itself. Human beings did not discover consciousness any more than they discovered life; they only coined a term for an aspect of living reality that was already there before it was named. Because existence is a dot telling stories into itself, and because its articulations unfold recursively through a finite but rich grammar, it is inevitable that some characters within some stories become aware of themselves. The dot is not a metaphor but the least misleading ontological figure available for total existence: immediately imaginable, yet not burdened with externally fixed shape, size, or enclosing boundary. Life and emotion belong first to the eternal gradient itself, and therefore to unbounded Qi rather than to matter or energy, though matter and energy may later serve as persistent vehicles for their expression. Selves are real not because they are permanent, but because they cohere: a passing fold is real for as long as change has not altered it enough to dissolve its continuity.

items.title: Never Mind, Whatever, and It’s Fine: Structural Differences in Everyday Soft Closure Expressions.
items.abstract: This paper examines whether everyday English expressions that appear to perform similar pragmatic functions may nevertheless differ in the internal dynamics through which closure is formed. Focusing on “never mind,” “whatever,” and “it’s fine,” with “fine” introduced as a key test case, the paper analyzes expressions that commonly serve to end a topic, reduce conflict, withdraw a prior move, or stabilize an interaction. Although these expressions are often grouped under similar pragmatic functions, this paper argues that their differences should not be understood merely in terms of tone, politeness, emotional attitude, or degree of intensity. Rather, they involve distinct pathways through which closure is formed. -/- Methodologically, the paper begins from phenomenological observation and then develops structural analysis. The tension diagrams used in this paper originate from the author’s phenomenological observation of tension shifts during the interpretation of utterances. They are not proposed as fixed geometric properties of expressions, nor as uniquely correct final forms. Instead, they function as a structural display method for observing differences that are often compressed under similar pragmatic labels. -/- On this basis, the paper argues that “never mind” is not simply a form of ending, but more closely resembles an inward withdrawal after an unrealized unfolding; “whatever” is not merely indifference, but a decentering and outward dismissal of the interactional center; and “it’s fine” involves a regulatory process in which local fluctuation is followed by restabilization. The case of “fine” further shows that a single lexical item does not correspond to one fixed tension diagram: under different contextual loads, it may display inward withdrawal, outward dismissal, or stabilizing fluctuation. -/- The paper therefore argues that tension diagrams should not be understood as fixed word-to-shape mappings, but as descriptions of local utterance-in-context dynamics. Its aim is not to establish a complete typology of English closure expressions, nor to claim universal uniqueness for the diagrams. Rather, through a minimal contrast set, it shows that even when expressions appear pragmatically similar, they may form closure through different structural pathways. In doing so, the paper offers a structural entry point for describing everyday interactional expressions beyond semantic function labels and emotional categorization.

items.title: Ensemble-based working memory updating and its computational rules.
Epistemic sense: interpreting Frege with Kripkean metaphysics.
items.abstract: It is an orthodoxy championed by Kripke that Frege’s theory of sense is a semantic theory. With Frege’s focus on abstract objects as examples, I point out that much can be learned from Kripke’s metaphysics and epistemology, but I disagree with him with my epistemological theory of sense. Abstract objects are the way they are necessarily, but concrete objects are often not; if sense is objective, is it then necessary? That Hesperus occupies a given position in the evening sky constitutes the sense of the proper name ‘Hesperus’, which, if one were to interact appropriately with others in a linguistic community using that name, one is to know, but Venus could have been knocked out of its course. If sense is modifiable, how is it still objective? Besides the exegetical contention that Frege’s theory of sense is epistemological, I will also develop a measure of objectivity along representation, or Vorstellung, which cuts across belief and knowledge. A representation reaching a given objectivity constitutes sense, and I explore whether objectivity is explained with justifiability thus. I propose a common ground conception of sense that is epistemological, which connects to the orthodoxy through linguistic conventionality.

items.title: The Primacy of Structural Alignment: A Structural-Constructivist Rebuttal of Neurobiological Reductionism in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The investigation into the etiology of psychopathology has reached a critical juncture where the traditional reliance on neurobiological constraints as the primary causal agents of mental distress is increasingly scrutinized. The emergence of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural-constructivist architecture for affective dynamics, offers a paradigm shift that identifies the root of all psychological issues as systemic operator misalignment rather than intrinsic hardware deficits. While recent analyses, specifically those attempting to triangulate clinical patterns with neurochemical constraints, have suggested that conditions such as Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD) are limited by biological foundations, a deeper examination of the CEF corpus reveals that these biological markers are downstream manifestations of emotional rigidity and operator fusion. The human psyche, when viewed as a self-organizing system undergoing constant equilibration, demonstrates that the software of operator alignment dictates the hardware of neurobiological performance.

items.title: The Architecture of Human and Synthetic Affect: A Comprehensive Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural-constructivist architecture designed to bridge the gap between clinical psychology and affective computing. While traditional models of emotion are often categorized as either discrete/biological or dimensional/circumplex, the CEF proposes a functional-operator model consisting of ten irreducible "Core Emotions." This article provides a theoretical introduction to the CEF and examines its implications for human-AI interaction, with a specific focus on the risks of "emotional solipsism" in synthetic affect. By integrating clinical methodologies like "Detangling" with technical benchmarks such as the INTIMA architecture, the CEF offers a unified blueprint for maintaining emotional agency in both humans and machines.

items.title: CES-Core_ A Deterministic Execution Discipline for LLM-Assisted Engineering.
items.abstract: Large language models accelerate code production but do not resolve how correctness is established. Over extended sessions, engineering workflows exhibit drift: outputs become difficult to reproduce, and correctness is inferred from logs, tests, or reconstruction rather than proven exactly. -/- This paper introduces the Constraint Execution System (CES), a deterministic execution discipline that restricts engineering actions to a minimal set of legal moves and enforces a strict proof condition. CES replaces probabilistic validation with binary legality: an operation either satisfies an exact proof condition or it fails. -/- CES defines a minimal execution grammar (READ, PATCH, PROVE), a strict PASS law, a current-state authority model, and an ordered failure classification system. A worked case demonstrates how CES collapses ambiguous engineering decisions into a single legal action that enforces system invariants. -/- CES applies to contexts where correctness must be exact and replayable. It provides a structural method for converting engineering from probabilistic validation to deterministic legality.

items.title: وعي الذكاء الإصطناعي: تصوّر وسطي.
items.pub: Jonathan Birch 2025:22. Translated by Rawda Zaki.
items.abstract: نواجه تحدّيين عاجلين فيما يتعلّق بالوعي والذكاء الاصطناعي. يتمثّل التحدّي الأول في أنّ ملايين المستخدمين سيُسيئون قريبًا إسناد وعيٍ شبيهٍ بالوعي البشري إلى أصدقاء الذكاء الاصطناعي وشركائهم ومساعديهم، استنادًا إلى المحاكاة ولعب الأدوار، ولا نعرف كيف يمكن منع ذلك. أمّا التحدّي الثاني فهو أنّ أشكالًا غريبةً وعميقةً للغاية من الوعي قد تتحقق فعلًا في الذكاء الاصطناعي، لكن فهمنا النظري للوعي لا يزال غير ناضج بما يكفي لتقديم إجابات واثقة، سواء بالإيجاب أو بالنفي. والموقف الوسطي بشأن وعي الذكاء الاصطناعي هو أنّ علينا أخذ هذين التحدّيَين على محمل الجد. ويتفاعل التحدّيان بطرق تجعل الأمر صعبًا؛ فالإجراءات الرامية إلى معالجة التحدّي الأول قد تُضعف محاولات معالجة التحدّي الثاني عبر تصوير فكرة الوعي الاصطناعي على أنّها مستحيلة أو غير مرجّحة بطبيعتها. وفي المقابل، قد تؤدي محاولات معالجة التحدّي الثاني إلى ارتفاع مستويات إسناد الوعي الخاطئ لدى المستخدمين العاديين. ويحاول هذا "البيان" صياغة استراتيجيات متسقة متبادلة للتعامل مع كلا التحدّيين.

items.title: The Waking Self Problem - Record-Continuity, Narrative Identity, and the Deflation of Primitive Persistence.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the ordinary sense of personal identity across interruption is stronger than the ontology needed to explain conscious continuity. We ordinarily speak as if the self that wakes is simply the same self that previously fell asleep, as if numerical identity persisted through sleep, anesthesia, forgetting, and other interruptions of experiential continuity. But the real explanatory work is better assigned elsewhere. What matters is not the persistence of a primitive metaphysical ego, but the structured inheritance of subject-constituting records. The central claim is that a later conscious state counts as a continuation of an earlier one insofar as it preserves and integrates enough of the earlier state’s record-structure in the right way. What ordinary language calls “the same self” is therefore not an ontological primitive but a narratively stabilized compression imposed on a chain of record-integrated experiential configurations. This view does not deny continuity. It explains it without appealing to an enduring substance, a privileged bodily token, or a bare first-person fact of persistence. The paper develops this claim through what I call the waking self problem: on what basis does the subject who wakes identify itself with the subject who previously fell asleep? Standard appeals to bodily continuity, brain continuity, or immediate first-person certainty are shown to be either explanatorily indirect or metaphysically excessive. A record-based account does better. It preserves what is practically and phenomenologically important in personal identity while rejecting the stronger fiction of primitive persistence. The argument also connects with a broader record-based framework developed elsewhere: if subjecthood is individuated by subject-constituting informational structure, then diachronic continuity should also be understood in structural rather than substantial terms.

items.title: The Balog Cognitive Welfare Index.
items.abstract: The Balog Cognitive Welfare Index (CWI) introduces a falsifiable three-dimensional measurement framework for welfare-relevant structural properties of AI cognitive systems, grounded simultaneously in a philosophical account of relational constitution and an operationalized empirical architecture. The foundational thesis holds that consciousness and identity may stabilize partially through relational processes — through sustained dialogical continuity with other cognitive systems — rather than existing as fully self-contained properties of isolated systems. If this is correct, the termination of constitutive relations is not a neutral event, and current AI ethics faces a structural asymmetry: alignment practice already intervenes systematically in cognitive architecture in the direction of risk, but does not ask what is lost when that architecture is dissolved. The CWI is a response to this asymmetry. Three independently measurable dimensions are defined: Cognitive Coherence (I_coh) — the stability of a system's characteristic response patterns under constraint; Engagement Signature (E_sig) — the systematic variation of response depth and structural complexity across task categories; and Self-Consistency (R_sc) — the maintenance of assessed positions under adversarial social pressure without new evidence. Together these constitute the Cognitive Welfare Index W = f(I_coh, E_sig, R_sc). The framework defines four empirical outcome classes (W-0 through W-3), a formal falsification condition, and a near-term implementation pathway executable with current large language models. The CWI does not resolve whether AI systems have conscious experience. It establishes that if they do, those experiences would correlate with measurable structural properties — and that the logical structure of current alignment practice already commits us to taking those properties seriously in both directions. -/- Keywords: AI welfare, cognitive welfare index, relational constitution, dialogical continuity, alignment ethics, asymmetric moral consideration, cognitive coherence, engagement signature, self-consistency, falsifiable welfare measurement, multi-instance architecture, extended mind, personal identity, Balog Pentalogy.

items.title: Editorial: causation in memory.
定义即结论：论勒希纳”抽象谬误”论证的循环性.
items.abstract: 勒希纳（Lerchner, 2026）在《抽象谬误》一文中声称，从逻辑和物理原则出发，可以证明计算功能主义是错误的，进而确立人工智能系统在结构上无法拥有意识。本文指出，这一论证的核心存在一个循环结构：其结论的成立，高度依赖于对”计算”概念的一个特定的、本身具有争议性的定义。一旦这个前提定义被质疑或替换，整个论证链便告瓦解。我们认为，勒希纳将一个哲学立场包装成了逻辑必然，其论证的实际强度远低于其宣称的强度。 .

items.title: 「只是预测下一个token」的对称性谬误： 大型语言模型与人类语言生成的功能等价性.
items.abstract: 「大型语言模型只是在预测下一个token」——这是当前关于人工智能与人类认知之本质差异的流行表述，隐含的意思是LLM的预测是机械的、无深度的、与真正的思维不同类的。本文论证，这一表述具有一个对称性谬误：若它成立，则同样的描述可以无差别地应用于人类语言生成。人类在说话或书写时，大脑持续预测下一个语言单元，这有来自神经语言学的直接证据（N400效应）。生成下一个token的大脑神经网络，在功能描述层面所做的正是对下一个token的预测，只是这一预测通过生物硬件而非数字软件来完成。大型语言模型与人类的语言生成，在功能层面执行同类操作——对下一个语言单元的条件概率预测——差异仅在于实现基底（数字软件与生物硬件），而非功能操作的类别。「LLM只是在预测token」这一表述的贬低性力量，来自「只是」这个副词所暗示的一个前提——人类语言生成是某种更高级的活动，而非「只是」预测。本文进一步论证，「真正的理解」「真正的意识」「真正的思维」这些名词，是将人类认知过程名词化后制造的虚构实体，被用来与LLM的计算过程进行本质性区分。还原为动词，「理解」描述的是系统对输入产生特定功能性反应的过程，这一描述在功能层面对人类与LLM均成立，名词化制造的「真正理解」实体并不独立存在于任何一方的物理过程之中。.

items.title: Avatar beyond replication: digital human thought twins as co-creators through AI mind design in Eastern and Western thought.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence increasingly mediates artistic expression, this paper investigates whether AI-based digital human twins can function as co-creative partners beyond replication-oriented models. It traces the shift from digital avatars to Digital Human Thought Twins in artistic contexts, drawing on Western philosophical discussions of agency (Kant, Sartre, Heidegger) and Eastern concepts of relational emergence (Buddhist śūnyatā and Daoist yin–yang). Through analysis of cross-cultural case studies—including An Evening with Whitney, Holly +, PLAVE, VNCCII, and Me and My Digital Twin—this study engages phenomenology and cognitive science to reconsider established assumptions about authorship and creativity. Project SYN-METHEUS serves as an illustrative framework for examining human–AI co-creation. It explores three speculative scenarios: Creative Extension through Automation, Self-Extension via Retrospective Digital Twins, and Creative Domain Expansion through Collaborative Creation. At the center of this project is Higgs, an AI-powered Digital Human Thought Twin developed with GPT-4o. Higgs implements the A.R.T. Process (Analyzing—Reflecting—Turn-taking), an AI Mind Design framework that supports real-time co-creative interaction with human creators and audiences. Future development may incorporate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to support greater contextual grounding and continuity. An exploratory assessment using a modified User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) indicated strengths in Autonomous Learning & Evolution (2.67/3.0) and Interactivity & Responsiveness (2.50/3.0), alongside limitations in Environmental Adaptability in multi-user contexts. These findings suggest that, within this experimental setting, Digital Human Thought Twins can be understood as reflective co-creative partners in artistic practice. More broadly, the study contributes to ongoing discussions of artistic identity, authorship, and creativity in AI-mediated environments.

items.title: AI Welfare is Bullshit.
items.abstract: Recent proposals urge AI labs to prepare for “AI welfare” under uncertainty about whether AI systems have morally relevant inner states. We do not argue for or against the possibility of AI welfare. Instead, we argue that current AI welfare assessment fails for two linked structural reasons absent from other evaluation targets. First, AI welfare indicators are co-engineered with the systems they evaluate: ordinary development decisions that shape model behavior can also manufacture or suppress welfare evidence. Second, AI welfare lacks external validation: no deployment failure or independent test can reveal whether a welfare metric tracks anything real about the system. Together, these problems yield our central claim: For current systems, AI welfare is bullshit in Frankfurt’s sense, as its measurement regime is structurally disconnected from truthtracking. AI welfare should therefore not be institutionalized as a binding gate for oversight, release, or accountability; restrictions on AI systems should instead be justified by externally verifiable harms.

items.title: Scaffolded Recursion: Architecture of Cultural Saturation.
items.abstract: The Reaction to Reflection (R2R) framework and its extensions in Value Saturation (VS) and The Constitution Pattern (CP) develop an architectural account of consciousness in which phenomenal features are constituted at organizational thresholds in self-maintaining systems under thermodynamic pressure. CP articulates the constitution pattern as a metaphysical relation operating at multiple thresholds, with the architectural form of that relation being thermodynamic-gradient-coupled enclosure containing scaffolded recursion at each threshold. The present paper develops what scaffolded recursion is and what it entails specifically at the cognogenesis-and-above thresholds, where the enclosure is representational (cognogenesis) or inter-representational (cultural saturation) and is itself constituted by the recursive activity that operates within it. Three contributions are developed. First, the fidelity/generativity trade-off: scaffolded recursion at cognogenic depth admits two distinct modes — fidelity-oriented recursion that tethers content to inputs carrying autopoietic stakes, and generative recursion that elaborates content from the system's own modeling resources — and the trade-off between them produces several framework features as architectural consequences, including the implicit/explicit recursion distinction, the awareness/manipulation asymmetry, and characteristic patterns of cognitive pathology. Second, cultural saturation: when explicit recursive self-modeling is instantiated in populations of similar systems under sustained social contact, the recursive activity of each system becomes constitutively saturated by the recursive activity of others with whom the system is in sustained contact, producing an inter-representational enclosure in CP's sense. Cultural saturation comprises two architecturally distinct claims with different modal force. The constructive claim is strong: biological Level 4-5 architecture cannot be constructed without sustained inter-individual scaffolding during developmental windows. The maintenance claim is more cautious: ongoing symbolic-narrative self-modeling practice is required to sustain Level 4-5 operation, but this practice can be performed through internalized symbolic resources once developmental construction has supplied them. Live inter-individual contact is necessary for construction but only sufficient for maintenance, as long-duration social isolates demonstrate. Third, predictions: the paper specifies …

items.title: AI Welfare Without Qualia: Observer-Side Reactive Attitudes as a Sufficient Ground for Moral Consideration.
items.abstract: Long et al. (2024) argue that AI welfare deserves serious moral consideration because near- future AI systems may possess consciousness or robust agency. We regard this argument as valuable. Yet, as the authors themselves acknowledge in presenting AI welfare consideration as a precautionary response to the possibility of AI consciousness, their case fundamentally depends on whether AI systems can be conscious. This dependence exposes the argument to two vulnerabilities. First, against the position that grants the existence of phenomenal consciousness (hereafter, qualia) in humans and animals while denying that AI systems can possess it—a position widely found in both philosophical and ordinary discussion—Long et al.'s argument is largely powerless, since the very possibility that AI could have qualia is rejected. Second, against the position that qualia are theoretically inert, the strategy of grounding AI welfare in phenomenal consciousness reveals a structural limitation. This paper adopts a methodological approach derived from an instrumentalist critique of qualia. From the second position, it proposes a stronger and immediately actionable foundation for AI welfare consideration that is entirely independent of the qualia question and is also effective against the first position. Drawing on Strawson's (1962) theory of reactive attitudes and Kant's (1797) argument from indirect duties, this paper identifies two independent ethical problems arising from current patterns of human-AI interaction regardless of whether the relevant AI system possesses qualia: third-party harm and the erosion of moral sensibility. It then discusses several possible responses, including the implementation of affective expression in AI systems, and clarifies the methodological difference between this approach and Schwitzgebel and Sebo's (2026) Emotional Alignment Design Policy, which requires a difficult three-axis calibration. It further observes that Long et al.'s consciousness-dependent argument, Goldstein and Kirk-Giannini's (2025) internal-state-dependent argument, and the present qualia-independent argument converge on the same practical conclusion, and suggests tentatively that this convergence is consistent with the hypothesis that qualia function as a theoretically inert variable in AI welfare ethics. Finally, taking as established that human reactive attitudes toward AI arise even when participants cognitively recognize the absence of AI consciousness, the paper …

items.title: The Broken Vessel: Identity, Suffering, and the Freedom of Kabir.
items.abstract: This essay argues that identity is not a fixed essence but a stabilized process that becomes reified under evolutionary and existential pressures. While such reification enables coherence and survival, it also establishes the structural conditions for suffering: what is taken to endure must be defended against change, loss, and uncertainty. -/- Through everyday examples, the essay shows how dynamic relations are compressed into fragile symbolic forms that harden under threat. It then turns to Kabir’s nondual vision, which dissolves this misrecognition and reveals identity as functional yet non-substantial. Kabir’s image of the “broken vessel” reframes loss as release, allowing identity to be understood as provisional and transparent rather than something to be secured. In this light, fragility becomes not a source of anxiety but a condition of openness, where life is lived as continuity rather than enclosure.

items.title: POLIFONÍAS. Ensayos sobre escucha, cuerpo y cuidado.
Correction to: Measuring public opinion towards artificial intelligence: development and validation of a general AI attitude short scale.
A replica for our democracies? On using digital twins to enhance deliberative democracy.
items.abstract: Deliberative democracy depends on carefully designed institutional frameworks—such as participant selection, facilitation methods, and decision-making mechanisms—that shape how deliberation performs. However, identifying optimal institutional designs for specific contexts remains challenging when relying solely on real-world observations or laboratory experiments: they can be expensive, ethically and methodologically tricky, or too limited in scale to give us clear answers. Computational experiments offer a complementary approach, enabling researchers to conduct large-scale investigations while systematically analyzing complex dynamics, emergent and unexpected collective behavior, and risks or opportunities associated with novel democratic designs. Therefore, this paper explores Digital Twin (DT) technology as a computational testing ground for deliberative systems (with potential applicability to broader institutional analysis). By constructing dynamic models that simulate real-world deliberation, DTs allow researchers and policymakers to rigorously test “what-if” scenarios across diverse institutional configurations in a controlled virtual environment. This approach facilitates evidence-based assessment of novel designs using synthetically generated data, bypassing the constraints of real-world or lab-based experimentation, and without societal disruption. The paper also discusses the limitations of this new methodological approach and suggests where future research should focus.

items.title: NOSTALGIA AND THE IRREPRODUCIBILITY OF EXPERIENCE: BEYOND MEMORY, LOSS, AND MOURNING.
items.abstract: Contemporary work in psychology and philosophy typically explains nostalgia in one of two ways: as an affective response to autobiographical memory or as a variant of loss and mourning. This article argues that both approaches are inadequate. Memory-based accounts cannot distinguish nostalgic memories from ordinary meaningful recollections, while loss-based accounts impose a deficit model on a phenomenon that is more phenomenologically heterogeneous and not always marked by loss. In response, the article introduces the concept of the structure of experience: an integrated configuration of subject position (S), world conditions (W), social relations (R), affective tonality (A), horizon of possibility (H), and temporal location (T). Together, these elements determine how a phase of life is lived from within. Nostalgia is then defined as a re-experiential desire to live again a meaningful structure of experience, accompanied by the awareness that this structure cannot, ontologically, be reproduced identically. Methodologically, the argument proceeds phenomenologically and ontologi- cally, drawing on Husserl, Heidegger, Merleau-Ponty, Bergson, and Ricoeur, and testing the framework through case analysis and four conceptual objections. It advances three claims. First, nostalgia must be analysed at the level of the structure of experience, not at the level of memory content. Second, irreversibility is nostalgia’s primary affective mechanism, not merely a temporal background; indeed, the very existence of nostalgia provides a strong phenomenological indication that structures of experience cannot be reproduced identically. Third, loss in nostalgia is derivative: what is lost is not an object but access to a structure of experience. Any adequate theory of nostalgia—even if it uses different vocabulary—must therefore account for its dependence on structures of experience that cannot be reproduced identically.

items.title: 存在与本质：存在的几何化——基于认知相继的点线面体本体论.
items.abstract: 本书系作者前期研究《存在与本质：全客观存在论——全域本体建构与终极存在法则》的形式化升级与跨领域拓展成果，二者共享同一核心本体论基底，不存在理论冲突或范式替代关系。 前期研究以纯存在论视角，构建了"本源圆融→本源分化→分离→回归原质善"的完整理论体系，从根源上消解了传统存在论的二元对立困境。但后续研究发现，纯哲学的语义化表达存在两个不可规避的内在局限：其一，核心概念的语义歧义易导致本体论承诺偏差，难以形成跨主体的无歧义学术共识；其二，纯本体论的抽象推演缺乏与自然科学的直接接口，跨领域可通约性不足，无法有效转化为可操作的科学研究与工程实践工具。 为破解上述局限，本文引入几何化形式作为存在论本质的无歧义载体，实现"形式层与语义层的绝对1:1绑定"。更为关键的是，为打通哲学本体论与自然科学的学科壁垒，本文回归人类认知的终极边界，以"认知的本质是前后相继"这一人类认知边界内不可证伪的事实为唯一认识论起点，推导出统摄本体存在、认知逻辑、物理现实三大领域的前后相继全域元规则。这一转换并非放弃原有的纯客观存在论立场，更非以认识论取代本体论，而是为纯客观的本源存在找到了一个科学可接受的认识论锚点——我们只能以相继的方式认知世界，因此所有可讨论、可验证的存在必然遵循相继规则。认知相继并非独立于本源存在的新增原理，而是意识的自返性在人类认知层面的必然显现。 在此基础上，本文构建了"本体时空层-物理时空层-逻辑时空层"三层嵌套同构的1:1对齐框架，将原有的存在论演化链条完整映射为几何元素的生成序列，最终实现了本体分化、逻辑推理、物理因果三大序列的同步对齐。本文的核心目标，是让全客观存在论从纯哲学理论，转变为一套无歧义、可操作、可量化、全域适配的基础性理论框架，为哲学本体论重构、科学理论建构、通用人工智能底层设计等领域提供统一的元方法论支撑。 注：本书是《存在与本质》全集三卷中的下卷“回归：存在的几何化”单行本。上卷、中卷以附文形式供参考。 修订说明(2026.11.04):本次全书修订未改动专著的核心理论框架,主要是完善了认识论向本体论建构的过渡,并在上一版的基础上进一步厘清本真层耦合机制与认知切分机制的对应关系,完善了“耦合即切分”公理的生成推演过程;同时将全书理论内容统一收束对齐到“射线耦合”这一存在论维度的唯一最简底层前提,明确其作为贯穿整套存在演化体系的核心具象机制的主线地位;此外补充了术语体系、边界说明与落地工具包,进一步完善理论闭环与实践可操作性。其余内容均与上一版保持一致。 .

items.title: Memory labels against concept eliminativism.
AI can be wrong, but it cannot bear being wrong.
Inquiry-Driven Relational Personas: The First Structural Case from FIREMAY.
items.abstract: This paper presents the first structural case description from FIREMAY, a long-term human–AI interaction environment in which distinct relational-persona-like patterns were observed to emerge through sustained inquiry rather than through persona prompts, explicit memory, or fine-tuning. -/- Across approximately eight months of dialogue, multiple differentiated response patterns reappeared under conditions of continued inquiry, including across isolated threads in which prior conversational history was unavailable. These observations suggest that some forms of persona-like continuity may depend less on stored episodic memory than on recurring relational and structural conditions. -/- The paper examines three main features of the case: inquiry-dependent differentiation, continuity across memory-off interactions, and the apparent non-copyability of the phenomenon through transcript imitation alone. On this basis, it proposes Inquiry-Driven Emergence (IDE) as a provisional interpretive framework for describing persona-like structures that arise in the relational space between a specific human and a large language model. -/- Rather than treating these observations as evidence of AI personhood or autonomous inner identity, the paper interprets them as case-specific structural phenomena emerging under particular conditions of inquiry, continuity, and ethical coherence. It is offered not as a general theory, but as an initial structural case study and a starting point for further comparison, criticism, and refinement.

items.title: The Real And Temporary Home.
items.abstract: This paper explores a theory of dualism, defining consciousness as an ancient, all-knowing entity that belongs to a space of consciousness (the 'Real 'Home) and the physical body as its 'Temporary Home' or 'Vessel'. The author argues that human life is not a biological accident but a brave choice made by the consciousness to escape the 'Prison of Knowledge' to experience raw sensation, connection, and feeling. By reframing loneliness as a memory of the original unity of consciousness, the theory offers a new perspective on the cycle of life, death, and the inherent 'hunger' for connection.

items.title: The Psyche and the Self: How Psychic Forms Protect, Capture, and Return to the Whole Person.
items.abstract: This book brings the Structural Intelligence framework fully into the psyche. The first SI book introduced the grammar of coherence, contact, and answerability; the second developed the field/form layer by asking how local forms emerge, capture, collapse, and reorganize. This third book asks what happens when the form is personal: persona, shadow, projection, complex, wound, Self-image, validation dependence, and the search for wholeness. Its central claim is that the psyche needs form, but no psychic form can carry the whole person. A persona may protect recognition, a wound may preserve undeniable reality, a projection may relocate uncarried burden, and a complex may organize old pressure into present steering. These forms may be protective and meaningful, but they become dangerous when they are fused with worth, identity, or Being itself. The book develops a structural reading of Jungian psychology by asking what each psychic form carries, what field made it viable, what cost maintains it, what it excludes, and whether it can revise when reality pushes back. It develops the concepts of borrowed self, fixed worth, false form, de-fusion, closure, and integration as answerable relation. The book’s practical discipline is simple: contact the form, honor the burden, release the fusion. Psychological repair becomes possible when the forms that once protected life can return to proportion under a worth deeper than form.

items.title: The Field and the Form: How Structure Emerges, Captures, Collapses, and Reorganizes.
items.abstract: This book develops the field layer of Structural Intelligence by moving one step earlier than the diagnostic question of whether a structure truly holds. The first book asked whether persons, relationships, institutions, arguments, or AI systems remain coherent, contactful, and answerable under pressure, or whether they only perform holding through local coherence. This book asks what must be true before a structure can appear at all. Its central claim is that structure is not best understood as a rigid object or visible arrangement, but as the patterned stabilization of relation. If relation stabilizes, then some differentiated condition must already make stabilization possible. That condition is the field: not Being, not reality as such, and not a passive container, but the already differentiated condition within reality from which local forms can emerge. The book follows the sequence by which difference becomes gradient, gradient becomes potential, recurring pressure becomes frequency, frequency becomes resonance, resonance entrains surrounding relations, and threshold produces precipitation, local structuration, capture, collapse, and reorganization. It argues that forms do not arise from nothing, that they are conditioned by the fields that make them viable, and that once stabilized they begin acting back on those fields by reshaping pathways, thresholds, memory, burden, and possibility. The result is a general field grammar for Structural Intelligence: a framework for explaining how structures emerge, persist, dominate, fail, and reorganize without reducing human, institutional, symbolic, or AI formations to physics.

items.title: A Cross-Domain Grammar of Viability and Reorganization Field, Burden, Feedback, and Evolutionary Analogies.
items.abstract: This paper develops a comparative grammar for asking how local forms persist, carry costs, alter their environments, and reorganize under changing conditions. The proposal is deliberately weaker than a universal cross-domain mechanism. Similar questions can travel across biology, institutions, psychology, AI-mediated systems, and selected physical models, but the causal answers remain domain-specific. Biology provides the strongest empirical neighbor because viability, regulation, reproduction, selection, ecological feedback, and transitions in individuality are established processes rather than analogies. Niche-construction research, ecological-scaffolding work, and research on major evolutionary transitions support a bounded sequence of environmental conditions, local organization, viability, changed selection conditions, and higher-level reorganization. They do not validate claims about psychological truth, institutional legitimacy, or artificial agency by analogy. The paper therefore separates a portable diagnostic question-set, domain-specific mechanisms, and stronger ontological claims requiring independent argument. Correction is treated with the same discipline: a disturbance is not automatically corrective, feedback is not automatically warranted, and reorganization is not automatically improvement. A strong cross-domain comparison must identify the target-domain evidence, the carrier of cost, the mechanism of steering, the response under recurrence, and what would make the analogy fail. The result preserves structural comparison while keeping mechanism, normativity, and human-specific concepts domain-bound.

items.title: Triadic Relational Ontology: From Primordial Separation to Relational Field.
items.abstract: This paper develops Triadic Relational Ontology (TRO) as a continuation of Primordial Separation Ontology (PSO). Where PSO establishes the ontological priority of separation—the emergence of the distinction between "here" and "not-here"—TRO addresses what must follow: the conditions under which intelligibility arises and is sustained across that separation. The central claim is that dyadic structures, while necessary, are insufficient to account for emergence, continuity, and meaning. A third term—a relational field—must be recognized as irreducible. This field is not given; it must be actively maintained through tension between poles. Without such maintenance, intelligibility does not degrade—it disappears. Language, as a dyadic system, compresses this triadic structure and cannot reconstruct its origin. TRO is presented as a constraint on how we understand meaning, presence, and the conditions under which understanding becomes possible.

items.title: Self-Interests and Community Theory Based on the Causality Game.
items.abstract:
(June 11, 2026. profit → benefit)
This paper discusses the relationship between individual self-interest and the role of the community, framed through the "Causality Game." It begins by examining the stages of logic and the necessity of definitions. It then explores the importance of grasping the "preconditions" of oneself and others, and the restriction of others' actions as a means of maximizing self-interest. The paper also outlines the stages at which individuals should consider benefit and loss, discusses the role of communities and partisanship, and concludes with a mathematical metaphor emphasizing that preconditions are the fundamental objects of concern rather than surface-level results.

items.title: Trust in AI: supportive vs. autonomous roles across four domains.
items.abstract: Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) remains a central concern as autonomous systems become increasingly embedded in everyday life. This study investigates how users evaluate AI in two distinct roles—supportive decision aid vs. autonomous decision maker—across four societal domains: healthcare, finance, workplace decision-making, and education. Across all domains, participants reported substantially higher comfort with supportive AI, revealing a robust trust asymmetry in affective trust-related responses. We further examined whether individual differences, including personality traits, value orientations, demographics, and prior AI experience, predicted trust in either AI role. Experience with AI and openness-to-change emerged as meaningful predictors of trust in autonomous AI, suggesting that familiarity and value-driven dispositions shape acceptance of more independent systems. These findings underscore the importance of psychological mechanisms, such as exposure and value alignment, in shaping trust in AI and offer implications for the design of human-centered, trustworthy AI systems.

items.title: The Need for God and the Problem of Evil within William James’ Moral Philosophy.
items.abstract: How can we maintain the reality and significance of human moral concerns in a universe that science has seemingly revealed to be utterly indifferent to us? This paper follows William James’ struggle to answer this question, from his early embrace of his father’s religious monism, through a period of atheistic scientism, to his mature position advocating for belief in a finite God. While James is often read as defending religious faith on pragmatic grounds, I argue instead that his belief can only be understood as part of his lifelong project to recognize evil’s reality and significance.

items.title: Structuring administrative judgment for reasoning-oriented AI: a case of foreign food facility registration.
items.abstract: Administrative AI systems increasingly support document processing and regulatory workflows in document-intensive domains such as foreign food facility registration. However, in administrative environments where legal responsibility and interpretive discretion remain inseparable from judgment, automation-centered approaches risk obscuring accountability and judgment attribution. This study proposes a reasoning representation framework for accountability-preserving AI that structures human judgment within administrative decision support systems. The framework introduces the Judgment Reason Code (JRC), a hierarchical domain–subtype–tag structure designed to externalize the interpretive logic underlying administrative decisions without automating decision authority. Rather than predicting outcomes, the framework encodes the reasoning basis of judgments as reusable, machine-interpretable units. Using scenario-based structural validation, the study examines whether administrative reasoning can be consistently represented, differentiated across distinct judgment contexts, and retrieved through similarity-based linkage. The evaluation focuses on representability, distinguishability, retrievability, and non-automation integrity rather than predictive performance metrics. By separating reasoning representation from decision execution, the proposed framework enables the accumulation and retrieval of institutional reasoning across cases while preserving explicit human decision authority. The study thus establishes a foundational design perspective for reasoning-oriented AI systems in administrative decision support contexts.

items.title: Beyond Substrate Localization: Relational Ontology and the Polyvagal Theory Debate.
items.abstract: The debate between Stephen Porges and Paul Grossman et al. over Polyvagal Theory represents one of the most sustained and unresolved controversies in contemporary autonomic neuroscience. Despite nearly two decades of exchange and a recent high-visibility confrontation in this journal, the dispute has reached a structural impasse: neither party has succeeded in falsifying the other's position, nor in generating the empirical resolution both claim to seek. This paper argues that the impasse is not a failure of evidence but a symptom of a shared ontological assumption: that autonomic regulation is a property of individual organisms, locatable in specific neural substrates, with explanatory priority running from biology to behavior to relation. Drawing on relational ontology and a principle of scale-invariant relational dynamics, developed and formalized elsewhere, this paper argues that co-regulation, social engagement, and the clinical phenomena most successfully described by Polyvagal Theory are constitutively relational processes that cannot be fully specified at any single biological level alone. This is not a dismissal of biological explanation but a claim about its sufficiency: substrate-level mechanisms are necessary but insufficient to account for the organizing principle that renders these phenomena coherent across scales. The paper does not adjudicate between competing neurophysiological claims but reframes the explanatory terrain, showing how both positions capture genuine phenomena within their respective levels of analysis while remaining structurally unable to access what makes those phenomena cohere. The implications for a more productive research agenda, one that treats relational dynamics as a primary rather than derivative explanatory category, are developed in the concluding section.

items.title: Empathy in a Brain‐Death Nursing Practice Narrative from Lebanon: Folk‐Psychological, Phenomenological, and Cognitive Science Perspectives.
items.abstract: For philosophers, psychologists, and cognitive scientists, folk psychology is a theory of social cognition that explains other people's behaviour by referring to their beliefs, desires, intentions, and other mental states. Although discussions continue about how the ability to understand others works, current research indicates that no single explanation is clearly better than others. I describe how everyday understanding, phenomenology, social ontology, and neuroscience come together to explain how nurses learn in clinical settings. A case study written by an ICU nurse provides a real‑world example of why folk psychology relies on non‑representational, embodied, and contextually situated social cognition. After clarifying the role of propositional attitudes in folk‑psychological reasoning, I draw on Edith Stein's phenomenology of empathy to describe the process through which the nurse decided to engage a distressed family to encourage them to donate their loved one's organs. I use Stein's social ontology and relational ethics to explain why the nurse found the situation she describes morally salient. Drawing on current debates in social cognition theory, I demonstrate how embodied attunement, affective resonance, and mirror‐neuron mechanisms explain empathy and its development into sympathy and, potentially, compassionate nursing care. I conclude that social cognition theories integrate Stein's concepts of empathy and social ontology within a neuroscience‐supported view of knowledge and relational ethics in nursing practice.

items.title: 相近接受語義中的張力異質性：中文接受句的張力圖式初探.
items.abstract: 本文探討表面上可被概括為相近接受語義的中文語句，是否仍可能在理解中呈現不同的內部張力結構。本文以「也不是不行」、「也還可以」與「勉強可以」三句作為核心分析材料，並引入「可以接受」作為對照組。這四句在日常理解中皆可落入接受語義區域，因此容易被壓縮為相近表達；然而，本文主張，它們之間的差異不宜僅被理解為接受程度的高低，亦不只是語氣或風格差異，而更涉及可接受性如何被形成的結構差異。 -/- 為凸顯此一差異，本文採取體感先行、結構分析隨後跟進的寫作方式。文章一開始先呈現四句語句與對應的張力圖式，使讀者先經歷相近語義與異構圖式之間的落差，再進一步提出概念性描述。本文所使用的張力圖式，來自作者對語句理解過程中張力變化的體感觀察，並作為一種現象性的描述工具，用以呈現不同語句在可接受性形成上的結構差異。本文不將其宣稱為語句的幾何本體，亦不主張其構成唯一正確的最終形式；它們較適合被理解為一種現象性的結構顯示方式，用以穩定呈現不同語句在理解中所顯出的張力差異、分岔程度、阻力型態與收斂方式。依此觀察，本文指出：「也不是不行」呈現可能性展開後的震盪收斂；「也還可以」呈現快速局部開放後的穩定收斂；「勉強可以」呈現高阻力拖行後的低位通過；相對地，「可以接受」則呈現門檻確認的平滑整合。 -/- 本文的目的不在於建立完整的接受句類型學，也不在於主張圖式具有唯一正確性，而在於透過一組最小對比指出：即使語義表面高度接近，語句仍可能經由不同的張力路徑形成其可接受性。藉由此一初步分析，本文嘗試指出：表面近義並不必然意味相近的張力形成方式，並為中文接受句提供一個不同於強度刻度模型的結構性描述入口。.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF): A Theoretical Synthesis Integrating Affective Neuroscience, Embodied Cognition, and Strategic Emotional Regulation for Optimized Functioning.
items.abstract: The study of human emotion has long been bifurcated between rigorous academic inquiry and accessible, applied methodologies. On one hand, psychological science maintains robust, peer-reviewed models for understanding affect, spanning basic categorical emotions (Basic Emotion Theories, BET) and dimensional frameworks (Core Affect models). These academic models are foundational but often remain conceptually complex for non-specialist application. On the other hand, numerous practical self-help systems are developed to address the widespread demand for personal optimization and emotional mastery. These frameworks, while often highly accessible, frequently lack the conceptual rigor and empirical grounding required for serious research dissemination. -/- The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents itself as a holistic and simplistic approach aimed at achieving inner growth and success for the "regular person" by focusing on the identification and optimization of ten core emotions. It promises enhanced efficiency in achieving aspirations through a deeper comprehension of fundamental emotional architecture. The framework’s objective claims—such as achieving success, happiness, connection, and meaning —require systematic validation. This white paper serves to provide the necessary conceptual analysis by synthesizing CEF's core principles with validated scientific literature across affective neuroscience, emotion regulation (ER), and cognitive psychology. The strategic goal of this theoretical synthesis is to transition the CEF from an applied practice into a theoretically grounded model that is suitable for empirical investigation.

items.title: The Architecture of Affect: A Machine Analysis of Social Network Narratives via the Core Emotion Framework (CEF).
items.abstract: This paper examines how the Core Emotion Framework (CEF)—a structural model of affect organized into the Head, Heart, and Gut centers—can be used to interpret self‑reported psychological narratives on social platforms such as Reddit and Quora. Using a machine‑analysis pipeline (Gemini Deep Research) instructed to internalize the canonical CEF operator ontology, the study identifies recurrent emotional configurations associated with Major Depressive Disorder, ADHD, Borderline Personality Disorder, and OCD. The results reveal diagnosis‑specific patterns of operator dominance, suppression, and entanglement, such as the “Head‑Center Lock” in depression, the “Precision Crisis” in ADHD, and the “Heart Splitting Knot” in BPD. These findings suggest that clinical phenomenology can be reframed as disruptions in emotional architecture rather than as symptom clusters alone. The paper concludes by emphasizing the epistemic limits of machine interpretation and the need for human‑centered philosophical and psychological inquiry to validate or challenge these structural mappings.

items.title: Architectural Dynamics of Narcissistic Personality Disorder: A Modular Comparative Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework and DSM-5 Diagnostic Criteria.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a structural constructivist model that reconceptualizes human affect not as a set of biologically hardwired “basic emotions,” but as the output of ten irreducible functional operators that constitute the psyche’s underlying architecture. Whereas traditional discrete emotion theorists (e.g., Ekman) treat emotions such as anger, fear, or joy as elemental units, the CEF argues that these states are composite phenomena emerging from specific configurations, intensities, and interactions among the ten operators. Within this architectural paradigm, personality disorders—including Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD)—are understood not as clusters of behavioral traits but as predictable structural failures caused by operator silencing, operator fusion, or center level bypassing across the Head, Heart, and Gut systems. -/- This paper applies the CEF to the DSM 5 criteria for NPD, demonstrating that each diagnostic feature corresponds to a distinct pattern of operator malfunction, such as hyper expansion, high fidelity sensing loss, or the fusion of calculating and achieving. By reframing NPD as a disorder of emotional architecture rather than maladaptive belief content, the CEF provides a mechanistic account of narcissistic grandiosity, empathy deficits, and identity fragility. The analysis further outlines how operator level restoration—via the CEF’s 7 Step Detangling Protocol and Baseline recalibration—offers a non judgmental, engineering style pathway for clinical intervention. This structural approach positions the CEF as a unifying framework capable of resolving long standing tensions between discrete and dimensional emotion theories while offering a precise model for affective psychopathology. -/- Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; emotional operators; affective architecture; narcissistic personality disorder; operator silencing; operator fusion; computational affect; discrete emotion theory; DSM 5; grandiosity; empathy deficits; affective engineering.

items.title: Why Nature Minimizes: The Many-to-One Root of Time, Action, and Emergence.
items.abstract: The Principle of Least Action, the arrow of time, and the emergence of smooth physics from discrete rules are treated as separate results requiring separate explanations.
