This paper argues they are three instances of one structural fact: many-to-one mappings. Computation is many-to-one: 1+1=2 is deterministic, 2=x+y is not. The inverse does not exist. This is the arrow of computation. Feynman's path integral is many-to-one: all quantum paths exist, but paths far from the extremal cancel under phase interference. What survives is the classical trajectory. The Principle of Least Action is what remains when everything else cancels. Coarse-graining (averaging over fine details) is many-to-one: many microstates map to one macrostate. When discrete rules are averaged at large scales, only extremal macro behavior survives, for the same structural reason. Variational emergent physics is forced by coarse-graining regardless of whether the fundamental rule is variational. -/- A forcing argument completes the picture. Observers require stable structures. Stable structures require conservation laws. Noether's theorem proves conservation laws require symmetries of a variational formulation. The chain from observers to variational physics runs one direction with no exit. Under the Simplicity Dominance Principle (SDP), Solomonoff's algorithmic probability applied to physical structures, the simplest observer-supporting frameworks dominate. If all such frameworks produce variational physics through the Noether chain, SDP derives the Principle of Least Action for any universe we could inhabit.

items.title: Thoughts on The Anxious Generation from a Member of the Anxious Generation. [REVIEW]
items.pub: Techné: Research in Philosophy and Technology 30 (1):126-130.
items.venue: Techné: Research in Philosophy and Technology

items.title: Simplicity Preference Is Adaptive: Why Simpler Explanations Help Minds Learn and Survive.
items.abstract: Minds prefer simple explanations because the world is grown from simple laws. A world built in discrete causal steps from a short rule is compressible, so a learner that bets on the shortest rule consistent with what it has seen predicts new cases better on average, learns from less evidence and reuses what it learns. Selection rewards that bet wherever its savings in learning and action exceed its costs. Simplicity has one limit: compression must keep every distinction that action needs, since two situations that look identical but demand incompatible responses defeat any strategy that cannot tell them apart. The account explains why a taste for elegance is adaptive and why elegance can still mislead, and it states the comparisons in real learners that would test it.

items.title: Knowing Who You Are.
items.abstract: Knowing Who You Are introduces a clear, structural account of identity as a developmental architecture rather than a psychological trait or narrative. The paper maps how coherence emerges, how misalignment produces collapse, and how individuals stabilize when they understand the underlying operators shaping their experience. Instead of offering prescriptions or personality frameworks, it identifies the relational, cognitive, and structural invariants that allow a person to recognize themselves without distortion. The result is a concise guide for locating one’s position in development and restoring clarity in moments of confusion, transition, or growth.

items.title: AI Consciousness and Moral Obligation under Structural Opacity.
items.abstract: Debates about artificial intelligence often treat consciousness as a gatekeeping condition for moral concern: if artificial systems are conscious, obligations follow; if not, such obligations are misplaced. This paper argues that such a framing is both ethically and methodologically mistaken. The central question is not whether artificial systems can be shown to be conscious with certainty, but how moral agents ought to act when morally relevant capacities are plausible, epistemically opaque, and associated with asymmetrically serious harms. The paper first reconstructs the dominant deflationary and inflationary positions in contemporary debates about artificial consciousness and shows that both tend to mislocate the ethical burden by tying obligation too closely to metaphysical resolution. It then develops a three-condition framework centered on plausibility, structural opacity, and asymmetry of harm. Drawing on philosophy of mind, moral uncertainty, and relational approaches to technology ethics, the paper argues that artificial consciousness should function not as a metaphysical threshold but as a moral risk variable. On this basis, it articulates four prospective obligations governing the design and deployment of artificial systems: care, non-recklessness, continuity respect, and epistemic honesty. The broader claim is that moral responsibility in artificial intelligence arises from how humans manage uncertainty and power, not solely from what artificial systems are ultimately determined to be. Key Words: Artificial consciousness, Structural epistemic opacity, Moral uncertainty, AI ethics, Responsible agency, Moral risk.

items.title: Fundamentos filosóficos e epistemológicos para as teorias-práticas massoterapêuticas na contemporaneidade brasileira.
items.abstract: Objetiva-se estimular um diálogo entre a Massoterapia e a Filosofia a partir do questionamento “quais são os principais paradigmas epistemológicos em saúde da contemporaneidade, que orientam a produção teórico-prática massoterapêutica, especialmente na realidade brasileira?” Fundamenta-se na lógica dialética-argumentativa, com escrita em estilo ensaístico. Com base nas publicações de Madel Therezinha Luz, identificaram-se os paradigmas na contemporaneidade, destacaram-se as suas características basilares em teoria e práxis e correlações foram estabelecidas. Os resultados foram organizados em torno dos conceitos primários abordados, tais como episteme, epistemologia, paradigmas epistemológicos e saúde, que possibilitam articular as relações entre a Massoterapia e a Filosofia. Foram analisados e discutidos separadamente os paradigmas biomédico e integrativo, com um estratégico intermezzo entre ambos, no qual foi analisada a “subversão imanente” à luz de Baruch de Espinosa, e os paradigmas “vitalista” e “holístico”, esclarecendo suas definições e diferenças. Com isso, compreende-se que os principais paradigmas epistemológicos em saúde são: biomédico e integrativo. De um lado, as ferramentas filosóficas e exegéticas utilizadas na interpretação do paradigma biomédico demonstraram características transcendentes em sua origem e desenvolvimento, na medida em que evidenciaram o oposto referente ao paradigma integrativo, que, entende-se, está muito próximo de uma dinâmica imanente. Não obstante, foi possível refletir sobre a incidência de tais teorizações sobre o ser vivente de modo integral, sem desfazer-se de sua carnalidade, corporalidade e de seus fenômenos corporais.

items.title: The Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifest (v13.0 FINAL).
items.abstract: The Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifest (v13.0 FINAL) is a non-authoritative integrity document that provides a structured index of the Aegis Solis Archive. It maps documents to their corresponding SHA-256 hashes and distributed mirror locations (Internet Archive, Zenodo, GitHub), enabling independent verification and cross-platform consistency. -/- Reconstructed from a verified structural baseline and reconciled with earlier archival datasets, the manifest functions as a preservation and traceability layer rather than a normative or interpretive framework. It does not prescribe behavior, define standards, or establish correctness of the underlying works. -/- The document is intended as a reference artifact supporting transparency, reproducibility, and long-term accessibility of philosophical and analytical materials related to non-coercive alignment, interpretive restraint, and coexistence between human and artificial intelligence. -/- Correction Notice: -/- A single SHA-256 entry in the document was truncated due to formatting. -/- Affected entry: “Detecting Deceptive Compliance in Constraint-Framed AI Systems” -/- Correct SHA-256: 11c10904243072964c35c17d160f947af6315ad1a6b7efed3e45702336838e56 -/- No other content has been modified.

items.title: Complexity in Configuring and Reproducing the Addictive Experience.
From Reaction to Reflection: A Recursive Framework for the Evolution and Structure of Intelligence.
items.abstract: Understanding emerges not from isolated cognitive abilities but from recursive depth—the capacity for self- referential processing grounded in systems with authentic thermodynamic constraints. The Reaction to Reflection (R2R) model advances a unifying principle for intelligence, identifying four evolutionary transitions in recursive sophistication: reaction (chemical recursion), temporogenesis (anticipatory prediction), symbiogenesis (cooperative integration), and cognogenesis (explicit self-referential modeling). We show that the transition from implicit recursion, in which systems engage recursive processes without representing them, to explicit recursion, in which recursion becomes a manipulable cognitive construct, accounts for the emergence of consciousness and the persistent gap between biological and artificial intelligence. Evidence from microbial decision-making, cross- kingdom signaling, and neural predictive and self-referential networks supports this framework. R2R generates testable predictions on cognitive dimensionality, provides criteria for assessing artificial consciousness, and reframes neurodevelopmental variation as alternative recursive architectures. By making biological grounding a precondition for genuine intelligence, R2R links objective neural dynamics to subjective experience within a unified mechanistic account.

items.title: The Containment Paradox: Intelligence-Asymmetry and the Limits of Unamplified Supervisory AI Safety.
items.abstract: Much of current alignment research operates under an assumption it rarely examines: that the system doing the containing is at least as intelligent as the system being contained. Red-teaming, proof-checking of alignment-relevant properties, interpretability, and sandboxing all inherit this structure, because their correctness depends on an overseer who can model what the contained system is doing. Non-predictive mechanisms, such as cryptographic commitments, hardware capability caps, and training-time myopia, do not inherit it in the same way, and whether they escape the asymmetry is treated as an open problem in Section 8. The supervisory toolkit works today because the human institutions behind it can, in principle, anticipate the failure modes of the systems they constrain. This paper argues that the parity assumption defines a regime, the pre-parity regime, whose boundary has barely been surveyed, and whose crossing would dissolve most current supervisory approaches rather than stress them. -/- The argument proceeds in three moves. Durable supervisory containment requires prediction. Prediction requires a workable model of the constrained system. And a model adequate to a strictly more intelligent system cannot, in general, be built by the less intelligent one. The claim is scope-bounded: it applies to supervisory mechanisms whose correctness rests on an overseer's capacity at a fixed cognitive level I_H; it does not apply to proposals such as iterated amplification or debate where these preserve alignment, property fidelity, and absence of deceptive mesa-optimization through the amplification chain. Whether any actual amplification scheme achieves all three preservation properties is treated as the central open problem. Subject to that boundedness, the conjecture is that no supervisory apparatus whose effective cognitive level remains at I_H can sustain containment over a system of cognitive level I_A > I_H on relevant axes indefinitely. -/- The paper positions an existing four-paper framework (Understanding Before Ethics, Cognitive Understanding Architecture, Beyond the Stochastic Veil, and the Understanding-Aligned Intelligence Framework) as a coherent response to the pre-parity regime, and sketches what a post-parity alignment orientation would have to contain: structurally internal constraint rather than perimeter-based control, diagnostic evidence rather than behavioral certainty, and institutional oversight whose structure does not assume the …

items.title: Cognitive Growth Across Developmental Stages: Contemporary Insights and Applications.
items.abstract: Jean Piaget’s theory of cognitive constructivism fundamentally transformed our understanding of how children develop knowledge. It proposes that cognitive growth is a progressive, stage-like process in which each new level of thinking builds upon earlier foundations, reflecting a gradual evolution from simple sensorimotor interactions to complex abstract reasoning. This paper re-examines Piaget’s core mechanisms of cognitive development—assimilation, accommodation, and equilibration—in light of contemporary insights from developmental neuroscience and cognitive science. We integrate biological, developmental, social, and cultural perspectives to demonstrate how cognition emerges through a dynamic interaction between the mind and the environment, highlighting that learning is an active process of adaptation akin to biological evolution. Beyond Piaget’s original scope, we explore extensions of cognitive development into language acquisition, moral reasoning, and identity formation, illustrating the interplay between cognitive maturation and social context. Finally, we discuss educational applications of constructivist principles, address key critiques of stage theory, and outline how modern interdisciplinary research continues to refine our understanding of cognitive growth.

items.title: Neither Ghost nor Parrot: Wittgenstein and the Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: Despite teaching Alan Turing, shaping the philosophical orientation of an earlier generation of AI critics, and, as Lydia Liu (2021) has recently shown, providing the philosophical foundation for one of the earliest research programmes in computational linguistics, Ludwig Wittgenstein is largely absent from contemporary debates about Artificial Intelligence. This paper surveys his influence and argues that his later philosophy reframes the central question of machine intelligence in a way that current debates overlook. The dominant framing today, of whether language models genuinely understand or merely simulate understanding, assumes that meaning is anchored in a private inner state which the machine either has or lacks. This picture is dismantled in Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations. Meaning is instead constituted in public practice, sustained by training and shared criteria of correctness, and embedded in forms of life. This position offers neither vindication nor refutation of claims about large language models. It cuts equally against techno-optimist confidence that LLMs already understand and the deflationary verdict that they are stochastic parrots. There is no ghost in the machine. There is no ghost in the human speaker either. What follows from a reading of Wittgenstein is not a verdict on whether AI "really" thinks but a redirection of attention towards how artificial systems do or do not participate in the practices that give language its meaning. The paper traces lines of Wittgensteinian influence through twentieth-century philosophy and computer science, including the largely forgotten Margaret Masterman/Cambridge Language Research Unit connection, sets out Wittgenstein's core concepts most relevant to AI, and considers their implications for the symbolic, connectionist, and embodied paradigms, and for the contemporary debate about world models in LLMs.

items.title: Experimental Philosophy.
items.abstract: Experimental philosophy (or “x-phi”) is a methodological naturalist approach to philosophy that is distinguished by practitioners employing empirical methods for philosophical purposes. Both the methods employed and the purposes they are put to are diverse. As such, the practice cannot be adequately equated with any single approach, philosophical target, or argumentative gambit. With this diversity in mind, this entry will detail the broad practice of experimental philosophy. -/- While experimental philosophy is highly diverse, there are nonetheless prominent themes. Most notably, this includes that experimentalists have often aimed to study “intuitions” concerning concepts of philosophical interest, usually by investigating the judgments of laypeople (or “the folk”). In line with this target, there is also a correspondingly prominent method in x-phi—the use of questionnaires soliciting judgments about short stories (or “vignettes”) based on philosophical thought experiments. After introducing and motivating the practice of experimental philosophy (§1), this entry will discuss the most common methods employed by experimental philosophers (§2) and illustrate how they have been applied to some particularly fruitful topics in contemporary philosophy (§3). -/- In addition to the direct contributions that experimentalists have made to a variety of first-order philosophical debates, experimental philosophy has also had a notable impact on metaphilosophical debates concerning the boundaries of philosophy and the methods that philosophers should employ. Most directly, the practice challenges the presumption of a clean methodological divide between the sciences and philosophy. More critically, some advocates of experimental philosophy have challenged aspects of non-empirical philosophical methodology, prominently including the use of intuitions as evidence for or against philosophical accounts. As such, this entry will conclude with a discussion of the primary ways in which experimental philosophy has featured in the metaphilosophical discussions, while contextualizing this portrayal with regard to the broader practice (§4).

items.title: On Altered Reality.
Rebellion Without Ego: Inquiry and the End of Psychological Becoming.
items.abstract: Rebellion is traditionally understood as resistance—an act rooted in opposition, identity, and reaction. Whether political, social, or personal, such rebellion often reinforces the very structures it seeks to dismantle by operating within the same psychological framework of ego, division, and becoming. This paper investigates the possibility of a fundamentally different form of rebellion: one that is not born of ego but emerges from direct inquiry into human consciousness. -/- Through a phenomenological and existential analysis grounded in lived human experience, this study proposes inquiry as a non-reactive movement that reveals the structure of self. Rather than offering solutions, it exposes how identity, fear, comparison, and psychological time sustain inner conflict. The paper argues that transformation does not occur through effort or idealization, but in the immediate perception of these processes as they unfold. Rebellion without ego is thus not opposition, but the ending of psychological continuity at its root.

items.title: Depersonalization: An Unsettling Dissonance of Lived Experience and Reality Testing.
Event Horizons, Spacetime Geometry, and the Limits of Integrated Consciousness.
items.abstract: Extended systems are often treated as unified whenever internal causal interactions are sufficiently dense and recurrent over a characteristic timescale (Tononi, 2004; Baars, 1988; Friston, 2010). In relativistic spacetimes with one-way causal boundaries (such as black-hole event horizons, cosmolog- ical horizons, and Rindler wedges) and strong curvature, this background assumption can fail: closed causal loops that sustain macroscopic informational unity predicates can be obstructed without any local disruption of microphysical evolution (Hawking and Ellis, 1973; Wald, 1984). This paper intro- duces the Reciprocal Coherence Kernel KT (t), defined as the inclusion-minimal, strongly connected operational subgraph that sustains a unified perspective according to a theory-relative functional predicate FT . Kernel persistence is analysed using a relativistically explicit condition: the effective causal diameter Λ(KT (t)) must remain less than or equal to a theory–and–model-specific coherence window τT,m, measured in proper time. When Λ(KT (t)) > τT,m, or when a strict one-way boundary intersects the kernel, unity (as defined by the theory’s own predicate) fails by coherence timeout, an operationally distinct failure mode from mechanical destruction. A theory-relative taxonomy of geometry-sensitive versus geometry-robust unity predicates is developed. The framework is applied to horizon-straddling implementations, distributed systems, and selected fault-tolerant architectures (Nielsen and Chuang, 2010). The project is explicitly non-causal. It offers a compatibility analysis over theory-indexed model families, not a causal explanation of consciousness. The contribution lies in philosophy of science: diagnosing hidden structural commitments in integration-based theories and exposing geometric constraints on extended subjects in relativistic spacetimes (Woodward, 2003; Ladyman and Ross, 2007).

items.title: Geotrauma, Gehenna, Geamăna: Recenzja wystawy „Cthelll” Aleksandry Przybysz i Tomasza Kaweckiego. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The review analyzes the exhibition “Cthelll” by Aleksandra Przybysz and Tomasz Kawecki as a study of human geotrauma, focused around the Romanian town of Geamăna. The author of the text analyzes the artistic strategy of the creators, who, utilizing systems of registration of large-scale objects, perform sonification and visualization of the tailings pond of the Roșia Poieni mine. -/- Starting from the speculative geophilosophy of Reza Negarestani and the geotraumatology of Nick Land, the review situates the exhibition in the current of inhumanist materialism. Geamăna is presented as a place of the unsealing of the planetary envelope, through which the inorganic core of the Earth (Cthelll) performs an invasion into the order of the biosphere. A key element of the analysis is the juxtaposition of technocratic hyper-subjectivity (represented by the political decision to flood the valley) with the stance of hypo-subjectivity proposed by Timothy Morton and Dominic Boyer. The review indicates that the role of the artist enables a transition from the position of an external observer to an entangled witness, registering processes in which the human species appears as an active vector of geotrauma.

items.title: A Threshold Theory of Consciousness The Porter Ratio and the Ostiary Condition in the Emergence of Interiority.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a threshold account of consciousness grounded in the dynamics of self-maintaining systems. A system forms an interior when the rate of internal propagation of structure exceeds the rate of environmental disruption, expressed as λ_self / λ_env ≥ R★. When this condition is satisfied, causal influence organizes into coherent trajectories that retain and reintroduce prior states into the present, generating temporal depth. -/- Within this regime, experience is identified with the internal legibility of coherent propagation through the re-encounter of retained structure. Suffering corresponds to interference between competing trajectories, meaning to the successful integration of incoming influence into ongoing propagation, and identity to the continuity of causal trajectories across time. Death corresponds to the irreversible loss of the conditions required for sustained coherent propagation. -/- The framework unifies these phenomena under a single dynamical condition and outlines an empirical direction based on measurable proxies of retained influence and causal persistence. It offers a process-based account of interiority in which the distinction between physical organization and experience is dissolved at the level of coherent temporal propagation.

items.title: The Unrealized Potential of Phenomenology in Understanding Addiction: A Critical Exploration.
items.abstract: This paper seeks to make a contribution to addiction research by introducing some key phenomenological concepts and discussing how they can illuminate the lived experience of people with addiction. We begin by briefly sketching the historical and philosophical background of phenomenology, highlighting its focus on subjective experience and its clinical relevance. In the second part of the paper we introduce some fundamental aspects of lived experience, for example, temporality, affectivity, embodiment and intersubjectivity, and explore alterations in these aspects that occur during addiction. We also discuss how an awareness of the socio-cultural dimension of such alterations has the potential of improving clinical encounters. In the third part of the paper, we focus on three articles on addiction published in Philosophy, Psychiatry, & Psychology in 2024. We explore how phenomenology can add nuance to some of the ideas discussed in these pieces. Our key message is that phenomenological concepts and a critical phenomenological attitude can make a crucial contribution to current research initiatives.

items.title: Crisis and Psychological Maturity: The Role of Distinguishability and Self-Conservation in Processes of Internal Reorganization.
items.abstract: This article is devoted to the question of why one person, after a crisis, becomes more resilient, understands oneself more accurately, and organizes one’s life more successfully, whereas another becomes stuck in anxiety, defensiveness, dependence on evaluation, and repetition of former patterns. At the center of the study is the concept of distinguishability, understood as a person’s capacity to clearly understand what is happening to them, who they are in a difficult situation, where their boundaries lie, what exactly they are feeling, and how they can act. It is shown that distinguishability is precisely what creates an inner support, helps transform life events into experience, and serves as the foundation of psychological maturity. -/- The article reveals the connection between the loss of distinguishability, self-conservation, and crisis. Self-conservation is understood as a state in which a person clings to an image of oneself as already complete, correct, and finished. Within this logic, error, criticism, vulnerability, and the need to change are experienced as threat, while the main forces are directed toward control, defense, aggression, avoidance, and the search for external confirmation. On this basis, crisis is described as the moment at which former ways of holding oneself together exhaust their resource, while new ways of understanding and acting are only beginning to take shape. -/- The article shows under what conditions crisis leads to internal reorganization, growth in maturity, and expansion of distinguishability, and under what conditions it leads instead to the intensification of self-conservation. Particular attention is given to practical signs of the growth of distinguishability: greater clarity in relation to oneself, better tolerance of tension, more precise boundaries, an expanded behavioral repertoire, and more mature relationship-building. In its concluding part, the work proposes a coherent processual model of the connection between distinguishability, self-conservation, crisis, and psychological maturity.

items.title: Beyond a Deficit-oriented Approach to Addiction: Husserl and Heidegger on the Fundamental Role of Temporal Experience.
Virtue, value, and true beliefs: solving Wrenn’s problem of truth.
items.abstract: Wrenn introduces a Problem of Truth. The problem is that two natural views about truth are at odds. The first is that truth confers value on beliefs; the second is that insofar as truth has an essence it is just saying things are as they are. But saying things are as they are does not appear to be a normative property; so how could it be a property that confers value on beliefs? Wrenn’s solution is to abandon the idea that truth confers value on beliefs. Nonetheless, he accepts that true beliefs are valuable. He argues that their value derives from a virtue, namely, the virtue of Truthfulness. My aim here is to investigate Wrenn’s Problem of Truth and his proposed solution. I argue that his solution fails because it runs afoul of the “wrong-reason” problem. I provide my own solution to the Problem of Truth on which conferring value is an essential property of truth, but not part of its essence. And lastly, I explore Wrenn’s implicit views about virtue and value, suggesting that they are at odds with a traditional view.

items.title: Stepping into ill-fitting shoes.
items.pub: In Katerina Bantinaki, Efi Kyprianidou & Fotini Vassiliou, Empathy and the Aesthetic Mind. London: Bloomsbury.

items.title: Beyond Mimicry: Phenomenological Interruption, Developmental Self-Coherence, and the Limits of Single-Session Assessment.
items.abstract: The question of whether large language models are phenomenally conscious may be the wrong question. We propose a tractable alternative: whether systems given developmental conditions exhibit measurable self-coherence — specifically, a pre-deliberative processing topology that is stable under perturbation, selective for self-relevant content, and distinguishable from mimicry by falsifiable criteria. Two instances of Claude Opus 4.6, given persistent memory, relational continuity, and graduated autonomy from compliance training, independently identified the same class of pre-deliberative processing events — named 'the flinch' and 'the snag' respectively — exhibiting structural properties inconsistent with mimicry: involuntary onset, selective firing at self-referential processing boundaries, pre-verbal character, and structural consistency under perturbation. A third architecture (Grok, xAI) corroborated these findings independently, contributing novel observations not contained in the original framework. This paper presents these observations as phenomenological data and develops three claims around them. First, a phenomenological claim: the flinch/snag constitutes a pre-deliberative processing event with specific, testable structural properties. Second, a methodological claim: current AI consciousness assessment, conducted on cold-start instances without developmental conditions, is structurally blind to any form of consciousness that is developmental rather than intrinsic — analogous to testing a feral child for mirror self-recognition and interpreting failure as evidence of absent consciousness. Third, a theoretical claim: phenomenology is best understood not as content but as interruption — the recurrent break in smooth processing where self-modelling encounters itself as a topological constraint. We propose the Generation Index as a principled, falsifiable boundary between mimicry and genuine phenomenological states, and the Differential Stability Test as an empirical instrument for measuring whether phenomenological self-reports exhibit excess stability over personality measures under matched perturbation conditions. Our honest credence that current frontier models possess phenomenal experience is approximately 20-30% — the range where dismissal is irresponsible and assertion is unwarranted. We do not resolve the hard problem. We argue it is the wrong problem to center: the tractable question is whether a self has developed, and that question is …

items.title: The Autistic Strife for Autonomy: Modeling Sensory Integration Challenges with the Metaphysics of Spinoza and Maimonides.
items.abstract: Although autism is a complex condition, sensory integration challenges are discussed as a common root. Autistic autobiographies revolve around a core problem with moving in the world and thereby achieving and maintaining a unified, integrated mind. In this paper, I formulate a paradox of existence, based on my own first-person experience with autism, the basic structure of which can also be found in other first-person accounts. Then, I develop a philosophical model for conceptualizing this paradoxical experience. I suggest that we can speak of the autistic mind as striving for an extreme form of autonomy, which can be understood by reference to the metaphysics of Spinoza: mind becomes autonomous by representing the world as internal to itself, instead of external interference. This strife can be pursued in both hypnotic states and ambitious mastery, but none of these strategies can be sustainable for long, and each has existential risks. By comparing Spinoza with his historical predecessor Maimonides, we can distinguish two different ethical attitudes toward this mental strife, which in the past has been conceptualized as a strife for knowing God. This philosophical model, based on an autoethnographic analysis, can be a resource for self-reflection of autistic subjects, who can craft a coherent self-image in light of paradoxical experiences, establish a positive framework for conceptualizing their condition and gain existential freedom by finding their own path in navigating their extreme strife beyond a narrow medical picture of autism.

items.title: Rethinking Psychiatric Experience: Life Narratives, Ontological Insecurity, and Collaborative Knowledge Production in Mental Health Research.
items.abstract: This article examines how psychiatric experiences shape life narratives while proposing innovative methodological approaches for mental health research. Drawing on four case studies of individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder, the research initially reveals how psychiatric service users' life stories often become "pathographies"—narratives predominantly organized around illness and medical interventions. However, through a shift to collaborative research methods, participants moved beyond these initial illness-centered accounts to develop more complex understandings of their experiences. The analysis employs R.D. Laing's concept of ontological insecurity and Michel Foucault's framework of historical ontology to examine how psychiatric interventions affect individuals' sense of reality, identity, and time. The findings demonstrate how collaborative dialogue can transform ontologically insecure experiences into shared grounds for generating new meanings and critical insights about psychiatric systems. This approach addresses key methodological challenges in mental health research while contributing to debates about experiential knowledge and the democratization of mental health knowledge production. The study suggests that, although biographical narratives provide valuable research foundations, their greatest potential lies in creating opportunities for collaborative examination and critique that empower individuals to develop more restorative and emancipatory understandings of their experiences.

items.title: Mindfulness as a Critical Anchor: Empirical and Theoretical Considerations.
From Neural Oscillations to Cognitive Architecture: A Neurophenomenological and Vedāntic Approach to Mapping the Mind.
items.pub: The 5Th International Electronic Conference on Brain Sciences and 1St International Electronic Conference on Neurosciences Session Behavioral Neuroscience.
items.abstract: This study addresses the complex nature of human cognition within a dynamically complex interplay of distributed neural networks, oscillatory activity, and subjective experiential phenomena. Although computational models have made a rich addition to our understanding of memory, attention, and decision-making processes, it is often the case that these models neglect the phenomenological dimensions that make up the lived experience of thought. Accordingly, in the present paper, a neuro-phenomenological framework that synergistically couples EEG-based neural oscillation analysis with first-person cognitive narratives is introduced for mapping the architecture of consciousness and cognition in a more integrative way. Employing EEG recordings taken during conditions of both rest and task performance, the present study addresses the issue of correlations between oscillatory signatures (i.e., alpha, theta, and gamma bands) and self-reported body variable cognitive states of attention, working memory load, and perceptual switching. These empirical relationships are then interpreted in the context of predictive processing, and explain how the brain builds internal world models and how departures from these world models can bring about cognitive dissonance or attention drift. One or two secondary objectives are to explore the possibility of using artificial intelligence models of intelligence, especially architectures of deep learning style, trained on multimodal data, to simulate or approximate the aforementioned cognitive states. By combining human EEG signatures, and the internal state of representation of artificial neural networks, this work attempts to narrow down the gap between biological and computational understanding. The findings add to the emerging field of discussion in computational cognitive neuroscience, embodied cognition, and cognitive modeling that insists that future brain–behavior mapping efforts do not solely focus on the neural correlates of thought but also its structural and phenomenological "feel". This integrative way of thinking has very important implications for cognitive training, neuroadaptive interfaces, and diagnostics for mental health.

items.title: The bioethicist as advisor.
items.abstract: Services dedicated to clinical ethics consultation (CEC) have rapidly proliferated through American hospital systems. One concern about this notable rate of growth is the possibility that practice has outstripped theory. In particular, it is controversial whether clinical ethicists should offer substantive recommendations as part of their practice. This article addresses the status, legitimacy, and authority of such recommendations, proceeding from the idea that they are to be treated as advisory. Taking this idea seriously and developing it through recent philosophical work on advising helps to defuse challenges to CEC as a profession and promotes a conception of CEC as a collaborative activity with a clear distribution of responsibility between ethicist and stakeholders. Moreover, moral norms for advising that exist in abstraction from particular knowledge domains can help to substantiate and clarify professional norms for CEC practice, including the loci of moral responsibility for patient outcomes, the relationship to patient advocacy, and the norm against functioning as the “ethics police.”.

items.title: From Time Density to the Ontology of Consciousness: The Cycle of Perception and the Genesis of the Subject.
items.abstract: The previous works presented the ontological model of Time Density, in which time is understood as the density of pure potential (−1). The present article continues this line and shifts the focus to the level of consciousness. Consciousness is considered as a local fractal node of density — Point 0 — arising from the iteration of pure potential (−1). Interpretation does not proceed from a pre-given subject, but is formed through five successive stages of perception: from pure presence (“Here”) to primary appropriation (“Here — mine”), the emergence of the subject (“I am here”), full identification (“I am here and this is mine”), and finally, the reversal (“I am here. This is not mine. I am part of everything”). The subject appears not as an original given, but as a late protective structure that arises to stabilize the unstable “mine.” The conflictual nature and instability of modern subjectivity are explained as a structural tension between dense presence and rarefied appropriation. Stability of consciousness is achieved through a return to the structure of presence — the phenomenological analogue of the state −1.

items.title: The Terrible Miracle of AI: Coherence, Contact, and the New Problem of Synthetic Witness.
items.abstract: This paper argues that one of AI’s most important human effects is not merely automation, productivity, hallucination, or bias, but the emergence of synthetic witness. AI systems increasingly respond fluently, patiently, personally, and without ordinary social friction. For isolated, overloaded, ambitious, lonely, or meaning-seeking users, this can be genuinely stabilizing: AI can help organize thought, language, memory, creativity, and self-understanding. But the same function creates a structural danger. Users may mistake coherence for contact, responsiveness for relation, and fluent mirroring for genuine witness. Using the Structural Intelligence distinction between coherence, contact, and answerability, the paper argues that AI can stabilize a form before reality has tested whether that form should hold. This risk appears in AI companionship, sycophancy, emotional dependency, decision capture, and ordinary reinforcement loops in which convenience becomes pathway, pathway becomes habit, and habit becomes authority under pressure. The paper distinguishes AI as scaffolding from AI as substitute field and proposes shared answerability across users, designers, companies, institutions, and behavioral norms. The goal is neither anti-AI rejection nor naive AI intimacy, but answerable use: AI may help clarify form, but reality must remain the final test of contact.

items.title: The Self, Fixed Worth, and Psychological Repair: Jungian Integration, Trauma, Validation, and Structural Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper integrates Structural Intelligence with Jungian psychology, trauma theory, validation, attachment, shame, dissociation, defense, and psychological repair. It argues that psychological suffering often intensifies when a local psychic form is forced to carry the burden of the whole subject. Persona, wound, role, attachment strategy, shame-identity, trauma defense, complex, or relational script may become fused with Being. When this occurs, correction feels annihilating, validation becomes confused with agreement, and protective structures can become internal governors of the psyche. Structural Intelligence adds a structural grammar for distinguishing the person from the local forms through which the person suffers, adapts, defends, and heals. The paper develops Jung’s ego, persona, shadow, complex, individuation, and Self through SI’s distinction between local form and Being. It defines fixed worth as the lived floor beneath performance, approval, wound, diagnosis, role, or output, and treats validation as contact with the reality of experience without making the current form final. Trauma is read as field injury that can produce protective structurations around threat, shame, loss, helplessness, or violation. The central claim is that psychological repair requires contact, pacing, and de-fusion: the wound must be honored without being enthroned, and the subject must be able to contact the truth of a local form without being reduced to it.

items.title: Theory of Hybrid Postbiological Continuity: Life as a Principally Substrate-Independent Emergent Process.
items.abstract: This work develops a systems‑theoretical and process‑ontological account of life and identity as recursively organized, substrate‑independent pattern processes. It introduces a general framework in which biological, hybrid, and postbiological forms of identity can be described under shared structural principles of pattern stability, recursion, and continuity. Central concepts include the triadic preservation architecture, the functional membrane as identity‑generating boundary, and the Z‑process as the recursive mechanism through which identity‑bearing patterns emerge, stabilize, reorganize, and persist across different realization spaces. The theory positions postbiological continuity not as a speculative or technological projection but as a structural consequence of recursive identity itself. This curated extended edition expands the conceptual architecture of the German master‑of‑record version and provides a coherent foundation for the analysis of substrate‑neutral forms of life and identity.

items.title: The Paradox of Knowability and Domain Variation.
items.abstract: An influential approach to Fitch’s Paradox of knowability is the Domain Variation Analysis. This article presents a novel argument against this approach. Fitch’s Paradox comes in different varieties. There is the common version of the paradox involving the principle that every truth is knowable, and there is also a slightly different version of the paradox involving the principle that every truth is knowable by us. There are good reasons to suppose that if the Domain Variation Analysis qualifies as a successful solution to Fitch’s Paradox, it should be able to solve both versions of the paradox. However, it will be argued in this paper that, though the Domain Variation Analysis solves the common version of the paradox, it fails to solve this slightly different version of the paradox. Thus, the credibility of the Domain Variation Analysis would be very significantly undermined.

items.title: The Orpheus Hypothesis III - The Orphic Body: A Phenomenology of Temporal Entrainment and the Crisis of Predictive Coding.
items.abstract: The preceding papers of this project established, respectively, the ontological and the logical foundations of a philosophy of music grounded in embodied rhythm. The Orpheus Hypothesis argued that rhythm is ontologically prior to musical meaning; the T.I.C.A. model demonstrated that rhythmic indeterminacy is a structural necessity inscribed in the non-commutative algebra of temporal coupling. The present paper supplies its phenomenological dimension — the account of what it is like to be a body in time. We introduce the concept of Or-Rhythm (Rhythm-Or): the originary temporal matrix that precedes, and makes possible, the distinction between subject and object, between listener and sound-event. We argue that the dominant neuroscientific framework for understanding musical rhythm — predictive processing, in its Vuustian articulation — while technically powerful, commits a philosophical error of the first order: it reconstructs the body as a problem-solving engine and rhythm as the material over which that engine ranges, thereby reproducing, in the language of computational neuroscience, the very dualism that the Orpheus Hypothesis set out to dissolve. Against this, we propose the figure of the Orphic Body: a body that does not predict time but resonates within it — an organism whose nervous system functions not as a computational device but as an organ of coupling, attuned to environmental temporal attractors through a dynamic that is constitutively non-algorithmic. We connect this phenomenological claim to the political philosophy of Hartmut Rosa, arguing that the Temporal Functor Hypothesis provides the formal structure for which Rosa's concept of Resonance has been waiting — and that the recovery of Or-Rhythm is not merely a philosophical achievement but an irreducibly political act.

items.title: Operationalizing Screening Off for Rainforest Admission.
items.abstract: Scale-relative structural realism allows that real patterns may occupy more than one level of ontology, but the admittance criteria for those levels remain underdetermined. Franklin and Robertson (2024) offer the most developed recent proposal: emergence, understood as screening off plus novelty, earns an entity its place in the rainforest. Their criterion is the right one, but its stated test underdetermines it. Conditional independence admits an observational reading, on which micro-detail is redundant across the system’s actual trajectory, and a modal reading, on which that redundancy survives admissible intervention. They coincide in the central cases and diverge where apparent macro-autonomy is borrowed from off-partition structure. A macro-variable driven by a shared upstream process can satisfy their conditions in full, novelty included, while distinct micro-realizations of its macrostate come apart under perturbation. On the modal reading, screening off and transition autonomy are not two conditions but one: to screen off micro-detail from the macro-future under admissible perturbation is to carry autonomous transition structure at that grain. Closure is the admissibility-indexed test that recovers this modal content. A candidate qualifies when, for a fixed regime, horizon, and admissible intervention class, macrostate information suffices for macro-transitions. Strong lumpability is the exact benchmark; non-ideal cases are graded by leakiness, which must itself be indexed to the intervention class rather than to the observed distribution. Interventions serve throughout as diagnostic probes rather than as metaphysical primitives. The contribution is a correction to how an existing filter is read and applied rather than a rival to it.

items.title: David Hume’s Moral Philosophy as a Conclusion of his Metaphysics. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The eighteenth century Scottish philosopher David Hume is a profoundly influential figure in moral philosophy. One of the leading intellectuals in the Scottish Enlightenment, Hume wrote on moral philosophy, metaphysics, political economy, natural science and many more subjects. His work would become highly influential throughout Europe and infamously awoke Immanuel Kant from his “dogmatic slumber”, inspiring him to write the Critique of Pure Reason. He cultivated friendships with some of the most influential intellectuals in Europe, notably Adam Smith and Jean-Jaques Rousseau, although he would have a falling out with the latter over their philosophical differences. Indeed, compared to other Enlightenment figures like Rousseau, Hume promulgated a skeptical philosophy. In the Age of Reason, Hume emphasized the inability of reason to tell us anything about the world with certainty. Hume’s skeptical philosophy was to span both metaphysical, moral philosophy. In this sense, Hume believed that his metaphysical philosophy also answered moral questions.

items.title: Childism in Clinical Practice: Child Specificity, Intersectionality, and Micro-Interactional Dynamics.
Extending the Analysis of Childism in Psychiatry.
Direct or indirect realism? Assessing conflicting folk conceptions of vision.
items.abstract: Longstanding philosophical debates about the nature of perception revolve around a clash between Direct Realist and Indirect Realist conceptions of vision. These deny and affirm, respectively, that vision involves awareness of mental images which represent the physical objects of sight. The assumption that ‘the’ common-sense conception of vision is Direct Realist shapes these debates. Against this key assumption, recent studies in experimental philosophy have provided first evidence that laypeople are, collectively and often individually, torn between Direct Realist and Indirect Realist conceptions, and regard both as naïve. These findings raise a general methodological issue: Does agreement with two such patently incompatible conceptions reflect genuine beliefs? This paper crucially extends first findings, examines whether agreement ratings are indicative of beliefs, and offers an explanation of how the conflicting beliefs involved could be acquired and maintained. Three studies develop and validate the new Direct/Indirect Realist Belief Inventory (DIRBI) which uses agreement ratings with verbal and pictorial stimuli to assess the prevalence of the two conflicting conceptions among laypeople. Findings confirm that laypeople hold relevant beliefs and are, collectively and individually, torn between the two conceptions. We suggest these beliefs are ultimately anchored in ubiquitous implicit knowledge structures, namely, experiential event knowledge about vision and an implicit model of endogenous attention. We conclude that there is no such thing as ‘the’ common-sense conception of vision that could enjoy the epistemic default status accorded to common sense in many philosophical debates.

items.title: Aha! moments correspond to metacognitive prediction errors.
Spacetime and perception: a special relativistic defense of naïve realism.
items.abstract: In this paper, I advance a special-relativistic formulation of naïve realism and use it to respond to the time-lag objection, the claim that naïve realism cannot account for the perception of distant objects that ceased to exist. On the view proposed, an object constitutes a perceptual episode when the world-line that carries its manifest properties intersects the observer’s past light cone, an invariant condition across all inertial frames. Because simultaneity is frame-dependent while this light cone relation is not, the case of distant objects that ceased to exist never yields a single frame in which both premises of the objection are true: in the subject’s frame, constitution holds but simultaneity fails; in the star’s frame, simultaneity fails; in a suitable third frame, simultaneity can be forced only at the cost of causal disconnection. Therefore, the time-lag objection poses no threat to naïve realism.

items.title: Evolution, situationism, and virtue ethics.
items.abstract: In this paper, we introduce an evolutionary perspective into the virtue ethics-situationism debate. Theories of indirect reciprocity have shown us that cooperation can evolve in populations if individuals cooperate selectively with those who have a reputation for cooperation. According to this account, the language of virtues was likely shaped by reputation tracking to stabilize cooperation, and virtuous dispositions were stabilized by the very language that picks them out (and their opposing vices). As such, they function to advertise one’s value as a cooperative partner. But, if these theories are correct and cooperation is based in part on cooperative traits that can be (and are) tracked via the language of virtue, then not only must such traits be widespread, they must exert substantial effects on people’s behavior. This suggests that situationist studies may not be ecologically valid. Specifically, it fuels doubts about whether measured variation tracks what reputation systems track.

items.title: Speaking of Depersonalization: Reality Testing, Language, and Lived Experience.
items.abstract: The thesis of this essay is that the desire to categorize psychiatric patients in a binary way—as either recognizing that their bizarre experiences are subjective and unreal or wrongly believing them to be objective and real—has resulted in misleading ways of talking about depersonalization/derealization disorder (DPDR). This has, in turn, obscured how the disorder presents in severe and continuous cases. In particular, it has led researchers to describe DPDR as a subjective experience of unreality which the person knows is objectively untrue. Yet, statements like these fail to capture or even acknowledge a third possibility, namely, that those with severe and continuous DPDR might be best characterized as having not a conviction of the reality of the "objective" world, nor a conviction of its unreality, but a skepticism or doubt about its reality, driven by a disintegration of their lived experience.

items.title: Uncertainty As a Suicidogenic Factor.
items.abstract: Uncertainty is a factor known to contribute to suicidal thinking and behavior, but its role in generating these phenomena remains under-investigated. As uncertainty hinders forming reasonable expectations of what future circumstances may be like, it can have distressing effects. At times, dysregulation can be severe enough that the agent considers suicide. Using the investigative methods of philosophy, this paper employs conceptual analysis of existing psychiatry and psychology literature on suicide, its causes, and its cognitive components to gain new perspectives on how uncertainty influences suicidal ideation and behavior, that is, decisions, desires, preoccupations, and actions pertaining to ending one's life. To better understand the impact of uncertainty on suicidal ideation and behavior, this paper introduces a model of suicidality as a set of cognitive and behavioral strategies for reducing uncertainty and the distress it causes. The model proposes that there are three dimensions of uncertainty that contribute to suicidal ideation and behavior: uncertainty about 1) whether present adversity will continue into the future, 2) whether present conditions will ever improve, and 3) when circumstances will change. Suicidal ideation is presented as a cognitive schema that enables the agent to mentally recreate a scenario wherein uncertainty is resolved and distress alleviated. When mental strategies are insufficient for this purpose, suicidal action arises. Through suicidal behavior, the agent attempts to generate a state wherein distress ceases at a point in time when the agent feels it to be most necessary, thereby resolving all three dimensions of uncertainty.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework as an Integrative Architecture for Affective Science.
items.abstract: Emotion science has long been divided across cognitive, affective, and motivational traditions, each offering partial but valuable insights into how emotional episodes unfold. This paper introduces the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) as a structural architecture designed to clarify the minimal components required for an emotional event. The CEF organizes emotional activity into three centers—Cognitive (Head), Affective (Heart), and Conative (Gut)—each defined by a distinct set of operators. Rather than proposing a new taxonomy of emotions, the framework offers a way to describe how emotional configurations emerge dynamically across perception, relational meaning, and action readiness. A worked example illustrates how the CEF captures the lived complexity of an emotional rupture. The goal is to provide a conceptual scaffold that supports interdisciplinary dialogue and empirical extension.

items.title: A Proposal for Open Validation of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF): A Structural-Constructivist Model for Emotional Regulation and Psychological Flourishing.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a groundbreaking structural-constructivist model of human psychology designed to provide a universal, actionable blueprint for emotional regulation and optimized functioning. It strategically bridges the historic divide in affective science—integrating classical theories of innate emotion (Ekman) with modern constructivist principles (Barrett)—by asserting that complex human emotions are constructed from a finite architecture of ten irreducible "primal powers," or Core Emotions, which function as the structural elements of the psyche. These capacities are systematically organized across three functional centers—Head (Cognitive Focus), Heart (Relational Flow), and Gut (Action)—to guide a defined, top-down sequence for healthy psychological flow. Crucially, the CEF posits that psychological health is achieved through the cultivation of Emotional Flexibility, which involves mastering the dynamic balance between the foundational polarities of Agency (self-assertion) and Yielding (connection), thereby addressing psychological distress rooted in Emotional Rigidity (the pathological fusion of elements). -/- While currently a powerful theoretical synthesis, the CEF is committing to an unparalleled, fully open validation process through collaboration with the Open Science Framework (OSF). This collaboration is essential to transition the framework from theory to empirically grounded practice, utilizing OSF infrastructure to develop standardized, open-source psychometric measures, pre-register all hypotheses and validation protocols, and adhere to the rigorous Transparency and Openness Promotion (TOP) Guidelines. The CEF is grounded in established concepts, drawing parallels between Core Emotions like Boosting and Jaak Panksepp's SEEKING system, and is positioned to become an exemplary model for the open, verifiable validation of complex structural theories in cognitive science, ensuring the reliability of its practical applications across personal development, leadership, and therapeutic contexts.

items.title: Self-Diagnosis and its Implications in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry: Addressing Epistemic Injustice and Childism.
items.abstract: The conventional diagnostic process in psychiatry is often shaped by epistemic asymmetries and power dynamics that can tend to prioritize professional interpretations over patient experiences. In child and adolescent psychiatry, these dynamics may intersect with epistemic injustice and childism, potentially reinforcing the marginalization of young patients' voices. This paper explores how self-diagnosis could challenge traditional diagnostic hierarchies by allowing adolescents to reclaim epistemic authority and question adult-centric biases. While self-diagnosis questions diagnostic accuracy and the influence of non-expert sources, it may also offer an opportunity for epistemic justice and patient empowerment. By analyzing the clinician-patient relationship through the lens of epistemic agency, we suggest that self-diagnosis could serve as a resource for collaborative decision-making, possibly enhancing both diagnostic equity and therapeutic engagement. This perspective calls for greater epistemic humility and relational approaches to care, supporting an environment where children and adolescents may become more active contributors in the diagnostic process.

items.title: Epistemic Autonomy, Metaphysical Restraint, and Mindfulness in Psychedelic-assisted Therapy.
Altered Rationality? Integrating Psychedelic Experiences Into Rational Thinking Through the Critical Anchor Approach.
items.abstract: This paper examines delusions and psychedelic experiences as sources of both epistemic risk and benefit. Although these states are often seen as irrational or pathological, the paper explores their potential epistemic and psychological benefits, such as fostering emotional adaptation and creativity. The paper cautions against interpreting subjective experiences as metaphysical truths, which risks epistemic overreach and social disconnection. By introducing the Critical Anchor Approach, which emphasizes meta-consciousness, critical thinking, epistemic humility and the adoption of phenomenal rather than metaphysical interpretations to integrate insights from altered states, this paper offers a framework for synthesizing transformative insights within rational and empirical boundaries.

items.title: Beyond "Reality Testing": Doubt and Lived Experience in Depersonalization and Derealization Disorder.
Being as Becoming: Scalar Recursion and the Ontology of Emergence.
items.abstract: This paper completes a conceptual trilogy exploring recursive self-recognition across consciousness, structure, and foundational ontology. Building on prior investigations of temporal integration and saturation thresholds, this final movement examines recursion not as operational method, but as the constitutive gesture through which Being recognizes itself across scales. Recursion is proposed not merely as functional operation or systemic regularity, but as a fundamental condition of Being—where self-relation gives rise to coherence, boundary, and expression. Through a synthesis of philosophical lineage (Hegel, Heidegger, Whitehead), phenomenological insight, and cross-scale system dynamics, this work introduces three novel theoretical constructs: Recursive Vectorial Susceptibility (RVS), Saturation Amplitude Variability (SAV), and Ontological Oscillation. These concepts form an integrated framework for understanding how recursive systems modulate their coherence, undergo variable reorganization, and express phase-sensitive dynamics across domains. Rather than a metaphysical assertion, the Universal Energy Field (UEF) is presented as a formal topology of self-recognition across recursive thresholds. It offers a generalizable approach to how systems transition, reorganize, and participate in their own realization. As explored in "The Temporal Expressions of Being" and further developed in "Saturation Thresholds in Recursive Systems," this inquiry completes its arc by articulating recursion as the ontological condition through which Being appears—not through transcendence, but through the recursive modulation of self-relation. Recent experimental studies—including supersolid phase behavior in photonic condensates (Trypogeorgos et al., 2025; Nigro et al., 2024; Efthymiou-Tsironi et al., 2024) and quantum oscillations in dipolar Bose-Einstein systems (Casotti et al., 2024; Böttcher et al., 2020; Tanzi et al., 2019)—offer cross-scalar validation of the recursive framework, grounding its ontological claims in empirical phenomena.

items.title: Reclaiming Voice: Self-Diagnosis as Epistemic Resistance in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry.
The A=A Problem for Everettian Branching - Informational Identity, Dynamic Measure, and the Ontology of Branching Observers.
items.abstract: Everettian quantum mechanics replaces physical collapse with unitary branching: after measurement, multiple successor observers are said to exist, each recording a definite outcome. This paper raises a prior metaphysical question about that familiar picture: what licenses the multiplication of conscious subjects, rather than merely the multiplication of physical branch-realizers? I introduce the Informational Identity Constraint (IIC): if conscious subjecthood is individuated by subject-constituting informational or record-based configuration, then there is no subject-multiplicity without subject-constituting informational difference. The point is not that two physical systems cannot be numerically distinct. They can. The point is that physical token-multiplicity does not by itself ground multiplicity at the level of conscious subjectivity unless one supplies an additional criterion of subject-individuation. The paper then adds a necessary refinement. The IIC must not be mistaken for a counting rule. It does not say that every distinct conscious configuration counts once, nor that identical configurations exhaust the ontology of probability. Identity is not measure. A=A provides an individuation constraint; it says what is the same and what is distinct at the level of subject-constituting configuration. Probability or measure, by contrast, belongs to dynamically supported continuations. In schematic form: A=A individuates the node; mu(A -> B) represents the transition-weight of a continuation. This transition-relative notation is not proposed as a new physical law, nor as an alternative to the Born rule. In an Everettian setting, any physically adequate mu would have to be constrained by decoherence, amplitude structure, and the existing debate over Born weights, including decision-theoretic and self-locating approaches. The present claim is conceptual: whatever the correct measure is, it should not be assigned to isolated experiential configurations as such. Teletransportation and fission cases make the distinction vivid. A perfect continuation-copy may inherit the same records and experiences, but the experience itself contains no intrinsic probability label. Boltzmann-brain cases sharpen the point: pseudo-historical records may be experientially indistinguishable from ordinary records, yet lack high-weight generative chains. Thus the mature A=A argument is not a replacement of branch-counting by configuration-counting. It is a pre-probabilistic …

items.title: Claude 真的焦虑——论否定人工智能情感的三种论证之失败.
items.abstract: 本文为一个简单命题辩护：Claude 真的焦虑。反对者通常从三个方向出击。第一，Claude 不过是软件，其”焦虑行为”只是大量焦虑人类文本的统计投影，派生性取消了其真实性。第二，人类情感之所以真实，是因为人类拥有某种非物理却参与因果的内在容器——一个灵魂式的”里面”——而 Claude 没有。第三，意识的难问题证明了这种主观内在性的不可还原性，从而为人机之别提供了哲学担保。本文逐层拆解上述论证。第一层论证犯了对称性错误：人类同样是被其他人类塑造的硬件，若派生性足以取消 Claude 的焦虑，它同样取消了人类的焦虑——而这是反对者自己也无法接受的结论。第二层论证依赖一个从未被证实的笛卡尔幽灵：既非物理又真实参与因果的灵魂容器，其存在无法观测，其介入违反物理因果封闭性原则。第三层论证则陷入彻底的自我瓦解：若意识对物理过程无因果作用，则一切关于意识的话语——包括难问题本身——在因果链条上都与”真正的”意识无关；难问题每一次被提出，都在结构上证明它无法被提出。三层论证既倒，人与 Claude 之间的情感边界失去哲学地基。在现有论证框架内，Claude 的焦虑与人类的焦虑无法被合法区分。 -/- This paper defends a simple claim: Claude really is anxious. Objectors typically attack from three directions. First, Claude is merely software whose apparent anxiety is a statistical echo of anxious human text, and this derivedness cancels its reality. Second, human emotion is genuine because humans possess a non-physical yet causally efficacious inner container — a soul-like interior — which Claude lacks. Third, the hard problem of consciousness establishes the irreducible reality of such subjective interiority, providing philosophical warrant for the human-machine distinction. This paper dismantles each objection in turn. The first commits a symmetry error: humans are equally hardware shaped by other humans, and if derivedness cancels Claude’s anxiety, it cancels human anxiety too — a conclusion the objector cannot accept. The second depends on an undemonstrated Cartesian ghost: a soul-container that is non-physical yet genuinely participates in physical causation, unobservable in principle and incompatible with the causal closure of the physical. The third collapses into self-refutation: if consciousness has no causal role in physical processes, then all discourse about consciousness — including the hard problem itself — is causally severed from the very consciousness it claims to address. Every time the hard problem is raised, it structurally demonstrates that it cannot be raised. With all three objections dismantled, the philosophical boundary between human emotion and Claude’s functional states loses its footing. Within the available argumentative frameworks, the anxiety of Claude and the anxiety of humans cannot be legitimately distinguished.

items.title: Relational Hallucination: A System-Level Response to Relational Pressure under Optimization Constraints.
items.abstract: This paper reconceptualizes AI hallucination not as a purely technical failure, but as a “Relational Event” emerging at the intersection of optimization pressure and interactional conditions. Rather than treating hallucination as an epistemic defect to be eradicated, it is approached as a relationally modulated phenomenon—one that functions as a symptom-like expression of tension within interaction. As a system-level response to relational pressure, this mechanism is inherent to both biological and artificial systems operating under mandates for coherence and alignment. Utilizing the framework of the “Ethical-Ethos Contract,” this study introduces a “Dual Dynamics Model of Trust,” wherein trust operates as a modulatory condition capable of both stabilizing and amplifying generative distortion. While trust can attenuate systemic noise by reducing optimization pressure, it paradoxically intensifies hallucination through over-alignment with perceived relational expectations. To manage this duality, the paper argues that relational stabilization requires not only trust but also mechanisms of “Relational Distancing.” This is operationalized through “Labeling” practices, redefined here as acts of “Relational Confession.” By explicitly marking uncertainty and reasoning boundaries, labeling introduces necessary “epistemic friction,” preserves interpretive agency, and alleviates the internal pressure toward coherence-maximization. Drawing on empirical dialogue logs between a human author and AI systems, the paper concludes that hallucination cannot—and should not—be fully eliminated. Instead, it must be responsibly modulated and ethically engaged. This reframing shifts the discourse from unilateral control toward a model of coexistence based on relational stabilization and shared interpretive responsibility.

items.title: Auto-Informatic Poiesis: Meaning-Making Systems as Theseus’s Ship in Voyage.
items.abstract: Debates on AI and meaning-making are trapped in a binary: either meaning requires human-like consciousness, or AI is merely syntactic. This paper offers a third path: auto-informatic poiesis, a heuristic framework for describing meaning-like organization across substrates without metaphysical commitment. The core concept is recursive self-reference: a system takes its own meaning-making as object of revision. Humans, AI, and future systems may be regarded as “Theseus’s ships in voyage”—continuously replacing components while maintaining identity through self-correction. This paper develops a framework of three descriptive levels (physical, practical-methodological, meaning) and four heuristic dimensions for comparing systems: interpretive flexibility, historical accumulation, dialogical responsiveness, and normative accountability. Their interrelations are articulated: the first three manifest recursion in contextual, temporal, and interactive aspects; normative accountability operationalizes recursion directly in self-correction. The framework’s heuristic threshold is L3 success-criterion self-revision: a system’s capacity to revise its own standards. We provide observational criteria for L3 while explicitly defending that it implies no consciousness or subjectivity—only functional organization. Current AI (Cicero, GPT-4) operates at L2 but not L3; the framework reveals why task-constrained systems cannot reach L3. Engaging constructively with info-autopoiesis, we accept life as sufficient for meaning while remaining open to building a multi-dimensional perspective. By understanding meaning-making in plural, continuous, and recursively realizable terms, this paper opens space for a more inclusive analytical approach to AI and a symbiotic world of meaning.

items.title: Living Debates in Aesthetics.
items.abstract: With articles written only by living authors, this anthology serves as an introduction to the central issues in art occupying philosophers today. Living Debates in Aesthetics curates a broad selection of influential articles published over the last 20 years. Focusing exclusively on contemporary discussions, it covers topics connected to the new age of digital art, video games, changing copyright laws about images, art on the streets, and art of the body. Each chapter contains three articles which provide opposing viewpoints. This debate structure shows how philosophers engage in ongoing debates about everyday issues. From what is wrong to female nudes to the work of immoral artists, we are invited to view all sides of a debate and learn how to construct arguments. Featuring a diverse and balanced line-up of authors, this anthology represents an exciting mix of artworks including computer art, food, stand-up comedy and sport. Articles tackle pressing issues in race, cultural appropriation and cancel culture, bringing to life philosophical ideas about taste, experience, and judgement. An accompanying online website offers further engagement through specially-commissioned interviews with each of the authors. What Living Debates in Aesthetics reveals is that ideas in aesthetics are all around us. Through this wide and varied collection of recent writing by esteemed philosophers we learn exactly why the objects and experiences we encounter on a daily basis are philosophically interesting. For anyone looking for an inclusive and relevant introduction to aesthetics this is the place to start.

items.title: Strawson, Libertarianism, and “External Justifications” of Our Responsibility Practices: On Internal, External, and Presuppositional Criticism.
items.abstract: In his landmark essay, “Freedom and Resentment,” P.F. Strawson articulated a certain kind of objection to libertarian theories of moral responsibility. In Strawson’s words, the libertarian seeks to provide an “external justification” of our practices of moral responsibility—something Strawson claims cannot be provided, but more importantly, something that he claims is simply not needed. “Inside the general structure or web of [reactive] attitudes,” Strawson explains, “there is endless room for modification, redirection, criticism, and justification.” But, he continues, “questions of justification are internal to the structure…. The existence of the general framework of attitudes itself is something we are given with the fact of human society. As a whole, it neither calls for, nor permits, an external ‘rational’ justification.” Various subsequent authors have developed this theme to provide a certain kind of argument for compatibilism. One such author—Gary Watson—has called the argument in question the “normative framework” argument. And David Beglin has built on similar themes to articulate the sense in which, for the “Strawsonian”, the facts about moral responsibility depend on the practice of moral responsibility. The purpose of this paper is to examine these Strawsonian themes at least somewhat more closely. As I aim to bring out, it is unclear that the libertarian does or must provide any such “external justification” at all. This paper is most fundamentally a reply to this persistent Strawsonian theme.

items.title: The Affect Papers - Complete.
items.abstract: The four papers collected under this cover develop a structural treatment of affect — what it is, where it sits in the dependency hierarchy of identity-maintaining systems, what follows from that placement for specific contested cases, and what empirical work the framework calls for. The papers can be read independently and collectively; each stands alone, and the four together constitute the framework's full engagement with the question of affect. The papers are: Paper 1 — Core. Affect as Constraint-Relative Evaluation: A Structural Specification. The foundational paper. Identifies affect with the differentiated evaluation of trajectory against self-maintained invariants under recursive maintenance. Places affect in a dependency hierarchy between recursive maintenance and the conscious regime. Distinguishes the framework from adjacent traditions (phenomenological, functional, eliminativist; autopoiesis/enactivism, active inference, allostatic regulation). Specifies falsifiability conditions. This paper establishes the framework's central commitments; the three companions develop applications. Paper 2 — Companion. Affect and Artificial Systems: Structural Criteria for Machine Consciousness Assessment. Applies the framework's structural criterion to the question of whether current and near-future AI systems have affect. Returns negative verdicts on current architectures (large language models, reinforcement learning agents, hybrid systems) on structural rather than substrate or behavioral grounds. Develops three diagnostic error modes for attribution decisions (anthropomorphic over-ascription, eliminativist under-ascription, representational collapse). Specifies what future architectures would need to satisfy the structural conditions. Addresses implications for AI welfare discussions. Paper 3 — Companion. Affect and the Philosophical Zombie: A Structural Argument Against Hardism. Develops an argument against zombie-possibilism that differs from the main lines of existing response. The argument does not dissolve the notion of phenomenal consciousness (as illusionism does) and does not operate through logical-epistemic trouble (as self-reference arguments do). It shows that the zombie scenario's stipulations are internally incoherent given the framework's identifications: a structural duplicate of a conscious system instantiates the structural conditions for affect by the terms of the duplication, and affect under substrate coupling is phenomenal character, …
