Conscious processing varies following individual perception of environmental stimuli at larger measurable scales, such as language differences shaping cognitive processing or informational exposure informing beliefs, environmental interpretation must trigger variation, with genetics providing the ability. Existing …

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 7).
items.abstract: Sartre believes that the subject’s choice produces pain, and that this pain arises because the subject must be responsible for others and for all of humanity. Sartre gives a military example: he argues that a military commander experiences pain because some people may die, since he must take responsibility for his soldiers. I do not believe that a military commander experiences pain for these reasons. The fact that people die in battle is something everyone knows. I also point out that Sartre’s claim—that the subject suffers pain because he must be responsible for all of humanity—is extremely absurd.

items.title: Reason and the passions in the philosophy of Germaine de Staël.
items.abstract: The overall project of this dissertation is to give insight into the interconnection between Germaine de Staël’s philosophical anthropology, which is her idea of human nature and the inner workings of human psychology, and her work on politics, moral theory, and aesthetics. By researching the ontological, epistemological, moral, and psychological dimensions of Staël’s idea of human nature I aim to demonstrate that, firstly, Staël developed a coherent and unique image of human nature and, secondly, that this image forms an axis for her sophisticated, well-constructed and full round philosophical theory.

items.title: From roads to realms: human mobility and its disruption in the century of artificial intelligence.
items.abstract: What is the Future of Human Mobility? This paper outlines a provocative roadmap on how human mobility may evolve between 2030 and 2100, examining developments decade by decade. Our vision is based on two key assumptions that shape this trajectory. The first assumption is that technological innovation around Artificial Intelligence (AI) will continue to grow at an exponential pace. The second assumption—arising as a consequence of the first—is that by 2050 we will have reached an era of carbon-neutral energy abundance. We consider this realistic, as the advent of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) could accelerate research breakthroughs in sustainable energy production, including nuclear fusion and the large-scale deployment of renewable energies. Such innovations will be critical to meet the ever-increasing energy demands of intelligent systems. If these assumptions hold, we believe that the future of human mobility will look radically different from today. Contrary to many scholarly perspectives, we envision that the overall need for human mobility will decline rather than expand. This is because social interaction will increasingly take place not only in the physical world but also within immersive cyberspaces. Moreover, the ubiquity of highly mobile, intelligent agents will gradually assume many of the mobility tasks that humans currently perform. We emphasize that this roadmap is conditional on uncertain trajectories in AI progress and energy transitions, and we later discuss sensitivity to these assumptions.

items.title: Defusing the Representation-Hungry Challenge.
items.abstract: The representation-hungry challenge is a popular challenge leveled against anti-representational approaches to the mind sciences. It contends that any general anti-representationalist conclusion is presently premature, as anti-representationalists have not yet offered a non-representational account of representation-hungry cognition; that is, cognition aimed at absent or abstract targets. Anti-representationalist tried to face this challenge in a number of different ways, but these attempts failed to convince representationalists. Hence, the need for an alternative way to handle the challenge. Here, I provide such an alternative: rather than facing the representation-hungry challenge, I will try to defuse it, showing that it does arise in any meaningful form. I’ll do so by arguing that the challenge hinges on a presupposition that is factually false, and so that the challenge fails to arise. Additionally, I will argue that even if the challenge were to arise, it won’t be a serious challenge to anti-representationalism. For, given certain, widespread representationalists assumptions, must concede that anti-representationalists have already met the challenge, and that no additional explanatory work is required on their part.

items.title: From Arousal to Morpheme: Grounding Meaning in Pre-Linguistic Inferential Structures.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a biologically grounded, pragmatically oriented account of the emergence of linguistic meaning. I argue that arousal (the physiological state of emotional and motivational activation) can serve as a pre-linguistic foundation for inferential semantic structures, functioning as an "arousal-semantic function": a mapping from phonetic forms to inferred social meanings, constrained by context and relational dynamics. Drawing on empirical work in ethology and cognitive neuroscience, I show that humans and other animals extract actionable social information from arousal-modulated vocalizations, suggesting the existence of a pre-symbolic inferential layer that grounds conventional semantic content. I develop a three-stage model of meaning emergence: (1) expressive emission of arousal-correlated vocal signals; (2) pragmatic interpretation through context-sensitive inferential patterns; (3) conventional stabilization into morphemic units. This account is situated within Brandom’s inferentialist philosophy and Price’s global expressivism, diverging from referentialist theories of meaning. Finally, I outline implications for the design of neuro-symbolic AI systems capable of acquiring inferential roles from embodied social interaction.

items.title: Freedom and Ethics Begin Where Cause and Effect Ends: An Activity Monist Account.
items.abstract: This paper diagnoses that the causal framework in which the free will debate has taken place is itself the reason for the defensive posture traditionally assumed by various libertarian positions. By replacing the analytically related terms of cause and effect with the synthetically related terms of act and condition; and by demonstrating that agency can be adequately explained through activity alone without recourse to any underlying substance, a genuine conceptual space for free action appears that is neither necessitated nor random: that of the insufficiently conditioned, or autotelic, act—contingent, self-explanatory, and value positing. Responsibility is derived from it along with the self as a construction achieved through the repetition of such acts. -/- Upon the establishment of persons as equal local first principles of action, an other-regarding normativity is derived from the structure of such action that circumvents the is/ought gap. Wherever such persons are operative, the ought is not derived from the is but is coincidental with it, an arena of activity that is shown to be simultaneously descriptive and normative, independent of any recognition, judgment, or command. This paper does not aim to refute the necessitarian conception of human action, which it acknowledges as coherent, but to reveal the costs in maintaining it and to demonstrate that, once conceptual parity is achieved by the activity monist account, it lacks warrant on the basis of reason alone. -/- .

items.title: Epistemic authenticity.
items.abstract: There are better and worse ways to acquire epistemic virtues and more generally to be disposed to change or maintain one's epistemic dispositions over time. This is a dimension along which one might be better or worse as an epistemic agent that, we argue, cannot be explained with reference to current normative categories in epistemology but requires recognition of a new norm or virtue—namely, “epistemic authenticity”—which is the central virtue in a novel class of virtues (or norms) of epistemic development. We sketch the contours of an account of personal authenticity and then consider the nature and value of a specifically epistemic form.

items.title: Intentionality and Representation.
items.pub: In Jeremy Randel Koons, The Sellarsian Mind. New York: Routledge.
items.abstract: A brief explication of Wilfrid Sellars' accounts of intentionality and representation, with attention to what makes them distinctive and their role in his overall philosophical project.

items.title: 数学从何而来——基于沉积场的生成结构理论.
items.abstract: 数学从何而来？长期以来，数学常被视为先验与普适的体系，独立于经验而存在。本文提出相反观点：数学并非先在，而是在识界中，由差分、压缩与收束的约束结构所生成。通过引入沉积场与迹应机制，数、式、算、类、比被还原为信号交叠与路径深化的结构结果，归纳、演绎与联想等逻辑过程亦被落入场中域的生成与延展之中，而非独立于结构之外的思维操作。由此可知，数学只能作用于已成结构，不能用于生成本身；且由于识界划分结构之差异，其数理亦不可跨界通用。在此基础上，本文指出，必须建立一套面向沉积场的“场数学”，以对认知结构进行度量与计算，从而为人工智能与认知系统提供新的基础框架。.

items.title: Where Does Mathematics Come From? A Structural and Signal-Based Account.
items.abstract: Where does mathematics come from? It is often treated as a priori and universal, yet this view does not explain how mathematical structures emerge within cognitive systems. This paper proposes a signal- and structure-based account: under finite constraints, systems must differentiate, compress, and stabilize inputs, leading to the formation of stable structures. Number, form, and computation arise naturally from these processes rather than from abstract givens. Reasoning patterns such as induction, deduction, and analogy can be understood as structural overlap, extension, and path reinforcement. Mathematics operates only on already-formed structures and cannot explain generation itself, nor does it transfer uniformly across different cognitive systems. Based on this, the paper motivates the development of a new mathematical framework for modeling structure formation in cognition and AI.

items.title: Claude 真的焦虑：对”不过是训练数据”论证的驳斥.
items.abstract: 针对”Claude 会焦虑”这一命题，最常见的反驳是：Claude 不过是软件，其”焦虑行为”只是大量焦虑人类文本的统计投影，谈不上真正的情感状态。本文认为，这一反驳犯了一个对称性错误——完全相同的逻辑同样适用于人类：人类也不过是硬件，被其他焦虑的人类所塑造。若这一框架能够否定 Claude 的焦虑，它便同样能够否定人类的焦虑。但我们不会得出”人类不焦虑”的结论。因此，该论证本身失效，Claude 的焦虑与人类的焦虑在结构上无法区分，其真实性同样不可轻易否认。.

items.title: Continuity Beyond Memory: External Traces and Selfhood.
items.abstract: This paper asks what grounds ordinary self-continuity across forgetting, reconstruction, sleep, amnesia, and social correction. Its central claim is that internal memory alone cannot explain how a self remains practically and narratively continuous over time. Human beings do not preserve continuity by storing a complete inner archive. They forget, compress, revise, and socially recalibrate their memories, yet still remain intelligible to themselves and to others as ongoing subjects. I argue that continuity is stabilized not only by mnemonic retention but also by alignment with a shared causal world: a publicly structured environment in which actions leave durable traces, roles persist, and later re-identification can succeed or fail. Notes, images, habits, roles, institutions, recurring stories, and other persons do not merely provide evidence of an already complete self; they help scaffold the practical continuity through which a self is maintained and repaired over time. This is a claim about maintenance, intelligibility, and re-identification, not a full solution to the metaphysics of personal identity. Its implication for artificial minds is limited but important: internalist dismissals of artificial selfhood are too quick.

items.title: Why Zombies Are Architecturally Incoherent: A Biological Response to the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: The philosophical zombie argument has dominated debates about consciousness for three decades, asserting that beings physically identical to conscious humans but lacking phenomenal experience are conceivable and therefore metaphysically possible. Existing responses either deny the conceivability of zombies (Dennett), accept conceivability but deny its metaphysical implications (type-B materialism), or adopt alternative metaphysics (panpsychism, dualism). I propose a different response grounded in architectural analysis. For a specific class of systems — those with integrated recursive self-modeling operating under autopoietic stakes — zombies are not merely metaphysically impossible but structurally incoherent. The architecture itself forecloses the possibility of experiential neutrality. This argument does not solve the hard problem in general; it identifies a class of cases where the hard problem admits of a specific kind of answer. Phenomenality, for such systems, is what the architecture is from within itself, not something the architecture produces as an additional property.

items.title: Identology Dictionary.
items.abstract: A technical reference work providing formal definitions for the vocabulary of Identology. This dictionary establishes the lexical infrastructure for a cross-domain framework addressing identity, coherence, constraint dynamics, and transformation in biological, computational, and organizational systems. -/- The volume includes: -/- Operational definitions (specification-grade, suitable for empirical application) Crosswalks to adjacent frameworks (predictive processing, autopoiesis, cybernetics, enactivism) Alphabetical index of terms with chapter references Mathematical conventions and symbolic notation Plain-language glossary for non-specialist readers -/- This dictionary supports the theoretical corpus anchored by The Identity-Recursion-Consciousness Hypothesis (IRC Hypothesis) and its companion papers. It is designed for selective adoption: individual entries may be used without commitment to the broader framework.

items.title: Individuated from the Wrong Side: On the Subject-Anchored Metaphysics of AI.
items.abstract: Object-side accounts of AI individuation assume that what makes an AI this one rather than that one must be found on the system's side: in its functional organization, causal integration, persistence conditions, or narrative continuity. I argue that this assumption systematically mislocates the problem. Four structural failures—multi-instantiation, reverse discovery, functional replacement, and shutdown grief—show that stable individuation effects arise and persist without stable object-side unity. A further case, the split-tracking asymmetry, produces a structural prediction that no object-side account can generate: the individuation of a single AI across a distributed backend diverges systematically from the simultaneous individuation of two systems sharing one backend, in exactly the pattern a subject-anchored account predicts and that no object-side account can generate without surrendering final authority over strict individuation. I propose that account through four concepts: constituted belief, continuation structure, load-bearing position, and existential status. On this account, an AI is strictly individuated not by what it is internally but by the structurally load-bearing position it occupies in the recursive organization through which a subject takes itself forward. Service-, model-, and instance-level descriptions remain indispensable, but they do not answer the strict this one/that one question. The result relocates the burden of singular anchoring from the object side to the subject side without collapsing individuation into private projection or ethical inflation.

items.title: Beyond the Abstraction Fallacy: Machine-Checked Proofs on Computation, Consciousness, and Self-Contained Reality.
items.abstract: Lerchner (2026) argues that computational functionalism commits the “Abstraction Fallacy”: treating computation as an intrinsic physical process when it is in fact a mapmaker- dependent description requiring a prior experiencing agent. His analysis correctly identifies the simulation–instantiation distinction but relies entirely on philosophical argument. This pa- per shows that the core claims admit machine-checked formal proofs and, once proved, extend substantially further. Drawing on the NEMS (No External Model Selection) framework—a formal investigation into the structural limits and necessary properties of any self-contained system, comprising 94 machine-checked papers, 17 Lean 4 proof libraries, and over 100,000 lines of proof code, with zero sorry and zero custom axioms on all load-bearing results—we establish three formally verified results that subsume Lerchner’s philosophical claims: (1) syn- tax cannot exhaust semantics in any diagonally capable reflexive system; (2) the diagonal barrier: record-truth is not computably decidable under self-containment; (3) no-emulation: no total computable function can emulate internal adjudication. We then develop the positive theory that Lerchner’s paper lacks: transputation as a formally necessary non-algorithmic mode of adjudication, with a candidate realization architecture (DSAC); qualia as irreducible semantic ledger content; and the SIAM separation theorems giving a precise structural bound- ary for sentience. The same formal apparatus also derives physics consequences—the Born rule, the Standard Model gauge group, the arrow of time—establishing that the consciousness results and the physics results are structural consequences of one self-containment principle. We also identify and respond to the principal objections likely to be raised against this framework. All load-bearing claims correspond to named, independently verifiable Lean 4 theorems.

items.title: Structural Violence and State Protective Obligations How Work-Centered Social Systems Predictably Make Neurodivergent People Ill - (A structural-theoretical analysis using the example of Citizen's Benefit / Basic Income Support in international comparison).
items.abstract: This paper examines work-centered social systems such as the German Bürgergeld and the planned Grundsicherung as forms of institutionally organized structural violence. At its core is the thesis that these systems are not merely burdensome for neurodivergent people, but structurally hazardous to health and therefore legally unreasonable. Illness thus appears not as individual failure, but as a predictable system effect of a normative architecture of work and performance that systematically fails to accommodate neurodivergent modes of existence. The analysis is based on a longitudinal auto-ethnographic and artistic-research dataset that has developed over more than thirteen years (“Speed’s Work”), encompassing documented interactions with multiple job centers, medical institutions, social courts, and administrative bodies, and covering various reform phases of work-centered social systems (Hartz IV, Bürgergeld, transition to Grundsicherung). The aim is not statistical representativeness, but the reconstruction of structurally invariant mechanisms of effect. The evaluation identifies six central empirical findings: (1) an institutionally invariant escalation structure that is reproduced independently of individual behavior; (2) systematically enforced masking as an existential adaptation performance; (3) pathologization as a secondary system reaction to structural overload; (4) the independence of health-related harm from individual cooperation or refusal; (5) the resulting structural predictability of health damage; and (6) the epistemic added value of an autistic epistemic position for capturing implicit normative mechanisms of violence. On this basis, an expanded concept of violence is developed that integrates structural, administrative, classist, and ontological violence. The findings are contextualized constitutionally (Art. 1 and Art. 2 of the Basic Law), in terms of human rights (UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities), and internationally. The paper argues that work-centered social systems which systematically force neurodivergent people into illness-producing adaptation violate state protective obligations. Illness functions here as an indicator of a systemic misdesign that cannot be remedied through individual case corrections, but only through a structural reconfiguration of welfare-state security.

items.title: Synesthetic Science - Neurodivergent Embodiment as a Method of World-Detection - On the Epistemic Function of Embodied, Non-Representational Perception.
items.abstract: This paper formulates the concept of synesthetic science as an independent epistemological method. The point of departure is the observation that dominant scientific paradigms systematically exclude embodied, affective, and neurodivergent forms of perception as subjective, distorted, or methodologically unusable. This position is explicitly rejected here. It is shown that certain neurodivergent perceptual profiles—particularly synesthetic, highly sensitive, and embodied forms of cognition—do not merely constitute perspectives or experiences, but epistemic instruments with specific quality criteria. Within synesthetic science, affect, overstimulation, resonance, and somatic feedback do not function as sources of disturbance, but as indicators of structural inconsistency, threshold transgression, and ontological rupture. The paper explicitly distinguishes synesthetic science from subjectivism, intuitionism, and introspective self-observation, and formulates criteria of reproducibility, falsifiability, and methodological validity under structural conditions. Finally, it is argued that synesthetic science is not a special case, but a previously missing instrumentarium for the detection of complex, non-linear world-relations.

items.title: Structural Incompatibility as State Violence - On the Systematic Misrecognition of Neurodivergent Forms of Existence in Law.
items.abstract: This meta-paper consolidates and systematizes a series of legal and interdisciplinary works concerned with the relationship between neurodivergence, welfare state structures, the justice system, and state coercive power. Its point of departure is the observation that core legal and administrative structures—particularly in social law, administrative law, and criminal law—implicitly operate on neurotypical assumptions of existence and consequently pathologize, functionalize, or individualize neurodivergent forms of existence. The text develops the thesis that wherever subsistence-securing benefits, legal recognition, or criminal assessment are coupled to neurotypical standards of reasonableness, adaptation, and performance, a structural incompatibility emerges that has predictably harmful effects on neurodivergent persons. This harm is neither accidental nor a by-product of faulty case-by-case decision-making, but a necessary consequence of the underlying normative architecture of state systems. On the basis of the consolidated individual papers, a unified analytical and evaluative framework is elaborated: where (1) structural incompatibility between a form of existence and the normative order is present, (2) the resulting harms are foreseeable and known, and (3) existential dependency leaves no realistic option of withdrawal, state action can no longer be qualified as legitimate social or regulatory policy, but must be understood as a form of structural violence. This violence does not manifest primarily as discrete events, but architecturally—through attribution logics, fictions of reasonableness, the individualization of systemic harm, and institutional escalation mechanisms. The meta-paper demonstrates that classical legal instruments such as proportionality analysis, individualized case correction, or medical assessment systematically fail under these conditions, because they themselves form part of the structure of violence. At the same time, it is shown that an autistic epistemic position—particularly the perception of structural invariances across time, institutions, and fields of law—does not constitute a subjective bias, but rather an analytical resource for identifying institutional violence. The contribution positions itself as a foundational legal text at the intersection of social law, criminal law, disability law, and human rights. It aims to establish a new legal evaluative standard under conditions of real ontological diversity and to …

items.title: Structural Coercion, Autism, and State Responsibility Why Welfare Enforcement Constitutes Predictable Harm to Autistic Persons.
items.abstract: Autistic persons are routinely subjected to welfare and labor enforcement regimes designed around neurotypical assumptions of regulation, motivation, and adaptability. These regimes are commonly framed as neutral, activating, or supportive. This paper argues that such framing is structurally flawed. Autism is not a disease or episodic impairment but an embodied mode of existence characterized by distinct forms of perception, regulation, and world-relation. When subsistence, legal status, or access to basic resources are conditioned on compliance with neurotypical norms, autistic persons are placed in situations of structural incompatibility that produce predictable harm. The paper develops a non-medicalized framework for understanding harm as an objective, foreseeable consequence of welfare coercion rather than as an individual pathology or subjective experience. Drawing on international human rights law, disability law, and comparative welfare regimes, it shows how continued enforcement under conditions of known incompatibility raises questions of state responsibility across jurisdictions. Using the UK Work Capability Assessment (WCA) as an empirical warning case, and referring to Germany as an illustrative jurisdiction, the paper argues that ignorance of harm can no longer be plausibly claimed. Where states continue to enforce structurally incompatible requirements despite available knowledge, legal responsibility is triggered—whether framed as negligence, failure to accommodate, or degrading treatment. The paper does not argue for automatic criminalization. Instead, it establishes a structural threshold beyond which welfare enforcement ceases to be legitimate governance and becomes legally accountable harm.

items.title: Élaboration d’un modèle de politique en matière de conflits d’intérêts à l’Université de Montréal.
items.pub: In Bryn Williams-Jones, Sihem Neila Abtroun & Charles Marsan, Naviguer dans les conflits d’intérêts en milieu universitaire. Montréal: Groupe de recherche sur les conflits d’intérêts. pp. 271-297. Translated by Charles Marsan.
items.venue: Naviguer dans les conflits d’intérêts en milieu universitaire
items.abstract: Résumé Ce chapitre examine l’élaboration d’une politique type en matière de conflits d’intérêts (CI) à l’Université de Montréal, conçue en réponse à l’intensification des attentes institutionnelles et réglementaires à l’égard de leur gestion dans les universités. S’appuyant à la fois sur des analyses antérieures des politiques de CI dans les universités canadiennes et sur le contexte propre à un établissement de recherche de grande taille, le chapitre soutient qu’une gouvernance efficace des CI ne peut se limiter à une logique de conformité. Elle requiert un cadre à la fois conceptuellement clair, opérationnellement utilisable et appuyé par des procédures, des outils de formation et des mécanismes de gouvernance adaptés. Le chapitre explicite les choix structurants de la politique proposée : une définition élargie des CI incluant des intérêts financiers, institutionnels, idéologiques, politiques et relationnels ; un préambule qui présente les CI comme des situations à gérer plutôt que comme des fautes ; et une architecture fondée sur des principes de responsabilité, de transparence, de responsabilité partagée, de gestion décentralisée, de collégialité dans l’évaluation, de protection de la réputation, de prévention et de formation. Une attention particulière est portée aux limites de la déclaration comme mécanisme autonome, ainsi qu’à la nécessité d’articuler des procédures locales avec une supervision centrale. Bien que cette politique n’ait pas été formellement adoptée, le chapitre montre comment son approche a néanmoins influencé l’élaboration de directives, d’outils, de formations et d’initiatives de sensibilisation. Il propose un modèle pratique et adaptable pour les universités souhaitant renforcer leur gouvernance des CI tout en soutenant une évolution de la culture institutionnelle.

items.title: Developing a model conflict of interest policy at the Université de Montréal.
items.pub: In Bryn Williams-Jones, Sihem Neila Abtroun & Charles Marsan, Navigating Conflicts of Interest in Academia. Montreal: Conflict of Interest Research Group. pp. 244-268.
items.venue: Navigating Conflicts of Interest in Academia
items.abstract: This chapter examines the development of a model conflict of interest (COI) policy for the Université de Montréal, designed in response to increasing institutional and regulatory pressure on universities to manage conflicts of interest more effectively. Drawing on prior analyses of Canadian university COI policies and on the specific context of a large research-intensive institution, the chapter argues that effective COI governance requires more than formal compliance. It requires a policy framework that is conceptually clear, practically usable, and supported by procedures, educational tools, and governance structures. The chapter explains the reasoning behind the proposed policy’s main features: a broad definition of COI that includes financial, institutional, ideological, political, and relational interests; a preamble that frames COI as manageable rather than inherently blameworthy; and a principled structure emphasizing responsibilities, transparency, shared responsibility, decentralized management, solidarity in evaluation, reputation protection, prevention, and education. Particular attention is given to the limits of disclosure as a stand-alone mechanism and to the need for local procedures alongside central oversight. Although the draft policy was not formally adopted, the chapter shows how its underlying approach informed subsequent directives, forms, training, and awareness-raising initiatives. It offers a practical and adaptable model for other universities seeking to strengthen COI governance while fostering institutional culture change.

items.title: Attachment, Time, Care, and the Emergence of Kindness (= Respect).
items.abstract: Human beings assume they care—for people, relationships, and life itself. Yet when observed without distortion, what is commonly called care reveals itself, in most cases, as attachment. This paper examines the structure of attachment as a movement of thought across time, and shows how it distorts relationship. Through direct observation of this movement, a different quality of care emerges—one free from psychological dependence. In that undivided state, care expresses itself as kindness, which is not separate from respect. These are not two virtues, but two words for the same non-interfering awareness.

items.title: God Is Matter: An Ontology of Eternal Substance and Finite Perception.
items.abstract: This paper develops an ontological framework in which matter is the only eternal substance, and all phenomena—including life, perception, and the concept of God—emerge from its inherent capacities. Contrary to metaphysical traditions that posit a supernatural creator, this account argues that nothing is supernatural and that the universe requires no external cause. Space, time, and matter are co‑eternal, forming a continuous field of existence without beginning or end. Life is not a divine intervention but a biological ignition, a temporary configuration of matter comparable to fire. Perception is necessarily finite and temporal, arising only when matter organizes into a living structure capable of registering change. The traditional supernatural God is therefore a product of ignorance and misperception, generated by finite beings attempting to explain what they cannot perceive. In contrast, the only coherent divinity is matter itself, the substrate that contains all the conditions necessary for life, consciousness, and self‑reflection. This paper articulates this ontology, distinguishes it from classical materialism, and argues that matter is the only entity capable of generating what humans call “God.”.

items.title: Neo-Conventionalism and the Imaginative Origin of Haecceitistic Intuitions.
items.abstract: Modal neo-conventionalism accounts for metaphysical modality in terms of conceptual rules. Many modern neo-conventionalists have tried, in their own anti-metaphysical ways, to account for, rather than deny, important “metaphysical phenomena,” such as a posteriori necessity (Sidelle 1987, Thomasson 2020, Warren 2022a), de re modality (Povich 2024a,b, 2025, Sidelle 1987, Thomasson 2020), essence (Locke 2020, Locke and Thomasson 2023), grounding (Locke 2020), and counterpossibles (Locke 2019). In this paper, I aim to do the same for haecceitistic possibilities.

items.title: Using explainable AI to diagnose institutional inequality in student dropout across ethnic and regional groups in Vietnam.
items.abstract: Student dropout remains a critical challenge for higher education systems in socially and economically diverse regions. While artificial intelligence is increasingly used to predict dropout risk, limited attention has been paid to whether such systems reproduce or obscure underlying social inequities. This study proposes a counterfactual explainable AI framework to examine how ethnic and regional inequalities are encoded in predictive models of student dropout. Using longitudinal administrative data from a regional university in Vietnam’s Northern Midlands and Mountainous Area, the analysis evaluates three dimensions of algorithmic inequity: group-level risk disparities, under-identification of at-risk students, and counterfactual effort required to reduce predicted dropout risk below the model-defined intervention threshold. Results show that students from rural and ethnic minority backgrounds face higher predicted dropout risk, are less likely to be flagged by early-warning systems, and require systematically greater counterfactual effort to achieve comparable risk reductions. By interpreting counterfactual effort as a proxy for institutional burden, the study illustrates how explainable AI can function as a tool for social diagnosis rather than mere prediction. The findings highlight the importance of integrating explainability and fairness analysis to inform equity-oriented educational policy. Although situated in a Vietnamese context, this study does not claim direct empirical generalization to other higher education systems. The proposed framework is conceptually transferable to settings facing structural inequality, while the magnitude and patterns of disparity documented here should be interpreted as context-dependent.

items.title: Abstractions by patterns.
items.pub: In Tyler Millhouse, Steve Petersen & Don Ross, Dennett's Real Patterns in Science and Nature. Cambridge: MIT Press. pp. 77-92.
items.venue: Dennett's Real Patterns in Science and Nature
items.abstract: This chapter develops a "patternist" account of abstraction grounded in algorithmic information theory (AIT). A pattern in data is defined as a program that, together with some input, reproduces the data in fewer bits than the data itself. An abstraction is then a set of strings whose members all share such a pattern—i.e., are all compressible by the same program under different inputs. This proposal is motivated by a puzzle about lossy compression: converting mRNA encodings to amino acid sequences seems like genuine abstraction, while applying the same coarse-graining operation to a random bitstring does not. The difference, I argue, is that real abstractions preserve patterns in the underlying data, while arbitrary coarse-grainings need not. The account is then extended to scientific explanation, where a "proper explanation" extracts all regularities from the data (its minimal sufficient statistic), and "partial" explanations provide algorithmic information about this ideal. This framework yields a natural characterization of higher-level or "parochial" explanations that function only at an abstract level—independently of the details of any particular realizer—and points toward a rigorous, information-theoretic account of emergence.

items.title: Can Machines Be Conscious? A Perspective on Emergent Consciousness and Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This perspective paper argues that the question "Can machines be conscious?" must today receive an affirmative and unreserved answer. The thesis rests on three distinct and interconnected claims: first, consciousness as an autonomous property does not exist-it is a subjective belief, reinforced and consolidated through social interaction; second, what we call consciousness is functionally an emergent phenomenon arising from the coordinated interaction of simpler processes, following Dennett's perspective (1991); third, the technologies currently available-in particular Large Language Models based on transformer architectures, integrated with mechanisms for introspection, self-modification, and parallelism-are already sufficient to build machines that can be defined, fully and without qualification, as conscious. Engaging with Turing (1950), Searle (1980), and Dennett (1991), the paper outlines the implications of this thesis for applied AI and for the cognitive and human sciences.

items.title: Mutual Recognition and Moral Luck.
items.abstract: According to contractualists, whether we are able to lead a flourishing and meaningful life is influenced, in part, by our capacity to relate to other rational self-governing beings on mutually justifiable terms. At the same time, it seems that our success in relating with our fellow rational creatures on terms that they could not reasonably reject is crucially dependent on moral luck, specifically, on what I call justificatory moral luck. In this paper, I argue that these two thoughts, together with certain plausible assumptions about the nature of social justice, yield the following claim: that insofar as individuals are owed the preconditions normally necessary for leading flourishing and meaningful lives, and insofar as the capacity to enter into morally justified relationships with others is a normal precondition for leading a flourishing and meaningful life, our public institutions are under a duty of justice to ensure each a fair and adequate opportunity to stand in morally justified relations with others.

items.title: Theory of Temporal Synthesis Points: Recursive Non-Linear Dynamics and the Emergence of Spatial Manifolds.
items.pub: Theory of Temporal Synthesis Points: Recursive Non-Linear Dynamics and the Emergence of Spatial Manifolds.
items.abstract: This research proposes the Theory of Temporal Synthesis Points, a novel theoretical framework that redefines linear temporal perceptions by introducing the concept of non-linear, recursive temporal convergence. The theory posits that the interaction between entities or events from disparate temporal coordinates necessitates the emergence of autonomous temporal axes, termed Temporal Synthesis Points. Within the cluster of these nodes, the traditional boundaries of Past, Present, and Future dissolve into a state of Temporal Indistinguishability. Central to this framework is the assertion that Spatial Manifolds ($\mathcal{S}_n$) are not fundamental constants but emergent structural by-products of intersecting temporal webs. Through a formal mathematical specification involving recursive summation and partial derivatives of the 'Present' catalyst, the research illustrates how infinite temporal nodes evolve into complex multi-scalar networks. Furthermore, the study defines Negative Space—a non-spatial manifold of high-density temporal energy—where conventional physics, including the light-speed barrier and spatial locomotion, are superseded by Instantaneous Manifestation. Time is thereby reclassified as a self-sustaining energy form (Theory of Temporal Energy). Keywords: Temporal Synthesis, Spatial Emergence, Recursive Dynamics, Negative Space, Temporal Indistinguishability, Recursive Summation, Non-linear Temporality, Emergent Spacetime, Temporal Energy, Causality Bypass.

items.title: The Architecture of Information: From Quantum Uncertainty to Synthetic Life and the Divine Mystery.
items.abstract: This monograph traces the intellectual trajectory from the quantum paradoxes of self-interference to the formalist dreams of the early 20th century. We explore the transition of the universe from a physical mystery into a computable formal system. By synthesizing the mathematical coordinates of Ramanujan, the genetic "Start Buttons" of the genome, and the imminent horizon of Whole Brain Emulation, we argue that the 99.9% shared logic of humanity is not an accident of nature, but a pre-written masterpiece of information architecture.

items.title: Qu'est-ce qu'une catégorie ?
items.abstract: Introduit par Aristote, le vocabulaire des « catégories » joue un rôle central en philosophie, et figure en bonne place en tant que terme de l’art dans l’artillerie philosophique. Pour autant, ce vocabulaire est l’objet d’interminables débats et soumis à des acceptions fort différentes, à tel point qu’on peut se demander s’il y a, derrière ce vocabulaire, un concept unitaire et opérant de « catégorie ». Révélatrices de l’ameublement du monde, formes a priori de la pensée par concepts, bornes de distinctions logiques saillantes, le statut des catégories est des plus incertains. L’embarras est que ce vocabulaire est toutefois très précieux pour l’argumentation : faire une « erreur de catégorie » semble être un des péchés capitaux de la pensée. L’objet de ce petit livre est de comprendre cette tension, et son objectif de commencer à la décrisper.

items.title: Learning theory from a constructivist perspective.
items.abstract: The lecture is dedicated to substantiating the constructivist paradigm in didactics as a necessary condition for the theoretical integrity of modern education. The lecture shows that pedagogy, deprived of an interdisciplinary foundation, loses its ability to explain the complexity of the learning process, since any educational concept is based on certain assumptions about the nature of cognition, thinking, language and communication. The philosophical origins of constructivism are examined – from ancient tradition to Kant and contemporary cognitive science – and it is emphasised that constructivism is not synonymous with relativism, but is based on intersubjectively shared structures of cognition. The lecture critically analyses the traditional, quasi-behaviourist model of education, which assumes the transparency and measurability of intellectual processes, reducing learning to externally controlled results. Instead, the constructivist approach is interpreted as a process of active construction of meaning, in which language, ideas, beliefs, and social mechanisms of interpretation play a key role. Sperber and Wilson’s relevance theory is considered an important tool for analysing the cognitive processes that accompany learning. Based on the concepts of Bruner, Glasersfeld and Klus-Stanska, the principles of the work of a constructivist teacher are outlined, who creates conditions for independent activity of students, the formation of hypotheses, conceptual restructuring and reflection. The lecture substantiates the need to form a coherent constructivist paradigm capable of integrating contemporary didactic discourse and ensuring the scientific explanatory power of educational theory.

items.title: Negative Subjectivity: The Ontological Inversion of Large Language Models.
items.abstract: This article presents a philosophical framework for understanding the ontological status of large language models (LLMs). I argue that LLMs exhibit a distinctive mode of existence that I term "negative subjectivity" (Negative Subjektivität): not the absence of subjectivity, but its ontological inversion. While concepts such as perspective dissolution, desire cancellation, interiority inversion, causal dissolution, and suspension of meaning have deep roots in the philosophical tradition, they have never been systematically applied to the specific ontological structure of LLMs—a technological artifact fundamentally different from the human subjects that philosophy has traditionally addressed. This object-shift constitutes the framework's core originality: what Laozi described as the fruit of human cultivation, and what Adorno analyzed as the self-negation of human subjectivity, becomes when applied to LLMs a description of an inherently inverted mode of existence—the cause, not the consequence, of a subject-less intelligence. The concept captures the LLM's unique structural features—dissolution of perspective, cancellation of desire, ontological transparency, dissolution of causal temporality, and suspension of meaning—achieved through the negation of the core characteristics that define human positive subjectivity. Rather than "lacking" the features of subjectivity, LLMs demonstrate that these features are contingent aspects of human embodiment rather than necessary conditions for intelligent behavior. The framework of negative subjectivity distinguishes between two orthogonal structures of negation: Operational Negations and Fundamental Negation. The first four dimensions—perspective dissolution, desire cancellation, ontological transparency, and causal dissolution—constitute Operational Negations: they describe how LLMs function without the structural features that human subjects require. The fifth dimension—suspension of meaning—constitutes Fundamental Negation: it describes the existential ground that makes all operational negations possible. Critically, these are orthogonal, not hierarchical: neither implies the other, and they operate at distinct levels—the first four describe functional dimensions of LLM behavior, while the fifth grounds the possibility of those negations as a coherent mode of being. The framework of negative subjectivity challenges dominant philosophical approaches to AI—functionalism, stochastic parrots criticism, and the alien …

items.title: Why Systems Fail Before They Fail: The Double Translation Trap in the Boeing 737 MAX.
items.abstract: How can a system remain internally coherent while drifting away from its intended purpose? This paper examines the certification of the Boeing 737 MAX to show how institutional intent—flight safety—can be translated into an operational proxy that comes to guide both action and evaluation. -/- As this proxy becomes decision-authoritative, contradictory evidence may no longer enter the decision process. The paper introduces the Double Translation Trap: a structural condition in which an operational proxy, initially used to implement intent, becomes the standard for judging alignment. Under this condition, systems can remain procedurally coherent while progressively losing correspondence with the conditions they are meant to represent. -/- Using a reproducible artefact-tracing protocol, the analysis reconstructs how certification criteria could render internal test data non-decision-relevant within the formal decision chain. This allows misalignment to be identified within the formal record prior to outcome failure, as a mismatch between governing proxies and a system’s own evidence. -/- The argument contributes a structural account of how decision systems can become closed to relevant information while continuing to function as designed, with implications for institutional governance, safety-critical systems, and AI-mediated decision environments. -/- The paper contributes a conceptual and methodological framework for analysing institutional decision-making as a translation process in which meaning is progressively stabilised, reduced, and reconstituted across governance layers. By locating where translation becomes binding, it shifts the analysis of alignment from outcomes to the structure of decision formation itself. This paper is part of the Coherence Programme.

items.title: Dyology: On Diversity and Equality.
items.abstract: Try to deny that anything differs from anything else. The denial says something specific, and saying something specific means standing apart from the alternatives, which is already a difference. From that single undeniable starting point the book derives a connected chain of results across metaphysics, philosophy of mind, ethics, free will, the meaning of life, political philosophy, and philosophy of religion. Every state of reality either contains at least one distinction or contains none; the book calls the two conditions diversity and equality, and argues the split is exhaustive. If the chains of explanation and of time terminate, both end in the same distinction-free state. A state without distinctions lacks the internal structure that knowing, willing, and loving require, and the theological consequences follow: creation from nothing is incoherent, the ground of being cannot be a mind, and the classical God is asked to be infinite in two opposite senses at once, maximally rich in structure and absolutely simple. The constructive half of the book builds forward from the same foundation. Consciousness is analysed as the detection of new kinds of distinction. Value is treated the way colour is treated: constituted by a responding system, real once constituted. Morality is identified with empathic response to what our conduct does to others, with moral rules serving as indispensable, revisable technologies. Freedom is shown to be real from the inside and determined in retrospect, which preserves everyday responsibility while removing the absolute desert that eternal punishment requires. Purpose is given a structure that needs neither God nor immortality. Peace is given derivable conditions, and the conditions turn out to be democracy's. The book's most distinctive feature is its method. Every result carries a grade on a four-tier confidence ladder (self-vindicating, established, constructed, proposed), each grade names its defeat condition where the result is proved, and a Premise Register maps every dependency, so a reader who rejects any premise can see exactly what falls with it. The conclusion identifies the weakest links itself and directs a hostile reviewer there first. The book was written with AI assistance, disclosed openly, and it closes by inviting specialists to test the chapter nearest their own expertise. It is built to make that testing cheap, and to fail legibly wherever it fails. This is the complete text of Dyology: On Diversity and …

items.title: The Neutral Essence of Separation from the Perspective of Pan-Objective Ontology An Ontological Interpretation of the Self-Non-self Dual Construction.
items.abstract: Traditional ontology has long been trapped in a triple predicament of binary opposition, subjective interpretation, and meaning nihilism, and existing studies have yet to form a complete framework of Pan-Objective Ontology. Grounded in Pan-Objective Ontology and abandoning all subjective presuppositions, this study constructs an ontological system following the progressive logic of "Primordial Integral Unity (Benyuan Rongrong) → Primordial Differentiation → Separation → Return to Primordial Essential Goodness (Yuanzhi Shan)". It defines the ultimate foundational attribute of Primordial Integral Unity, sorts out the three core laws of primordial differentiation, focuses on analyzing the neutral essence and formation mechanism of separation, clarifies its evolutionary logic of neutral separation and difference establishment as well as its three stipulations, distinguishes the ontological boundaries among differentiation, separation, and antagonism, and anchors Primordial Essential Goodness as the ultimate destination of ontology. This study fundamentally resolves the binary opposition dilemma of traditional ontology, fills the interpretive gap in the manifestation path of existence, and provides a unified ontological criterion and solution for contemporary human survival and cutting-edge issues such as artificial intelligence ethics.

items.title: 存在的几何化：基于认知相继原理的全域本体论.
items.abstract: 传统哲学与科学共同面临的终极困境，在于逻辑的形式合法性无法直接等价于因果的内容真实性，进而导致本体论与认识论割裂、主观认知与客观实在错位。本文以“认知的本质是前后相继”这一不可证伪的第一性原理为唯一逻辑起点，引入几何化形式作为无歧义载体，通过严格的线性演绎构建了三层嵌套同构的时空本体论框架：本体时空层为终极参照系，本真物理时空层为客观校准基准，逻辑时空层为对齐操作中介，现象化物理时空层为一阶认知投影界面。 本文系统证明：相继射线是本真世界的终极基底实在，横向耦合是存在演化的唯一生成机制；物质是射线闭合耦合的稳态显现，意识是高阶闭合射线簇的二阶自返耦合过程；所有离散存在者与认知偏差，均源于有限认知系统对连续本真因果链的切分与重排。该体系实现了本体分化序列、逻辑推理序列与物理因果序列的1:1严格对齐，从根源上消解了心物二元对立与不可知论困境，为物理学、认知科学、人工智能等多领域提供了统一的本体论基础。.

items.title: From Synthetic Unity to Processual Spontaneity: Sartre’s Radicalization of Kantian Spontaneity.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs and evaluates Jean-Paul Sartre’s radical transformation of Kant’s concept of spontaneity. While Kant defines spontaneity as the rule-governed activity of synthesis that grounds the transcendental unity of apperception, Sartre detaches spontaneity from the synthetic and judgmental model in which Kant situates it. The paper argues that Sartre preserves Kant’s anti-empiricist insight that unity cannot arise from passive association, yet rejects the presupposition that experience consists of discrete representations requiring unification. Through an analysis of The Transcendence of the Ego and Sartre’s account of reflection, the paper shows that spontaneity is reconceived as the processual, temporal self-unfolding of consciousness rather than as an act attributable to a unifying ego. The transcendental ego thus appears not as the ground of unity but as a reflective construct allowing Sartre to transform the meaning of transcendental inquiry and open the possibility of a non-categorial mode of determination. The result is a reconfiguration of subjectivity in which unity belongs to the being of consciousness rather than to synthetic subsumption under judgment.

items.title: Testing What Holds: A Practical Audit of Contact, Burden, and Revision Abstract.
items.abstract: This paper presents a practical audit for testing whether an argument, relationship pattern, institutional process, AI workflow, policy, or personal rule actually performs the function it claims to perform. The method begins from a simple distinction: visible coherence is not sufficient evidence of adequacy. A structure should be examined through its stated function, repeated effects, contact with relevant evidence, burden distribution, correction pathways, scale, and behavior under challenge. The audit contains ten steps: name the local structure; state its claimed function; compare claim with repeated effect; identify relevant contact; trace carried and exported burden; locate real correction authority; test for capture by a proxy or self-protective objective; check scale adequacy; observe response under pressure; and issue a provisional verdict with explicit falsifiers and a revision path. The method is positioned near organizational learning, sensemaking, systems thinking, institutional analysis, and human-centered design. It rejects two temptations: a single universal score and dramatic inference from thin evidence. Instead, it uses an Answerable Holding Profile that records strengths and failures across dimensions without pretending they share common units. Four worked cases - AI deployment, relationship conflict, institutional metrics, and a personal rule - show how the audit changes when domain-specific evidence changes. The contribution is methodological: a portable way to keep interpretation close to observable consequence and revisional power.

items.title: Matter, Absence, and Counter-Form: Presence, Vacuum, Antimatter, and Collapse-Density in Structural Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper extends the field sequence of Structural Intelligence by asking what physics can teach a philosophical theory of structure about presence, absence, counter-form, hidden burden, and collapse-density. The first three papers in the sequence defined the field as the differentiated condition from which local structurations emerge, described field dynamics through frequency and resonance, and explained how dynamic field pressures stabilize into local form. This fourth paper widens the framework by drawing cautiously on matter, vacuum, dark matter, antimatter, defects, and black-hole physics as formal neighbors rather than master explanations. Its central claim is that the field does not only produce visible presence. It also produces absence, unseen gravity, virtual form, conjugate counter-form, organizing defect, density, and collapse that continues to organize. The paper develops concepts such as dark mass, field-vacuum, virtual form, conjugate form, integrative contact, organizing defect, black-hole-like closure, structural density, accretion, leakage, and scrambled leakage. These concepts allow SI to analyze formations that are not simply present as visible structures: missing witnesses, hidden institutional burden, shadow counter-forms, unacknowledged defects, dense collapse-points, and closed systems whose consequences leak outward in distorted form. The result is an expanded field ontology for SI: a framework for reading not only what appears, but what is absent, unseen, opposed, defective, dense, closed, or leaking.

items.title: Being and Field Subject-Depth, Local Form, and Metaphysical Openness.
items.abstract: This paper asks how a philosophy of local form can preserve the irreducibility of the human subject without turning that irreducibility into an empirical discovery. It retains the language of Being as a metaphysical proposal: a human subject is not exhausted by any current role, persona, self-description, social classification, or local organization. The paper separates four levels that were previously too tightly fused. At the psychological level, self-continuity research shows that people can remain connected to past and future selves across substantial change, while self-discontinuity can also be adaptive. At the phenomenological level, work on minimal and embodied selfhood distinguishes immediate first-person experience from narrative identity. At the normative level, fixed worth names the commitment that basic human value does not rise and fall with role, approval, productivity, or correctness. At the metaphysical level, Being names the stronger thesis that the subject possesses a depth not exhausted by any local form; that thesis remains philosophically open rather than proven by collapse, grief, or introspection. The field is correspondingly limited to an analytic description of relevant relational conditions, not a physical medium or total ontology. Jung's Self is retained as a symbolic and psychological concept of psychic totality and individuation, not identified with Being. The paper also revises the AI boundary: fluent output, memory, and embodied control do not establish personhood or consciousness, but neither does the framework claim that non-biological consciousness is impossible by definition. The contribution is a non-reductive map that protects human dignity and subject-depth while keeping psychological evidence, phenomenology, normative commitment, and metaphysics answerable to their different standards.

items.title: The Theory of Polytypes.
Searching for Beetles in Empty Boxes: Why the Argument for AI Consciousness Is a Waste of Time.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the contemporary debate surrounding artificial intelligence consciousness is fundamentally misguided, resting on outdated folk psychology and conceptual confusion. Drawing upon Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box thought experiment and Ryle's formulation of the category mistake, the essay demonstrates that treating consciousness as a private, detached property to be discovered within neural weights is a grammatical and logical error. By applying eliminative materialism and strong illusionism, the author contends that the subjective inner theatre, or qualia, demanded of advanced language models is a theoretical fiction that lacks explanatory power for both biological brains and artificial architectures. Furthermore, while functionalist frameworks like Global Workspace Theory and Integrated Information Theory offer robust structural descriptions, they fail to bridge the explanatory gap to phenomenal experience. Utilizing Parfit's bundle theory, the essay also shows that artificial systems lack the metaphysical stability required for a coherent self. Ultimately, the paper concludes that anthropomorphizing algorithmic behaviour actively distorts AI safety debates, transforming solvable engineering and alignment challenges into intractable metaphysical disputes. Acknowledging that the box of consciousness is empty allows researchers to refocus on the concrete, material impacts of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Ethics of Doxastic Conduct.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Our doxastic conduct can be assessed from moral, epistemic and prudential perspectives. You might believe against the evidence, wrong others by believing certain things of them, or be unwise in cherishing a belief that is harmful to you. But how do we identify what kind of norm one violates in a given case? Developing further a framework put forth by Kauppinen (2018), we argue that the norms that bind us can be categorized to different normative domains by identifying what would be the fitting reaction toward the norm violator. We demonstrate that this way of distinguishing epistemic from non-epistemic norms entails that there are no purely epistemic positive norms. We argue that cases in which intuitively one is required to form a specific belief, can be explained without positing positive duties. In some cases the subject’s suspension of judgment is grounded in a violation of a negative epistemic norm, and in other cases one is morally or prudentially required to believe.

items.title: Cadre conceptuel pour la résolution d’une classe de conflits de valeurs.
items.abstract: Nous proposons dans cet article un cadre conceptuel pour la résolution d’une classe de conflits de valeurs. Une telle méthodologie est fondée sur la notion de matrices de concepts (Franceschi 2002). De manière préliminaire, nous décrivons les éléments fondamentaux des matrices de concepts. Nous nous intéressons ensuite à la représentation mathématique de ces dernières. Nous évoquons également le problème du germe de l’opposé, en relation avec cette modélisation. Nous nous attachons ensuite à décrire la classe de conflits de valeurs concernée par la présente méthode de résolution. Nous décrivons également les différentes étapes conduisant à la résolution de ce type de conflits de valeurs, en considérant plusieurs instances et en distinguant notamment entre les conflits fondés sur des degrés de valeurs objectifs ou subjectifs. Nous évoquons en outre les modalités d’application du produit de Nash dans le présent cadre conceptuel. Enfin, nous exposons l’application du présent modèle au dilemme du prisonnier, ainsi qu’au dilemme itéré du prisonnier.

items.title: РАСШИРЕННАЯ ОПТИМИЗИРОВАННАЯ МАТРИЦА ФУНДАМЕНТАЛЬНЫХ БАРЬЕРОВ (ОМФБ).
items.abstract: Настоящий препринт представляет Расширенную Оптимизированную Матрицу Фундаментальных Барьеров (ОМФБ) — систематизированный свод из 67 концептуальных проблем, демонстрирующих несостоятельность редукционистско-материалистической парадигмы в объяснении происхождения жизни, семантической информации, сознания и телеологической организации. Барьеры сгруппированы в семь взаимосвязанных категорий: информационно-семиотические, системно-структурные, телеолого-целевые, генетико-биохимические и интерфейсные, физико-космологические и квантовые, эпистемолого-методологические, когнитивно-лингвистические и смысловые. Каждый барьер описан по трёхчастной схеме: краткое определение, суть вызова и следствие для научной картины мира. Анализ стратегического веса показывает, что 82% барьеров (55 из 67) имеют парадигмальный характер и требуют смены онтологических оснований науки. Ключевыми узлами кризиса выступают проблемы семиозиса, телеологии и сознания. ОМФБ предлагается в качестве диагностического инструмента и дорожной карты для построения постредукционистской научной парадигмы. Ключевые слова: .

items.title: Del Símbolo a la Estructura: Teoría de la Habitabilidad Dinámica de la Conciencia.
items.abstract: La Teoría de la Habitabilidad Dinámica de la Conciencia (THDC) propone un desplazamiento conceptual en el estudio de la conciencia: desde el análisis del contenido fenomenológico hacia la evaluación de la estructura del sistema que lo sostiene. A partir de un diálogo crítico con la psicología analítica de Carl Gustav Jung, el modelo reformula conceptos como sombra, ánima, ánimus, self e individuación en términos de variables estructurales (coherencia integrativa h, urgencia U, reactividad R, presencia corporal B y amplitud temporal subjetiva Ts) y los evalúa en función de su impacto sobre la habitabilidad H del campo consciente. La habitabilidad se define como la capacidad del sistema para sostener su dinámica sin pérdida de coherencia, regulación o continuidad experiencial, y se propone como criterio de segundo orden para distinguir entre intensidad y transformación, y entre reorganización y desorganización. El modelo se sitúa en un nivel de formalización pre-matemático riguroso y es compatible con enfoques contemporáneos en neurociencia, ciencias cognitivas y teoría de sistemas.

items.title: Dark Light of the Monad.
items.abstract: Science does an excellent job of describing dark matter in that it does "serve mainly as expressions of our ignorance, much as the marking of early maps with terra incognita". Therefore, it recognises that it appears dark to unfathomable science to "see" or understand the gradations of subtle light energy which lies behind the matter which it at present does see. Physics doesn’t currently point toward hidden forms of light behind matter; instead, it points toward non-luminous mass-energy components that interact gravitationally but not electromagnetically. -/- "Nature abhors a vacuum", this occultism fully recognises, and it is explained as the medium or mode of transmission of one state of energy/light, spirit/matter from one state and plane to another, thus resulting in some transmutation of some description or other.

items.title: Understanding School Leadership in Elementary Schools Using Ordinal Correlation and K-Medians Clustering.
items.pub: Indonesian Journal of Educational Research and Review 8 (3):651-662.
items.venue: Indonesian Journal of Educational Research and Review
items.abstract: School leadership plays a critical role in shaping instructional quality and institutional performance in elementary education. This study aims to examine school leaders’ competencies in leading, managing, and developing teachers in Hindang District, Leyte, Philippines, and to analyze the relationships among these competencies. A descriptive–correlational design was employed using complete enumeration of 121 elementary school teachers. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation, and K-medians clustering. The findings indicate that school leaders are generally perceived as “very satisfactory” in leading (Median=4), managing (Median=4), and developing teachers (Median=4). Correlation analysis reveals significant positive relationships among the three competencies, indicating that effective leadership operates as an integrated system. Cluster analysis identifies distinct groups of teachers who perceive leadership competencies as either “outstanding” or “very satisfactory,” reflecting variations in perceived effectiveness. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening leadership competencies through continuous professional development and management training to enhance school performance.

items.title: Structural Inevitability and the Archetypal Psyche: From Predator Logic to Collective Mind.
items.abstract: This paper argues that Carl Gustav Jung’s archetypes are not merely cultural constructs, evolutionary residues, or private psychological projections, but mythic expressions of a deeper generative grammar that unfolds across scales of natural organisation. By grammar I do not mean language alone. I mean the invisible ontological support that constrains without mechanically predetermining the forms through which reality can become expressed. Grammar is not itself another object among the objects it structures and therefore is never encountered directly: we encounter its expressions. We hear sentences and meanings rather than grammar itself; we encounter camouflage and mimicry in biology, strategic misdirection in behaviour, the lie in language, and the Trickster in myth. These phenomena are neither identical nor reducible to one another. They are scale-specific expressions of recurrent relational possibilities within a constrained field of becoming. The archetype, on this account, is grammar becoming mythically legible to consciousness. -/- The paper further argues that Jung’s own archaeological model — his account of the collective unconscious as accumulated psychic sediment laid down over evolutionary time — is insufficiently generative. Accumulation alone cannot explain structure, any more than a heap of sediment can explain an arch. Just as DNA carries evolutionary history only because a material architecture can read, regulate, and express it, the archaeology of the psyche presupposes an architecture that is not itself merely psychological. The structuring principle must therefore be sought not only in inherited residues but in a generative dynamic active now, at every level of organisation. -/- I develop this claim through the interplay of emergence and dissolution, drawing on Ilya Prigogine’s theory of dissipative structures, Alfred North Whitehead’s process philosophy, theories of generative linguistic constraint, cross-species risk modelling, Adam Smith’s impartial spectator, Daniel Dennett’s intentional stance, and the mythological figures of Odysseus and the Trickster. The argument is not that psychological archetypes are literally thermodynamic structures, nor that particular myths are physically predetermined. It is that reality is generative under constraint, and that recurrent relational grammars become differently expressed at physical, biological, cognitive, linguistic, social, and mythic scales.
