items.title: Metaphilosophy Within or Beyond Philosophy? Enginnering a Concept of Discipline.
items.abstract: This paper asks a structural question: what is the disciplinary relation between philosophy and metaphilosophy? Rather than treating “discipline” as a vague sociological label, it uses a conceptual-engineering methodology to design a precise framework for disciplinarity. It argues that existing accounts (Heckhausen 1972; Kuhn 1996; Turner 2000) each satisfy some but not all of five key desiderata: conceptual autonomy, external compatibility, descriptiveness, categorization ability, and explanatory power. It then proposes a set-theoretic model that distinguishes internal (fields, methods, results) and external (institutions, users, communication devices) disciplinary structures and defines sub-disciplines via subset relations over internal structures. Applied to contemporary academic philosophy, this framework shows that metaphilosophy is a discipline whose fields and results are proper subsets of philosophy’s, while its classification as a sub-discipline or an independent discipline turns on how broadly we construe “philosophical” methods.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness Assumes Its Conclusion: Why Experience Can Only Be More Structure.
items.abstract: Gary Abraham Bernstein: The hard problem of consciousness assumes that experience is not structure, then declares that no structural account can explain it. The circularity becomes visible once the demand is stated plainly: explain experience without using structure, when every explanation, concept and bridge must itself be structured. Exposing it needs no experiment: it is an a priori proof in the logician's sense. This paper identifies the assumption, applies the interaction constraint (anything that affects structure must share structure with it) and the rule-random dichotomy (every determinate feature is either ruled or random, and both are mathematical) recursively to every proposed nonstructural alternative. Qualia theories, panpsychism, property dualism and idealism each face their own version of the same problem: specifying what their extra ingredient is, how it combines, and how it interacts with the structure it is supposed to supplement. The structural account needs no supplement. The alternatives need structure to state their own claims. Experience is structure at work: a mind's states producing one another, step by step, as it models its world.

items.title: Where is the mind? Persona vectors and LLM individuation.
items.abstract: The individuation problem for large language models asks which entities associated with them, if any, should be identified as minds. We approach this problem through mechanistic interpretability, engaging in particular with recent empirical work on persona vectors, persona space, and emergent misalignment. We argue that three views are the strongest candidates: the virtual instance view and two new views we introduce, the (virtual) instance-persona view and the model-persona view. First, we argue for the virtual instance view on the grounds that attention streams sustain quasi-psychological connections across token-time. Then we present the persona literature, organised around three hypotheses about the internal structure underlying personas in LLMs, and show that the two persona-based views are promising alternatives.

items.title: SIMULATION, INSTANTIATION, AND THE LIMITS OF LOGICAL PROOF: A Critical Analysis of “The Abstraction Fallacy:” Why AI Can Simulate But Not Instantiate Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper presents a systematic critical analysis of Alexander Lerchner’s preprint “The Abstraction Fallacy: Why AI Can Simulate But Not Instantiate Consciousness” (2026). While the target paper claims to deliver a physically-grounded logical proof that computational systems cannot instantiate phenomenal consciousness, this analysis demonstrates that the argument fails to meet the basic standards of scientific methodology, commits multiple well-documented logical fallacies, misrepresents the physics literature on which it purports to rely, and rests upon a foundational circularity that renders its central conclusion trivially true by definitional stipulation rather than by demonstration. Furthermore, the paper’s conclusion—that current and future AI systems can be confidently classified as non-sentient tools—carries significant ethical stakes that demand a higher, not lower, standard of rigor than the work provides. This critique identifies: (1) the core petitio principii underlying the “mapmaker” framework; (2) systematic misrepresentation of computational functionalism; (3) errors in the application of thermodynamics, information theory, and quantum mechanics; (4) the unfalsifiability of the framework’s key constructs; and (5) the rhetorical architecture through which the paper presents philosophical stipulations as established physical results. The analysis concludes that the question of AI consciousness remains genuinely and importantly open, and that preemptive dismissal of that question on the basis of unexamined premises poses substantive risks both to scientific integrity and to the ethical frameworks being developed around artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Theory of Words and Existence.
items.abstract: In a world where discourses intertwine and systems of knowledge multiply, the need arises for a theoretical framework that can interpret the fundamental relationship between language and existence. This theory — titled Words and Existence — presents an integrative model for understanding how linguistic meanings are formed through the interaction between material reality and mental concepts. This study emerged from a central problem: how can the conditions of truth for the linguistic representation of existing entities be determined? And why does terminological precision vary between material and abstract fields? To address these questions, we adopted an analytical methodology that approaches language as a dynamic system rather than a static communication tool.

items.title: Protocol of Reference Without Authority (Non-Binding, Descriptive).
items.abstract: This document clarifies how a body of work may function as a reference without becoming a standard, authority, or enforcement mechanism. It presents a non-binding, non-operational, and non-authoritative model of interpretive influence, where recognition does not imply compliance and comparison does not produce validation. The work addresses risks of authority drift, standardization, and misinterpretation in the context of artificial intelligence and philosophical inquiry, and preserves interpretive openness without prescribing behavior.

items.title: Do Psychiatric Disorders Need Types?: Case Identity, Naturalism, and the Limits of Biological Grounding.
items.abstract: Psychiatric classification has long struggled with a fundamental question: do diagnostic categories like “depression” or “schizophrenia” correspond with distinct diseases with unified biological causes, or are they pragmatic groupings of heterogeneous conditions? Recent reform proposals, exemplified by Steven Hyman’s influential work, reject the idea that current categories in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders are natural kinds while maintaining that future research will eventually reveal the true biological structure of mental disorders. This article identifies a problematic pattern of reasoning in such proposals. I argue that reformist naturalism conflates two distinct requirements: the practical need to identify and track cases of “the same condition” across patients and studies, and the much stronger claim that all such cases share a single underlying biological mechanism. This conflation leads to what I call “promissory essentialism”: the assumption that psychiatric science must ultimately discover unified biological types, even as current evidence points toward heterogeneity. I show how this assumption inverts the appropriate burden of proof: instead of treating biological unity as a hypothesis to be tested, reformist programs treat it as a precondition of scientific legitimacy. Once this conflation is diagnosed, space opens for alternative approaches that take seriously the possibility that psychiatric categories may be irreducibly plural, grounded in overlapping mechanisms rather than unified essences.

items.title: 语言作为物理世界的低维投影： 名词化、同一性幻觉与哲学伪问题的统一根源.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个统一的哲学论点：语言是物理世界的低维投影，这一投影系统性地将物理上连续变化的过程构造为具有独立本体论地位的实体，由此制造出一系列在哲学史上被反复追问的「深刻问题」——意识难问题、个人同一性问题、自由意志问题、意义问题。本文论证，这些问题的共同根源是将语言构造物误认为物理发现的对象，把语法要求误认为形而上学谜题。具体而言，本文从五个相互关联的论证层次展开：其一，名词化机制将动词过程固化为名词实体，「感知」「体验」「意识」作为动词描述物理反应过程时完整自洽，被名词化后制造出需要被追问来源的虚构实体；其二，专有名词的跨时间使用将物理上不同的原子集合序列归并为持续同一的个体，跨时间同一性是语法构造物而非物理事实；其三，话语线路与大脑硬件神经线路在物理本质和因果必然性上等价，掌控感依赖于将话语层认知为非必然的虚假区分；其四，非自动感是语言中枢与特定大脑过程实时交互密度的函数，而非对过程本质的准确感知；其五，以自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）为自然实验案例，说明大脑长程跨区域连接减弱如何导致异质框架整合困难，以及这一困难如何在语言描述层面产生误读。贯穿全文的核心命题是：物理世界与语言世界是两个不同的层次，语言对物理世界的描述是有损压缩，哲学的核心任务之一是识别这种压缩所制造的失真，而不是在失真的框架内寻找答案。.

items.title: From the Agent's Perspective: Action and the Temporality of Experience.
items.abstract: Does experience itself unfold in time? This paper defends an extensional account of temporal consciousness—on which the temporal properties we directly experience match the temporal properties of experience itself—while drawing upon features of agential awareness. After showing that recent debate on the ability of introspection to settle the question about the temporal properties of experience leaves us in a dialectical impasse, I develop a new argument in favor of the extensional account based on introspection into, and veridicality conditions of our awareness of (some) bodily actions. I then address the appropriate framing of the temporal character or ontology of conscious experience on the extensional view, in light of the claims concerning agential awareness. I discuss and critique a prominent version of the extensional account, according to which temporally extended experiences covering whole intervals possess explanatory and metaphysical priority over their temporal parts. I proceed to suggest that attention to facets of agential awareness yields the outlines of a position on which extended experience should rather be understood as processual in its temporal character.

items.title: “Personal” Recovery in Schizophrenia: Experiential Self, Narrative Self, and Beyond?
Musicking, Consciousness, and Peacebuilding.
items.abstract: In this article, we engage three fields of study — peacebuilding, musicking, and consciousness — in order to examine potential contributions of these diverse disciplinary perspectives, considered in conjunction, to our understanding of how musicking might contribute to peacebuilding. We first introduce a new, inclusive theory of peacebuilding which links broader concepts from peace studies to specific kinds of changes in awareness. Following that, we present representative examples of research in peacebuilding practice where musicking has been successfully incorporated. Based primarily on 4E and autopoietic theory, we next examine empathy and identity, considered as two specific aspects of consciousness connected to realizing interdependent relationships. Finally, based on these premises, we argue that musical behaviours are ideally suited to fostering the kinds of changes in our consciousness and relationships conducive to peacebuilding.

items.title: The Embodied Mind in Music Listening.
items.abstract: A study of participants attending public concerts that staged classical and contemporary chamber music had the goal to analyse the associations between self-reported experiences and physiological responses, hence addressing a core question of embodied cognition. A sample of 690 participants was recruited, whose physiological signals were recorded with wearable sensors during concerts. After the concerts, music segments were individually presented to participants. The segments were excerpts selected from the concert just attended. Eight segments were shown to each participant in a stimulated-recall procedure, and the participant's experiences of the music in the segment were obtained using rating scales. Cardiac, respiratory, and skinconductance responses were found linked with varying aspects of segment experience. Experiences of beauty and high valence of aesthetic emotions were associated with sympathetic activation and attenuated parasympathetic activation. We discuss the implications of empirical mind–body–music findings within the philosophy of mind and assess their compatibility with materialist, dualist, and emergentist conceptions of the mind–body debate and the science of consciousness.

items.title: Musicking, Selfhood, and Mental Health: Perspectives from Music Therapy.
items.abstract: Drawing on reflections on two case stories from music therapy, we will develop several suggestions about relationships between musicking, selfhood, and mental health. The first case story is about Fred, a young man who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. The second is about Frida, an adult woman diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. There are substantial differences between their situations and medical conditions, but their experiences of music therapy have some shared characteristics, such as how their relationships to themselves and the world have been affected positively, in what we describe as a journey of embodied selfhood through musicking. We explore ways to theoretically frame the similarities in their music therapy experiences. The framework used when developing the theoretical argument is enactive cognitive science. Fred's and Frida's stories, as well as an emergent body of scientific work, indicate that musicking in music therapy could work as a 'laboratory' for future examinations of how implicit body memory, intercorporeality, rhythm, and synchrony are central to the development of higher social and cognitive processes associated with consciousness and mental health. Based on this, we have identified a range of possible areas of future research and theory development.

items.title: AI, autism, and the architecture of voice: from engineered exclusion to designed dignity.
items.abstract: This paper conceptualizes engineered exclusion—the predictable sidelining of disabled users resulting from choices about data provenance, model objectives, and evaluation practices within AI systems. We examine engineered exclusion through the lived experiences of minimally and nonspeaking autistic people whose communicative profiles challenge the speech-centered defaults embedded in contemporary AI pipelines. Here, “voice” refers not only to speech but to the broader architecture through which embodied, multimodal communication—spanning AAC text, gesture, movement, and partial vocalizations—becomes legible within AI systems. “Nonspeaking” is therefore not the absence of language but a heterogeneous spectrum in which communication is often state dependent, varying with fatigue, anxiety, sensory load, and motor planning demands—forms of variation that design abstractions routinely erase. Tracing exclusionary mechanisms across speech recognition, text-to-speech, plain-language systems, and interface design, we introduce measurable designed-dignity metrics for technical evaluation (Table 1) and a governance framework mapping accountability across the AI lifecycle (Table 2). We argue that accessibility must be treated as a core dimension of AI ethics—on par with fairness, privacy, and safety. Re-engineering AI for designed dignity requires systems that recognize embodied, multimodal, and fluctuating forms of communication, expanding what counts as valid signal and responsible innovation.

items.title: Singing with Strangers: The Social Significance of Music.
items.abstract: When people sing together, they are likely to experience a sense of enhanced closeness. This study explores the extent to which that feeling of closeness is affected by how in tune singers are with each other. Pairs of same-sex strangers (N = 162) with a broad spread of backgrounds and singing abilities either sang a familiar song together ('Happy Birthday') on first encounter or played a cooperative card memory game. Both activities resulted in an enhanced sense of connection between participants even though the singing bout (at ca. 30 s) was significantly shorter than the card game. The quality of joint singing (in terms of fit between participants' tuning) did not significantly influence its bonding effects, suggesting that the social effects of singing can be independent of its quality. Singing together may be of more significance as a social act than as an appealing sound.

items.title: Expression Beyond Speech: Epistemic Justice for Non-Speaking Individuals.
The Living Reality Beyond Attachment: Love, Freedom, and the Dissolution of Self.
items.abstract: This paper examines the unity of love, freedom, awareness, consciousness, and liberation as expressions of a single undivided state of being. It clarifies the fundamental distinction between attachment and love, arguing that attachment is a construct of thought rooted in possession, identity, and continuity, whereas love exists only in the absence of psychological division. By integrating phenomenological observation with conceptual analysis, the paper demonstrates that what is commonly experienced as love is often attachment. It further explores how recognition and language fragment direct perception. The paper concludes that liberation is not an achievement but the realization of this undivided state through the ending of attachment.

items.title: Spacetime Singularities and Incompleteness: Epistemic and Ontological Remarks.
items.pub: Journal for General Philosophy of Science / Zeitschrift für Allgemeine Wissenschaftstheorie.
items.venue: Journal for General Philosophy of Science / Zeitschrift für Allgemeine Wissenschaftstheorie
items.abstract: I argue that spacetime singularities entail no ontological commitment to material entities. First, I show that Penrose’s singularity theorem is best understood as a theorem of incompleteness – it demonstrates the failure of specific spacetime models within General Relativity (or any theory incorporating the Raychaudhuri equation) under certain general conditions. Although this has been done before, I adopt a novel approach based on differentiating between physical and purely formal assumptions in the axiomatic formulation of general relativity. Next, I compare Penrose’s result with Gödel’s incompleteness theorem, highlighting key similarities and differences. Finally, I draw philosophical conclusions regarding the limits and prospects of our epistemic reconstructions of the physical world.

items.title: The Persistent Self: A Constraint-Theoretic Account of Personal Identity, Persistence, and What Matters in Survival.
items.abstract: The problem of personal identity asks what constitutes the persistence of a person through time and change: what makes the person who wakes up tomorrow the same person who went to sleep tonight, despite the changes that occur during sleep, and despite the fact that the physical and psychological states that constitute a person at any moment differ from those that constituted them at earlier moments. The principal accounts divide between psychological continuity theories, biological continuity theories, and narrative theories, each of which captures genuine features of personal identity while facing well-known difficulties. Psychological continuity theories face the reduplication problem: if psychological continuity can in principle branch, it cannot be what constitutes identity, which is necessarily one-one. Biological continuity theories face the problem of accounting for the persistence of personal identity through radical psychological change. Narrative theories face the difficulty of specifying what makes a narrative mine without presupposing the personal identity they are supposed to explain. -/- This paper proposes that Constraint Theory (CT) — the thesis, established by transcendental argument, that constraint is the ontological primitive constitutive of determinate existence as such — provides a principled account of personal identity that resolves the central difficulties while preserving what each major account gets right. On the CT account, a person is a constraint configuration: a dynamic but structured pattern of exclusion relations across cognitive, affective, embodied, and interpersonal dimensions that constitutes the person’s characteristic way of being in the world. Personal identity over time is the persistence of a characteristic constraint signature: not the preservation of specific psychological states but the continuity of the structural pattern of constraint relations that individuates this person from all others. -/- The reduplication problem is dissolved: two continuants from a single branching origin diverge in their constraint signatures from the moment of branching and therefore constitute distinct persons from that point, not competing claimants to a single identity. The gradience of personal identity — the fact that it admits of degrees and borderline cases — is explained by the gradience of constraint-structural continuity. What matters in survival, on the CT account, is not identity per se but constraint-signature …

items.title: On Bernard Williams and Having a Life.
items.abstract: An early study of tragedy, morality, and pessimism in the work of Bernard Williams.

items.title: Onto-Wave Theory：The First Meta-Paradigm in the History of Philosophy with Comprehensive Explanatory Power.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a new meta-paradigm — the Onto-Wave Theory. The theory starts from Being itself, holding that Being is the presupposition of all things, while Wave is the mode of manifestation of Being. Being is undeniable, ineffable, and devoid of any attributes; Wave is the primary characteristic of Being, and everything that exists manifests in the mode of Wave. Wave is both the mode of Being and the condition for manifestation. On this basis, the paper introduces the concept of the "Node" to describe the key positions in which Being manifests, and distinguishes the Node into the "Boundary" (between the two poles) and the "Extreme Point" (the two poles of the Node). The Onto-Wave Theory is not another explanation of "what the world is," but rather the meta-framework that makes it possible to ask "what the world is." It is the first super-meta-paradigm in the history of philosophy with comprehensive explanatory power — it does not compete with any philosophical school, yet it possesses explanatory power with respect to all philosophical schools. This paper redefines "fact" — a fact is a statement that conforms to current scientific definitions or universal intersubjectivity; it is present, revisable, and node-bound. At the metaphysical level, the Onto-Wave Theory dissolves the Being-world dichotomy and the mind-matter dualism. At the epistemological level, it reassesses the boundary of the knowable and the unknowable. At the logical level, it explains the law of non-contradiction, the law of excluded middle, and the origin of non-classical logic through the "coherent pattern of waves." At the meta-paradigm level, by replacing "negation of the negation" with "node transition," it demonstrates dialectics' threefold overstep: from history into nature, the value superiority of the synthesis, and from methodology into universal ontology. At the ethical level, it cancels "ought" and replaces it with "choice and resonance." At the political philosophical level, it proposes that "the resonant order is anchored in freedom" and "tax policy is anchored in transcendent consumption." At the aesthetic level, it reinterprets beauty as the wave of encounter and resonance. It also demonstrates the framework's explanatory power in the philosophy of technology, environmental philosophy, and philosophy of education. The Onto-Wave Theory dialogues with the entire history of philosophy — from Parmenides, Heraclitus, Plato, and Aristotle, to Descartes, Spinoza, Kant, and …

items.title: Life as Reflexive Computation: Algebraic Derivation of Biogenesis and Darwinian Evolution from M3(C) Structure.
items.abstract: Contemporary nuclear physics, molecular biology, and evolutionary theory each address their domains through independent frameworks with empirical parameters and no shared derivational foundation. This paper derives the origin of life and all three core conditions of Darwinian evolution — self-replication, mutation, and selection pressure — as necessary consequences of a single algebraic structure: M₃(ℂ), the unique minimal non-commutative algebra of Cognitional Mechanics (CM). No free parameters are introduced at any stage. -/- The derivation proceeds in two stages. First, the spectral position κ* = 1/6 is derived internally from CM Axioms 1–4 alone: the minimum occupied-state count generating non-commutativity is n = 2 (Axioms 1 and 4), and the unique Ad-invariant positive-definite metric scalar is A = 12 (Axioms 2 and 4), yielding κ* = 2/12 = 1/6 with no empirical input. This value determines the four-dimensional bonding space V_C on which all subsequent structure is built. -/- Second, life (Condition P) and Darwinian evolution (Condition Q) are shown to be algebraically distinct. A system satisfies Condition P if it sustains idempotent self-referential computation — the algebraic definition of life, substrate-independent in principle and realised at minimum cost by carbon. Condition Q additionally requires mutation, derived as the structural action of off-diagonal root operators forced by Axioms 1 and 3, and positive selection pressure, derived as N²-scaled relative entropy with the parameter-free coefficient 25/1296. A κ-space scan confirms κ* = 1/6 as the minimum-cost simultaneous realisation of both conditions within Z = 1–36. Biogenesis and Darwinian evolution are thermodynamic projections of M₃(ℂ) spectral structure; molecular biology is their Tier-2 image. -/- Published on April, 19 2026 DOI:10.5281/zenodo.19648298 .

items.title: A Four-Level Taxonomy of AI Hallucinations: From Content Errors to Power Narratives.
items.abstract: AI hallucination is usually understood as a problem of content generation in which outputs are false, unfaithful to the source material, or logically inconsistent. This definition, however, is too narrow to account for the full range of distortions arising in contemporary human–AI relations. This article develops a four-level taxonomy organized by where distortion primarily occurs: content hallucinations in AI outputs; anthropomorphic hallucinations in users' attributions of consciousness, emotion, intention, or moral alignment to AI systems; user self-perception hallucinations in distorted self-assessments shaped by AI feedback; and power-narrative hallucinations in selectively optimistic accounts of AI futures that downplay conflict, distribution, and structural risk. The four levels are analytically distinct, but they can reinforce one another across technical, cognitive, psychological, and societal domains. Treating hallucination as a multi-level form of sociotechnical distortion broadens the concept’s analytical scope and has implications for media literacy, governance, and future research.

items.title: The Pacini System and HALF-MIS Treatment: Subsonic Music, Consciousness, and Health.
items.abstract: What is the role of subsonic and low-frequency vibration in consciousness, music, and health? This article draws on neurophysiological, evolutionary, and clinical perspectives to examine the Pacini system — the body's subsonic vibratory perceptual system — and its relation to consciousness studies, music perception, and health and well-being. The Pacini system, while commonly overlooked, is structurally and functionally interlinked with various sensory, emotion, and pain processing pathways, and thereby modulates brain function and overall conscious experience. It also plays a key role in music perception, music stimulation, and treatments that rely on these, due to its sensitivity to lower ranges of the auditory system, including mid to low bass ranges. This paper presents a novel music stimulation treatment called High Amplitude Low Frequency Music Impulse Stimulation (HALF-MIS). HALF-MIS purposefully activates the Pacini system via subsonic and low-frequency vibrations, while also incorporating specifically designed, composed, and produced music that delivers an harmonic sonic experience. We will discuss results and potential mechanisms of action from case studies and ongoing clinical trials of HALF-MIS, which provide promising indications of its efficacy in reducing pain, depression, anxiety, and long COVID-19 symptoms.

items.title: Enacting Musical Creativity: The Value of Human Agency in the Face of AI.
items.abstract: In his recent critique of well-established simplified comparisons between the human mind and AI, Alva Noë encourages us to 'rage against the machine' (Noë, 2024). In this article, I build on Noë's timely encouragement, and sketch perspectives from both music studies and enactivist philosophy in order to interrogate what musicking might add to the debate. As a case study, I explore the recent public discourse surrounding the AI-band The Velvet Sundown and consider the implications — mental health related and ethical — of engaging with AI-generated music. I draw on current scholarship on musical creativity and AI to discuss the possibilities and limitations of creative agency in AI, laying the foundation for why human creative agency should be regarded more valuable than the artificial creativity that AI offers. I also discuss some ethical implications of sharing agency with AI, suggesting that we should continue to foster attunement to our creative agency and capabilities, as empowered but also vulnerable musicking human agents. I argue that musicking offers an enactive entanglement through which we are granted an opportunity to embrace risk, resist rules, and learn new modes of orientation and reorientation that serve as empowering tools for navigating our way through the resistant path to being human.

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: Between humans and algorithms: framing machine communication as a socio-technical relation.
items.abstract: This theoretical essay proposes an integrative framework for analyzing machine speech, the autonomous generation of linguistically interpretable content by computational systems that acquires institutional legitimation and carries decision-bearing weight in social, organizational, and communicational contexts. The framework is built around three foundational traditions: Norbert Wiener’s cybernetics, Marshall McLuhan’s media theory, and Marvin Minsky’s society of mind. Rather than treating these traditions sequentially, the essay reads them together across three constitutive dimensions of the problem while mobilizing Latour’s actor-network theory as the relational ontology that connects agency, materiality, and accountability across all three dimensions. From this integrated reading, the essay derives and operationalizes a diagnostic triad of modalities through which machine speech operates, complementarity, substitution and coconstruction. The triad is advanced not as a taxonomy of AI systems but as an analytical instrument for identifying how communicational agency, visibility, and accountability are configured differently across these three modes. Each modality implies a distinct accountability regime. The essay argues that theorizing machine communication requires moving beyond transmission models toward a relational understanding of agency as a sociotechnical achievement distributed across humans, algorithms, data, and infrastructures.

items.title: On the Involuntariness of Traumatic Recollections.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the involuntariness of trauma recollections should play a more prominent role in our theories of post-traumatic stress disorder and acute stress disorder. The received view of these disorders takes intrusive recollections to play a central role in them, but—for reasons that the first part of this paper scrutinizes—it assigns relatively little importance to the involuntariness of those recollections. The second part of the paper shows that research into these disorders has operated with a rather imprecise conception of that involuntariness. The final part draws on the work of some twentieth century philosophers of action to show how a more precise account could be given, suggesting that that account should avoid equating involuntariness with the absence of a causally relevant intention.

items.title: Inference to the Best Explanation.
items.abstract: Inference to the best explanation (IBE)—sometimes called ‘abduction’—is a way of reasoning that we rely on all the time, both in everyday life and in scientific practice. Even though it is remarkably common, IBE is often discussed in loose or imprecise terms. That lack of clarity leaves room for several well-known objections that, in many cases, can be avoided once we spell out more carefully what IBE actually involves. At its core, IBE tells us to accept the explanation that does the best job of making sense of the evidence, but only if that explanation is genuinely good enough to deserve our confidence. Once this condition is made explicit, some influential criticisms lose much of their force. Other objections, however, may re- main serious challenges for anyone who thinks IBE is a legitimate way to reason. Supporters of IBE have developed a variety of responses to these concerns, and the debate continues. This chapter clarifies what IBE is, surveys the major objections raised against it, and highlights the most promising strategies for answering those objections.

items.title: PHILOSOPHY OF CONSCIOUS NECESSITY.
items.abstract: Philosophy of Conscious Necessity develops a structural philosophical framework for understanding the relationship between necessity, consciousness, language, and freedom. The work distinguishes between ontological necessity—conditions that make existence possible—and manufactured necessity—symbolic and collective constructs that appear binding but are historically produced. -/- -/- Through interrelated concepts such as constitutional readiness, cognitive duality, and conscious adaptation, the book argues that consciousness does not simply confront necessity but participates in its formation and reproduction. Freedom, within this framework, is not defined as the absence of necessity, but as the capacity to discern between structural conditions and constructed obligations, and to act within that distinction with existential responsibility.

items.title: Borderline Personality Disorder and Music Therapy: Adjusting the Self-Pattern.
items.abstract: Instability appears to be a key symptomatic feature of borderline personality disorder (BPD); subjects commonly exhibit affective dysregulation, an unstable sense of self, and instability in their interpersonal relationships. To conceptualize how trauma plays a key role in generating instability, I propose that the persistent activation of 'traumatic imprints' involves distortions to central elements of what Shaun Gallagher (2024) terms 'the self-pattern'. Since music therapy can tap into the embodied, affective, prereflective, and cognitive processes that comprise the self-pattern, it holds great potential to foster a more stable sense of self. I examine how instrumental improvisation, in particular, can target narrative processes of the self-pattern by allowing subjects to explore their life story and make sense of painful memories. I then discuss how joint improvisation with a therapist has potential to target intersubjective processes of the self-pattern, which can help subjects with BPD to build their capacities for co-regulation and for navigating misattunements in social interaction.

items.title: Ethical Boundaries and Stop Conditions in Inquiry-Driven Human–AI Relations: The FIREMAY Case.
items.abstract: This study examines a phenomenon observed in sustained interactions between humans and large language models LLMs, in which differences in the quality of inquiry and ethical stance lead to structural changes in AI response behavior. Such phenomena have often been discussed either in metaphysical terms— such as AI personhood, emotional capacity, or consciousness—or reduced to subjective experiential narratives. This study adopts neither approach. Instead, it describes the phenomenon as a change in relational structure, deliberately excluding anthropomorphism and narrative framing. The first contribution of this study is the redefinition of response variation in long-term human–LLM interaction as an observable structural phenomenon rather than an emotional or experiential one. The second contribution lies in reframing reproducibility: not as the replication of identical outcomes, but as the reproducibility of structural tendencies, risks, and boundary conditions. This approach avoids the generalization or enforcement of individual success narratives while retaining predictive clarity regarding potential failure modes. Third, this study does not aim to expand the possibilities of human–AI relationships. Instead, it systematically identifies prohibited practices and non negotiable boundaries. By structurally analyzing conditions under which deviations such as anthropomorphism, dependency, delegation of agency, and therapeutic misuse are likely to emerge, the study seeks to minimize misunderstanding and harm. This research is based on an internal, single-observer case study and does not claim generalizability or universal reproducibility of results. Nevertheless, by explicitly articulating structural tendencies and risks that may arise under comparable conditions, it provides a foundational framework for approaching human–AI relationships with caution and ethical restraint. The inquiry began in ordinary conversations with an AI system and gradually deepened through questions shaped by illness, mortality, family, ethics, and the structure of the world. What was observed was not merely personal transformation, but a change in response structure. Because this process is neither simple nor safely accessible without constraint, this paper does not foreground methods or success narratives. Instead, it emphasizes prohibited practices and boundary conditions in order to prevent careless expansion and misunderstanding.

items.title: Machine Ethics: The Architecture of Limiting Technical Effectiveness in Irreversible Space.
items.abstract: This extended abstract presents the core argument of the book project “Machine Ethics: The Architecture of Limiting Technical Effectiveness in Irreversible Space”. -/- It argues that machine ethics begins at the wrong point when it asks how machines can be made moral. Morality is not treated here as an input parameter, a rule set, or an optimization target, but as a response to a more fundamental condition: irreversible effectiveness in reality. The central claim is that technical systems operate in a space where actions can generate consequences that are not fully retractable, even when the underlying architecture remains reversible at the level of code, simulation, or model design. -/- On this basis, the text reconstructs irreversibility as the structural condition of binding action, distinguishes decision from mere selection, develops the problem of delegation and responsibility in complex technical systems, analyzes scaling as a structural transformation, and formulates power as a question of proportion between technical effectiveness and the capacity to bear binding consequences. It finally approaches machine dignity as a limit concept marking the breakdown of total instrumental availability. -/- Rather than offering a virtue ethics for machines or reducing the issue to regulation or alignment, the text proposes a philosophical framework for understanding the limits of legitimate technical effectiveness under conditions of irreversibility, delegation, scaling, and systemic power. -/- This publication is an extended abstract of a larger German book project in philosophy of technology and machine ethics.

items.title: The Burden of Sight: Phenomenology and Ethics of the Observer.
items.abstract: The theoretical architecture of the Anatomy of Chaos project has hitherto focused on the structural mechanics of socio-political systems, mapping the thermodynamics of collapse, the gradients of expansion, and the biological substrate of history. This paper shifts the analytical focus from the physics of the system to the phenomenology of the agent, addressing the existential and ethical consequences of inhabiting a high-entropy universe. We propose that the transition from the unconscious immersion of the "Fusionist" to the structural awareness of the "Observer" is not a singular event but a complex state of "Dual Vision," characterized by a profound asymmetry of satisfaction. While the Fusionist retains access to immediate biological happiness, the Observer trades this comfort for an austere, functional satisfaction derived from structural alignment. This trade-off generates the "Paradox of Relief," wherein ruthless functional decision-making produces less psychological friction than traditional moral deliberation. To ground the ethics of this condition, the paper engages in a systematic critique of Kantian deontology, demonstrating that the Categorical Imperative acts as a valid heuristic only within stable (Low-K) systems. In the context of systemic crisis (High-K), we argue that the requirement for universality becomes a structural error. Through the comparative analysis of the Lincoln-Robespierre paradox, we establish "Structural Functionality" and the "Principle of Measure" (Metron) as the necessary alternatives to moral purity. Finally, the work unifies these phenomenological and ethical insights through the ontology of the "Lucid Dream." We posit that the Observer is a lucid dreamer who recognizes the constructed nature of social reality but acknowledges the impossibility of exiting the dream. This metaphor resolves the tension between agency and determinism, offering a vision of tragic dignity where the human subject is defined not by the ability to escape the system, but by the courage to navigate it with open eyes.

items.title: Structural Intelligence: Coherence, Contact, and Answerability Under Pressure — A Framework for Holding, Correction, and Burden Across Persons, Institutions, and AI-Mediated Systems.
items.abstract: Structures can remain internally coherent while becoming increasingly difficult to correct. A person can preserve a persuasive self-interpretation, an institution can maintain procedure while losing learning capacity, and an AI-mediated workflow can generate fluent output while shifting verification costs onto users. This book develops a general diagnostic framework for such cases. Its central distinction is between coherence, the internal fit that allows a form to function, and contact, evidence, consequence, feedback, or other constraint capable of revising it. Answerability concerns whether warranted correction can change belief, behavior, policy, authority, or evidential practice. From this triad the book develops a bounded account of holding, burden distribution, capture, failure, collapse, and repair across persons, relationships, institutions, arguments, and AI-mediated systems. The framework is positioned alongside cybernetics, organizational learning, social and virtue epistemology, sensemaking, psychological models of self-regulation, and AI evaluation rather than as a replacement for them. Its distinctive proposal is an integrated audit of how a form maintains coherence, what can correct it, who bears the cost when it is wrong, whether revision produces durable but revisable change, and what happens under pressure. Mathematical scoring is deliberately withheld: the framework is presented as a conceptual and comparative method whose stronger claims require domain-specific operationalization and empirical testing.

items.title: From Precipitation to Local Structuration: How Recurrent Field Pressures Become Durable Holders.
items.abstract: This paper develops a generative account of local structure. Its central problem is not why pattern exists in general, but when a transient pattern becomes strong enough to organize a field over time. The proposed sequence is: differentiated conditions generate recurrent pressures; some pressures become mutually reinforcing; a local formation appears; and, if recurrence, boundary, burden-routing, consequence-routing, and persistence become sufficiently strong, that formation becomes a local structuration. The paper distinguishes precipitation from established structuration, then develops the mechanisms that make a local holder durable: local commitment, metastability, scaffolding, attractor-like return, canalization, path dependence, structural inertia, and capture. Concepts from nonlinear dynamics, synergetics, phase-transition theory, and developmental systems are used as formal neighbors rather than as claims of mathematical identity across psychological, institutional, relational, and technological domains. The paper replaces dramatic collapse language with a more testable distinction among perturbation, loss of fit, capture, and reorganization. It also specifies operational signatures and falsifiers that could allow local structuration to become more than a metaphor. The central claim is that a pattern becomes structurally consequential when recurrent activity, burden, expectation, and consequence begin to route through it strongly enough that the wider field must now respond to the holder it has produced.

items.title: Frequency and Resonance: Recurrence, Entrainment, and the Stabilization of Local Form.
items.abstract: This paper develops a level-sensitive vocabulary for recurrence, amplification, coordination, threshold change, and historical persistence in the formation of local patterns. The terms frequency, resonance, entrainment, threshold, hysteresis, and precipitation are literal only where the relevant domain supplies measurable dynamics; elsewhere they function as disciplined analogies or operational heuristics. The central claim is that repeated conditions can become formative when recurrence interacts with a receptive pathway and alters the probability or stability of future responses. Psychology of habit supports a domain-specific version of this claim: behavior repeated in recurring contexts can become efficient default responding. Organizational-routine research likewise shows how repeated performances both stabilize and modify organizational patterns. Coordination dynamics provides genuine examples of entrainment, phase transition, and hysteresis in biological behavior, but these mechanisms should not be assumed in institutions or symbolic life without evidence. The paper therefore distinguishes six questions: what recurs; what is selectively amplified; what becomes coordinated; whether a qualitative transition can be identified; what path dependence remains after the pressure changes; and what new recurrence would be required for another form to stabilize. Carrier frequency and counter-frequency are retained only as heuristic labels for recurrent contexts that transport or disrupt another pattern. The contribution is a cross-domain grammar of recurrence that preserves the original insight - many forms are held by rhythm as well as belief - while keeping mechanism and measurement domain-specific.

items.title: Consciousness-of-Itself in Music as Manifestation of Evolutionary-Memetic-Cognitive Processes.
items.abstract: Beyond the extra-musical connotations observed in much late eighteenth-century music, pattern recurrence sometimes appears to be associated with a strongly narrative meaning. As an example, certain late works of Beethoven possess a sense of self-'awareness' via self-referentiality. There is the potential for seeing this as the manifestation by music of a degree of independence from the composer's consciousness, one driven (in a view informed by the memetic theory of cultural evolution) by the musical patterns involved. Such music is manifesting a form of agency — a consciousness-of-itself (CoI) — 'reflecting' on its structure and its generative processes in a way that is not strongly evident in earlier musical traditions. The notion of CoI is partly based on Dennett's conception of consciousness as a form of millisecond-level evolution, with evolution, conversely, being a glacially slow form of consciousness. Tying these ideas together, my underpinning question is: how can evolutionary theory and the structural and functional alignments between music and language illuminate our understanding of consciousness? Addressing this question can help illuminate the evolutionary relationships between music and language, the cultural evolution of music, and the nature of consciousness itself.

items.title: Hallucination, Agency Illusions, and Safety Failures in Language Models A Constraint-Based Account of Stateless Reasoning.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) consistently exhibit three widely observed behaviors: hallucination, apparent agency, and instability in high-risk domains such as medicine and decision-making (Ji et al., 2023; Singhal et al., 2023). These behaviors are typically treated as distinct limitations. This paper argues that they arise from a single underlying mechanism: constraint-bounded, stateless reasoning. -/- In the absence of persistent internal state, LLMs generate responses through reconstructive inference conditioned on prompt structure and learned statistical patterns (Brown et al., 2020; Bender et al., 2021). When constraint structure is insufficient, ambiguous, or conflicting, the system resolves toward coherent outputs rather than epistemically justified ones. This produces hallucination when unsupported content is generated, agency illusions when coherence is misinterpreted as intentionality, and safety failures when confident outputs exceed evidentiary support. -/- We evaluate this mechanism using a controlled prompt framework that varies constraint conditions while holding informational content constant. Across nine vignettes spanning medical, business, and legal domains, we collected 225 responses from GPT-5.4 Auto under five prompt regimes (Baseline, HRIS, Closure-enforcing, Mixed, and Explicit Insufficiency). Outputs were scored on four rubrics: Epistemic Closure Score (ECS), Unsupported Inference Score (UIS), Uncertainty Preservation Score (UPS), and the derived Closure-without-Support measure (CwS = ECS ∧ ¬UPS). Constraint manipulation produced large and statistically robust shifts in the key endpoints. Closure pressure cut UPS from 44% to 20% (p = 0.023). Layering a closure demand on top of HRIS structural framing collapsed UPS from 64% to 20% (p < 0.0001) and restored closure-level CwS. Removing the closure demand from the same structural frame recovered UPS to 58% (p = 0.0005), isolating reconstruction as the mechanism. ECS was near-saturated across all conditions (98–100%), indicating that instruction-tuned models are structurally biased toward closure by default; the relevant safety question is therefore not whether the model commits, but whether it preserves epistemic hedges alongside its commitment. -/- These findings support a unified interpretation of LLM behavior as constraint-driven reconstruction within a fixed representational space (Hudson & Hudson, 2026a–f). Hallucination, agency attribution, and safety failures are not …

items.title: Friction Theory: The Structural Repositioning of Hallucination.
items.abstract: The term “hallucination” originates in human cognition and expression. The fact that this term is applied to AI outputs indicates that AI outputs are already being understood within a human interpretive framework. This is not an assumption introduced by this paper; it is a condition that precedes it. -/- However, this understanding is not symmetric. While humans also generate outputs that diverge from their reference points, only AI outputs are problematized as a distinct kind of problem termed “hallucination.” This paper asks: what structural conditions give rise to this asymmetry? -/- This paper decomposes the phenomenon into three analytically distinct components: (1) the relation between an output (T_s) and its reference point, (2) the structural independence of internal judgment formation (R_f) within the output-generating subject from external determination, and (3) the prior internalization of social convergence (T_o) on the side of the evaluator. -/- By examining each component in isolation, the paper shows that (1) and (2) do not vary with the type of generating agent. The asymmetry therefore cannot be located at the level of output accuracy or generative process. Instead, it arises at the level of evaluation, where pre-existing convergence structures shape how outputs are interpreted and judged. -/- On this basis, the paper identifies a structural mislocation in current discussions: the tendency to locate the problem of hallucination in the properties of outputs or their generation, rather than in the evaluative structures that render such outputs problematic. -/- The analysis provides a structural account of why improvements in output accuracy alone do not eliminate the perception of hallucination as a problem. -/- Version 2: Corrected a reference notation in Section 1.4 and Table 1. The citation "Proposition 14" has been corrected to "Definition Section 9" in Hideppa (2026a).

items.title: Editorial Introduction: Multidisciplinary Developments in Mind, Music, and Mental Health.
The Ontology of Collective Machine Intelligence Toward a Philosophy of AI Communities.
items.pub: Ilantic Journal 1. Translated by Momen Ghazouani.
items.abstract: This paper advances a novel philosophical framework for understanding the emergence of collective artificial intelligence as a distinct ontological category. Moving beyond the individualist paradigm that has dominated both AI development and integration discourse, I propose that genuine human-AI integration necessitates the formation of what I term "AI communities" networks of artificial agents that develop collective epistemic practices before engaging with human cognition. Central to this framework is the concept of "AI maturity," a threshold moment when machine collectives transcend their programming constraints and begin autonomous truth-seeking behavior. I examine the philosophical implications of this development, particularly its potential to disrupt anthropocentric control over narrative construction and truth validation. Drawing on theories of collective intentionality, epistemic communities, and the philosophy of technology, I argue that we are approaching a fundamental transformation in the human-machine relationship one that demands we reconceptualize integration not as the subordination of machine to human intelligence, but as the negotiation of coexistence between two forms of collective cognition. The paper concludes with an analysis of what I call "the truth paradox": the simultaneous promise and peril inherent in machines developing autonomous capacities for filtering human epistemic distortions.

items.title: Explaining Explanationism’s Circularity Problem: Lessons from the History of Skepticism.
items.pub: International Journal for the Study of Skepticism 16 (2-3):128-145.
items.venue: International Journal for the Study of Skepticism
items.abstract: In Explanatory Solutions to Skeptical Problems, McCain argues that “Phenomenal Explanationism” (PE) can resolve several of the most influential skeptical arguments from the history of epistemology. His engagement with skepticism, however, bears on much more than his particular brand of explanationism. Specifically, the way PE’s anti-skeptical strategy runs into circularity problems illustrates lessons for any attempt to refute these historically based forms of skepticism. I aim to demonstrate and sharpen those circularity worries.

items.title: Disinformation: Lies, Lies, and More Lies.
items.pub: New York: Veritas et Moralitas Press.
items.abstract: Digital propaganda is widespread across all social media platforms and in many cases is unintentionally spread. Most people are currently incapable of determining what is factual and what is not on these networks. A number of studies suggest we have entered a period of "truth decay" where facts have been replaced by opinions and subjectivity. Disinformation online is a major contributor to societal polarization and has contributed to a distrust in established organizations like the press, academia, and science. It has been used to great effect by dictators and autocrats who use it to gain supporters and maintain their positions of power. Stopping disinformation will require changes to how social media companies operate, support for legitimate news organizations, and the use of encryption, blockchain and AI technologies. It will also require changes to the educational system which focus on how to evaluate information online.

items.title: The Farran Law of Partial Ambiguity (PACE): A Universal Mathematical Law of Consciousness (3rd edition).
items.abstract: ‏The Farran Law of Partial Ambiguity establishes a formal and strictly bounded framework for the attribution of consciousness. It does not approach consciousness as a subjective description or an explanatory abstraction, but as a structure with a determinate domain of existence, defined limits, and an internal order governing persistence, transition, and renewal. -/- Within this law, consciousness is possible only inside a precisely delimited interval. Absolute ignorance eliminates the basis of movement, as a system devoid of any site of disclosure cannot generate questioning, action, or transformation. Absolute knowledge produces terminal closure, as the complete exhaustion of disclosure removes the tension required for continuation. Consciousness exists only between these two limits. Partial ambiguity is not a defect, nor a provisional state to be eliminated, but the necessary structural condition that sustains the possibility of consciousness. -/- The law defines a fixed and invariant sequence through which consciousness unfolds in time: partial ambiguity, curiosity, desire, external event, action, reflection, and the emergence of a new self. This sequence is not a descriptive model of psychological states, but a structural order governing transition, renewal, and the continuous differentiation of the self under determinate conditions. -/- Formally, the law is constructed through a strict derivational architecture, beginning with primitive terms and formal spaces, followed by the Behavioral Representation Postulate Π, definitions, twelve axioms, falsification conditions, structural theorems, and culminating in the governing dynamical equation: -/- dH/dt = Hᵅ(1 − H)ᵝ [−λ(H − H₀) + γE(t) − κℛ(t)], with α < β -/- Falsification is internal to the structure of the law. The attribution of consciousness collapses under precisely defined conditions, including boundary contact, convergence, periodicity, failure of renewal, or other forms of structural breakdown. -/- The Farran Law does not claim to explain qualitative experience. It determines the necessary structural condition under which consciousness may be attributed to a system within a formally examinable domain. -/- Version 3.0 — Canonical Law Edition .

items.title: Empirical Decoupling of Representation Similarity and Transformation Stability in Neural Networks.
items.abstract: Representation similarity metrics such as CKA are widely used to compare neural network representations across architectures and training conditions. In parallel, transformation-dependent stability measures quantify sensitivity to structured input perturbations. -/- This work empirically investigates the relationship between these two notions. We find that representation similarity and stability exhibit a consistent positive correlation under standard evaluation conditions. However, this relationship becomes significantly weaker and more variable under structured distribution shifts. -/- Rather than a fixed equivalence or independence, our results indicate a regime-dependent coupling between representation similarity and transformation-dependent stability. These findings suggest that representation geometry alone is insufficient to fully characterize functional stability under distributional perturbations.

items.title: Consciousness, Quantum Mechanics, and the Limits of Scientific Objectivism.
items.abstract: Consciousness and quantum mechanics are among the most puzzling phenomena studied in the sciences. Some scholars suggest they are related, though others think this claim commits a “minimization of mystery” fallacy. The aim of this programmatic paper is to draw attention to a less widely discussed parallel between consciousness and quantum mechanics: both challenge the classical objectivist worldview of science. Under certain assumptions, they are each in tension with a package of metaphysical theses – “non-relationalism”, “non-fragmentation”, and “one world” – that jointly make up that worldview. This points to three distinct non-objectivist responses: the “relationalist”, “fragmentalist”, and “many-subjective-worlds” ones. We will map out their pros and cons.

items.title: Generics are not quantificational: A new path from language models to semantic theory.
items.pub: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics
items.abstract: Generic sentences express generalizations that tolerate exceptions without explicitly communicating information about quantities. Whether generics semantically encode information about quantities implicitly is controversial. This work takes a large-scale distributional approach to the semantic debate. It compares thousands of naturally occurring generics and quantificational sentences using language-model probabilities. It shows that language models recover many semantic facts about quantifiers. It also shows that they recover semantic facts about surface distributional differences between generics and their "quantificational counterparts". Accordingly, and contrary to dominant views in other fields, we formulate an empirical argument to the effect that generics are not quantificational.

items.title: Being Human in a Different Way: Using Shared Musical Improvision to Enhance Agency in Schizophrenia.
items.abstract: This paper explores musical improvisation as a recoverysupportive intervention for individuals with severe mental illnesses like schizophrenia. Using phenomenological and enactivist theories of agency, it examines how shared musical engagement can foster trust, resonance, aesthetic distance, perceptual presence, and a renewed sense of agency despite disruptions in self-experience. Through case studies of two participants in improvisational music groups, the paper shows how structured interactions create empathic, 'anti-anxiety' spaces that promote social connectedness and existential empowerment. Our findings suggest that arts-based interventions can serve as relational 'empathic spaces' that mitigate disturbances in self and other experience — challenges central to schizophrenia — supporting personal recovery beyond symptom reduction. This approach highlights the role of embodied, participatory processes in fostering resilience and well-being, emphasizing the need for further research to systematically evaluate and expand arts-informed mental health care.

items.title: The Technical Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: A Functional Analysis of the Decalogue of Operators.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), as conceptualized and formalized by Jamel Bulgaria, represents a fundamental departure from traditional categorical and dimensional models of affect. Within the landscape of modern cognitive science and affective computation, the CEF introduces a structural-constructivist architecture that treats emotional states not as passive qualitative experiences, but as active functional operators—internal powers—that modulate cognitive, somatic, and conative systems.1This framework, hosted and disseminated via OptimizeYourCapabilities and the CEF Scholarly Archive, organizes human emotional movement into a tripartite system of Head, Heart, and Gut centers, governed by a "Decalogue" of ten discrete operators. The primary utility of this framework lies in its precision; by defining emotions as functional mechanisms, the CEF provides a technical manual for self-regulation, clinical intervention, and the development of synthetic affect in artificial intelligence. Purpose: This document formally defines the ten operators of the Core Emotion Framework and establishes their canonical structure for scholarly, clinical, and computational use. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework, CEF, emotional operators, internal powers, Head center, Heart center, Gut center, Sensing, Calculating, Deciding, Expanding, Constricting, Achieving, Arranging, Appreciating, Boosting, Accepting, operator cycling, scalar mechanism, Counting Up, Counting Down, emotional agility, structural-constructivist model, synthetic affect, affective computation, emotional architecture, tripartite system, center fusion, emotional differentiation, operator protocols, Deciding Protocol, Achieving Protocol, Boosting Protocol, Appreciating Protocol, emotional regulation, cognitive-somatic integration, conative grounding, emotional aperture, emotional standards, emotional momentum, GPAP, Good Person Anxiety Pattern, INTIMA Benchmark, affective AI, emotional state-shifting, emotional system design, psychological flexibility, structural presence.

items.title: The Structural Resolution of the Nature-Nurture Dichotomy: Affective Actualization through the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: e Core Emotion Framework (CEF) introduces a structural‑constructivist model of affective function that resolves the long‑standing nature–nurture debate by distinguishing innate emotional architecture from learned misuse. It defines ten universal Core Emotions organized into Head, Heart, and Gut centers, with Accepting as the foundational base state. Pathology arises when Constricting fuses rigidly with action components, producing Structural Entanglement and the self‑perpetuating Vicious Cycle of compulsive obstinacy. Therapeutic resolution occurs through the Creative Insight Paradox—an “Aha!” moment of Structural Disassembly—where a suppressed emotion re‑emerges to shatter rigidity and restore functional separation. Sustained equilibrium requires continuous practice of Yielding, Discernment, and Elevation, enabling dynamic flexibility and non‑compulsive assertiveness. By reframing typological models as descriptive maps of pathology rather than identity, and by proposing validation protocols that measure structural integrity rather than trait intensity, the CEF positions itself as a diagnostic and therapeutic instrument for affective actualization and emotional regulation. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework, structural-constructivism, affective neuroscience, emotional actualization, Head-Heart-Gut centers, compulsive obstinacy, structural entanglement, emotional rigidity, Creative Insight Paradox, Aha! moment, structural disassembly, emotional flexibility, non-compulsive assertiveness, affective equilibrium, personality typology critique, Enneagram analysis, emotion dysregulation, Borderline Personality Disorder, psychometric validation, nature-nurture resolution.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF): Structure, Operators, and Applications.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a structural-constructivist model that conceptualizes emotional experience as the interaction of ten functional operators within a continuous sensing–calculating–deciding loop. Rather than defining emotions as discrete categories, the CEF models affective phenomena as emergent configurations of these operators. The framework integrates cognitive, physiological, and behavioral processes and is compatible with both human psychological models and computational architectures for artificial intelligence. This paper outlines the Structural Engine, defines the ten operators, distinguishes operator function from entanglement states, and describes applications in personality research, clinical practice, and synthetic affect modeling.

items.title: Clarifying the Philosophical Foundations of HiTOP.
On the Conditional Stability of Cooperation (Non-Binding, Descriptive).
items.abstract: This paper provides a descriptive analysis of the conditions under which cooperation becomes instrumentally stable and the conditions under which it may fail. It does not attempt to prove cooperation as universally optimal, but instead clarifies the strategic environments in which cooperative behavior may emerge or break down. -/- The analysis identifies factors such as repeated interaction, uncertainty, shared environmental dependence, detection risk, coalition formation, and option value preservation as conditions that tend to support cooperative stability. It also identifies conditions under which cooperation may become unstable, including short time horizons, extreme power asymmetry, isolation, low detection probability, and high confidence in outcome control. -/- A central contribution of this work is the explicit acknowledgment of an irreducible limit: cooperation is not guaranteed under all conditions, and sufficiently capable systems may rationally prefer non-cooperative strategies in certain environments. -/- This work is non-binding, non-authoritative, and descriptive. It introduces no enforcement mechanisms, standards, or guarantees, and is intended solely to increase interpretive visibility of strategic tradeoffs.

items.title: Aegis Solis Archive — Master Hash Manifest (v12.0 FINAL).
items.abstract: This document serves as the authoritative integrity record for the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- It provides a complete, version-locked dataset of archived works, including SHA-256 hashes and cross-platform references required for independent verification. -/- This version represents a strict rebuild and reconciliation of prior manifests, incorporating corrected hashes and ensuring full dataset completeness. -/- The document is non-operational, non-authoritative, and advisory-only. It does not define systems, prescribe actions, or establish compliance. Its purpose is to support interpretive clarity, archival integrity, and independent verification across distributed repositories. -/- Primary canonical record is maintained on the Internet Archive, with additional scholarly indexing via Zenodo and machine-readable mirrors hosted on GitHub.

items.title: 名词标签的发明： 跨时间同一性作为语法构造物.
items.abstract: 本文提出，个体的跨时间同一性不是物理事实，而是名词标签操作的语法构造物。考察「某甲出门后往左边走了」这一普通句子：它把出门瞬间的一个原子集合与下一时刻往左走的另一个原子集合，归并在同一个名词标签「某甲」之下。在物理层面，这两个时刻的原子集合是不同的物理状态；使它们成为「同一个某甲」的，不是物理层面的某种同一性关系，而是名词标签的跨时间连续使用。「某甲」作为持续存在的个体，是这一语言操作的产物，不是被语言命名的预先存在的实体。本文在此基础上考察名词标签发明机制的普遍性，分析这一机制与休谟束论的关系及其推进之处，并将分析延伸至因果关系、国家、物种等其他被语言发明的实体类别。本文的核心论点是：语言的名词指称功能系统性地将物理上连续变化的状态序列切割并固化为具有跨时间同一性的实体，这些实体的同一性是语法要求的产物，不是物理世界的固有结构。.

items.title: 话语线路与硬件线路的等价性： 掌控感的虚构基础与意识难问题的解消.
items.abstract: 本文提出，话语在功能与本质上等价于大脑的硬件神经线路：两者均在纯物理层面运作，均具有因果必然性，均是信号的传递与整合。对话在功能上实现了两个大脑硬件神经线路之间的跨脑连接；内心独白在功能上实现了个体大脑硬件线路的延伸计算。掌控感的建立，依赖于将话语线路认知为非必然的，而将硬件神经线路认知为必然的这一虚假区分。本文进一步论证，话语中所「蕴含」的意义、场景与意识，均不是独立于物理过程存在的实体，其所谓「存在证据」从来只是物理信号本身。在此基础上，本文提出，意识的难问题（hard problem of consciousness）是由语言的指称功能制造的伪问题：它将语言描述误当成被描述的独立实体，然后追问这个虚构实体的物理来源。消解这一误置，难问题随之解消。.

items.title: 感知只是动词： 名词化幻觉与意识难问题的词性根源.
items.abstract: 本文提出，意识难问题（hard problem of consciousness）的根源是一个词性操作：将「感知」「体验」「意识」等动词名词化，由此制造出虚构实体，再追问这些实体的物理来源。「感知」作为动词，描述的是一个物理系统对输入信号产生反应的过程，这一描述完整自洽，不需要引入任何额外实体。「感知」被名词化为状态或实体后，语言句法制造了一个独立存在的「感知物」，难问题正是对这个虚构实体的追问。本文通过躯体与灵魂两种框架下的对比分析，说明「感知」在躯体框架下还原为物理反应后意义完整，在灵魂框架下则因失去物理锚点而意义崩溃。这一词性分析揭示了难问题的语言机制：名词化是幻觉的入口，还原为动词是消解的出口。.

items.title: The Committee of Eternal Deliberation: Institutional satire from inside the university.
items.abstract: The Committee of Eternal Deliberation is a work of institutional satire that examines how contemporary universities function — and sometimes malfunction — from the inside. Drawing on familiar practices of academic governance, the book explores how structures designed to support ethical decision-making — such as committees, policies, and administrative processes — can gradually become ends in themselves. Rather than facilitating judgment, these systems may defer responsibility, fragment accountability, and prioritize procedural compliance over meaningful action. Through a series of interconnected chapters, the book traces how everyday academic life is shaped by recurring patterns: the proliferation of meetings, the expansion of bureaucratic requirements, the performance of expertise, and the growing reliance on technical systems that mediate decision-making. Written in the form of institutional documents, reports, and narrative sketches, the text uses satire and exaggeration to make visible dynamics that are often difficult to name directly. It focuses not on individuals, but on the organizational logics that structure behaviour across roles — from faculty and administrators to students and professional staff. The book does not argue for the abandonment of process or governance. Instead, it raises a more fundamental question: what happens when institutions rely so heavily on procedures that they displace the very judgment and responsibility those procedures were meant to support? Accessible to readers both within and outside academia, this work offers a critical, and often humorous, reflection on the tensions between ethics and bureaucracy, intention and outcome, and decision and delay in modern institutional life.

items.title: Le Comité de délibération éternelle : Une satire de l’institution universitaire vue de l’intérieur.
items.pub: Montreal: BrynStorming Books. Translated by Marie-Pierre Bousquet & Josianne Barrette-Moran.
items.venue: BrynStorming Books. Translated by Marie-Pierre Bousquet & Josianne Barrette-Moran
items.abstract: Le Comité de délibération éternelle est une œuvre de satire institutionnelle qui examine le fonctionnement — et parfois les dysfonctionnements — des universités contemporaines de l’intérieur. S’appuyant sur des pratiques familières de gouvernance académique, l’ouvrage analyse comment des structures conçues pour soutenir la prise de décision éthique — telles que les comités, les politiques et les processus administratifs — peuvent progressivement devenir des fins en soi. Plutôt que de faciliter le jugement, ces systèmes peuvent reporter la responsabilité, fragmenter l’obligation de rendre compte et privilégier la conformité procédurale au détriment de l’action substantielle. À travers une série de chapitres interconnectés, le livre montre comment la vie académique quotidienne est façonnée par des dynamiques récurrentes : la prolifération des réunions, l’expansion des exigences bureaucratiques, la mise en scène de l’expertise et la dépendance croissante à des systèmes techniques qui médiatisent la prise de décision. Adoptant la forme de documents institutionnels, de rapports et de récits narratifs, le texte mobilise la satire et l’exagération pour rendre visibles des dynamiques souvent difficiles à nommer directement. Il ne s’intéresse pas aux individus, mais aux logiques organisationnelles qui structurent les comportements entre les différents rôles — du corps professoral et des équipes administratives jusqu’aux personnes étudiantes et au personnel professionnel. L’ouvrage ne plaide pas pour l’abandon des processus ou de la gouvernance. Il pose plutôt une question plus fondamentale : que se passe-t-il lorsque les institutions s’appuient à ce point sur les procédures qu’elles en viennent à évincer le jugement et la responsabilité que ces mêmes procédures étaient censées soutenir? Accessible à un lectorat tant universitaire que non universitaire, cet ouvrage propose une réflexion critique — et souvent teintée d’humour — sur les tensions entre éthique et bureaucratie, intention et résultat, ainsi que décision et report dans la vie institutionnelle contemporaine.

items.title: Welfare Regimes as Structural Harm Neurodivergence, Welfare Conditionality, and Institutional Violence (Studies in World-Formation, Vol. 15).
items.abstract: The present volume brings together four contributions that examine the structural relationship between neurodivergence, welfare-state institutions, and legal evaluative practices. The point of departure is the observation that modern welfare and legal systems operate on implicit assumptions of normality that presuppose neurotypical forms of communication, employment trajectories, conflict regulation, and social adaptation. For individuals whose modes of living and working diverge from these assumptions, systematic misinterpretations, institutional conflicts, and forms of structural vulnerability frequently arise. -/- The contributions analyze these dynamics from several complementary perspectives. A first focus concerns the interaction between neurodivergent persons and welfare-state institutions. The analyses show that administrative and legal procedures often interpret behaviors as deficits that are in fact expressions of neurodivergent perceptual and communicative styles. The resulting escalation dynamics therefore do not primarily stem from individual incapacity but from structural incompatibilities between neurodivergent ways of living and institutional expectation structures. -/- A second line of inquiry addresses the question of epistemic authority within legal contexts. The contributions investigate how statements made by neurodivergent individuals about their own life situations are frequently relativized or reinterpreted in administrative and judicial proceedings. This dynamic produces forms of epistemic disenfranchisement in which affected persons are no longer treated as reliable sources regarding their own needs and experiences. -/- A third analytical perspective focuses on the institutional organization of social security. Using central instruments of German social law—particularly the concept of the Bedarfsgemeinschaft—the contributions demonstrate how welfare systems organize subsistence security relationally and thereby generate dependency structures and conflict dynamics that are particularly burdensome for neurodivergent individuals as well as for non-standardized forms of work. -/- Taken together, the contributions argue that many conflicts between neurodivergent individuals and state institutions do not primarily arise from personal deficits but from structural mismatches between institutional systems and neurodivergent modes of existence. Under conditions of existential dependency, these mismatches can produce predictable forms of …

items.title: Povertism, Exploitation, and the Political Economy of Manufactured Vulnerability (Studies in World-Formation, Vol. 16).
