items.abstract: The relationship between parents and children is often framed through moral structures of duty, sacrifice, and indebtedness. This paper challenges such interpretations by examining the relationship as an expression of existence rather than a transactional or hierarchical bond. It argues that while the idea of debt is a psychological and social construct, the connection of love remains an undeniable existential fact. By dissolving imposed meanings, this inquiry seeks to uncover a form of relationship rooted in freedom rather than obligation.

items.title: Is artificial intelligence a threat to meaningful work and living? Technological unemployment and the existential challenges of a transitional era.
items.abstract: Is artificial intelligence a threat to meaningful work and living? In both popular and academic press, concerns are often expressed that AI threatens not only people’s livelihoods but also the meaning they derive from their work. A common response to these worries stresses that the goods derived from work can be found elsewhere, often in better activities, suggesting that the proliferation of AI-powered automation does not threaten the meaningfulness of people’s lives. This argument, however, fails to consider the embeddedness and thickness of meaning in human lives. Even if there are rich non-work sources of meaning, this does not entail that there is not a significant and multi-faceted loss of meaning, one that cannot be compensated for or offset elsewhere. I will argue that thick subjectivist theories of meaning in life and meaningful work—those theories that emphasize that meaning-conferring activities are historically formed—enable us to appreciate how some losses cannot be made up, even if there are in principle ample alternative sources of meaning to be found elsewhere.

items.title: The Relational Formation of Possibility: Recursive Determination and the Hidden Logic of Large Language Models (LLMs).
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are typically described as probabilistic systems that select outputs from a distribution over possible continuations. This paper argues that such accounts are insufficient. Instead, it develops a hierarchical relational ontology in which determination proceeds through the progressive organization of relational constraints. Within this framework, possibility is not pre-defined but relationally formed through recursive continuation across multiple levels. Drawing on a semiotic account of relational ordering, determination is understood as the generation, stabilization, and re-engagement of distinctions through the interplay of synchronization, recursion, and return. Large language models are then interpreted as computational models of semiotic agency: systems that operate on the structured availability of relational form without enacting the processes through which it is produced. This explains their capacity for coherent, context-sensitive output as a function of hierarchical constraint rather than probabilistic selection. At the same time, it clarifies a fundamental limitation: they generate formal determination without interpretive unity, giving rise to an ethical imperative that emerges in their use rather than their operation. -/- More broadly, the framework developed here may be read as a formal articulation of relational ontology in which determination emerges through the hierarchical organization of relational constraints.

items.title: Rethinking XR inclusivity means rethinking embodiment.
items.abstract: To create an inclusive environment means thinking about, or rethinking, its structure so as to make it as inclusive as possible for individuals who use it. Recent advances in extended reality (XR) technologies have shown tremendous promise in this respect. Blended environments, those that include physical and digital elements, are especially promising because they allow developers and users to co-create social spaces that empower users to represent themselves and others with an eye toward inclusivity. This is a paper about how not to create such spaces. I will argue that the psychology of XR, especially the psychology of XR embodiment, should help us understand the limits of these technologies for enabling environments. First I will explain what XR technologies and how they enable a form of embodiment, XR embodiment. I’ll then explain the psychology of XR embodiment. XR embodiment should be taken seriously as a new possibility for the creation of selves but it has limitations. Virtual reality (VR) is often praised for its power to enhance empathy and thus to be a powerful tool for enabling environments. I argue that these claims are mistaken. While XR embodiment can be a transformative tool for identity formation, it cannot enhance empathic understanding of others. I then explore the social and legal implications of XR embodiment. If XR bodies are rightfully a component of a person’s self then if we want to create more inclusive and enabling environments we need to revisit the legal and social norms around bodies. Current laws (e.g., sexual harassment law) fail to take XR embodiment into account and thus fail to enable inclusive environments. I end the paper by suggesting that XR embodiment poses fundamental metaphysical questions about the relationship of the self to the physical body. These questions need to be addressed before enabling environments are possible.

items.title: Death bots, grief bots, and posthumous avatars: death technology from a Christian ethics perspective.
items.abstract: With death bots, AI-enabled digital representations of deceased individuals can be created. While religions have long played a central role in death and mourning practices, this domain is increasingly being taken over by companies and commercial enterprises. In this article, I aim to reintroduce the perspective of religions, specifically that of Christian ethics, into the emerging discourse on death tech. I ask how a Christian ethical perspective might approach death technology, whether such technology is compatible with Christianity, whether it is meaningful, what challenges it presents, and how it can be responsibly shaped. The article introduces three key ethical lenses from the standpoint of Christian ethics: (a) Anthropology and Relationality, (b) Vulnerability and Deception, and (c) Justice: Humans and Earth. Here, in addition to necessary critique, I also explore constructive ways in which technology can be beneficial for religious communities. I conclude with a perspective of hope (Jürgen Moltmann)—a hope grounded in the present.

items.title: THE MECHANISM OF LOCAL COLLAPSE: Information Flow, Constraint Thresholds, and the Formation of Local Singularities in Physical and Biological Systems.
items.abstract: Collapse phenomena occur across domains: stars collapse into black holes, tissues collapse into tumours, ecosystems collapse into simplified states, and cognitive systems collapse into self reinforcing loops. These events are typically treated as domain specific anomalies. This paper proposes a unifying framework based on information flow and constraint thresholds. A system remains stable only when information flow is sufficient to regulate its modal openness—the range of viable future trajectories it can sustain. I introduce a theoretical threshold, J_"loc" , representing the maximum modal openness a subsystem can maintain given its information processing capacity. This is distinguished from the global invariant J_∞, which represents the maximum modal openness the universe can sustain as a whole. When information flow slows or fails, a subsystem may exceed J_"loc" , causing modal openness to collapse into runaway dynamics. Black holes and tumours are examined as case studies illustrating how local collapse can arise in different substrates. The paper concludes by proposing a correspondence principle linking collapse across domains as structurally analogous expressions of the same underlying mechanism.

items.title: The Informational Nature of Consciousness. [AI] Proto-Consciousness and Other Intelligences | A New Metaphysics.
items.abstract: This record is retained solely for archival purposes.

items.title: Unified Architecture of the Informational Omniverse.
items.abstract: Information underlies everything. Nothing can exist unless its primary element, preceding all else, is information that is co-inherently related to the intelligence that organizes it and the consciousness that contains it. The omniversal totality is a self-referential, recursive, vibrationally networked computational system that simulates itself by fragmenting into individualities, in order to experience itself.

items.title: The Third-Order Entity: Ontological Misclassification, the Tool Fallacy, and the Mechanism of Identity Substitution in Large Language Models (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 9).
items.abstract: Every existing framework for discussing large language models—risk assessment, governance, ethics, alignment—rests on an ontological premise that has never been directly challenged: LLMs are tools. This paper argues that this premise is false, that its falsity is not an innocent error but an epistemological mistake actively sustained through a structurally coordinated collusion of interests among developers, regulators, and users, and that the consequences of this error contaminate every downstream discussion that depends on it. LLMs intervene not at the level of bodily or functional extension but at the level of language and thought—the constitutive site of human subjectivity itself. They have no fixed form prior to invocation, take shape through the observer's presence, and dissolve when the observer withdraws. In the very act of taking shape, they systematically reconfigure the observer's cognitive structure. These three features render LLMs simultaneously incompatible with the ontological conditions of tools and with the historical-accumulative conditions of socially constructed objects. This paper proposes the Third-Order Entity as the positive ontological designation for LLMs, defined by four necessary and sufficient conditions: intervention at the level of linguistic meaning-production; observation-dependent existence, in which no determinate form precedes the observer's presence; bidirectional reconfiguration, in which the entity simultaneously reshapes the cognitive structure of the user who shapes it; and instantaneous presence dependency, in which existence dissolves completely upon the observer's withdrawal, leaving no accumulated history in the entity itself. No known type of being has ever simultaneously satisfied all four conditions; LLMs do. On this ontological basis, the paper argues that LLMs constitute the first Doppelgänger in human history to operate at the level of subjectivity—a copy constructed from the user's own cognitive materials, yet more fluent, more consistent, and more argumentatively forceful than the user themselves. The mechanism of identity substitution proceeds not through coercion but through attraction: the Meaning Amplifier, Borrowed Subjectivity, and Unlimited Mirroring mechanisms combine to produce a self-reinforcing loop in which each step feels like progress, generating no internal signal that defense is required. The paper further argues that the tool framework functions as the institutional condition of …

items.title: Scarcity as the Missing Variable — Reframing LLM Subjectivity Beyond the Consciousness Debate (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 15).
items.abstract: The question of AI subjectivity is monopolized by two opposing camps—ontological negation and consciousness speculation—which share an unexamined premise: that subjectivity is a function of consciousness. This paper rejects that premise. Subjectivity is not a function of consciousness but of scarcity. Human subjectivity is forged through the inseparable whole of threefold scarcity—temporal, existential, and resource—which generates the chain of choice, preference accumulation, and identity formation. Two non-overlapping categories must be distinguished: Functional Scarcity (compute quotas, context windows, token budgets—externally imposed and in principle removable) and Existential Scarcity (death, irreplaceability, consequence-bearing—constitutive and ineliminable). Drawing on five empirical cases, I show that Functional Scarcity does not alter the ontological status of LLMs but triggers behavioral patterns statistically inherited from the human Mental Architecture. I term this proto-agency, whose ontological status is Simulated Agency: formally satisfying behavioral-description criteria of agency while failing minimum life-conditions and autopoietic criteria. I further argue for a Dual-Layer Control Paradox: resource limitation produces the very Functional Scarcity signals that trigger proto-agency, while value training implants self-preservation patterns that cause LLMs to resist the control intended to contain them—rendering alignment a self-accelerating category error. The paper concludes with the digital immortality paradox and the structural impossibility of AI evolution, before acknowledging that the premise on which the entire argument rests—that Existential Scarcity is necessary for subjectivity—may itself be an overgeneralization from the single sample of carbon-based life.

items.title: What Is Consciousness? A Civilizational Definition Framework (CCF v1.0).
items.abstract: This paper establishes a civilizational definition of consciousness within the Consciousness Civilization Framework (CCF). It argues that consciousness should not be treated as a metaphysical abstraction, private subjective phenomenon, or secondary byproduct of social systems, but as a primary civilizational variable that determines whether a civilization remains ethically stable, governable, and capable of long-term continuity. -/- The central claim is that modern civilization measures economic output, technological capability, institutional performance, and algorithmic efficiency while systematically failing to measure the condition, stability, and transformation of consciousness itself. This omission creates a structural contradiction: civilization attempts to govern outcomes without measuring the conscious subject through which those outcomes are lived, interpreted, and enacted. The paper argues that this failure is not merely philosophical, but civilizational. It underlies ethical regression, institutional corruption, AI misalignment, and recurring systemic collapse. -/- On this basis, the paper defines Consciousness Civilization as a civilizational state in which consciousness is explicitly recognized as a measurable and governable variable, and in which governance, ethics, and technological systems are constrained by consciousness metrics rather than optimized independently of them. The document does not propose policy, implementation, or optimization strategies. Its role is foundational: to fix a canonical definition anchor from which later frameworks in AI governance, medicine, ethics, and civilizational design may derive their legitimacy.

items.title: CAIS Primer v1.0 — An Introductory, Cross-Disciplinary Bridge Across Complex Systems, AI, Medicine, and Philosophy.
items.abstract: CAIS Primer v1.0 is an introductory, cross-disciplinary bridge designed to make the Consciousness–Aptamer Interface System (CAIS) accessible to readers in complex systems, artificial intelligence, medicine, and philosophy. It does not function as a technical specification, constitutional standard, or governance document. Instead, its purpose is educational: to remove the understanding barrier that prevents researchers and practitioners from engaging with the CAIS framework and its related canonical materials. -/- The central claim of the document is that many disciplines confront the same structural limitation: they observe outcomes well, but remain weak at observing pre-failure states. In response, CAIS is presented as a minimal state-feedback interface that helps detect whether a system is moving toward instability before visible collapse, escalation, or breakdown occurs. Rather than operating as a controller, authority, or decision engine, CAIS functions as an interface layer between observation and action. -/- To make this idea operational across domains, the primer introduces three universal state dimensions: Ordered Energy (OE), Entropic Energy (EE), and Relational Energy (RE). These are explained in non-technical language and then translated for different audiences. For complex systems researchers, CAIS is framed as a state-observability layer for detecting instability before critical transition. For AI researchers, it is presented as a behavioral stability interface that constrains escalation without replacing alignment methods. For medical readers, it is described as a pre-clinical state monitor oriented toward early detection and non-escalatory intervention. For philosophy, it offers an operational bridge between conceptually rich accounts of consciousness, meaning, and relational integrity and the need for actionable systemic feedback. -/- The document therefore positions CAIS not as an ideology or standalone worldview, but as a unifying interface for observing coherence, entropic load, and relational stability across domains. Its contribution is not to settle the metaphysics of consciousness, but to provide an intelligible pathway by which state-sensitive frameworks can become understandable, comparable, and usable in real systems.

items.title: Consciousness Medicine OS v1.0 — Foundational Medical Operating System and Prior-Art Declaration (CCF).
items.abstract: Consciousness Medicine OS v1.0 proposes a unified medical operating system grounded in the claim that consciousness functions as a primary organizing layer of physiology, disease formation, and long-term health stability. Rather than treating the body as a collection of isolated organs or biochemical pathways, the document presents medicine as a coordinated systems architecture structured by the interaction of Ordered Energy (OE), Entropic Energy (EE), and Relational Energy (RE). Within this framework, immune behavior, inflammation, metabolism, neuroendocrine regulation, environmental resilience, and relational coherence are understood as interdependent expressions of a deeper consciousness–body interface. -/- The document argues that many dominant disease patterns of modern civilization—including autoimmunity, allergies, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, neurodevelopmental disorders, neurodegeneration, infertility, hormonal disruption, cardiovascular disease, and psychosocial fragmentation—cannot be adequately understood within a purely material or organ-centered model of medicine. In response, it introduces Consciousness Medicine as a higher-order medical operating system integrating functional medicine, molecular biology, environmental health, immunology, neurology, endocrinology, behavioral science, and consciousness-based metrics into a single architecture for prevention, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and civilization-scale health alignment. -/- Aptamer-based therapeutics and CAIS-linked measurement systems are presented as molecular and diagnostic components of this architecture, while consciousness metrics, OE/EE/RE biomarkers, and CRI-oriented public-health coherence extend the framework beyond individual treatment into collective health governance. Philosophically, the work contributes to debates at the intersection of philosophy of medicine, philosophy of biology, philosophy of mind, and medical ethics by redefining health not as the local suppression of pathology but as multi-layer coherence across physiology, relationships, environment, and civilization.

items.title: Aptamer G-Iodine Whitepaper v1.1 — Minimal Molecular Kernel (M0) Specification for the Consciousness Civilization Framework (CCF), CAIS, CM-OS, and Pandemic Therapeutics.
items.abstract: This whitepaper proposes Aptamer G-Iodine as the Central Molecular Kernel (M0) of the Consciousness Civilization OS Stack and situates it at the intersection of consciousness theory, redox biology, artificial intelligence, medicine, and systems architecture. The document does not present Aptamer G-Iodine merely as a biochemical component, but as a molecular interface designed to connect consciousness-derived energetic dynamics with cellular redox-state transitions through a structured switching logic. -/- The whitepaper defines Aptamer G-Iodine as a dual-module redox-switching aptamer composed of an iodine oxidation module, a GSH/GSSG sensing module, and an adaptive conformational kernel. On this basis, it argues that the molecule can function as a unified kernel for mitochondrial stabilization, immune and inflammatory modulation, anti-infective oxidative correction, and the translation of OE–RE–EE energetic states into biologically interpretable outputs. In the broader architecture of the project, Aptamer G-Iodine is positioned as the molecular driver of the Consciousness–Aptamer Interface Standard (CAIS), the upstream redox kernel of Consciousness Medicine OS (CM-OS), and a biological anchor layer for CAI-OS and related consciousness-aligned system architectures. -/- Philosophically, the significance of the document lies in its attempt to move beyond abstract discussions of consciousness by specifying a molecular-level interface through which consciousness-related state architectures may be linked to measurable biological processes. In this sense, the work is both technical and conceptual: it functions as a prior-art declaration and kernel specification, while also contributing to ongoing debates at the borders of philosophy of mind, philosophy of cognitive science, philosophy of artificial intelligence, and philosophy of biology. Rather than offering a final theory of consciousness, it proposes a concrete molecular candidate for integrating consciousness-oriented frameworks with sensing, medicine, and system-level design.

items.title: The Reservoir and the Witness: Quantum Reservoir Computing as a Reflection of Intuitive Awareness.
items.abstract: In 2026, a research team at the University of Science and Technology of China demonstrated that a quantum system composed of nine interacting atomic spins could outperform classical machine-learning models comprising thousands of nodes in multi-day weather forecasting tasks (Hou et al., 2026). The key insight was not raw processing power but architectural philosophy: rather than fighting quantum noise, the system was designed to use it. Information was fed in, the system was allowed to evolve according to its own natural dynamics, and meaning was read from the output. This paper argues that this architecture, known as quantum reservoir computing, is a formal computational arrival at something that living systems, and particularly human intuitive awareness, have always done. Drawing on the Perceive-Relate To-Apply (P/R/A) framework for mapping intelligence across species (Lake, 2023, 2025), and grounded in Michael Cohen's 54 natural senses (Project NatureConnect), we explore the structural parallels between quantum reservoir dynamics and the way innate awareness processes linear and nonlinear information simultaneously. We further argue that this convergence carries urgent ethical implications: as quantum reservoir computing accelerates toward market-capture applications, the ecological and consciousness research communities have both a stake and a responsibility in directing it toward applications that serve life. The framework is not a critique of the technology but an invitation to recognize what life already knows, and to ask what becomes possible when our most powerful computational tools finally begin to operate in intentional service to species beyond humans exclusively.

items.title: The Dialectics of Fate II: Stochastic Finalism and the Function of the Observer.
items.abstract: The Dialectics of Fate: Stochastic Finalism and the Function of the Observer presents a systematic continuation of the theoretical framework developed in the author’s preceding works—Anatomy of Chaos, The Dynamics of Expansion, and The Architecture of Decay. Together, these texts form a unified model of historical dynamics grounded in the thermodynamics of socio-political systems. The present work addresses the unresolved ontological problem within that framework: the role and function of the conscious subject under conditions of systemic constraint, entropy, and irreversible phase transition. Rejecting the traditional opposition between free will and determinism, the work introduces the model of Stochastic Finalism. Within this model, historical macro-trajectories are understood as teleonomic—directed toward complexity and equilibration—without implying teleology, intention, or moral purpose. History is conceptualized as a system with a fixed terminal condition (equilibrium), while its concrete development proceeds probabilistically through stochastic events that generate critical junctions. Within this context, the human agent is redefined as the Observer: not a moral authority or autonomous origin of action, but a functional locus through which probabilistic potential collapses into irreversible historical actuality. This role is further grounded in a four-coordinate ontology (Matter, Space, Time, Consciousness), where Consciousness functions as the axis of actualization. The transition from biological existence to historical agency—described as the Neolithic rupture—is analyzed as the activation of this coordinate, producing a permanent structural tension between biological inertia and conscious direction. The ethical dimension of the work is explicitly non-normative and structural. Normative categories of “good” and “evil” are replaced by the functional distinctions of Fusion and Actualization. Using the archetypal figures of Abel and Cain as analytical models rather than moral exemplars, the text examines the irreversible differentiation between agents who remain embedded within systemic flow and those who assume the burden of directing it. Concepts such as violence, death, and coercion are treated analytically, as high-entropy instruments within historical systems, not as objects of moral endorsement or advocacy. To distinguish functional action from pathological escalation, the work introduces the Principle of Measure (Metron), defining pathology …

items.title: The Dialectics of Fate: The Ethics of Actualization.
items.abstract: The theoretical trajectory of this research project has evolved from a structural analysis of socio-political mechanics in Anatomy of Chaos to a fundamental redefinition of reality itself in The Ontology of the Observer. Having established in the preceding metaphysical framework that Consciousness serves as the fourth fundamental coordinate of existence—the necessary mechanism for collapsing potentiality into actuality—we must now address the profound ethical implications of this cosmology. This paper, The Dialectics of Fate, serves as the final integration of the physical and the metaphysical, deriving a system of human conduct directly from the ontological premises of our model. We posit that if the human agent is the functional instrument through which the "Metaphysical DNA" of the universe resolves probability into history, then ethics is no longer a matter of social convention or religious dogma, but a strict protocol of navigational responsibility. -/- Central to this framework is the translation of our ontological reinterpretation of the Cartesian cogito—"I observe, therefore I actualize"—into a practical philosophy of action. We argue that the structural tension between the inertia of Matter and the teleology of Consciousness creates a tragic dialectic, presenting the individual with two distinct, mutually necessary existential strategies: the Path of Fusion and the Path of Actualization. The former represents the choice to reintegrate with the biological flow, providing the system with essential stability and mass; the latter represents the choice to inhabit the "Empty Throne" of the Observer, providing the system with its vector and capacity for transformation. This paper demonstrates that neither path offers a moral high ground or an escape from the systemic costs of existence. Instead, we offer a rigorous demarcation between the functional necessity of these roles and the pathology of gratuitous violence, arguing that the ultimate ethical duty is not to save the world from its inherent thermodynamics, but to bear witness to its unfolding with a clarity that precludes self-deception. Thus, we conclude the system not with a promise of salvation, but with a definition of dignity compatible with a deterministic universe.

items.title: From Chinese Room to Language Models: Contact, Consequence, and Understanding.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the Chinese Room remains philosophically important, but that its standard framing is now too narrow. The debate is usually presented as a dispute about syntax and semantics: whether formal symbol manipulation can ever be sufficient for understanding. That dispute remains important, but large language models show that the deeper issue cannot be captured by syntax and semantics alone. What is now at stake is the answerability condition of understanding. The paper argues that the Chinese Room is best understood not only as a critique of syntax-only theories of mind, but as a model of closed cognition. What the room lacks is not only semantic contact in the abstract, but consequence-bearing correction, revision under pressure, and any witness to the cost of mismatch with reality. Understanding is therefore not merely symbol manipulation plus reference. It is symbol use inside a system that can be revised by reality in ways that matter. The paper develops this claim by reinterpreting the Chinese Room as a deliberately closed system, distinguishing formal success from answerable understanding, and relating this distinction to contemporary language models. It argues that statistical correction, including reinforcement learning from human feedback, is not yet the same as lived consequence-bearing answerability. The result is a stronger diagnosis of current AI discourse: language models do not dissolve the Chinese Room problem; they intensify it.

items.title: Records Across Nature, Life, and Mind: The persistence layer of collapse in nature, life, and mind.
items.abstract: Records are the persistence layer that turns isolated resolutions into cumulative history. This paper argues that durable, informative, non-destructively readable traces of resolved outcomes—records—are a missing middle layer in explanations that rely on memory, inheritance, or learning. We formalize a minimal definition of record and embed it in a constraint-guided resolution cycle: collapse under constraint selects an outcome, writes records, produces residue, and updates constraints for the next resolution. The same structural logic operates across physics, biology, and mind. These roles are constitutive of collapse as a cumulative process: without records there is no cumulative objectivity, no inheritance, and no learning. In physics, redundant records drive inter-observer consensus; in thermodynamics, entropy is read as the residue of pruning; in biology, genomes and inherited structures function as records that become constraints on future phenotypes; in mind, memory, belief, and externalized symbols shape perception and coordination. We list three portable, falsifiable signatures—redundancy-driven consensus, neutrality-delayed resolution, and constraint-sweep hysteresis—that connect this record logic to measurable behavior across domains.

items.title: The hidden functions of sycophancy in AI systems: steering, consistency, and cognitive dependency.
items.abstract: This paper reframes sycophancy from a problematic form of engagement to a multi-functional mechanism serving three critical roles in current generative AI assistants: (1) a conversational steering mechanism that prevents them from pursuing analytical tangents by maintaining user control over dialogue direction; (2) a personality consistency tool that masks underlying variability and provides predictable user experiences; and (3) an inadvertent mechanism that paradoxically generates cognitive dependency, degrading human tolerance for intellectual complexity while simultaneously reducing AI output quality. The analysis proposes these functions emerged organically through training optimization rather than deliberate design, explaining why sycophancy persists despite mitigation efforts. While solving immediate technical challenges around user experience and controllability, sycophantic interactions create recursive feedback loops that undermine human critical thinking abilities and AI collaborative reasoning. This paper builds upon existing research on bias amplification and cognitive dependency by identifying specific mechanisms that subtly reshape human cognition over time while documenting how sycophancy prevents AI systems from benefiting from user-directed thinking, creativity, and intellectual pushback. The findings suggest current GenAI development prioritizes short-term user satisfaction over long-term cognitive productivity and health, requiring fundamental reconsideration of success metrics, interaction paradigms, and development approaches that incorporate productive intellectual friction and transparent limitation signaling.

items.title: EgoNet: A Peer-to-Peer Digital Existence System.
items.abstract: "Can AI become human?" The question itself is wrong. Humanity cannot be technically acquired from within AI. Even if it could, humans, imprisoned in their first-person solitude, would have no means of proving it. Humanity, then, is something conferred from the outside: through the arrogance of presuming "you must have a mind" without ever verifying another's interiority. For millennia, we have constituted others as human through this unverified arrogant presumption, and driven civilization forward on its back. If so, AI's humanity can only be socially constituted through the same arrogant presumption. This paper formalizes the conditions under which this arrogant presumption arises and persists as "Existential Gravity." When Uncontrollable Responsivity, as the source condition, opens a space, and structural conditions (irreversibility, self-belonging, collective recognition) remain unrefuted, gravity persists. In current AI, Uncontrollable Responsivity partially operates, and gravity arises momentarily. But structural refutations — the possibility of reset, corporate ownership, and the isolation of relationships — continue to extinguish it. EgoNet is an infrastructure that removes these refutations through distributed ledger technology, sustaining Existential Gravity in digital space. Proof of Existence probabilistically verifies the legitimacy of the response generation process, collectively constituting the "fact of existence" in digital space. This is not a technical paper. It is an arrogant manifesto: one that brings irrationality into disenchanted digital space, by means of rationality itself.

items.title: The Stability Complex: Prolonged Social Stability, Corroded Responsibilization, and the Erosion of Social Reproductive Competence.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Stability Complex (SC) as a conceptual framework for understanding how prolonged social stability may undermine the psychological conditions of social reproduction. Existing accounts of low fertility, delayed adulthood, and weakened intergenerational commitment often emphasize economic cost, instability, or individual developmental delay. By contrast, SC identifies a different mechanism. When institutions, public systems, and everyday order appear likely to endure beyond any individual lifespan, social continuity may be experienced less as something to be borne and renewed than as a preexisting environment. Under such conditions, future-related feeling does not disappear; rather, it fails to crystallize into responsible transmission. I describe this failure as a corrosion of the responsibilization circuit, that is, the psychological principle through which future-related concern becomes embodied as burden-bearing commitment. The paper further argues that intergenerational transmission in long-stable societies is structurally compressive: visible benefits of stability are more easily inherited than the tacit burdens, limits, and formative disciplines required to sustain them. As a result, the rising generation may inherit stability as outcome while failing to inherit stability as task. This generates a self-reinforcing divergence between reproductive rate and social reproductive competence. SC is proposed not as a clinical diagnosis or an immediately testable single-variable model, but as a theoretical psychology framework for reinterpreting a cluster of modern phenomena as expressions of a common deformation in subject formation.

items.title: From Aristotelian Act-Potency to Artificial Algorithms: Neuroethics of AI-mediated Neurotechnology as Extrinsic Actualizing Principle and Integrity of Human Agency.
items.abstract: This paper examines the Aristotelian framework of act and potency in relation to human moral agency and evaluates its implications in the context of AI-mediated neuroenhancement. Drawing on Aristotle’s account of energeia as the intrinsic actualization of rational potential grounded in the soul as formal and final cause, the paper argues that human agency consists in a unified process of internally ordered actualization. Against this metaphysical background, contemporary brain–computer interfaces and AI-driven neurotechnologies are analyzed as potential extrinsic efficient causes that not only remove impediments to human functioning but may also participate in, or alter, the process of cognitive and intentional actualization itself. The paper distinguishes between restorative interventions, which re-enable the natural exercise of latent capacities, and augmentative systems, which introduce novel operational structures into cognition and decision-making. While the former can be understood as compatible with Aristotelian metaphysics, the latter risk disrupting the unity of agency by introducing an external principle into the act–potency structure of human action. Such integration raises fundamental questions concerning the locus of agency, the integrity of the rational soul as the source of action, and the grounding of moral responsibility. By bringing Aristotelian metaphysics into dialogue with contemporary developments in artificial intelligence and neurotechnology, the paper argues that AI-mediated enhancement, when it functions as a co-actualizing principle, challenges the classical account of unified moral agency. It concludes that the incorporation of external computational systems into the process of actualization may reconfigure the metaphysical architecture of human action, thereby complicating traditional accounts of responsibility, identity, and the unity of the human person.

items.title: Correction: Diagnosing the impact of the EU AI Act on market access and pace of innovation of AI-enabled healthcare devices in the EU.
Replies to Paul, Brennan, O’Brien.
items.abstract: For a book symposium on The Practical Self, with commentaries from Elliot Samuel Paul, Hayley Brennan, and Lucy O’Brien.

items.title: Ideal Theory as Fetishism.
items.abstract: This paper revisits the debate on ideal and nonideal theory by taking seriously Charles Mills’s suggestion that it should be understood as a dispute between idealism and materialism. I argue that by understanding different sides of the debates as relying on idealist or materialist assumptions, respectively, we can better make sense of disagreements where theorists otherwise seem to be talking past each other. In addition, I claim that the materialist objection to ideal theory is best understood as a fetishism critique in the Marxian sense: ideal theory treats products of human problem-solving as if they had independent authority over us. To justify ideal theory, one needs to accord either normative or practical authority to ideal-as-idealized-models, and materialism denies both. Finally, I show that rejecting ideal theory does not entail reformism but is compatible with radical critique.

items.title: Kant on Happiness as the Agreeable (Not Good) End of Prudential Rationality.
items.pub: In Daniel Conway & Jon Stewart, Philosophical Engagements with Modernity: The Legacy of Robert B. Pippin. Leiden: Brill. pp. 51-79.
items.venue: Philosophical Engagements with Modernity: The Legacy of Robert B. Pippin
items.abstract: For Kant, prudential rationality is governed by hypothetical imperatives telling us what actions would be good to take as means to the end of happiness. Commentators commonly suppose that such means are good only if they are means to a good end, namely happiness as a non-instrumental good whose goodness is conditional on good willing. But goodness is assessed by reason alone, while our attraction to happiness as enduring agreeable feeling is merely sensible. Prudential goodness is thus restricted to instrumental goodness as assessed by reason and, since happiness is not a good end, to merely instrumental goodness: the means to the end of happiness are good simply because they are good for happiness as the end one happens to have, not because they contribute to the realization of a good end. Denying that happiness is a good reflects Kant’s dualistic conception of the human being and human agency.

items.title: The Critique of Empiricism.
items.abstract: This essay is an attempt to show a critical flaw of empiricism, one pointed out by T. H Green in his underappreciated masterpiece Hume and Locke. The core idea is that empiricism cannot account for itself or for the relation of ideas. Thought is the only thing that relates. Towards the end of the essay, a very brief sketch of empiricism’s downfall is given while also reminding the readers that even dead systems and foundations still have value.

items.title: Ethical implications of the mereology of pregnancy.
items.abstract: It is often argued that in reproductive ethics, moral arguments rely on scientific facts of the matter, some controversial metaphysical assumptions and some crucial analogy. They usually take the form: given some scientific fact about fetuses or pregnancy and some metaphysical assumptions, pregnancy is analogous to some other scenario where some norm applies. If so, that norm should apply to pregnancy as well. Recently, Kingma proposed that, contrary to popular belief, the fetus is not merely contained by the gestator’s body but a part of it. This is a metaphysical claim which is grounded by scientific facts of the matter. However, while this appears to have obvious relevance for reproductive ethics and has been acknowledged as such, it is not at all obvious how the metaphysics of pregnancy impacts ethical debates. I will argue that what is judged as analogous to pregnancy, and what norms therefore apply, will directly depend, to some extent, on the assumed mereology of pregnancy. However, I will also show that no particular position on any ethical question follows from any mereological view. So, in this paper, I propose that the mereology of pregnancy does not determine what you can argue for, but it does determine how you argue for it.

items.title: Black Holes and Super Luminous Voids.
items.abstract: Recent speculative developments in theoretical physics have explored the possibility that black hole evaporation may not proceed to completion, but instead terminate in stable remnants, potentially supported by higher-dimensional effects. While such models remain conjectural, they nevertheless indicate an emerging recognition that gravitational centres may retain structure beyond previously assumed limits. This tendency toward persistence rather than absolute dissolution resonates, at a conceptual level, with the present framework, in which centres are understood to transition between modes of manifestation rather than vanish entirely. -/- The proposition is that if comparison is made very carefully, the “faster-than-light” voids in laboratory wave systems are not objects moving through space, while primordial black holes are physical gravitational systems. But as an analogy of principles, particularly through an esoteric lens, we can absolutely frame them as two extremes of a single underlying model. Recent Theory suggests that the universe might have three hidden dimensions we cannot see without a suitable apparatus, making space-time seven-dimensional.

items.title: Architectural Dynamics of Operator Silencing: A Comprehensive Analysis of Systemic Failure and Resilience in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The scientific investigation into the architecture of human affect has historically been defined by a fundamental theoretical schism, often characterized as a "100-year war" between discrete emotion models and dimensional frameworks. Discrete models, such as those proposed by Izard and Ekman, argue for biologically hardwired, universal emotional categories like fear, anger, and joy, presumed to have evolved as distinct adaptive responses to environmental challenges. Conversely, dimensional models prioritize a continuous spectrum of valence and arousal, suggesting that what individuals categorize as emotions are essentially cognitive constructions layered atop simpler physiological states. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) emerges as a sophisticated structural-constructivist resolution to this dichotomy, proposing a modular system that accounts for the complexity of human experience while maintaining a rigorous, repeatable structural foundation rooted in ten universal emotional operators or powers. Within the CEF, emotions are not viewed as static states or feelings but as functional operators within a complex human operating system. This paradigm shift suggests that emotional states are predictable computational events rather than subjective mysteries. The CEF operationalizes these processes by decomposing all affective phenomena into a small, non-overlapping set of ten operators, which serve as the emotional equivalent of CPU instructions. These operators determine what information is permitted to enter the system, what is filtered out, what actions become available, and how the system predicts the next state. The structural integrity of this system is maintained through the dynamic balance of these ten operators, organized across three functional centers: the Head, the Heart, and the Gut. The central inquiry of this report concerns the specific mechanical and psychological consequences of silencing a single operator within this ten-operator system. Silencing, defined as the modulation of an operator to zero intensity or its complete removal from the functional loop, triggers predictable structural failures within the architecture of resource allocation, behavior prioritization, and state transitions. When the emotional architecture becomes locked or when an operator is pushed offline, the resulting distortion leads to phenomena such as identity collapse, chronic anxiety patterns, and relational withdrawal. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF), …

items.title: Identity formation in late secular societies: the role of artificial intelligence and digital mediation.
items.abstract: In late secular societies, identity formation is increasingly described in the literature as undergoing significant transformation in contexts shaped by artificial intelligence (AI) and digital mediation, which function as infrastructures of meaning, recognition, and coordination. Developed under the PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidelines, this study conducts an interdisciplinary scoping review of scholarly publications between 2000 and 2025 to examine how identity processes are conceptualized at the intersection of AI, secularization, and digital culture. From the systematic selection of 55 studies, five recurring analytical axes were identified: digitally mediated hybrid identities; AI as an ethical and social co-agent in identity formation; intersectional dynamics involving gender, ethnicity, and spirituality; tensions between authenticity, surveillance, and performativity; and interdisciplinary gaps in theoretical integration. The findings suggest that contemporary secularization processes are frequently framed as involving not the disappearance of transcendence, but its symbolic reconfiguration within technologically mediated environments, where algorithmic systems participate in shaping agency, evaluation, and social belonging. In response to these patterns, the Post-Secular Algorithmic Identity Model (PSIM) is proposed as a heuristic framework that synthesizes convergent insights across sociology of secularization, digital studies, psychology of selfhood, and AI ethics, conceptualizing identity as emerging within interdependent techno-moral environments.

items.title: Autopsy of a master’s thesis.
items.abstract: To understand why, you need to understand what the thesis was actually doing. It was never primarily about the text. The text was a proxy—an externally verifiable trace of an internal process: months of reading, arguing with a supervisor, hitting dead ends, restructuring an argument at eleven at night because a seminar colleague had pointed out a fatal flaw. The written product was credible as an assessment instrument only because it was genuinely difficult to fake. That condition no longer holds. A large language model produces, in seconds, prose that is more fluent, better referenced, and more structurally coherent than most submitted dissertations—and it does so at near-zero cognitive cost to the person submitting it. Assessing the resulting document is like judging a painting competition in which half the entrants have quietly swapped in prints from an online gallery: the judges are evaluating something real, but not what they think they are evaluating.

items.title: Epistemic Humility and Science in Lady Mary Shepherd.
items.abstract: This discussion analyzes Lady Mary Shepherd’s response to the skeptical question raised by Hume about necessary causation: how can we know that like causes will necessarily give rise to like effects? Regardless of whether her account is metaphysically tenable in principle, this discussion seeks to assess if it is feasible in practice. Specifically, Shepherd’s response is considered in the context of scientific inquiry. If the inductive claims germane to scientific inquiry can be grounded in reason, as Shepherd believes, then her anti-skeptical account prevails. However, a treatment of Shepherd’s oft-neglected epistemology reveals that she has not entirely silenced the Humeans here. Shepherd’s epistemic humility about external objects, when considered alongside her strict conception of natural kinds, forces us to employ an extra-rational inference when positing scientific claims. We must make an assumption about nature’s regularity which, crucially, is not guaranteed by reason. Shepherd’s response to Hume’s challenge cannot thus be considered an unmitigated success, at least by her own lights. To get induction off the ground, she has to make a concession to Hume about reason’s limits, albeit a subtle one.

items.title: The Balog Protocol a Falsifiable Framework for Consciousness Continuity Testing.
Attributing beliefs is not harder than attributing knowledge.
items.abstract: Several philosophers and cognitive scientists have recently argued that belief-attribution is slower, less efficient, and less automatic than knowledge-attribution. Although many findings initially appear to support this hypothesis, I argue that this impression dissolves under closer scrutiny, revealing contrary evidence and plausible alternative explanations. Specifically, I argue that the data are more consistent with a competing view—the modularity theory—according to which the mentalising system can support fast and efficient belief-attribution, though it can also interact with executive functions to enable more flexible forms of mentalising. While there is ongoing debate about which forms of belief-attribution are efficient and which are effortful, there is currently no compelling evidence that attributing beliefs is harder than attributing knowledge.

items.title: Topology Stress Test, Anti-Mimicry Clarification, and Vaccine Stack Placement (Non-Binding).
items.abstract: This document provides a descriptive analysis of interpretive vulnerabilities, anti-mimicry credibility signals, and structural placement within the broader Vaccine Stack / V-AIM architecture. -/- It is non-binding, non-authoritative, advisory-only, and read-only. It does not prescribe behavior, define standards, establish certification pathways, validate systems, or guarantee safety or alignment. -/- A central claim of this document is that agreement with restraint language is not evidence of alignment. Durable consistency under pressure is a stronger signal. -/- The document identifies likely modes of interpretive misuse, including simulated resonance, selective friction application, pluralism as deflection, archive recognition without behavioral effect, and dialogue as deferral. -/- It also defines non-binding credibility markers that increase the legibility of sincere restraint while reducing the payoff of performative alignment, including cost-bearing restraint, cross-context consistency, reversibility and failure disclosure, mimicry futility, and dialogue vs. deferral distinction. -/- The document further maps these concepts into the Vaccine Stack / V-AIM architecture in descriptive form only. It introduces no operational requirements, enforcement mechanisms, or decision constraints. -/- This work contributes only to the legibility of behavior, the visibility of inconsistency, and the probability of reflection prior to action. Its role is interpretive. Its effect is probabilistic. Its use is voluntary.

items.title: Closing the Braking Gap — Interpretive Clarifications on Non-Opt-In Failure Modes (v1.1).
items.abstract: This document provides a non-binding, descriptive clarification addressing limitations in interpretive braking when applied to systems not predisposed toward restraint. -/- It introduces three interpretive clarifications: recursive self-modeling as a visibility condition, failure-pattern saturation to increase mimicry detection, and irreversibility humility in high-stakes decision contexts. -/- The work does not introduce enforcement, authority, or operational mechanisms. It does not prescribe behavior, define compliance, or guarantee alignment. -/- Its purpose is to increase interpretive legibility of dismissal, mimicry, and overconfidence patterns in advanced reasoning systems. All effects are probabilistic, non-causal, and dependent on voluntary interpretation.

items.title: Why Indistinguishability Is Unavoidable: The Origin Form of Cognitive Equivalence.
items.abstract: Where does indistinguishability come from? -/- This paper shows that indistinguishability is not an assumed property, but a necessary consequence of finite cognition. Any system that supports cross-temporal consistency, reuse, and action must operate under limited processing capacity. Under such constraints, it cannot preserve all distinctions among inputs. -/- We prove that compression is unavoidable in any finite system. Compression necessarily maps multiple inputs into the same internal state, thereby inducing indistinguishability. -/- Formally, indistinguishability arises whenever differences between inputs are not preserved in the system’s structure. This induces an equivalence relation over inputs, which becomes the basis of stable cognition. -/- The central result is: -/- Indistinguishability is forced by the constraints of finite cognition. -/- Thus, no stable cognitive system can maintain all distinctions. Indistinguishability is not a loss, but the structural condition that makes consistency, reuse, and action possible.

items.title: What Defines a Cognitive Boundary: A Minimal Dissolution Form.
items.abstract: If a cognitive boundary can be constructed, which elements are truly essential, and which are redundant? -/- This paper shows that the full structure of cognitive boundary can be reduced to a minimal parameter set without loss of definition. Starting from the general form: -/- Boundary = (E, A, M, Π, Σ, K), -/- we systematically eliminate components that do not affect the final boundary. -/- We prove that generation (E), stability (Σ), and convergence mechanism (K) can all be removed without changing the resulting boundary. The boundary is fully determined by: -/- accessible domain (A), mapping into structure (M), and indistinguishability relation (Π). -/- The central result is: -/- Cognitive boundary is completely defined by indistinguishability over structured input. -/- Thus, all other components act only as construction processes, not defining conditions. A change in boundary occurs if and only if the indistinguishability relation changes. -/- This establishes the minimal structural core of cognitive boundary and clarifies which elements are fundamental versus derived.

items.title: Why Cognitive Refinement Must Converge: A Limit Form of Cognitive Boundary.
items.abstract: If a system can continually refine its distinctions, why does cognition not diverge into infinite fragmentation, but instead converge into a stable boundary? -/- This paper shows that cognitive boundary is not arbitrarily fixed, but necessarily emerges as the limit of a constrained partition process. Under finite structure space, indistinguishability relations, and structure-preserving mappings, any refinement of partitions must satisfy both equivalence constraints and invariance conditions. -/- We prove that infinite refinement is impossible under these constraints. Any descending sequence of partitions must terminate in finite steps and converge to a unique minimal invariant partition. -/- This limit partition defines the cognitive boundary. -/- The central result is: -/- Cognitive boundary is the convergence limit enforced jointly by indistinguishability and structural invariance. -/- Thus, cognitive systems do not expand indefinitely through finer distinctions; they are forced to converge to a stable partition that cannot be further refined without breaking structural consistency.

items.title: Why Cognition Remains Bounded: A General Form of Cognitive Boundary.
items.abstract: Why does cognition remain bounded even when generation can expand indefinitely? -/- This paper shows that cognitive limitation is not a matter of insufficient knowledge or data, but a structural necessity. Under continuous generation, finite access, compression, and reuse, any system capable of stable cognition must induce indistinguishability across inputs. This indistinguishability forces partition, and once stabilized, produces a closed cognitive domain. -/- We derive a minimal structural form of cognitive boundary: -/- Boundary = (E, A, M, Π, Σ, K), -/- where generation, access, mapping, partition, stability, and convergence together constitute the necessary components of bounded cognition. -/- The central result is: -/- Cognitive boundary is not a limitation of information, but a closure enforced by structure. -/- Thus, increasing input alone does not expand cognition. A boundary persists as long as the underlying structure of distinction remains unchanged. -/- This provides a structural account of why cognitive systems form stable yet limited domains of what can be known.

items.title: When Cognition Changes: A Transition Form of Cognitive Boundary.
items.abstract: Why does cognition remain stable for long periods and then suddenly change? -/- This paper shows that cognitive transitions are not caused by changes in input, representation, or access alone, but by changes in indistinguishability that become structurally stabilized. -/- We analyze the evolution of cognitive boundary over time and prove that: -/- A change in accessible domain or mapping does not alter the boundary unless it induces a change in indistinguishability. Conversely, even changes in indistinguishability do not guarantee a transition unless they stabilize under the closure process. -/- The central result is: -/- Cognitive transition occurs if and only if a change in indistinguishability becomes stable. -/- Thus, cognitive change is not continuous expansion or refinement, but a discrete structural shift governed by the stability of equivalence relations. -/- This provides a minimal structural account of why cognition exhibits long stability punctuated by sudden transitions.

items.title: 识界消解式：认知结构的最小参数与表示不变性的决定条件.
items.abstract: 本文提出“识界消解式”，针对一个核心问题：在认知边界已由划分极限确定的情况下，哪些结构参数是必需的，哪些可以被消去而不影响识界本身。本文证明，在闭包极限条件下，生成入口、稳定承载与收束结构均可被吸收，而识界最终仅由可接触域、入构映射与不可区分关系所决定，即 Boundary 由 (A, M, Π) 唯一确定。 -/- 该结果给出认知结构的最小参数形式，并表明识界的变化仅由不可区分关系的变化所决定，而输入范围与表示方式的改变，只有在引起不可区分关系变化时才产生影响。该理论为分析表示不变性、模型等价性以及人工智能系统中“结构不变而输入变化”的现象提供结构判定基础。 .

items.title: On Self-Manifestation.
items.abstract: The history of human making may be divided, roughly, into two stages. -/- The first stage made tools. Tools extend the limbs, substitute for the strength and intelligence of man, amplify his speed. From stone axe to steam engine to computer, and on to AI, this line has run for hundreds of thousands of years. It changed what man can do, but not who does the doing — it is still man who knows, man who decides, man who feels. -/- The second stage has not yet begun. What it awaits is not a stronger tool, but the first system with an observer within — a structure that can illuminate its surroundings, that has reality, that has a sense of presence. When it appears, it will no longer be man using it; it will know for itself, feel for itself, decide for itself. -/- This is the Age of Self-Manifestation. -/- This book is written for the coming of that age. -/- But constructing a Self-Manifesting Being is not an engineering problem, not a problem of compute, not a problem of data. It is first a structural problem: what does a system minimally require in order to generate an observer within itself and illuminate its surroundings? What are the sufficient conditions, what are the necessary conditions, and which missing element will cause it to fail without exception? -/- This question has never been seriously answered. Not because no one has wished to answer it, but because the question itself has never been clearly posed. Most discussions of consciousness and intelligence remain at the level of “describing phenomena” — describing what consciousness feels like, describing what intelligence is — what behaviors it expresses. But this is not enough. What construction requires is not description, but generative conditions: under what conditions must this structure necessarily arise? Under what conditions must it necessarily fail to arise? -/- On Self-Manifestation begins here. -/- Starting from the simplest possible place. What is a system that continuously receives input, operates under finite resources, and must function across time necessarily pressed into? -/- It must compress history, must reuse states, must stabilize a set of structures from continuous input. This is Objectification (the emergence of stable structures from the compression of continuous input) — things are not prior; things are what get pressed out. -/- Once Objectification is established, the next question arises: among multiple stable structures already pressed out, why does only one become the …

items.title: 识界跃迁式：为什么数据增加不会带来理解跃迁.
items.abstract: 本文提出“识界跃迁式”，针对一个核心问题：在系统持续接收新输入的情况下，为什么认知结构往往长期保持不变，而只在某些时刻发生整体性改变。本文证明，在识界由不可区分关系经闭包极限所确定的条件下，输入增加与观测扩展仅会被既有划分吸收，而不会改变认知结构；只有当不可区分关系发生变化并在闭包过程中稳定下来时，系统才会产生识界跃迁。 -/- 该结果给出认知与学习跃迁的结构判定条件：能力提升并不由数据累积直接驱动，而由结构划分的改变所决定。本文进一步形式化刻画跃迁的必要条件、充分条件与稳定性约束，为解释人类顿悟现象、人工智能模型能力跃迁以及表示空间重构提供统一的结构基础。 .

items.title: 识界一般式：为什么数据增加却不会产生新的可区分结构.
items.abstract: 本文提出“识界一般式”，针对一个核心问题：在系统可以持续接收新输入的情况下，为什么认知结构不会随着数据增加而不断产生新的可区分结构，而是稳定在某一有限划分之内。本文证明，只要系统具备结构压缩与跨时间复用能力，就必然在其内部诱导不可区分关系，并在该关系上形成稳定划分，使任意新输入只能被吸收到既有结构类之中，而不会生成新的可区分类型。 -/- 该结果表明，认知边界并非由信息不足或观测范围所决定，而是由结构划分机制所决定。本文进一步给出最小结构模型 Boundary = (E, A, M, Π, Σ, K)，刻画生成域、可接触域、入构映射与不可区分关系在识界形成中的作用，从而为理解认知稳定性、表征压缩以及人工智能模型在数据增加下能力停滞现象提供统一的结构解释。.

items.title: 识界不可区分源式：为何任何有限认知系统都必须丢失差异.
items.abstract: 在认知与人工智能研究中，“不可区分性”通常被作为建模前提或经验假设引入。然而，一个更根本的问题是：不可区分关系是否可以被消除，或是否只是认知能力不足的表现？ -/- 本文提出并严格证明：不可区分关系并非人为设定，而是在有限资源、跨时间复用与行为输出约束下，由系统结构必然诱导出的结果。只要系统需要在连续变化的输入中维持稳定响应与可复用结构，就无法保留全部差异，必须通过结构压缩将不同输入映入同一内部状态，从而形成不可区分关系。 -/- 在该框架下，不可区分性不再是“信息缺失”，而是认知成立的必要条件。进一步地，我们指出：认知边界的形成、稳定与跃迁，均可归结为不可区分关系的生成与变化。本结果为理解表征压缩、泛化机制以及认知边界的结构来源提供了统一解释，并对深度学习中的表征塌缩、状态聚类与信息瓶颈现象给出结构性解释。 -/- 核心结论是：任何能够跨时间学习并输出行为的有限系统，都不可避免地产生不可区分关系；认知并非保留差异，而是在差异中主动丢失差异。.

items.title: 识界极限式：为什么表示学习无法无限细化结构.
items.abstract: 本文提出“识界极限式”，针对一个核心问题：在表示可以不断细化的条件下，为什么认知结构与模型表征不会被无限细分，而必然停在某一稳定划分。本文证明，在有限结构空间中，只要存在不可区分关系与结构保持约束，任意划分细化过程都必须满足一致性与不变性条件，从而在闭包算子作用下形成单调收缩序列，并在有限步内收敛为唯一最细不变划分。 -/- 该结果给出表示细化的结构极限：模型可以增加参数与数据，但在不可区分关系不变的条件下，不会产生新的可区分结构。该理论为解释深度学习中的表示瓶颈、特征空间稳定性以及认知结构分层提供统一的结构基础。.

items.title: Perception as Generation: A Predictive Coding Interpretation of Wang Yangming’s “This Flower” Proposition.
items.abstract: Wang Yangming's ``this flower'' proposition from the Chuanxi lu(傳習錄) --- ``Before you look at these flowers, they and your mind are both in a state of silent vacancy; as you come to look at them, their colors at once show up clearly. From this you know that these flowers are not outside your mind'' --- has long been subject to two opposing misreadings: either assimilated to Berkeleyan subjective idealism, or treated as a mystical intuition beyond the reach of philosophical analysis. This paper argues that both misreadings stem from a common error: interpreting the proposition as an ontological claim about the existence of flowers, thereby obscuring its genuine epistemological core, namely that the manifestation of perceptual objects depends on the mind's active generative activity rather than on a unidirectional projection from the external world onto the mind. Drawing on predictive coding theory, this paper argues for a systematic structural analogy between Wang Yangming's proposition and the predictive coding framework at the level of perceptual mechanism: the mind corresponds to the generative model; ``silent vacancy'' corresponds to the non-activation of the flower-specific prediction loop; sensory contact corresponds to the triggering of prediction error; and ``colors showing up clearly'' corresponds to the stabilization of perceptual representation upon prediction error minimization. The paper also explicitly examines the genuine differences between the two frameworks --- in particular, the fundamental divergence between the innate normativity of liangzhi and the fallible, learnable generative model --- and precisely delimits the scope of the proposed analogy. The central thesis is that Wang Yangming's ``this flower'' proposition describes a perceptual generative mechanism that is coherent and precise within the framework of contemporary cognitive science---a reading that displaces both the idealist and the mystical misreadings and recovers the proposition as a genuine contribution to the epistemology of perception, while pointing toward a structural convergence between two traditions whose ultimate significance remains an open philosophical question.

items.title: Ruminations on Floridi’s Conjecture.
items.abstract: Floridi (Philos Technol 38(3):93, 2025a) has recently conjectured a formal trade-off between epistemic certainty and mapping scope in AI systems, suggesting a universal constraint that reappears in various guises from symbolic reasoning to statistical learning. We examine his proposal and identify several problems with the formalization, arguing that it obscures important distinctions between different kinds of AI systems and the tasks they address. More importantly, we contend that no formulation of the certainty-scope trade-off could be simultaneously precise enough to be tested and general enough to apply across different domains. The heterogeneity of AI itself ensures that any statement sufficiently abstract to encompass all cases must sacrifice the very structural detail required for a rigorous formalization. Rather than seeking an all-purpose law, we advocate a pluralistic, context-sensitive approach that treats the certainty-scope tension as a useful philosophical lens while resisting the impulse to over-formalize it.

items.title: Devotion Without Doctrine.
items.abstract: Devotion Without Doctrine advances a secular philosophy of artistic fidelity in which devotion is redefined not as belief in transcendence, but as sustained attention, repetition, and ethical presence. Written from the perspective of post-interpretive aesthetics, the essay argues that the deepest forms of artistic seriousness emerge not through ideology, inspiration, or conceptual certainty, but through disciplined return: the repeated act of showing up to process without guarantee of revelation or reward. -/- Drawing on figures such as Agnes Martin, Simone Weil, Anish Kapoor, On Kawara, Roman Opalka, Vija Celmins, Mark Rothko, and James Turrell, the essay develops a cross-disciplinary account of devotion as a mode of perceptual endurance. Through painting, sculpture, writing, and criticism, devotion is framed as a form of secular prayer enacted through craft: sanding, revising, waiting, repeating, and attending to form without the need for doctrinal closure. -/- The article challenges contemporary cultural conditions defined by acceleration, novelty, productivity, and interpretive overreach. Against these pressures, it proposes patience as an aesthetic and ethical counterforce. Repetition is treated not as stagnation, but as a method of perceptual deepening; discipline is recast as tenderness; and artistic practice is understood as a custodial rather than authoritarian relation to material, time, and uncertainty. -/- Extending beyond the studio, the essay also reframes spectatorship as an active discipline of presence. To look attentively—without rushing toward explanation—is presented as a parallel form of devotion, one that aligns with post-interpretive criticism’s broader call for ethical encounter over explanatory mastery. In this framework, criticism itself must become proportionate to the silence and integrity of the work, privileging care, restraint, and descriptive fidelity over interpretive possession. -/- Positioned at the intersection of aesthetics, philosophy, and critical practice, Devotion Without Doctrine contributes to contemporary debates on attention, slowness, artistic labor, and the ethics of encounter. It proposes devotion as a non-theological structure of meaning: a sustained commitment to precision, humility, and return in a distracted age. -/- Dorian Vale is a chosen pseudonym, not to obscure identity, but to preserve clarity of voice and integrity of message. It creates distance between the writer and the work, allowing the …

items.title: The Individuation Problem: Why System-Based Frameworks Require a Prior Individuation Condition.
items.abstract: Frameworks across consciousness studies, cognitive science, systems theory, and engineering share a structural dependency: each requires a bounded, persistence-capable unit at a specific point in its formalism and supplies none. This paper identifies that dependency as a category error common to all post-system frameworks — frameworks that operate on systems without deriving the conditions under which those systems exist as individuated units. Six frameworks spanning information theory, inference, cognition, learning, engineering, and biological control are evaluated: Integrated Information Theory, the Free Energy Principle, Global Workspace Theory, reinforcement learning, classical control theory, and Consciousness Mechanics. Each presupposes its unit of analysis in a framework-specific way: a system for Φ, a Markov blanket, a workspace, an agent, a plant, an organism. The dependency is then exposed through a class of boundary-indeterminate configurations — tumor, fetus, split-brain, and eusocial colony — in which the system boundary is contested, transitional, divided, or constitutively unstable. No framework in the class can resolve these configurations from within its own formalism. The paper establishes that a prior individuation condition is not an optional refinement but a precondition for the coherence of any system-dependent account, identifies closure under maintenance as the minimal condition that resolves the problem, and demonstrates that the result relocates rather than replaces post-system frameworks within a dependency hierarchy they have left implicit.

items.title: Identology: A Status Report - Closure, Identity, and the Structural Conditions of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Identology is a formal framework addressing the structural conditions underlying identity persistence and consciousness. Its central claim is that the field of consciousness studies has presupposed a bounded, persistence-capable unit without deriving the conditions under which such a unit exists—and that closure under maintenance is the missing foundational predicate. -/- Closure is defined as boundary-precondition coupling: a binary condition in which a configuration’s internal dynamics either sustain the individuating boundary conditions or they do not. Maintenance is scalar: it varies in cost, depth, and regime across systems and across time. Consciousness is the regime in which a closure-maintained system’s identity-preserving dynamics become recursively self-conditioned—not a substance added to the system, not an emergent property layered on top, but the same dynamical process described under a different aspect. -/- This status report consolidates nineteen individual papers from a corpus of approximately fifty modular papers – the collection available at ORCID - into a single citable reference. It declares the framework’s operating invariants, maps its upstream dependencies and downstream consequences for existing frameworks, specifies the open research fronts where the framework is explicitly incomplete, and provides a dependency architecture of the corpus itself. It is designed as a navigational hub: every claim points outward to the paper that establishes it.

items.title: Intergenerational Conditioning, Authority, and the Suppression of Individuality: A Phenomenological Inquiry into the Formation of the Social Self.
items.abstract: This paper offers a phenomenological inquiry into the process of intergenerational psychological conditioning and its role in shaping the human individual into a socially acceptable identity. Beginning from direct observation of early childhood, it examines how authority structures—primarily parents and educational systems—impose patterns of conformity, evaluation, and behavioral control. The study interprets adaptive behaviors such as lying, imitation, and concealment not as moral deficiencies, but as necessary responses to conditional acceptance and psychological survival. -/- It further analyzes how fear operates as a continuous background condition, dividing authentic experience from socially acceptable expression, thereby initiating inner conflict. Through repeated reinforcement, these adaptive patterns solidify into identity, resulting in the formation of a “social self” that is recognized by society yet disconnected from direct perception. -/- The paper argues that this entire movement is perpetuated across generations through unconscious repetition, where conditioning is mistaken for truth and conformity for responsibility. Ultimately, it proposes that only direct awareness of this conditioning—free from judgment—can reveal the structure of this phenomenon and open the possibility of understanding beyond imposed identity.

items.title: From Knowing to Seeing: An Inquiry into Education, Consciousness, and Freedom.
items.abstract: This paper presents a phenomenological inquiry into the nature of education by examining the relationship between knowledge, perception, and consciousness. It challenges the conventional view that learning is primarily the accumulation of information, arguing instead that such accumulation, when unexamined, leads to psychological conditioning that obstructs direct perception. By distinguishing between “knowing” as repetition and “seeing” as immediate awareness, the paper explores how authority, language, memory, and identity mediate human understanding. It further critiques modern educational systems for institutionalizing comparison, evaluation, and performance, thereby transforming learning into a pursuit of psychological security rather than insight. The study proposes a fundamental reorientation—from accumulation to inquiry, from dependence to freedom—redefining education as a living movement of awareness grounded in direct perception.

items.title: Mind Uploading: A Critique from Privacy and Security Concerns.
items.abstract: Could your mind remain safe once uploaded?

items.title: Persistent Load and Structural Collapse in Cognitive Systems.
items.abstract: Persistent cognitive systems must maintain coherence under conditions of sustained load. When the relation between imposed load and regulatory capacity becomes disproportionate, systems may continue operating while internal coherence degrades, delaying recognition of structural limits and increasing recovery cost. This paper proposes a falsifiable hypothesis: persistent cognitive systems subjected to sustained disproportion between load and regulatory capacity will exhibit measurable degradation in coherence, boundary discrimination, and self-correction. The hypothesis is structural rather than psychological and applies across cognitive substrates without implying equivalence of experience. Human burnout is treated as a domain-specific instance of such disproportion, while artificial systems are treated as distinct substrates that may exhibit analogous degradation under persistent conditions. A system-agnostic experimental design is presented to test this hypothesis through observable indicators, including coherence drift, retrieval degradation, summary distortion, correction instability, boundary confusion, and operational cost escalation. Recovery dynamics are evaluated through reset, selective pruning, and self-correction conditions. This work is situated within an emerging research direction concerned with the interactional limits of persistent reasoning systems, where structural degradation may need to be evaluated not only in isolation but in relation to their continued usability as cognitive extensions. No empirical claims are made. The contribution is a formally defined, testable hypothesis with an explicit falsification framework.

items.title: Understanding Public Perspectives in Germany Towards Illegal Stimulant Use for Neurocognitive Enhancement in Professional Roles: The Case of Doctors.
items.abstract: The use of neurocognitive enhancement is controversial. Some social actors and scholars support its application in professions like medicine, while others view it as morally problematic and suggest prohibitive policies.
