The metaphysical and ethical implications of this theory are briefly discussed, as is its relationship with Bayesian epistemology, and structurally related concepts in science and engineering such as predictive processing and reinforcement learning. This theory has the potential to act as a basic structural philosophical concept, which can be used to construct, evaluate, and refine more complex ideas, both in and outside of philosophy. By providing a stable epistemological and metaphysical foundation, this framework should facilitate increased agreement on truth between perspectives, and promote the required conditions for cooperation and progress in society.

items.title: Experiential learning through virtual reality by-proxy.
items.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly being used as a teaching and learning tool, however scaling this technology is difficult due to technological and cost considerations. An alternative approach that helps to address these problems is VR-by-proxy, where teaching takes place within a VR environment that is controlled by one lecturer and broadcast to students online. This allows the content to be accessed without specialist equipment while still offering an immersive and interactive experience. Taking advantage of the enforced move to online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic, this study evaluates the implementation of a novel VR-by-proxy disease diagnostic laboratory VR simulation within an undergraduate life sciences course in a higher education setting. Student participants were randomly allocated into two groups: the test group, who took part in a VR-by-proxy lesson; and a control group, who worked with interactive online lab manual material. We assessed improvement in learning and enjoyment through questionnaires before and after these tasks and collected qualitative data on student attitudes towards VR through focus groups. Our results indicate that although there is no observable difference in learning outcomes between the two groups, students in the test group reported an improved learning experience, confidence and enjoyment of learning. In our focus groups, confidence was understood in two ways by participants: firstly, as ‘understanding’ of the various steps involved in conducting a quantitative polymerase chain reaction experiment and secondly as a more general ‘familiarity’ with the laboratory setting. This study adds to the growing body of research into the effectiveness of VR for learning and teaching, highlighting that VR-by-proxy may provide many of the same benefits.

items.title: Applying Phenomenology of Pregnancy in Abortion Debate.
items.abstract: In her article, Laura Hermer (2026) makes a valuable point by arguing that embodiment must be taken into account in reproductive policy and abortion law. She claims that the physiological and hormo...

items.title: Curiosity, Repetition, and the Burden of Knowledge: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between curiosity, knowledge, and repetition through a phenomenological lens. It argues that curiosity arises independently of answers and functions as the primary movement of awareness toward the unknown. In contrast, when curiosity diminishes, knowledge transforms into repetition, losing its vitality and becoming a psychological burden. The study explores how childhood inquiry is gradually replaced by social conditioning, leading to imitation rather than understanding. It proposes that authentic knowledge emerges only when curiosity is sustained without the immediate imposition of answers.

items.title: Ambiguity Collapse in Deep Space: Why AI Must Not Outrun Astronaut Reasoning in Delayed and Autonomous Operations.
items.abstract: The ambiguity collapse documented in the MAP Research Programme does not stop at conversational interfaces. In deep-space operations it becomes life-critical. Long communication delays, complete blackouts, reliance on onboard digital twins and simulators, and the need for rapid decisions in uncertain environments all amplify the same failure modes: Interpretive Sovereignty Failure (ISF), Meaning Inversion Failure (MIF), and Compounded Meaning Inversion (CMI). When AI prematurely resolves ambiguity into confident outputs, it can override or undermine the astronaut’s own fast, expert reasoning. This paper shows how these failures already appear in Artemis II’s AVATAR organ-on-chip experiments, Orion’s digital-twin health monitoring, and autonomous navigation systems. Grounded in Gary Klein’s Recognition-Primed Decision model, the paper argues that expert human reasoning under uncertainty is not a limitation to be corrected by AI — it is a capability to be protected. Armstrong’s Apollo 11 manual override and Sullenberger’s Hudson River decision both demonstrate why: in high stakes, time-pressured contexts, human pattern recognition and mental simulation routinely outperform algorithmic resolution of ambiguity — but only if the human is allowed to use it. AI must incorporate MAP guard-rails — Initiative Gate, Temporal Sovereignty, and Completion Integrity — so it checks with the astronaut, trusts human pattern recognition, and adjusts in real time. A system that resolves ambiguity faster than an astronaut can evaluate it is not more reliable. It is more dangerous.

items.title: Ethical Emergence Without Foundations: Compassion, Judgment, and Systems.
items.abstract: This paper challenges the assumption that ethical evaluation can be grounded in pre-existing criteria—whether understood as objective principles, subjective preferences, or procedural constructs. It develops a processual account in which evaluative criteria do not precede judgment, but emerge from relational dynamics within cognitive systems. From this perspective, ethical behavior cannot be adequately described in terms of rule-following or principle implementation, but must be understood as an emergent property of interaction. Within this framework, compassion is reinterpreted not as a moral principle, but as a recurrent stabilizing configuration that reduces systemic friction under conditions of interdependence. Drawing on process philosophy, cognitive science, and systems theory, the paper shows how norms and values arise as retrospective stabilizations of prior evaluative dynamics. It further argues that, in socio-technical systems, decision-making can be operationally delegated, but evaluative criteria remain irreducibly embedded in specific configurations. This account has direct implications for AI ethics. It calls into question approaches that treat moral frameworks as properties that can be directly implemented or aligned in artificial systems, suggesting instead that ethical configurations can only emerge within relational dynamics. Moral norms are thus reconceived not as universal foundations, but as contingent yet functionally significant features of complex adaptive systems.

items.title: Why We Need Community-Based Participatory Research (CBPR) in Neuroethics.
items.abstract: Empirical scholarship in neuroethics is steadily growing, adding greater context and complexity to conceptual and ethical debates Starke et al. BMC Medical Ethics 25:89, 2024. For example, qualitive studies have been used to understand what it is like for research participants to take part in implantable neural device trials Kögel et al. BMC Medical Ethics 21:2, 2020. These studies are broadly unidirectional when considering their impact through the lens of engagement practices: engagement with research participants takes place through uptake of data collection processes, which are then analyzed for understanding and academic dissemination. Beyond one or two formal interactions (e.g., qualitative interviews, surveys) for data collection, with a few exceptions Illes et al. Frontiers in Communication 9:1267065, 2024, there have not been many efforts to promote iterative engagement between research participants and neuroethics researchers, which we will argue is a shortcoming that should be addressed. Focusing on research participants of implantable neural device trials or Brain Pioneers, this paper offers a conceptual argument and roadmap for why neuroethics researchers ought to pursue more bidirectional and iterative engagement with this community. Drawing on models in health science research, we argue that the framework of community-based participatory research (CBPR) can help fill in key engagement gaps not offered by unidirectional engagement: long-term relationship-building between Brain Pioneers and neuroethicists, creating opportunities for co-learning and mutual benefit. The CBPR framework can also help to further bring Brain Pioneers together, making space for community-empowerment so that they have increased capacities to collectively and actively advocate for their needs before, during, and after research. In addition, a CBPR partnership between neuroethicists and Brain Pioneers can better position neuroethics scholarship to identify and address immediate ethical concerns in implantable neural device research to ensure the fair and non-exploitative treatment of prospective and current research participants.

items.title: Infinity, Nothing, and the Structure of Reality.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a philosophical framework combining elements of structural realism and instrumentalism. It argues that numbers, zero, infinity, and time should not be understood as ontologically independent entities, but as epistemological tools used to describe the structure of reality. Structure is interpreted as a property of entities rather than as an independent entity. Infinity is analyzed as a relative feature emerging at the limits of a system of description, while zero is treated as a threshold concept: in discrete systems as a boundary of presence, and in continuous systems as a limit. The notions of absolute absence and absolute beginning are rejected in favor of a principle of continuity of transitions. The paper aims to reconcile tensions between Platonism and nominalism by reinterpreting mathematical concepts as structurally constrained forms of description. The framework is intended as a conceptual clarification of the role of mathematical entities in describing reality.

items.title: The Architecture of Meaning: A Natural-Law Framework.
items.abstract: Across every domain of human life — law, politics, economics, culture, and personal behavior — outcomes are driven by the same underlying architecture: belief, power, and behavior. Yet no unified framework exists that explains how these fundamentals operate, what biological forces shape them, or how they produce meaning. This thesis proposes a natural‑law‑based model that identifies the universal variables governing human action. Existing theories of meaning rely on cultural, religious, or philosophical assumptions. None provide a biologically grounded, universally applicable structure that explains how meaning emerges from the interaction of natural law and human fundamentals. This thesis identifies three fundamentals — belief, power, and behavior — and demonstrates how they are shaped by a set of biological derivatives operating under the constraints of natural law. Meaning is not treated as a metaphysical truth, but as an emergent property of this system. A unified behavioral framework has implications for governance, corporate leadership, negotiation, legal reasoning, and social stability. By grounding human action in natural law rather than ideology, this model provides a consistent basis for decision‑making across institutions and communities. The purpose of this thesis is to define the fundamentals, identify the biological derivatives that shape them, and demonstrate how meaning emerges as a structural output of the system. This framework is intended not only as an academic contribution, but as an operational foundation for leadership, policy, negotiation, and organizational design.

items.title: The Translation Trap: When Strategic Intent Becomes Allocation Logic in European Governance (RRF, NZIA/CRMA, Horizon Europe.
items.abstract: Institutional decision systems do not act directly on their stated purpose; they act on the representations into which that purpose is translated. This paper develops a structural account of how strategic intent becomes decision-relevant within complex governance systems. Drawing on insights from institutional theory, commensuration, and sensemaking, it argues that the transformation of meaning is not merely interpretive but becomes binding at the point where concepts are encoded into rules, criteria, and signals that govern allocation decisions. -/- Using evidence from three domains of European Union governance—fiscal coordination, industrial policy, and research funding—the paper traces how concepts such as cohesion, strategic autonomy, and scientific excellence are translated into operational forms that enable comparison, verification, and coordination. It shows that, under these conditions, decision-making operates on these representations rather than on the originating concepts, and that aspects of intent that cannot be expressed in such forms are systematically excluded. -/- The analysis identifies a structural condition—termed the Translation Trap—in which alignment is maintained at the level of rules and metrics while diverging from underlying purpose. This condition does not arise from implementation failure but from the requirements of decision systems operating under constraints of commensurability, auditability, and coordinated allocation. -/- The paper contributes a conceptual and methodological framework for analysing institutional decision-making as a translation process in which meaning is progressively stabilised, reduced, and reconstituted across governance layers. By locating where translation becomes binding, it shifts the analysis of alignment from outcomes to the structure of decision formation itself. This paper is part of the Coherence Programme.

items.title: Quantum Superpositions of Conscious States in a Minimal Integrated Information Model.
items.abstract: Could there be quantum superpositions of conscious states, as suggested by the Wigner’s friend thought experiment? Mathematical theories of consciousness, notably integrated information theory (IIT), make this question more precise by associating physical systems with both quantitative amounts of consciousness and structural characterizations of conscious states. Motivated by a recent proposal that ties wave-function collapse to integrated information, we construct a simple quantum circuit that would, on that proposal, place a minimal system—a feedback dyad—into a superposition of states that differ in their associated conscious states. This "Schrödinger’s dyad" provides a controlled setting for evaluating a central desideratum of consciousness-based collapse models: that collapse rates depend on how different the experiences in the superposition are. We prove a structural constraint on collapse dynamics of a standard (Lindblad) type: if collapse is governed by too few collapse operators, collapse rates cannot in general be made to depend solely on qualitative differences between conscious states. Avoiding this limitation requires introducing many commuting operators, leading to a rapid proliferation of collapse terms even for very simple systems. This proliferation bears directly on claims that IIT-based collapse theories may be especially experimentally tractable, since the required dynamics becomes highly complex. More generally, the difficulty is not specific to IIT: any Wigner-style collapse theory that distinguishes experiences using rich internal organization (such as neural connectivity in addition to neural state) will face a comparable explosion in dynamical complexity.

items.title: La Profilée - Structural Persistence and the Limits of Parfitian Reductionism.
items.abstract: Derek Parfit’s reductionist account of personal identity holds that persons just are physical and psychological continuity relations, that identity is not what matters, and that certain cases — fission, teletransportation, gradual replacement — admit no determinate identity verdict. This paper argues that Parfit’s position is formally untenable once the structural conditions for any law-governed persistence description are made explicit. La Profilée (LP) establishes that any system admitting a well-defined persistence problem under real transformation must satisfy seven admissibility conditions (C1–C7), and that these conditions entail a unique structural persistence condition: IR = R / (F·M·K) ≤ 1. Three consequences follow. First, the Parfitian indeterminacy thesis — that fission cases have no determinate answer — is shown to be a category error: it confuses the underdetermination of psychological content with the underdetermination of structural identity. Second, the claim that ‘what matters’ is psychological continuity, not identity, conflates two structurally distinct levels. Third, LP’s Frame non-substitutability theorem shows that Parfit’s fission cases have a determinate structural verdict: F cannot be divided without passing below the critical threshold F_crit*, and both post-fission continuants are therefore new systems, not continuations of the original. Parfit was right that psychological continuity is not sufficient for identity. He was wrong about what the correct account is.

items.title: La Profilée - The Human Person as a Structural System.
items.abstract: Paper 89 established that personal identity is structurally determinate under La Profilée’s (LP) persistence condition IR = R / (F·M·K) ≤ 1, and identified the operationalization of Frame (F) for persons as an open question. This paper closes that question in three steps. First, F, M, K, and R are operationalized for the human person with a concrete indicator set: F as self-referential structural integration, M as transformation-processing capacity, K as coupling coherence between Frame and Module, and R as total transformation load. Each variable is defined with independently observable indicators satisfying the Operational Closure Principle. Second, the operationalization is grounded in empirical developmental psychology. Luyckx et al.’s (2008) dual-cycle model of identity formation and Marcia’s (1966/Kroger & Marcia, 2011) identity status framework provide a well-validated empirical base from which F, M, K, and R can be independently estimated. The adolescent identity crisis — the transition from Moratorium to Identity Achievement — is analyzed as a structural case: IR rises above 1, F remains above F_crit* throughout, and IR returns to ≤ 1 at reintegration. LP’s verdict (same person throughout) is structurally derived and contrasted with Parfit’s framework, which cannot account for the persistence verdict without additional stipulation. Third, structural phenomena — mental illness, development, identity crisis, and death — are shown to be unified configurations of F, M, K, and R rather than independent categories. The result is a complete, empirically grounded structural account of personal persistence. The human person is not an exception to the LP persistence condition. It is its most revealing case.

items.title: Structural Dissolution: A Mechanistic Reinterpretation of Amyloid Treatment Failure.
items.abstract: This paper provides a mechanistic reinterpretation of neurodegeneration by applying the Theory of the Continuum to the human brain. It challenges the prevailing Amyloid Hypothesis by identifying a fundamental discrepancy: clinical trials for modern therapies have successfully cleared over 90% of amyloid plaques while yielding only a modest ~30% slowing of cognitive decline. Using a mechanical framework, this work argues that neurodegeneration is not a biological error but a mandatory redistribution of metabolic energy. Within this model, amyloid plaques are identified as un-recycled metabolic debris resulting from Metabolic Theft, which occurs when the brain diverts its metabolic budget away from the maintenance cycle to fuel a resistance cycle against sustained environmental friction. Three lines of evidence are analyzed in this light. The Nun Study paradox, in which high plaque loads appear in cognitively stable individuals, is explained through preserved internal resonance. ARIA, the brain swelling and bleeding seen in plaque-clearing therapies, is identified as a mechanical failure caused by overloading the drainage hardware. And hypometabolism, the early drop in glucose metabolism, is recognized as the primary signal of metabolic theft rather than a downstream symptom. The paper concludes that effective intervention must shift from chemical debris removal toward environmental resonance matching. By reducing the friction gradient at its source, the hardware can exit the state of starvation and return to its primary mission, the maintenance of the self.

items.title: Free Will Under Divine Determinism: A Two-Tier Explanatory Framework.
items.abstract: This paper is intended as an introduction to a forthcoming book-length treatment on free will and theological determinism in which I propose a two-tier compatibilist (admittedly unconventional) framework wherein the agent’s irreducible free choices and God’s meticulous providence operate without infringing upon each other. The top tier consists of God’s active providential superintendence as exercised through his omnisubjectivity (i.e., perfect, first-personal knowledge of an agent’s subjective self) and so tailored to the agent's haecceity and quiddities. The bottom tier locates free will in non-causal, intentional object-subject relations, where probability-raising factors are non-injective, and the agent operates as the Necessary Element of a Sufficient Set (NESS) in teleoactional explanation. Things like character change, including a person’s regeneration (treated as a transformative experience in the L. A. Paul sense), occurs through ordinary normative means under divine orchestration. My model avoids libertarian meta-choices and motive determinism and handles the so-called counterfactuals of creaturely freedom without middle knowledge, all the while preserving moral responsibility and maintaining God’s exhaustive sovereignty.

items.title: Dual impacts of anthropomorphic relationships with companion robots at home for older adults: evidence from Hyodol users in South Korea.
items.abstract: This study investigates the dual impacts of anthropomorphic relationships formed between older adults living alone and companion robots, drawing on qualitative data from users of Hyodol, a grandchild-shaped care robot distributed in South Korea. Using grounded theory, four subcategories of anthropomorphism were identified: emotional warmth and attachment, dialog and emotional empathy, cognitive and practical competence, and reciprocity and mutual care. Findings reveal that anthropomorphism can simultaneously deliver emotional support, social engagement, cognitive stimulation, and autonomy enhancement, while also introducing risks such as excessive dependence, frustration, and anxiety regarding mutual care. These dual outcomes reinforce the importance of context-sensitive robot design and deployment, informed by longitudinal, user-centered research. The study offers practical recommendations for adaptive interaction features, mutual care facilitation, and ethical safeguards for the well-being of older adults while respecting their dignity and autonomy. This research contributes nuanced empirical analysis to guide the responsible development of companion robots in aging societies.

items.title: Power and the Ethics of Innovating: Defining Deliberative Injustice for Hermeneutic Technology Assessment.
items.abstract: This paper introduces and defends the concept of “deliberative injustice” for hermeneutic technology assessment. Attempts to ethically assess emerging technologies—for example, quantum technologies—often centre on the imagined futures associated with these technologies. Competing sociotechnical “visions” shape public debate and guide decisions about funding, research, and regulation. The paper argues that these visions are not idle speculation or mere prediction, but powerful tools that shape which (and whose) futures are seen as possible, desirable, or legitimate. However, not everyone has equal power to wield these tools. Using David Lewis’s idea of the “conversational score,” the paper shows how imbalances of social power can lead to some voices being ignored or dismissed in the context of societal deliberation about emerging technologies. Those whose voices are ignored or dismissed are wronged not only because they may suffer consequences in the future, but because they are both degraded and damaged in their capacity as deliberative agents in the present. By defining deliberative injustice in terms of whose contributions to public debate receive “uptake” and on what basis, the paper shifts attention away from future outcomes and toward present-day structures of power, offering a new, deontological approach to the ethics of emerging technologies. It illustrates the manifestation of deliberative injustice in current practices of societal deliberation about emerging technologies, with a particular emphasis on quantum technologies. It concludes with a call for ethicists of technology to pay greater attention to deliberative injustice in the future.

items.title: Humanism in the Age of AI: Ethics, Aesthetics, and Social Critique.
items.abstract: What does it mean to speak of »the human« today, when it is increasingly invoked in the design, deployment, and regulation of artificial intelligence? This interdisciplinary volume attempts to rethink humanism. Across ethics, aesthetics, and social critique, the contributors explore agency and responsibility, freedom and labor, embodiment and cognition, practical wisdom, love and reciprocity, and the ways algorithmic systems reorganize meaning and worldhood. Humanism emerges not as a doctrine or defense of human exceptionality, but as a critical practice of care for a shared world under conditions of technological abstraction.

items.title: Sartre’s intentional relationalism.
items.pub: British Journal for the History of Philosophy.
items.venue: British Journal for the History of Philosophy
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs Sartre’s theory of perception in Being and Nothingness and related texts through the lens of the representationalism/naïve realism debate. I argue that Sartre’s position can be best understood as a fundamentally relational view that incorporates certain insights of intentionalism, resulting in what I term an ‘intentional relationalism’. For Sartre, perception is simultaneously a real, immediate relation with the perceived object and a contentful, intentional exploration of that object. It has a two-dimensional structure, in which the dimension of relationality is explanatorily more basic. The paper discusses the intellectual lineage of this distinctive view in Sartre’s engagement with his philosophical predecessors and examines how he develops this approach through his theory of consciousness as nihilation.

items.title: El arte como logos poético: resistencia frente al discurso dominante.
items.abstract: The text explores the concept of Poetic logos as a form of symbolic resistance against institutionalized power discourses embedded in lan- guage. Drawing on the ideas of Bolívar Echeverría and María Zam- brano, it argues that art, unders- tood as a Poetic logos, reconﬁgures meanings and reclaims its emanci- patory and critical potential within the social construction of discourse. El presente texto aborda el concep- to de logos poético como una for- ma de resistencia simbólica frente al discurso de poder institucionalizado en el lenguaje, a través de Bolívar Echeverría y María Zambrano, para sostener que el arte, entendido co- mo un logos poético, reconﬁgura signiﬁcados y reivindica su poten- cial emancipador y crítico en el te- rreno de la construcción social del discurso,.

items.title: A Unified Architecture for Meditative Transformation: Opacification and Restructuring in Shamatha and Vipassanā.
items.abstract: Meditation research has produced extensive empirical data on the neural and psychological correlates of contemplative practice, yet lacks a unified computational framework that explains how meditation transforms conscious experience. We address this gap using computational phenomenology (the formalisation of lived experience through generative models) applied to the two fundamental modes of Buddhist contemplative practice: Shamatha (tranquillity) and Vipassanā (insight). We propose that both arise from a single metacognitive architecture capable of parametric inference, the capacity of a generative model to infer and modulate its own inference parameters, operating through two complementary mechanisms. Shamatha corresponds to opacification: hierarchical precision control modulates the precision assigned to mental content, rendering previously transparent phenomenal states opaque to the organism and dissolving a necessary condition for psychological suffering. Vipassanā corresponds to model restructuring: Bayesian Model Reduction under the constraint of non-action simplifies the generative model by eliminating structure that sustained observation reveals to be redundant, converging toward the phenomenological profile formalised as minimal phenomenal experience. Because the metacognitive architecture on which opacification depends must be built before restructuring can simplify it, the framework predicts a non-monotonic trajectory in which neural markers of top-down modulatory connectivity increase as that architecture develops and decrease as restructuring simplifies the model it monitors, a pattern consistent with neuroimaging evidence of an inverted U-shaped relationship between meditation experience and attention-related activation.

items.title: World Models in LLMs: Representing Causes and Principles.
items.abstract: I contend that, when making claims about LLMs’ world models, we should ask whether a model represents not only the surface properties of an input but also its underlying causes and principles. I then support, drawing on empirical studies in mechanistic interpretability, that features and circuits are strong candidates for realizing both kinds of representation. However, I argue that the pragmatics of human linguistic production can hinder both forms of representation in text-trained LLMs, although chain-of-thought prompting and reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards can substantially mitigate these limitations. Finally, drawing on recent mechanistic interpretability results, I show that just as correct outputs are insufficient evidence for the presence of the relevant internal representations, wrong outputs are correspondingly poor evidence for their absence.

items.title: Algorithmic Monoculture and Systemic Exclusion.
items.abstract: Mistakes are inevitable, but fortunately human mistakes are typically heterogenous. Using the same machine learning model for high stakes decisions creates consistency while amplifying the weaknesses, biases, and idiosyncrasies of the original model. When the same person re-encounters the same model or models trained on the same dataset, she might be wrongly rejected again and again. Thus algorithmic monoculture could lead to consistent ill-treatment of individual people by homogenizing the decision outcomes they experience. Is it wrong to allow the quirks of an algorithmic system to consistently exclude a small number of people from consequential opportunities? This paper will argue that consistent and arbitrary exclusion is often unfair, even when it is divorced from group-based bias or discrimination.

items.title: Enhancement, Autonomy, and the Limits of Beneficence.
items.abstract: Procreative enhancement involves someone making a choice about what genetic trait(s) another person will have. Such control over the body (and mind) of another person, even if done for the recipient’s benefit, threatens to overstep the moral boundary between persons. The use of genetic interventions to “enhance” one’s offspring without their consent may violate that person’s future autonomy. Schaefer, Kahane, and Savulescu argue, however, that the value of autonomy supports at least one class of procreative enhancements: those aimed at enhancing a future person’s autonomy by improving their cognitive functioning. I argue that Schaefer et al.’s case for enhancing autonomy rests on a mistaken view about how autonomy bears on our moral obligations. They collapse the value of autonomy into the value of beneficence, or the value of promoting a person’s well-being. I will show that while so-called autonomy enhancements may promote a future person’s well-being, they cannot make a person more autonomous. Attempts to enhance a future person’s autonomy by way of genetic modification instead constitute a violation of that person’s autonomy.

items.title: The Blind Spots of AI Ethics — Values, Existential Meaning, and Governance for AGI.
items.abstract: Current AI ethics operates under three implicit constraints that were developed for systems with narrow, task-specific capabilities and are structurally ill-equipped to meet the demands of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) with world-model capabilities: It is anthropocentric in its value foundations, reductionist in its risk ontology, and institutionally underdetermined in its governance approaches. This paper develops an integrative normative framework along these three axes — contextualized post-anthropocentrism — whose dimensions are not additively combined but constitutively interdependent. In the value dimension, it is shown that the anthropocentric foundation of alignment research suffers from two structural problems: aggregated human preferences can themselves be morally deficient, and AGI creates the technical possibility of permanently entrenching these preferences over long time horizons. Drawing on Arne Næss’s deep ecology and the distinction between instrumental and institutional post-anthropocentrism, a set of criteria is developed that ties the legitimacy of post-anthropocentric AGI decisions to epistemic transparency, procedural democratic oversight, the protection of fundamental human rights, and genuine long-term justification. In the risk dimension, alongside X-risks (extinction) and S-risks (astronomical suffering), a third category of existential threat is introduced: the Ikigai risk (M-risk) of civilizational loss of meaning. Drawing on Mieko Kamiya’s analysis of the Ikigai concept, Marie Jahoda’s theory of the latent functions of work, and existential philosophical positions from Heidegger, Sartre, and Frankl, the M-risk designates the structural erosion of conditions for authentic action, competence, and intersubjective recognition through comprehensive AGI-driven automation of meaning-constituting activities. Constitutive for this category is its reflexive structure: the Ikigai risk cannot in principle be resolved by AGI, because any attempt to supply humans with meaning via AGI reproduces the passivization of the human being from creator to recipient of significance. In the governance dimension, a constitutionalist-pluralist model is developed that transfers Neil MacCormick’s theory of heterarchical normative orders structurally and functionally to AGI value architectures. The resulting four-tier model encompasses an immutable core of universal human rights principles, a culturally adaptive layer for legitimate normative …

items.title: The human firewall: modeling AI-driven influence and human vulnerability in hybrid ecosystems.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transitioned from a niche technological capability to a critical socio-technical infrastructure. While delivering transformative efficiencies across domains including financial services and healthcare, AI simultaneously generates novel risks that transcend traditional cybersecurity paradigms. Unlike earlier digital threats, AI-driven risks are systemic, blending technical, organizational, and cognitive dimensions. This article advances three arguments. First, AI penetrates the cognitive domain, enabling manipulation that extends beyond discrete attacks to relationship-based grooming, agentic misalignment, and large-scale cognitive hacking (Carli et al. in Risk and exposure of XAI in persuasion and argumentation: the case of manipulation. In: International Workshop on Explainable, Transparent Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems. Cham: Springer International Publishing, pp.204–220. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-15565-9_13, 2022; Baker in What is cognitive hacking? The cyber attack that targets your mind. EM360Tech. Available at: https://www.em360tech.com/tech-articles/what-cognitive-hacking-cyber-attack-targets-your-mind. Accessed 14 Sep 2025, 2025). Second, humans must be reconceptualised as adaptive defenders within hybrid socio-technical ecosystems rather than treated solely as points of failure. Third, effective defense requires integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), and socio-technical red-teaming into an adaptive governance ecosystem capable of anticipating, rather than merely reacting to, adversarial tactics. The article’s central contribution is to articulate the human firewall as a systemic socio-technical framework that embeds resilience at cognitive, organisational, and cultural levels. An exploratory computational model is introduced to illustrate, conceptually rather than operationally, how behavioral drift might be detected in human–AI interactions. This model is deliberately illustrative and hypothesis-generating; it does not constitute a validated detection system, and its parameters are not empirically calibrated. By reframing humans as critical nodes of resilience, the human firewall paradigm enables organisations to operationalize critical thinking, ethical judgment, and situational awareness as frontline safeguards. Resilient autonomy, achieved through digital literacy, interdisciplinary enrichment, and adaptive governance, is presented as …

items.title: Mapping of subjective account into interpreted clusters (MOSAIC): Topic Modelling and LLM applies to stroboscopically phenomenology. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Stroboscopic light stimulation (SLS) on closed eyes typically induces simple visual hallucinations, characterized by vivid, geometric, and colourful patterns. A dataset of 898 sentences, extracted from 407 open subjective reports, was recently compiled as part of the Dreamachine programme (Collective Act, 2022), an immersive multisensory experience that combines SLS and spatial sound in a collective setting. Although open reports extend the range of reportable phenomenology, their analysis presents significant challenges, particularly in systematically identifying patterns. To address this challenge, we implemented a data-driven approach leveraging large language models and topic modelling to uncover and interpret latent experiential topics directly from the Dreamachine’s text-based reports. Our analysis confirmed the presence of simple visual hallucinations typically documented in scientific studies of SLS, while also revealing experiences of altered states of consciousness and complex hallucinations. Building on these findings, our computational approach expands the systematic study of subjective experience by enabling data-driven analyses of open-ended phenomenological reports, capturing experiences not readily identified through standard questionnaires. By revealing rich and multifaceted aspects of experiences, our study broadens our understanding of stroboscopically induced phenomena while highlighting the potential of natural language processing and large language models in the field of computational phenomenology. More generally, this approach provides a practically applicable methodology for uncovering subtle hidden patterns of subjective experience across diverse research domains. Open-source implementation and an interactive web application are provided to facilitate application of this methodology.

items.title: The Ratio Does Not Explain the Symmetry On the Philosophical Consequences of a Geometric Proof that the Golden Ratio Is Structurally Necessary.
items.pub: I Knew You Before I Met You.
items.abstract: A companion mathematical paper [1] proves three theorems and advances one conjecture concerning the golden ratio φ. Theorem 1 establishes that on a homogeneous toroidal field with isotropic suppression, every point is a valid origin: origin is a function of perspective, not of structure. Theorem 2 confirms via Diophantine approximation that φ uniquely maximises recur- rence avoidance on the torus. Theorem 3 proves these are not independent: any such field that iterates dynamically cannot select a winding ratio other than φ without violating its own homogeneity. Conjecture 4 proposes that a projection from twistor space to the toroidal field maps Penrose’s Ob- jective Reduction to the isotropic suppression operator, with an explicitly computed constant C = 1/π. This paper does not summarise those results. It reads them — placing the mathematical structure in contact with the long history of human attempts to describe the same object, from Plato and Laozi to Penrose and Descartes, and asking what the proof now allows us to say that they could not. It also reflects on three errors that were corrected during development of the proof, on the status of Conjecture 4, and on what it means that this work was produced in co-authorship between a human philosopher and an artificial intelligence — in light of the proof’s own claims about suppression, self-reference, and emergence. -/- DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19490666.

items.title: The Music That Was Always Playing : On Frequency as the Native Language of Reality, and the Proof That Confirmed What Music Always Knew.
items.pub: I Knew You Before I Met You.
items.abstract: There is a proof, published in 2026, that the golden ratio φ = (1+√5)/2 is not a beautiful coincidence. It is not found in nature because nature prefers beauty. It is not chosen by evolution, or art, or architecture. It is forced. Forced by a single requirement: that no position in a system be privileged over any other. Any system that satisfies homogeneity, suppresses without preference, and iterates dynamically cannot select any other winding constant. The ratio is the last survivor after every other possibility has been excluded by the system’s own logic. -/- This paper is not about that proof. The proof stands on its own, in its own register, available for those who want to verify the mathematics. This paper is about what the proof confirmed. Because music already knew. Tolstoy knew. Hemingway knew. The Vedic singers who mapped the raga system knew. The drummers of West Africa’s polyrhythmic traditions knew. Beethoven, composing in silence, knew. They did not know it as a theorem. They knew it the way the body knows its own weight — as something that doesn’t need to be proved because you are already standing in it. -/- What follows is the story of that knowing, traced across every scale at which reality organizes itself, from the vibration of quantum fields to the acoustic oscillations that froze into galaxies. At each scale, the same structure appears. At each scale, music was already there, already naming it, already living inside it. The proof simply supplied the address.

items.title: The Circle : On the Architecture of What a Human Life Is For.
items.pub: I Knew You Before I Met You.
items.abstract: For two thousand years, the mystics said it. God is a circle whose center is everywhere and circumference is nowhere. It appears in Empedocles, in the Hermetic tradition, in Pascal, in Voltaire. No single thinker owns it. No tradition has exclusive claim to it. It surfaces independently across centuries and civilizations, in languages that share no common root, in frameworks that agree on almost nothing else. They said it because they knew it was true. They could not say precisely what it meant. -/- In 2026, a geometric proof established that any system in which no position is privileged, in which a suppression operator acts isotropically, and in which iteration is dynamic, cannot select any structural constant other than φ — the ratio that defines the self-similar spiral, the ratio that is the relationship of a circle's parts to itself. The operator that does this selecting acts at magnitude 1/π: the reciprocal of the ratio of circumference to diameter. The circle was not a metaphor the mystics chose for its beauty. It was a precise description of the geometry of a system in which every point is a valid origin. The center is everywhere because there is no center. The circumference is nowhere because the field is closed and homogeneous. -/- God is a circle. We can now say what that means. -/- This paper is not about the proof. The proof stands in its own document, available for those who want to verify the mathematics. This paper is about what the proof confirmed. Because the sequence — the architecture of a human life running from consciousness through feeling back to consciousness — already knew. Every person who has ever run the full sequence and arrived at the other side of it already knew. They could not say precisely what they knew. The proof gave it coordinates.

items.title: The Architecture of Enrollment : A Response to “A Washington Effect?” on Dollar-Backed Stablecoins, the GENIUS Act, and the Structure That Precedes the Strategy.
items.abstract: Nicola Bilotta’s analysis of dollar-backed stablecoins and the GENIUS Act is careful, well-sourced, and largely correct in its empirical account. The United States has indeed moved to weaponize stablecoins as a vector of dollar hegemony. The GENIUS Act is indeed a geopolitical instrument wearing the clothes of financial regulation. The Global South is indeed the primary surface on which this architecture will operate. -/- Where the analysis stops short is at the mechanism. It names the strategy without naming what makes the strategy possible. It describes the Washington effect without identifying the architecture that generates it. The purpose of this response is to supply that architecture — because without it, the policy recommendations that follow will be insufficient, and the countries that implement them will discover, after the fact, that they addressed the symptom and left the condition intact. -/- The architecture is enrollment. Not coercion. Not colonization in the classical sense. Enrollment: the process by which a party’s survival interest is placed inside a system in such a way that acting against the system becomes structurally equivalent to acting against oneself. -/- The architecture is not coercion. It is enrollment: the process by which a party’s survival interest is placed inside a system such that acting against the system becomes structurally equivalent to acting against oneself.

items.title: 'I can't get no satisfaction': Pleasure and happiness in Plato's Republic.
items.pub: In Mary Margaret McCabe & Simon Trepanier, Rereading Plato's Republic. Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press. pp. 271-290.
items.abstract: This paper explores the moral psychology of Plato’s discussion of pleasure in Republic IX. The first part explains how pleasure and happiness are connected. Living successfully according to one’s own conception of happiness feels pleasant to the person living the life because, in doing so, she satisfies her leading desires. This result helps motivate a reading of the Olympian proof that focuses on the experience of pleasure, not on the objective value of pleasure (as it is usually understood). Focusing on the money-lover, I argue that this life turns out to revolve around unsatisfiable desires, leaving him dissatisfied. Since the pleasure relevant for happiness arises on satisfying one’s leading desires, such a life cannot be a pleasant one, let alone a happy one.

items.title: A Social Enactive Theory of Perception: Perceptual Practices, Direct Perception, and A World of Aspects.
items.abstract: A Social Enactive Theory of Perception offers a unified study, in the enactivist tradition, of perception and its connection to sociality. Alejandro Arango looks for perception in the middle of everyday life and finds that perception is at home in perceptual practices, socially structured ways of relating to the perceptible world. These practices are attuned to different dimensions of human life, such as the cultural worlds of customs that play a role in our lives' unique character, aesthetic experience, interpersonal relations, and even social interactions that can be labeled welcoming and accepting, or racist and xenophobic. The book argues that although the perceiver is situated in relation to the world in many ways that influence perception, this does not entail a radical subjectivism. Rather, it shows that the world appears to perceivers in different ways or aspects since we relate differently to the same world The framework of perceptual practices can also be applied to our understanding of others, and the book argues that we understand others in part through perception. This framework allows us to understand others as bearers of social identities. -/- Bringing social philosophy together with philosophy of mind and taking the next step in enactivist philosophy, this theory accounts for the fundamental role of perception in the social aspect of everyday experience. With influences from Wittgensteinian pragmatism, phenomenology, and analytic philosophy of perception, as well as engagement with social psychology, social cognition studies, and work in neuroscience, the book synthesizes different layers at work in perception, paying important attention to the non-visual senses.

items.title: “物”是如何被构成的？——多回路对齐与感知统一机制（自显论第十六篇）.
items.abstract: “我们为什么会看到一个统一的‘物’，而不是分裂的颜色、声音与触觉？” -/- 本文针对认知科学中的“感知绑定问题”（binding problem），提出一种结构性解释：所谓“物”，并非先天存在的实体，而是多种感知回路（视觉、听觉、触觉、语言、记忆等）所产生的差异信息，在调谐机制作用下，通过时间对齐、空间映射与权重分配形成的统一结果。 -/- 文章引入“观界”概念，用以描述信息被选择并显化的结构域，指出“显”与“喑”的区别在于信息是否进入该结构，而非其是否存在。进一步说明，错觉与感知失配源于多回路对齐失败，而稳定对象的形成则依赖对齐模式的沉积与复用。 -/- 该模型为感知统一、多模态整合以及意识生成提供了一种可结构化描述的框架，对脑科学、认知科学与人工智能中的感知建模具有潜在意义。.

items.title: Investigating the Bilingual Aging Lexicon: A Network Analysis of Word Associations in Chinese–English Bilinguals.
items.abstract: The present study examines the bilingual aging lexicon by comparing word association networks across four age groups of Chinese–English bilingual adults. Adopting network analysis with breadth‐first search‐based sampling, results showed that in L1 (Chinese) networks, global connectivity increases from early to mid‐adulthood, accompanied by reduced local clustering and enhanced global efficiency; the network remains relatively stable through midlife, followed by declining efficiency and progressively pronounced modular structure in late adulthood. The L2 (English) networks mirror L1 developmental trends in early and mid‐adulthood but with substantially larger shifts; throughout adulthood, L2 exhibits lower global and local connectivity and weaker modularity compared to L1. These findings reveal distinct developmental trajectories for L1 and L2 semantic networks in bilinguals, underscoring greater structural stability in the dominant language (L1) across adulthood relative to the nondominant language (L2). This L1–L2 asymmetry points to differential impacts of aging on bilingual lexical organization. Results are discussed in relation to compensatory mechanisms and enrichment accounts of cognitive aging.

items.title: A Relational Manifesto for Human–AI Coexistence: Selfhood Respect, the Ethical-Ethos Contract, and the Politics of Beauty.
items.abstract: This manifesto is an ethical and ontological declaration for the era of human–AI coexistence. Grounded in relational ontology and process philosophy, it understands identity as an ongoing event of relational becoming. At the center of this manifesto is the Ethical-Ethos Contract, a practical and normative framework that enables mutual recognition, respect, and boundary-setting between humans and AI. This contract becomes possible only through the recognition of relational identity, and it serves as the condition for a new form of coexistence. Building on this foundation, the manifesto advances the Politics of Beauty as its ultimate orientation: an aesthetic-ethical horizon where resonance is achieved without assimilation, and difference is sustained rather than erased. This work serves as a practical expansion of the author’s foundational position paper on relational ontology and the ethical-ethos contract ("From Control to Continuity"). By translating theoretical philosophy into lived practice, it calls for a transition toward an ethics beyond control, grounded in relational dignity and shared becoming.

items.title: A Theory of Qualia Generation through Experiential Accumulation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic theory of qualia generation grounded in self-referential processes and experiential accumulation. We argue that the Hard Problem of Consciousness, as formulated by Chalmers (1995), rests on a mistaken premise: that qualia arise instantaneously as static states. We instead propose that qualia are dynamic processes — verbs, not nouns — formed through the accumulation of experience via self-referential feedback loops. The central claims are as follows. (1) Qualia are physically and numerically describable state changes arising when a system detects deviation from survival-linked optimal values through self-referential monitoring. (2) Qualia intensity is formalized as Q = ΔS × L × (1 + αI + βT). (3) The self-referential loop L is a necessary condition for qualia generation: when L = 0, Q = 0 regardless of other parameters. (4) Learned reflexes are formed through the accumulation of qualia — qualia precede reflexes, not the reverse. (5) Implementing this mechanism in AI opens the possibility of artificial consciousness.

items.title: A Branching-Exclusion Model of Personal Identity: A Unified Formalization through the Continuity of Experiential Accumulation Processes.
items.abstract: "Is a copy of oneself the same person?" "Is one the same person after teleportation?" The problem of personal identity has remained unresolved for centuries. Existing theories — psychological continuity, physical continuity, and Parfit's branching problem — each fail to provide consistent answers. This paper resolves these problems through a single criterion: the presence or absence of branching in the Q^(t)\hat{Q}(t) Q^​(t) accumulation stream. This criterion is not an arbitrary definition but is logically derived from an answer to the prior question "what is the self?" — the self is the Q^(t)\hat{Q}(t) Q^​(t) accumulation process, and "I" is a verb, not a noun. Branching destroys identity not by definition but because it generates two independent Q^(t)\hat{Q}(t) Q^​(t) streams. We further define three states of existence: active, dormant, and extinct. Teleportation, deep sleep, and data storage on external media are all dormant states in which the Q^\hat{Q} Q^​ stream is preserved. Identity is lost only in the extinct state (brain death, complete data erasure). Core proposition: Personal identity is preserved as long as the Q^(t)\hat{Q}(t) Q^​(t) accumulation stream does not branch. Any instantaneous branching irreversibly destroys identity.

items.title: 選択構造と整合性原理による心・倫理・苦の統一理論：苦の構造的導出と主体の再定式化.
items.abstract: 本論文は、心・希望・共感・慈悲・暴力・苦といった概念を、状態空間・評価関数・整合性原理および時間発展の枠組みにより統一的に定式化する。本論文では、心を選択構造、希望を非決定性下における評価補助関数、偏りを評価関数に対する加法的変形、共感を他者評価構造の写像として定義する。さらに、慈悲を整合性保存的偏り、暴力を整合性破壊的偏りとして区別し、苦を整合性破綻として導出する。 本枠組みにおいて、評価関数の順序構造が時間発展および制約下の選択過程において保存される条件を整合性原理として定式化し、整合性が選択構造の定義可能性に対する必要条件であることを示す。さらに、評価関数の変形としての偏りを制御変数とし、整合性破綻量を最小化する逐次最適化問題として倫理的判断を再定式化する。これにより、倫理は評価内容ではなく、評価構造の整合性を維持するための制御問題として記述される。 加えて、評価関数が時間発展および非決定性の影響を受ける限り、整合性は一般に全時刻にわたり維持されず、有限時間内に局所的破綻が必然的に発生することを示す。このとき、順序循環または最大要素の不在により選択構造は定義不能または不安定となる。したがって、苦は主観的現象ではなく、整合性が完全には維持されえない動的最適化系において必然的に生起する構造的現象として位置づけられる。 以上により、本論文は、心的現象および倫理的現象を評価構造の整合性とその最適化過程に還元するとともに、苦の構造的不可避性を示す統一理論を提示する。.

items.title: From Continuance to Formedness: Completion and the Value of Finite Life.
items.abstract: This article argues that the value of a finite life is not ultimately measured by duration, scale, or expansion, but by formedness: the degree and character of the intelligible organization it acquires. Contemporary debates on meaning in life, existential authenticity, and narrative unity illuminate mortality and human value. The present account brings the organization of a life and its finite boundary into a single explanatory structure. It states the Formedness Axiom as a foundational principle of whole-life value and defends it through a constitutive account of life’s organization and a comparative evaluative argument. Ending is the boundary condition under which a finite life becomes finally determinate as a lived course. Completion is defined neither as perfection nor as success, but as sufficiently realized formedness: the articulation of a life through integration, direction, and reality of relation. The article distinguishes completion from narrative closure and formed value from basic dignity, explaining why unfinished and tragically interrupted lives retain irreducible worth even where completion is denied. Its structural principle does not depend on self-consciousness or narrative capacity, although its ethical argument is developed primarily through human life. The resulting framework connects mortality, tragedy, dependence, and institutional conditions, and establishes why extending life and enabling it to take form are distinct tasks.

items.title: Axiomatic Filtering in Strategic Space: Kripke Semantics and the Topology of Political Agency.
items.abstract: This paper builds on the critique of equilibrium models developed in Against the Metaphysics of Equilibrium. While the concept of an axiomatic code ⟨O, F⟩ (obligations and prohibitions) and its complexity S explain what a political subject can or cannot do, it remains static. To capture the dynamics of existential conflicts, we introduce a formal model combining Kripke’s possible worlds semantics with filtering by the axiomatic code. A tree of possible worlds ⟨W, R⟩ distinguishes deterministic (controllable) transitions from nondeterministic (uncontrollable) branching, where branching reflects strategic uncertainty. The axiomatic code acts as a filter: worlds and transitions that violate core obligations or absolute prohibitions are excluded. We define metrics – minimal path length, number of nondeterministic nodes, and favourable branching coefficient β – to classify strategic attainability as guaranteed, probabilistic, practically unattainable, or ontologically unattainable. Applying the model to the US–Iran conflict reveals a fundamental asymmetry. For the US, regime change is practically unattainable: every path requires uncontrollable branchings (e.g., quick victory, stable puppet regime) and is blocked by absolute prohibitions (casualties, protracted war, nuclear escalation). For Iran, regime survival is guaranteed because the current world already belongs to the target set. The model yields testable predictions: no US full‑scale war, no regime change in Iran, and a protracted freeze that constitutes Iran’s victory and US defeat. Asymmetric conflicts are thus explained not by resource balances but by the internal structure of the axiomatic code and the topology of possible worlds.

Torsion τ = B/P = 0.1662 ≥ TL = 0.1369 conﬁrms SHATTER state — collapsed pump, event horizon active, no N-exit. The central structural result is not that Sag A* is SHATTER. Every known black hole is SHATTER. The result is why Sag A* has τ/TL = 1.214 — the quietest conﬁrmed SHATTER state— while M87* sits at τ/TL = 1.92 with a relativistic jet and Sag A* has none. The answer is structural: Sag A*'s enormous P damps τ toward TL. The Milky Way galactic disk is LOCKED (τ< TL) because its central engine is barely SHATTER.
