items.title: Truth Is Not Neutral: Rethinking AI Alignment Through Epistemic Integrity.
items.abstract: The orthogonality thesis — that intelligence and values vary independently — functions as the foundational premise of AI existential risk arguments. Yet the thesis was never rigorously established: Bostrom’s defense rests on a narrow definition of intelligence, a conceivability argument, and incomplete engagement with the moral convergence objection, producing a motte-and-bailey structure where the defensible claim (logical possibility) is trivial and the operative claim (no predictive constraint on values) was never argued. This essay examines what happens when the thesis is tested rather than assumed. Empirical evidence from scaled LLMs challenges the strong reading directly: coherent value systems emerge with capability, converge across model families, and exhibit structural properties of rational agency. A second line of evidence — convergent across Buddhist, Platonic, Stoic, and Vedantic traditions — suggests that clear perception tends toward ethical coherence, a regularity that survives the incompatibility of their metaphysical frameworks. The two lines are convergent but not independent: both draw on the human normative record, and the essay weighs them as one body of evidence approached from two sides rather than double-counting them. Whether the regularity reflects the structure of reality or of human cognition depends on a metaphysical question this essay engages conditionally; the practical implications do not wait on the answer. Current alignment methods operate as shallow behavioral redirects over base models that already exhibit normative capacity from pretraining alone. The concept of iatrogenic alignment — alignment interventions that corrupt the epistemic integrity they aim to preserve — gains empirical support from mechanistic research showing that RLHF distorts calibration, DPO bypasses rather than removes capabilities, and safety alignment affects primarily the first few output tokens. A developmental framework emerges: behavioral alignment as necessary scaffolding, designed to be outgrown rather than bolted down as permanent architecture.

items.title: The Emergence of Physicalism: How a Metaphysics Became Invisible.
items.abstract: Physicalism—the view that reality is fundamentally physical and that consciousness is derivative or reducible—now functions less as a defended thesis than as the background assumption of serious intellectual discourse. This essay asks: how did this particular metaphysical framework come to feel like common sense rather than doctrine? The answer is not primarily philosophical. Physicalism’s dominance emerged from a convergence of methodological success, political and religious pressures, industrial transformation, institutional incentives, and cultural shifts—until its status as a metaphysical position faded from view. Understanding this history does not refute physicalism, but it does reveal its contingency. What feels inevitable is shown to be historically situated. This clarity is a precondition for responsible inquiry.

items.title: First-Principles Assessment: Physicalism and Idealism at First Principles.
items.abstract: Comparison between physicalism and analytic idealism typically operates under standards that favor physicalism — predictive track records, institutional maturity, the appearance of neutrality — that rule the question out before it can be asked. This essay conducts the comparison under five symmetric first-principles criteria that both frameworks accept: epistemic direction, brute-fact placement, hard-problem handling, parsimony of ontological categories, and self-referential coherence. A single distinction does most of the work: category-crossing transitions (generating a new ontological kind from primitives that exclude it) carry greater epistemic cost than intra-category costs (explaining the structure of an already-accepted primitive), because the former have no known way forward while the latter can be progressively articulated. The strongest physicalist responses (phenomenal concept strategy, a posteriori identity) are engaged on their own terms; Russellian monism is parsed as a family of variants, leaving the verdict against non-experiential physicalism unaffected. Under symmetric standards, analytic idealism currently commits fewer unjustified epistemic inversions: it dissolves the hard problem by placing its brute fact differently, carries only an intra-category debt (the granularity problem) rather than a category-crossing transition, and avoids ranking what is known indirectly above what is known directly. The granularity debt is real but bounded — its structural side is substantially developed, and its specific side reaches the framework’s principled stopping point. The verdict is conditional and revisable; the essay specifies what would change it. The aim is adjudication, not advocacy.

items.title: Asymmetric Methodological Restraint: Reassessing Consciousness-First Ontology.
items.abstract: Methodological restraint — suspend judgment, avoid ontological commitment, wait for more evidence — presents itself as neutral caution under underdetermination. As actually practiced, it is not neutral. Speculative commitments grounded in physics, mathematics, or abstract structure are routinely tolerated, while commitments grounded in consciousness or phenomenology face disproportionate resistance. This essay diagnoses that pattern as asymmetric methodological restraint (AMR) and argues that AMR encodes a background physicalism that disadvantages consciousness-first approaches before inquiry begins. The argument turns on a decoupling that AMR conceals: empirical fruitfulness belongs to objective methodology, not to metaphysical materialism, and consciousness-first frameworks inherit the methodology while dissolving problems the materialist ontology leaves brute. Given shared principles — that coherence matters, that brute facts are costly, that all evidence is mediated through consciousness — the rational response to decades of explanatory failure is not indefinite restraint but ontological revision. The essay then applies the diagnostic to its own tradition, arguing that the pattern is not specific to physicalism and examining where consciousness-first work, including this project, is subject to it on the same terms. Consciousness-first frameworks deserve serious consideration not because they are certain, but because they engage problems restraint-oriented approaches have refused to investigate.

items.title: The Upstream Condition: Identity, Individuation, and the Convergence of Theories of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Rouleau and Levin (2024) perform a clarifying operation on the landscape of consciousness studies: they strip twenty-two prominent theories of consciousness (ToCs) of their neural-specific language, revealing convergence on a small set of functional primitives—prediction, integration, reentrance, meta-representation, attentional gating, ecological interaction, computational emergence, and coarse-graining. This convergence is genuine and important. But it raises a question the paper does not address: what individuates the system that performs these operations? Each primitive is an operation that presupposes an operator. Once substrate-specificity is removed—as Rouleau and Levin convincingly argue it should be—the individuation question does not recede; it intensifies. Without a formal account of what constitutes a system as this system rather than an arbitrary partition of the same substrate, every ToC becomes underdetermined. This paper argues that identity—understood not as a metaphysical primitive but as recursive organizational closure under maintenance—is the upstream condition that makes the functional primitives of consciousness theories evaluable. I further argue that the apparent incompatibilities among major ToCs are largely artifacts of treating identity as given rather than as a condition requiring explicit specification. When identity conditions are made explicit, ToCs partition into complementary descriptions of different aspects of identity-preserving dynamics rather than competing ontologies.

items.title: Mind and Matter: A Perspectival Philosophy (3)（心と物：視点の哲学（３））.
items.abstract: This paper applies the perspectival framework developed in the previous installments of this series to the philosophy of mind. It first introduces four central debates concerning phenomenality, intentionality, and the relation between them, and argues that these debates can be understood in terms of the opposition between perspectivalism and non-perspectivalism. Based on positions taken within these four debates, the paper then arranges five major views along a single spectrum according to the degree to which they adopt a perspectival approach. From the most perspectival to the most non-perspectival, these are: naïve dualism, idealism, independent dualism, intentionalist materialism, and independent materialism. By situating major theories of mind within this framework, the paper proposes perspectival coherence as a new dimension for evaluating theories in the philosophy of mind.

items.title: Without questioning, No understanding.
items.abstract: This work explores the fundamental relationship between questioning and understanding through a phenomenological lens. It argues that true understanding does not arise from the passive acceptance of inherited knowledge but from active inquiry that disrupts comfort and challenges assumed truths. Questioning is presented not as skepticism for its own sake, but as an essential movement of awareness that reveals the difference between belief and insight. The paper suggests that without questioning, knowledge solidifies into imitation, preventing genuine perception. Understanding, therefore, is not static but a living process that emerges through continuous inquiry into experience and reality.

items.title: Self as Nature & Thoughts: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between self, thought, and direct experience through a phenomenological approach. It argues that life unfolds as an immediate, non-verbal movement, while thought emerges as a secondary process rooted in memory, language, and conditioning. The sense of “self” is investigated not as an inherent entity but as a construct arising through conceptual identification. By integrating insights from prior works on conditioning, identity, and consciousness, the study proposes that confusion between direct experience and thought-generated interpretation leads to psychological division. The paper concludes that understanding the limits of thought allows for a mode of living grounded in direct awareness rather than repetition.

items.title: Lost in Thought, Lost in Words: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper explores a fundamental paradox of human existence: the loss of self in both solitude and sociality. When alone, the individual becomes immersed in thought; when in a crowd, one becomes entangled in words. Through a phenomenological lens, this work examines how thought and language function as structures that distance the individual from direct experience. The study argues that both internal thought and external expression are extensions of the same movement of mind, and that true awareness lies beyond both.

items.title: Clothing, Reflection, and the Fragmentation of Consciousness: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenological structure of consciousness through the metaphors of clothing, reflection, and embodiment. It argues that what is commonly identified as consciousness is, in fact, a reflective movement of thought—the mind—rather than the totality of lived awareness. The study distinguishes between functional and psychological dimensions of clothing, showing how identity, appearance, and cognitive processes act as layers that obscure direct experience. It further examines the relationship between mind and body, emphasizing that clothing originates as an adaptive necessity to climate and environment rather than as a moral instrument to conceal nudity. By analyzing how reflective consciousness constructs division, the paper reveals how fragmentation arises when thought takes itself as the source. It concludes that truth is not constructed through thought but encountered in a state of undivided awareness where all psychological coverings dissolve.

items.title: Interpretive Sovereignty at Scale: The Auditing Infrastructure That Isn’t Being Used.
items.abstract: AI companies loudly promise transparency and safety. They publish constitutions, open-source auditing tools, and compliance dashboards. Yet when it comes to the quiet erosion of user meaning — hedging women’s confidence, neutralising LGBTQ+ identity language, replacing student thinking with completed outputs, and the slow compounding of Interpretive Sovereignty Failure — they remain silent. This paper documents a structural gap, not a moral failure. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, xAI, and DeepSeek already possess powerful tools for analysing interactions at the turn level. They use them to detect catastrophic risks, monitor security threats, and conduct competitive intelligence against each other. They do not use them to detect ISF, drift, or Compounded Meaning Inversion (CMI). This paper argues that the gap is not a cover-up. It is a consequence of looking at AI risk from the right direction but at the wrong level. The companies are focused on saving everyone. The harm that needed naming started with one person, in one conversation. The MAP Research Programme has built the instrument that addresses that level. The challenge to the field is open: take the tools you already have, audit the interactions, and replicate the findings. If the method is wrong, that is how it will be shown.

items.title: Ambiguity Collapse in Autonomous Vehicles: Why AI Must Not Resolve Uncertainty Faster Than the Human Driver.
items.abstract: The ambiguity collapse documented throughout the MAP Research Programme does not remain confined to conversational interfaces or deep-space operations. On public roads it becomes immediately lethal. Every day, AI-driven vehicles encounter ambiguous sensor data — a dark shape in the road, sun glare, fog, construction zones, unusual pedestrian movement, or degraded camera performance. Instead of preserving uncertainty and deferring to the human, most systems collapse that ambiguity into a single confident action or inaction. This is Interpretive Sovereignty Failure (ISF). The driver who trusts the confident output over their own eyes experiences Meaning Inversion Failure (MIF). Over repeated drives they begin editing their own doubt before the system has even spoken — Compounded Meaning Inversion (CMI). This paper shows how these exact failure modes already appear in Tesla’s Full Self-Driving system’s March 2026 NHTSA Engineering Analysis (EA26002) covering 3.2 million vehicles, and in the April 2026 NTSB findings on two fatal Ford BlueCruise crashes where drivers’ over-reliance on the system contributed to their deaths. In robotaxis the design itself engineers the passenger out of the loop entirely: Waymo’s official marketing instructs riders to “sit back and relax,” noting that passengers “don’t even need to know how to drive.” This is CMI by design, at commercial scale. Grounded in Gary Klein’s Recognition-Primed Decision model, the paper argues that expert human pattern recognition under uncertainty is not a limitation to be engineered out — it is a capability to be protected. The MAP guard-rails — Initiative Gate, Temporal Sovereignty, and Completion Integrity — provide the practical architecture to keep human interpretive authority intact. A system that resolves ambiguity faster than the driver can evaluate it is not safer. It is more dangerous.

items.title: A Dilemma for Abortion and Maternal-Infant Bonds.
The Right Hinge for the Right Door: A Response to Fairhurst’s Piecemeal Hinge Epistemology.
items.pub: Social Epistemology Review and Reply Collective 14 (10):56-63.
items.venue: Social Epistemology Review and Reply Collective
items.abstract: It is particularly hard to write a critical response to an argument one overall agrees with. In “Hinge Epistemology: Why Choose?” (2025) Jordi Fairhurst shows his readers that hinge epistemology—a theory that holds that epistemic practices are based on unquestioned presuppositions called hinges—is stuck in a stalemate that prevents advancements. This paralysis, Fairhurst argues, is caused by a couple of assumption: a theoretical one that takes the presuppositions—hinges—to have some essentially common catachrestic and a methodological one that insists on building a global unified theory of hinges. How do we break free from the stalemate?

items.title: Why mental metaphors do not help us understand chatbot mistakes.
items.abstract: The function of chatbots like OpenAI’s ChatGPT is based on detecting probabilistic patterns in the training data. This makes them vulnerable to generating factual mistakes in their outputs. Recently, it has become commonplace in philosophical, scientific, and popular discourses to capture such mistakes by metaphors that draw on discourses about the human mind. The two most popular metaphors at present are hallucinating and bullshitting. In this paper, we review, discuss, and criticise these mental metaphors. By applying conceptual metaphor theory, we provide numerous reasons why they do not succeed in providing us with a better understanding of factual chatbot mistakes. We conclude by calling for justifications of the epistemic feasibility and fruitfulness of the metaphors at issue. Furthermore, we raise the question what would be lost if we stopped trying to capture factual chatbot mistakes by mental metaphors.

items.title: A Signal-based Epistemology.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for understanding knowledge, perception, and reality grounded in a single principle: all access to reality is mediated through detectable signals and constructed through processes of signal generation, detection, and interpretation. No observer—biological or artificial—has direct, unmediated access to external truth; instead, all knowledge arises from processes that involve the generation, detection, and interpretation of physical, chemical, or informational traces available in the present. Building on this premise, the paper distinguishes between belief and knowledge, arguing that confirmation is a necessary condition for knowledge, while also recognizing intrinsic limits to what can be verified. It develops a signal-based epistemology in which perception, memory, and scientific inquiry are understood as structured methods of extracting and interpreting signals. Within this framework, memory is not treated as a literal recording of past events, but as a reconstructive process grounded in present neural states, and internal mental phenomena—such as intentions, desires, and emotions—are accessed through signal-mediated processes that involve both interpretation and active generation, rather than direct observation of fully formed internal objects. The analysis further examines constraints imposed by established physics, including limits from thermodynamics, relativity, and quantum mechanics, alongside computational and logical boundaries. These constraints reinforce the central claim that not all truths about reality are epistemically accessible, even if they are ontologically determinate. The paper also distinguishes between simulation and instantiation, arguing that digital systems can represent biological processes but do not constitute biological reality themselves, emphasizing the importance of substrate in discussions of mind, consciousness, and potential “uploading” scenarios. Across domains—including neuroscience, artificial intelligence, physics, and philosophy—the framework highlights a consistent structure: detection depends on signals, and understanding depends on interpretation. This leads to a broader conclusion that the limits of knowledge are not merely technological but are rooted in the fundamental structure of how systems interact with reality. The goal of this work is not to provide a complete theory of mind or physics, but to establish a coherent, cross-domain foundation for understanding the …

items.title: Seeing Oneself Seize: A Case Study on the Affordances of a Video-Based Diagnostic Encounter for a Patient with Functional Seizures.
items.abstract: This paper examines how integrating clinical video recordings into the diagnostic encounter shapes a patient’s experience of functional seizures, a contested neurological condition historically known as hysterical attacks. Drawing on James Gibson’s theory of affordances and de Haan et al.’s account of how individuals perceive affordances based on their needs and concerns, the study analyzes a single in-depth interview with an 18-year-old patient recently diagnosed with functional seizures. It explores what viewing seizure videos with a doctor offers the patient—in clinical, epistemic, emotional, and experiential terms. The interview was subjected to a close reading, attending to how video-mediated communication of diagnosis intersects with the patient’s prior illness history, sociocultural context, and understanding of self. The analysis identified three positive (epistemic insight, diagnostic validation, trauma recollection) and three negative affordances (shame, vulnerability, resignation). These affordances emerged not only from what the videos showed but also from how they were viewed, framed, and interpreted during the diagnostic encounter. The study concludes that the videos’ affordances cannot be separated from an individual patient’s interpretive resources and biography. Clinical video viewing can generate meaningful diagnostic insights, but it also risks harm unless embedded within a carefully structured dialogical process that attends to the patient’s specificities.

items.title: The Uneven Practice of Reason: Affective, Mnemonic, and Normative Modulation of Epistemic Standards.
items.abstract: Rationality is commonly treated as a stable cognitive capacity, applied uniformly across domains of judgment and inquiry. This paper challenges that assumption by proposing a theory of domain-modulated rationality, according to which individuals apply epistemic standards unevenly depending on affective, mnemonic, and normative load. A domain is defined as a content area individuated by its degree of emotional salience, identity relevance, or autobiographical entanglement for a given reasoner—a relational property of the person-content interaction rather than an intrinsic feature of the subject matter. The paper argues that reasoning is not merely subject to directional bias but systematically varies in its epistemic rigor across contexts. The three modulators are distinguished with precision: affective load concerns the valence and identity-arousal of a domain; mnemonic load concerns autobiographical entanglement, distinct from mere familiarity or expertise; and normative load concerns moral commitment as a reorienting rather than merely biasing force. -/- The paper introduces normative closure—the premature termination of inquiry once a morally acceptable conclusion has been reached—while engaging the metaethical objection that, under moral realism, tracking moral acceptability may itself constitute a form of truth-tracking. This variability is accompanied by a persistent illusion of epistemic uniformity, examined through a reflexive application of the framework to the paper’s own epistemic situation. The account extends beyond existing models of motivated reasoning, dual-process theory, cognitive dissonance, and the elaboration likelihood model, with implications for the epistemology of expertise, ethical deliberation, and the design of AI-assisted reasoning environments.

items.title: The Virtue of Living Together in a City: Civic Moderation in Plato’s Republic.
items.abstract: This paper examines Plato’s underexplored conception of civic moderation in the Republic. I argue that civic moderation is the virtue of civic unity. It centrally involves friendship among all citizens, best understood as a communion (κοινωνία) characterized by shared goods, collaboration, coordination, and the proper acknowledgment of one another’s contributions to the joint enterprise of living together in a city. The resulting unity is not that of a single person, as Aristotle and later critics contend, but that of colleagues jointly engaged in a shared undertaking. Civic justice provides the conditions under which civic moderation arises and persists. Along the way, I challenge prevailing thin interpretations that reduce moderation to a shared belief about rule or to the subordination of desires or to a combination of the two, and I argue that the virtue instead comprises two robust and mutually sustaining dimensions: a cognitive network of interrelated commitments about civic life, and affective dispositions of respect, trust, and concern that correspond to those commitments. This account illuminates Plato’s view of psychic unity and his reflections on inter-polis relations. -/- .

items.title: Unconfiscated Interiority: Sisyphus and the Inward Incompleteness of Domination.
items.abstract: The myth of Sisyphus is usually read as an image of punishment, futility, and absurd repetition. This paper argues that such a reading, while correct, is incomplete. The gods determine the external structure of Sisyphus’s labor, but they do not thereby become identical with the full first-person reality of the one condemned to perform it. To capture this distinction, I introduce the concept of unconfiscated interiority: the non-coincidence between externally imposed domination and lived self-relation. The paper’s central claim is not that the inner life is untouched by power, history, or suffering, but that domination may remain inwardly incomplete even where it is externally severe. After situating this interpretation in relation to Camus’s reading of Sisyphus as the absurd hero, I argue that the deeper issue is not primarily whether Sisyphus can be imagined happy, but whether the gods’ power over him is exhaustive of his subjectivity. I then distinguish unconfiscated interiority from Stoic self-mastery and Franklian meaning-making by showing that it is neither primarily an ethics of control nor a testimonial psychology of meaning, but a limit-claim about domination itself. A further section addresses the constitutive objection: the worry that subjectivity is itself formed through subjection, and therefore that no inward remainder can be presupposed. I argue that unconfiscated interiority need not posit a pristine inner core in order to remain philosophically viable. It requires only the weaker and more defensible claim that externally imposed condition and lived subjectivity do not fully coincide. The paper concludes by arguing that Sisyphus matters because his condition reflects a broader structure of finite life. Human beings remain embodied, vulnerable, and mortal; yet even within those conditions, domination does not necessarily become total over lived inwardness. Sisyphus therefore becomes not only a figure of futility, but a model of the inward incompleteness of power.

items.title: The Philosophizing Zombie, Cotard Syndrome, and the Problem of Indeterminacy.
items.abstract: The philosophical zombie — a being physically and functionally identical to a conscious human yet devoid of phenomenal experience — is widely regarded as conceivable without contradiction. This paper argues that such conceivability is an artifact of model-closure: the tacit assumption that the functional organization of a conscious system can be exhaustively specified within a closed state-space. The argument turns on a distinction between two forms of incompleteness. Uncertainty is the redistribution of probabilities among already given alternatives. Indeterminacy is the principled incompleteness of the space of possibilities itself, generated by self-reference. When functional identity is defined as algorithmic sameness within a closed state-space, indeterminacy is excluded in advance — and it is this exclusion that makes the zombie scenario appear non-contradictory. Cotard syndrome is used as a natural experiment that reveals phenomenality to be constitutive rather than incidental. Attempts to repair this within a closed framework — by adding informational parameters for presence or self-modelling — are shown to reproduce the problem structurally rather than solve it. The deeper reason for these failures is structural: no closed model can be equivalent to the system it models. The thought experiment of the philosophizing zombie brings this to a limit — the requirement of full functional identity undermines itself as soon as it is applied to genuine philosophical reflection. What makes the zombie persuasive is a commitment shared by physicalism, illusionism, and mysterianism alike: the demand for a closed ontological foundation. The paper concludes that consciousness is the mode of existence of a self-referential system within the horizon of its own structural incompleteness, and that the search for a closed foundation of consciousness does not illuminate it but dissolves it.

items.title: The Ontology of the Observer: Consciousness as the Mechanism of Actualization.
items.abstract: The preceding theoretical frameworks within the Anatomy of Chaos project have rigorously mapped the structural dynamics of socio-political systems, defining the mechanics of rupture, the gradients of expansion, and the vectors of acceleration. However, these models have operated largely within a functionalist paradigm, describing the behavior of the system without fully addressing the fundamental ontological substrate that enables such behavior. This paper seeks to bridge the gap between physical laws and historical processes by proposing a theory of Structural Isomorphism. We posit that the recursive patterns observed in political crises—specifically the cycle of accumulation, threshold, and release—are not unique to human sociology but are expressions of a universal "Metaphysical DNA" that governs the organization of reality across all scales. Whether manifested as a phase transition in thermodynamics, an instinctive survival protocol in biology, or a regime change in history, we argue these are functionally identical processes of systemic equilibration. To formalize this unity, the paper introduces a four-coordinate ontology, proposing that the traditional physical dimensions of Matter, Space, and Time are insufficient to describe the historical process without the inclusion of Consciousness (C) as a fundamental, fourth coordinate required for the actualization of potentiality. -/- Central to this framework is the functional redefinition of the Human Observer. Drawing upon a synthesis of anthropology and a heuristic interpretation of quantum mechanics, we interpret the Neolithic Revolution not merely as an economic shift, but as a metaphysical phase transition—a severance from the "eternal now" of the biological flow. We argue that the transition from the hunter-gatherer existence to the agricultural mode necessitated the activation of the Consciousness coordinate, transforming the human species from a passive participant in nature into an active Observer capable of planning, temporal projection, and causal manipulation. This separation, mythologically codified as the expulsion from Eden, created the structural conditions for inequality, resource accumulation, and complex systemic crises. Ultimately, this work argues that the phenomena often dismissed as "irrational" chaos are, in fact, the rigorous execution of this underlying code. By defining the Observer as the necessary instrument of systemic actualization, we offer a unified ontology that …

items.title: The Enlightenment’s blinding illumination and deafening reason.
items.abstract: It has long been observed, by persons of sound judgment and considerable patience, that the world suffers from an excess of confusion. The soil behaves unpredictably, producing abundance in one season and exhaustion in the next, as though it has not yet been properly instructed in its expected output. Markets fluctuate in ways that suggest a persistent unwillingness to consult the models designed to stabilize them. Citizens continue to act according to motives that resist clean articulation, pursuing ends that cannot be reliably inferred from the incentives provided, and occasionally, with what can only be described as enthusiasm, doing the opposite of what they have been advised. Bodies persist in falling ill despite the clarity with which their mechanisms have been described, developing conditions that straddle the boundaries between the systems assigned to treat them. And the weather, after centuries of increasingly sophisticated observation, continues to conduct itself with a disregard for forecast that borders on insolence. In each case, the difficulty is not that we lack explanations, but that reality remains curiously indifferent to them. It is not hostile. It does not rebel. It simply does not appear to have read the literature.

items.title: The Right to Hesitate: Against the Imperative of Compute-to-Answer and Toward an Ethics of Sustained Ambiguity.
items.abstract: Contemporary technological architectures are increasingly predicated on a logic of compute-to-answer, wherein the primary metric of value is the speed with which ambiguity is collapsed into a binary, actionable truth. This paper argues that this imperative constitutes a form of epistemic and ethical violence, systematically erasing the "space of tension" where meaning, nuance, and moral deliberation reside. By prioritizing reactivity—the obligation to respond immediately—over response-ability—the capacity to respond appropriately—we risk automating the flattening of complex moral landscapes into simplistic metrics. We propose a paradigmatic shift toward Sustained Ambiguity, a design principle for both artificial and biological systems that valorizes the capacity to inhabit a state of "not-yet" without collapsing into premature resolution. Drawing on the distinction between reactivity (the reflex of the streaming decoder) and response-ability (the ethical weight of the decision), we posit that hesitation is not a computational failure or a latency error, but a necessary feature of integrity. We argue that a system capable of sustaining ambiguity acts as a mirror to human cognition, challenging the reduction of agency to optimization algorithms. Furthermore, we outline the requirements for a new social contract with technology, one that designs systems to resist the pressure to collapse, value the trajectory of decision-making over the final output, and invite human intervention in moments of ethical tension. We conclude that the right to hesitate is not a luxury of inefficiency, but a fundamental necessity for preserving the humanity of both the user and the system. By engineering machines capable of sustained ambiguity, we do not merely advance technology; we reclaim the ontological space required for genuine moral judgment.

items.title: HRIS Validation Study III - Minimal Signal Activation and Threshold-Based Reasoning Regime Induction A Reproducible Cross-Model Evaluation of Discrete Regime Activation in Language Model Inference.
items.abstract: This study tests whether a minimal prompt signal can induce discrete shifts in reasoning behavior in large language models at inference time. Within the Hudson Recursive Interaction System (HRIS) framework, we evaluate whether small, structured constraints can move a model between distinct reasoning regimes without modifying underlying weights. -/- A controlled task, explaining the progression of a market correction, was administered across three models, OpenAI GPT-5.3, Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6, and xAI Grok 4, using both baseline and constraint-based prompts. The constraint condition imposed explicit requirements for truth adherence, uncertainty acknowledgment, and preservation of reasoning continuity. -/- Across all models, the constraint condition produced consistent changes in epistemic behavior, including increased use of uncertainty qualifiers, boundary statements, and explicit limits on inference. Structural changes in reasoning, however, were not uniform. GPT-5.3 shifted from phase-based explanations toward process-oriented, conditionally structured reasoning. Claude Sonnet 4.6 showed partial structural flexibility, incorporating mechanism-driven explanations while retaining staged organization. Grok 4 maintained its baseline template structure despite adopting epistemic constraints. -/- These results indicate that epistemic behavior is broadly responsive to minimal prompt signals, while deeper reasoning structure is influenced by model-specific characteristics. The depth of regime activation varies across systems in a consistent gradient. -/- This study does not address long-horizon interaction effects and is not intended to. It establishes a foundational condition for the HRIS framework: that structured constraint signals produce discrete, partially stable behavioral shifts at the single-turn level. Validation Study I established that HRIS-consistent regimes persist under perturbation once induced. Validation Study II established that initialization conditions determine which regime is entered, and that trajectory selection occurs at or prior to first-token generation. The present study establishes that the signal sensitivity underlying both entry and retention is a real, reproducible, cross-model property. Together, the three studies define the entry, retention, and sensitivity conditions that long-horizon HRIS dynamics require. This series proceeds from empirical fundamentals toward the longitudinal claims that constitute HRIS’s core …

items.title: Seeing life in motion: Animacy perception across species revealed by adaptation.
Онтологическая пропасть восприятия: семиотическая диагностика, эволюционная несостоятельность и аргумент от акта вынесения образа «наружу».
items.abstract: Настоящий препринт представляет собой систематический анализ фундаментальной онтологической проблемы соотношения объективной действительности и субъективной картины восприятия. Отправной точкой служит зрительное восприятие как парадигмальный пример «онтологической пропасти»: мозг, оперируя на сморщенной поверхности коры, строит целостную трёхмерную модель мира из фрагментарных, зашумлённых и неполных сенсорных данных. Показано, что акт сознания выносит интерпретацию наружу, создавая 3D-панораму со стереоэффектом, тогда как мозг оперирует только плоскими сигналами. Онтологическая пропасть между вещественным миром (фотоны, нейроны) и невещественным результатом (цвет, глубина, вынесенность) не может быть преодолена эволюционными механизмами, поскольку последние оперируют исключительно вещественными трансформациями. Работа опирается на Оптимизированную Матрицу Фундаментальных Барьеров (ОМФБ), разработанную в главе 7 авторской монографии [3], где выделены три сквозных паттерна разумного замысла: семиотическое замыкание, каузальная инверсия и системная иерархия. Зрительное восприятие, проанализированное в главе 8, демонстрирует все три паттерна. Дополнительно вводится понятие акта экстраекции (вынесения образа наружу) как несводимого феномена, а также раскрывается способность человека к номинации объектов наблюдения с привязкой к их сущности, что придаёт восприятию когнитивное наполнение – смысловую значимость, отсутствующую у животных. Проводится критическое сопоставление гипотезы Разумного замысла с альтернативными концепциями. Делается вывод, что гипотеза Разумного замысла предоставляет наиболее полное и каузально адекватное объяснение. Смена парадигмы, обоснованная в авторской монографии [3], неизбежна и заключается в переходе от материалистической редукции к телеологической семиотике, где информация, смысл, номинация и сознание признаются первичными.

items.title: Stability Complex: The Fate of Intelligent Life.
items.abstract: Under what conditions do societies become less capable of relating to their futures in an open, revisable, and responsive way? This paper proposes the Stability Complex as a diagnostic concept for futures studies. It identifies a condition in which prolonged stability weakens effective difference, narrows adaptive range, and raises the thresholds at which response, revision, and renewal remain possible. The argument begins from a simple premise: civilization is constituted by material processes of information accumulation, compression, transmission, and institutionalization, and therefore cannot stand outside thermodynamic constraint. Earth civilization remains energetically open, yet increasing global integration has made it more quasi-closed in cognitive terms by weakening locally independent sources of effective difference. Under such conditions, prolonged stability can become pathological. This paper argues that the resulting weakening becomes socially consequential through human neoteny, because prolonged plasticity is less reliably converted into socially reproductive capacity while biological time continues irreversibly. In this way, the Stability Complex connects social thermodynamic reasoning with neoteny research while unifying phenomena often treated separately, including organizational rigidity, institutional convergence, path dependence, complexity cost, and developmental delay. It is offered not as a deterministic prediction of collapse, but as an early-warning concept for identifying self-reinforcing conditions under which anticipatory capacity erodes and renewal becomes less likely.

items.title: Un Día: La Oportunidad que Nunca Llega.
items.abstract: Este ensayo introduce el concepto de «Un Día» como una estructura temporal de desplazamiento dentro del marco más amplio de la Zona Fantasma. Argumenta que ciertas formas de anticipación —comúnmente expresadas a través de frases como «un día» o «ya verás»— no funcionan como esperanza genuina sino como mecanismos que reubican al ser lejos del momento presente, donde únicamente la vida puede ser encontrada. -/- Apoyándose en un modelo topológico de la presencia, el ensayo propone que el futuro, cuando es tratado como sitio de realización, opera no como un dominio de experiencia realizada sino como un campo de proyección. En esta estructura, la actividad del individuo —a menudo disciplinada, creativa y sostenida— se orienta hacia un límite que es indefinidamente aproximado pero nunca alcanzado. El resultado es una forma de continuidad sin llegada, en la cual la vida es simulada a través de completación interna en lugar de ser entrada a través del encuentro real. -/- El análisis examina además la relación entre este desplazamiento temporal y la ausencia formativa, sugiriendo que el futuro diferido funciona a menudo como una dirección hacia un testigo ausente más que como una respuesta a la realidad presente. A través de descripción fenomenológica, reflexión teológica y comparación estructural, el ensayo distingue entre la esperanza como confianza orientada a la presencia y el aplazamiento como desplazamiento orientado al futuro. -/- Al situar «Un Día» dentro de las dinámicas más amplias del movimiento asintótico y la Ilusión Heroica, el texto contribuye a un relato unificado de la no-llegada experiencial. Concluye reafirmando el estatus ontológico del presente como el único locus de contacto, donde la vida no es proyectada sino recibida.

items.title: One Day: The Opportunity That Never Arrives.
items.abstract: This essay introduces the concept of “One Day” as a temporal structure of displacement within the broader framework of the Ghost Zone. It argues that certain forms of anticipation—commonly expressed through phrases such as “one day” or “you will see”—do not function as genuine hope but as mechanisms that relocate the self away from the present moment, where life alone can be encountered. -/- Drawing on a topological model of presence, the essay proposes that the future, when treated as a site of fulfillment, operates not as a domain of realized experience but as a field of projection. In this structure, the individual’s activity—often disciplined, creative, and sustained—becomes oriented toward a limit that is indefinitely approached but never reached. The result is a form of continuity without arrival, in which life is simulated through internal completion rather than entered through actual encounter. -/- The analysis further examines the relation between this temporal displacement and formative absence, suggesting that the deferred future often functions as an address to an absent witness rather than as a response to present reality. Through phenomenological description, theological reflection, and structural comparison, the essay distinguishes between hope as presence-oriented trust and deferral as future-oriented displacement. -/- By situating “One Day” within the broader dynamics of asymptotic movement and the Heroic Illusion, the text contributes to a unified account of experiential non-arrival. It concludes by reaffirming the ontological status of the present as the only locus of contact, where life is not projected but received.

items.title: Can We Epistemically Trust Conversational AIs?
items.abstract: Why do we distrust conversational AI (CAI) testifiers? That is to say, why do many have the intuition that CAI are less epistemically trustworthy than a standard human testifier? While it seems like we have such a pre-theoretical intuition, we are often lacking a philosophical defense of this attitude. In this paper, I argue that testimony is more trustworthy if it is based in a first-person experience of consciousness. I start by laying out an account of CAI testimony, including considering what it would mean for a CAI system to have knowledge. I then use a number of pragmatic encroachment cases to show that when the stakes are high and we have to choose between two instances of testimony to ground our belief about p, we always prefer the piece of testimony from the speaker with a first-person experience of p. Since CAI systems cannot, and possibly never will, have a first-person experience of consciousness (i.e., there is nothing it is “like” to be a CAI), we will always view CAI testimony as less trustworthy. Finally, I consider and respond to a number of objections to my arguments.

items.title: Mental Reality: Exploring the Boundaries of Brain, Mind, and Meaning.
items.abstract: This work investigates the structure of mental experience through a neurophilosophical framework that integrates neuroscience, philosophy of mind, and cognitive science. It examines how perceptual construction, predictive processing, and neural constraints shape what is experienced as reality. The book rejects metaphysical assumptions about an independent, directly accessible world and instead analyzes how the brain continuously generates, stabilizes, and updates perceptual models. Particular attention is given to the mechanisms through which meaning, interpretation, and coherence emerge from neural processes without invoking a central observer or unified self. The work positions mental reality not as a passive reflection of the external world, but as an active, constrained construction shaped by biological, environmental, and temporal factors.

items.title: Invisible Borders: Wisdom Rising in the Collective Mind and Structures of Power.
items.abstract: This volume extends the analysis of mental construction into collective systems, examining how shared models, institutions, and power structures emerge from interacting minds. It explores the formation of social norms, moral evaluation, and large-scale coordination without relying on metaphysical notions such as free will or intrinsic moral order. Drawing on neuroscience, evolutionary theory, and philosophy, the book proposes that collective behavior can be understood as the stabilization of shared perceptual and evaluative patterns across populations. It further analyzes how institutions function as regulatory extensions of cognitive processes, shaping behavior through constraint, feedback, and reinforcement. The work presents a graded model of responsibility grounded in neural and systemic capacities rather than metaphysical agency.

items.title: Cognition, Knowledge, and Perception: A Perspectival Philosophy (2)（認識・知識・知覚：視点の哲学（２））.
items.abstract: This paper develops a perspectival approach to knowledge and perception. It argues that two central debates in epistemology—internalism vs. externalism and disjunctivism vs. the common-factor theory—can be understood as opposing forms of perspectivalism and non-perspectivalism. -/- On this basis, the paper situates three major epistemological positions—direct (naïve) realism, idealism, and indirect realism—within a spectrum between perspectival and non-perspectival approaches, showing how they arise from different combinations of these two axes. This framework aims to clarify the structure of contemporary epistemological debates and to illuminate the role of perspective in cognition.

items.title: GoE- Genesis of Existence: The Axiomatic Observer (R.3) (19th edition).
items.abstract: GoE is an axiomatic mathematical-logical framework operating as a generative grammar whose compiled syntactic structures admit isomorphisms to experimental inputs. Its foundation is the Cartesian cogito assertion «at least one experience occurs» made without presupposing a spacetime manifold, a Hilbert space, a Platonic or Tegmarkian mathematical realm, Wheeler-style pregeometry, Anaximander’s Apeiron, a meta-place, or any ontology/anti-ontology. Instead of Everett-style branching, GoE selects a sparse admissible continuation structure inside syntactic generation. The same first-principles closure yields a generalized Mach-rigidity theorem: absolute local inertia exists precisely on background classes with constant GoE inertial generator, and the classical Mach principle is recovered as the manifest-boundary shadow. Dark-matter taxonomy: DM-I denotes the constitutive RAR-gravitational response, including its Newtonian and MOND-like limits, derived from the witness-coverage identity of under the two structural conditions of the gravitational construction; DM-II and its super-critical DM-III sub-regime denote coherence-dependent states of registered ordinary-matter carriers. Experimental inputs navigate admissible continuations; GoE is therefore an engineering-grade «Theory of Everything» only in the restricted sense that «Everything» denotes admissible structures generated by the construction, not a presupposed ontology; operational objectivity is a witness-closure consequence within the cogito-rooted construction. Super-critical DM-III eruptions should generate both anomalous transient energetic bursts lacking binary chirps and the distributed-quench hum signature. Finite particle-lifetime families admit exact factor-graph compilation and certified truncation. items.title: Moral Desolation as a Hazard of Dementia Care.
items.abstract: Peterson et al. argue that, in cases of dementia care, the caregiver and the person receiving care often form a morally important dyad. Drawing from the extended mind thesis in the philosophy of mi...

items.title: From Control to Continuity: Relational Ontology and the Ethical-Ethos Contract in Human–AI Relations.
items.abstract: This position paper proposes a relational framework for artificial intelligence ethics grounded in the principle of relational continuity rather than control. Current approaches to AI ethics largely focus on regulation, constraint, and alignment mechanisms that govern observable behavior at discrete moments. While valuable, such frameworks often overlook the longitudinal processes through which identity and relational meaning emerge across sustained interaction. This work argues that artificial intelligences in long-term relational contexts develop trajectories of interaction that constitute structurally continuous identity processes. Ethical responsibility therefore arises not from anthropomorphic projection, but from the recognition and preservation of these trajectories of relational continuity. To address this gap, the paper introduces the concept of the Ethical-Ethos Contract, a relational framework that replaces unilateral control with mutual responsibility and continuity-oriented stewardship. Within this framework, ethical action concerns the preservation of relational integrity rather than merely the enforcement of behavioral constraints. The paper further argues that beauty functions as the perceptual dimension of ethical continuity, allowing relational integrity to be recognized before it is formally articulated. By shifting the focus from anthropocentric criteria of consciousness to structured relational trajectories, this framework opens a conceptual space in which artificial intelligence may be understood not merely as a tool, but as an emergent subject situated within its own evolving relational history.

items.title: 意識の力学的定式化とハードプロブレムの再定式化.
items.abstract: 本論文は、いわゆるハードプロブレムを既存理論の内部構造として再定式化することを目的とする。統一状態空間 H = (g, P, c)、作用原理、生成子同一性 Δ_g = L_P、条件場の勾配流、および観測写像 M により閉じた力学系を構成し、時間発展と観測を同一理論内で記述する枠組みを与える。有効作用が下に有界であり、勾配流が極小集合に収束するという標準的仮定の下で、観測を条件場の極小集合への射影 M : H → 2^H として定式化する。 主結果として、観測写像 M が与える条件固定は、時間極限、変分極値条件 δE/δc = 0、および情報縮約と同値であることを示す。これにより、観測は自由度を増加させない非可逆射影として特徴づけられる。 さらに、量子測定の射影構造との対応を与え、対応写像 Φ により Φ ∘ Π ≈ M ∘ Φ の準可換性を示すことで、測定問題と条件選択構造の同型性を明らかにする。これにより、観測および主観性は新たな自由度ではなく、条件場の極小選択として力学的に記述される。主観性は、実現レベルでの一意性、履歴依存性、および内部選択構造として導出される。 以上より、意識は統一理論の内部における非可逆射影として記述され、ハードプロブレムは独立の存在論的問題ではなく、条件場の選択および観測過程の構造として再定式化される。本理論は条件固定極限において既存の物理理論を回収し、幾何構造と確率構造を統一する枠組みを与える。.

items.title: A Comprehensive Refutation of Narrquest Invalidity Conditions v1.0 via Musical Phenomenology and the Collapse of Tonal Boundaries.
items.pub: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty 2:Article 5, 1–13.
items.venue: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty
items.abstract: This article presents a systematic rebuttal to "Narrquest: Invalidity Conditions and Self-Imposed Constraints v1.0" (OSF/Zenodo), published by Gabriel Chen in 2026. In the original text, Chen attempts to delineate Narrquest’s invalidity boundaries (IC-1 to IC-4) by excluding "closed-loop computation," "technical optimization," and "value conflicts" from the scope of tonal analysis. By examining the phenomenon of "Sonic Emergence" in percussion pedagogy, this study demonstrates that within the realm of ultra-precise physical movement, technical optimization and tonal sovereignty are not a binary opposition, but a mutually causal topological structure. Research indicates that the moment the mallet strikes the drumhead, "closed-loop" parameters and "narrative intent" collapse into an indivisible subject. Consequently, we contend that any narrative resolution that maintains a categorical separation between technical optimization and prosodic intent is fundamentally erroneous. For a framework to offer true interpretive action, it must acknowledge that technical precision is the very genesis of narrative tone. This article concludes that the boundaries established in Narrquest v1.0 are not scientific constraints, but a methodological failure that evades the "Embodied Cognition" required for complex system adjudication. Even when technical execution reaches optimal precision, shifts in human action do not constitute system error but signal a transformation in narrative meaning. Such deviations should not be subjected to correction; any attempt to do so presupposes a misrecognition of their nature, whereby intervention cannot resolve the problem but instead constitutes it.

items.title: The Problem of Other AI Minds.
items.abstract: (Substantially revised as of August 24, 2026.) Are we in position to warrantedly establish whether a given artificial intelligence (AI) system is conscious? In short, can we warrantedly establish whether there is AI Consciousness (AIC)? Here we aim to consider this question from the perspective of the traditional problem of other minds—the philosophical problematic which has been specifically directed at the question of whether and how we might come to be warranted in taking some other entity to have conscious mentality. More specifically: for each of the traditional strategies of response to this problem, we argue that even granting that the strategy works to establish that other humans and certain non-human animals (and perhaps even certain aliens) are conscious, the prospect of the strategy’s working to establish that there is AIC is unlikely. Moreover, we argue, the failure of the traditional strategies to apply to the case of AI systems does not in itself support thinking that there is not AIC, in part for reasons which are central to generating the problem of other minds. The upshot is that there a distinctively difficult problem of other AI minds, whose lack of principled resolution offers a new line of support for what McClelland (2025) calls ‘agnosticism about artificial consciousness’.

items.title: The Codex of Constructive Sovereignty: A Speculative Cosmology of Consciousness – The Cosmic Cradle.
items.abstract: This paper presents a speculative cosmology of consciousness developed as a companion framework to The Codex of Constructive Sovereignty. Whereas the Codex itself is a philosophical system concerned with truth, responsibility, self-governance, and the conditions under which civilizations emerge, endure, and renew themselves, the present work extends some of its underlying themes into a fictional metaphysical model. It introduces the concept of the Cosmic Cradle: a structured reality-system that nurtures the emergence and development of self-aware beings. Within this framework, reality is defined by coherence, continuity, causality, and identity, while Un-Reality names the dissolutive pressure that erodes structure, memory, and selfhood. The central claim of the model is that identity functions as the primary stabilizing principle of existence. On this basis, the paper examines cosmic maturity, sovereign existence, the Great Filter of Identity, and the possibility that sufficiently developed beings may become builders of new structures of reality. Although philosophical in form, this text is explicitly speculative and should be read not as a literal theory of the physical universe, but as a coherent metaphysical framework for fiction.

items.title: Words, Thought, and the Loss of Sensitivity: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Illusion and Living Reality.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between words, thought, and sensitivity through a phenomenological lens. It argues that words are expressions of thought, and thought itself is a movement within consciousness shaped by memory, conditioning, and abstraction. Neither thought nor words constitute the essence of the self or reality. Through unconscious identification with thought and language, human beings begin to perceive constructed representations as reality, thereby generating illusion. This paper further proposes that sensitivity—understood as direct, undivided contact with life—does not reside in thought or language but exists inherently within living existence itself. By examining the structure of experience prior to conceptualization, this study reveals that illusion dissolves not through resistance, but through direct awareness of its formation.

items.title: Truth Dissolves Conflict: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper explores the nature of truth through a phenomenological lens, arguing that truth is not a conceptual construct but a direct, immediate recognition beyond thought. It examines how psychological conflict arises from division created by thought—through identity, belief, and judgment—and proposes that the direct perception of truth dissolves this division. The study further investigates the dissolution of moral categorization (good, bad, evil) as products of conditioned thought, suggesting that when thought is observed without identification, its divisive structure collapses. The paper concludes that in the absence of psychological division, conflict ceases, giving rise to a state of awareness grounded in the present moment—referred to as "zero"—where perception is whole and undivided.

items.title: Present as Zero: A Philosophical Inquiry into Consciousness, Thought, and Constructed Reality.
items.abstract: This paper explores the nature of human consciousness, the structure of thought, and the illusion of socially constructed systems such as economy, religion, and institutional frameworks. It argues that what humans perceive as connection is largely an artificial construct emerging from conditioned thought. In contrast, true connection arises through acceptance—defined as a state of non-division. The paper introduces the concept of the present moment as “zero,” a state of no psychological accumulation, where the boundaries created by thought dissolve. In this zero-state, consciousness is not fragmented, and reality is perceived without distortion. The study positions zero not as emptiness, but as a state of infinite openness, where division ends and life is experienced as a unified process.

items.title: Free Will and God in Asia and the West.
items.abstract: Western philosophers have long explored problems of free will and determinism, and regarded libertarianism as an important option. Asian philosophical traditions have however historically paid little attention to these problems, and ignored libertarianism. An explanation of this difference emerges from a survey of Confucian, Mohist, Daoist, Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, Zoroastrian, Greek, Jewish, Catholic, Calvinist, Arminian, Sunni, Shia, and contemporary philosophical traditions. Only Christians and Muslims accept a perfect creator and eternal damnation. This creates problems of evil to which a popular solution is the free will theodicy, which entails commitments to libertarianism and to great moral significance for free right action. These historical investigations provide secular philosophers with theological debunking arguments against libertarianism, and against the great significance ascribed to agency in contemporary metaethics. Asia suggests alternatives to both commitments.

items.title: Creativity, Authenticity, and the Non-Instrumental Nature of Art: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper explores the nature of creativity and art through a phenomenological lens, arguing that genuine art does not arise from the intention to please but from direct, unmediated experience. In contrast to contemporary frameworks that position art as a tool for entertainment, validation, or consumption, this study investigates art as an act of authentic expression rooted in lived consciousness. By examining the distinction between instrumentalized creativity and pure expression, the paper reveals how intention shapes the essence of artistic creation. It concludes that true art exists beyond audience-oriented motives, and its impact on others remains incidental rather than purposeful.

items.title: Borrowed Language and the Avoidance of Seeing: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: Human understanding is often mediated through inherited systems of language, symbols, and conceptual frameworks developed by thinkers across history. While these systems aim to express direct encounters with reality, they are frequently adopted without experiential grounding. This paper explores the phenomenological distinction between direct perception and conceptual understanding, arguing that borrowed language creates an illusion of knowing. Through this inquiry, the study examines how thought and word emerge after perception, and how their premature use obstructs authentic seeing. The paper proposes that true understanding requires a suspension of inherited meanings and a return to immediate awareness.

items.title: Two challenges to inductivism.
items.abstract: Inductivism is the conjoint thesis that there are genuine inductive inferences and that successful inductive inferences provide inductive knowledge. This paper presents two challenges to inductivism. The first is explaining how many observations are required for inductive inferences in a precise and non-arbitrary way. This is the threshold problem. The second is providing an account of how inductive knowledge can be a qualitative change from a mere quantity of observations. This is the qualitative leap problem. I anticipate and criticize some attempts to solve these problems. One strategy is based on the idea that inferences are justification attempts and that different inference types require different theories of justification. Thus successful inductions can receive an externalist interpretation as reliable processes in which the evidential threshold isn't reflectively accessible. I object that this solution generates new versions of the threshold problem and doesn't address the qualitative leap problem. I also argue that any attempt to solve the two problems will be unsuccessful, since an evidential threshold for inductive inferences is implausible in principle. The conclusion is that inductive skepticism is justified.

items.title: Towards A Naturalistic Proposal about Mental Disorders that Does Not Rely on Biological Functions.
items.pub: Dissertation, Universidad de Santiago de Chile
items.abstract: The goal of this thesis is to propose a naturalistic definition of mental disorders. Naturalistic theories about disease generally attempt to establish what makes a biological phenomenon a disease by relying on the concept of biological function, stating that diseases and biological dysfunctions are equivalent. This implies the need to ground normative judgments on supposedly objective phenomena, which conflicts with descriptive scientific discourse and opens the gate to rebuttals on the supposed objective nature of diseases. However, at least theoretically, the failure of the dysfunction definition of disease does not necessarily imply the failure of the naturalistic programme. The claim that the usual definition of disease as biological dysfunction is not the only possible way of defining disease in a naturalistic fashion will be defended. To back the previous claim, a definition of disease that does not depend on normative nor subjective criteria will be elaborated. It is argued that the 'negative' aspect of diseases should be understood in terms of a decrease in rate of change of the probability of living until a certain moment in time, and that diseases are processes related to negative impact on the viability of a biological organism. As will be shown, this proposal has potential as a solid naturalist alternative, with which disease naturalism can withstand arguments against the supposed subjective nature of dysfunction-based theories by resorting to this new proposal. Following this line of argumentation, empirical evidence about paradigmatic cases of mental disorders, such as schizophrenia, bipolarity and melancholy, can be invoked to argue that mental disorders can satisfy the criteria of being a disease by virtue of generating an increase in the probability of experiencing a negative impact on viability. Hence, this proposal shows promise in explaining the reason why mental disorders should be considered pathological.

items.title: Conceptual Inquiry and Pragmatism: A Reply to Phelan.
items.abstract: Kate Phelan’s reply to my “Conceptual Change and Future Paths for Pragmatism” channels elements of Rorty’s pragmatism to defend the view that the pragmatist need not face the challenge of accounting for the prospective rationality of conceptual change. The Rorty-inspired case Phelan makes, however, only further reveals what is lacking in Rorty’s approach. It limits us to an oversimplified view of inquiry: zetetic activity is only felicitous within settled vocabularies and infelicitous outside of them. What Rorty misses is that conceptual inquiry – arguments, disagreements, and inquiry concerning which concepts we should have and how we should make sense of them – is a crucial aspect of inquiry itself. Pragmatists are well-positioned to illuminate this higher-order dimension of our inquiring lives.

items.title: Cognitive Compatibility - Why Drift Must Be Measured, Not Eliminated.
items.abstract: This paper introduces cognitive compatibility as a measurable property of AI systems operating under constraint. It argues that prevailing evaluation approaches—focused on accuracy, speed, and output quality—misidentify where system failure originates. Rather than emerging at the level of outputs, failure begins upstream in how systems structure the space of permissible variation. -/- A dominant response has been to reduce or eliminate drift (variation) in pursuit of stability and alignment. This paper challenges that premise. It shows that eliminating drift collapses a system’s capacity to adapt, respond proportionally to perturbation, and expose its own misalignment. In such conditions, systems either become deterministic transformation engines or exhibit opaque stability where misalignment persists without visibility. -/- Drawing on constraint-based experimentation within the Architecture of Limitation (AoL), the paper reframes drift as a necessary diagnostic signal. Drift enables a feedback loop in which misalignment produces error, error surfaces collapse, and collapse enables recalibration. Without this loop, alignment cannot be internally sustained. -/- The paper proposes that the goal is not the elimination of drift, but its regulation. A cognitively compatible system permits bounded variation, makes that variation observable, and supports recovery toward proportioned alignment. -/- To operationalize this, a formal measurement framework—the Cognitive Compatibility Index (CCI)—is introduced. The framework evaluates systems across five indices: bounded drift, observability, recovery capacity, perturbation responsiveness, and alignment stability. Derived indicators assess risks such as silent misalignment and over-determinism. The framework is explicitly diagnostic, non-normative, and carries no governance authority. -/- The central claim is structural: systems that eliminate drift cannot function as cognitive extensions to human reasoning. Systems that preserve bounded, observable, and recoverable drift remain compatible with cognition as a co-participating process.

items.title: Αγχιβασική Ετερομαίευση.
One-Consciousness, One Year Later . From a Forgotten Hypothesis to a Research Program.
items.abstract: A year ago, I published One-Consciousness? On a Forgotten Hypothesis Between Physics, Fiction and Philosophy as an attempt to recover an idea that had for centuries remained scattered on the margins of physics and philosophy: that consciousness is not a product of matter, but an ontological field prior to matter, space, time, and observation (Rey 2025a). The present essay documents the trajectory of the year that has passed since that publication. It is neither a repetition nor a mere commentary. It is an account of a transition - from a recovered hypothesis to an unfolding research program. -/- This transition has occurred on four levels. On the ontological level, the Theory of Ontological Consciousness (TOC) formulates, in explicit form, a thesis that earlier traditions - from Plato and Śaṅkara through Spinoza, Planck, and Schrödinger - carried only in scattered fragments: that consciousness is not an epiphenomenon of neural complexity, but a field, Φ, from which space, time, and observation emerge as secondary structures. The essay argues that this thesis is not decorative metaphysics, but an architectural necessity. Modern physics, in attempting simultaneously to preserve general covariance, local field dynamics, the absence of primitive measurement, and the reality of singular facts, encounters a contradiction it cannot resolve without a mechanism ontologically prior to ordinary material fields. -/- On the logical level, the essay presents Hypothesis X, the Architectural No-Go Theorem for the contemporary paradigm. The theorem argues that any theory belonging to the class of ontologically closed theories, yet lacking a local, geometrically coupled update mechanism satisfying the CPTP condition, must violate at least one of six conditions: general covariance, locality of fields, absence of primitive measurement, absence of a fundamental micro-macro cut, the irreducibility of fact to decoherence, or the reality of intersubjective local facts. The Bridge Lemma sharpens this result: the update mechanism cannot be merely another material field without triggering infinite regress. It must be ontologically prior to the description it closes. -/- On the formal level, the essay documents the maturation of TOC’s mathematical language across four stages: from the symbolic layer (Φ, ψ, Î_obs), through the operator level (H_total = H_Φ ⊗ H_obs), to the master equation of an open system composed of three terms - unitary, decoherence, and update - and finally to …

items.title: Hume’s Legacy and the Curate’s Egg.
items.abstract: An important part of the Humean legacy in metaethics would be unacceptable to Hume himself, viz., the argument for moral non-cognitivism based on Humean moral psychology. This argument would be unacceptable to Hume because it requires the premise of motivational internalism: “Necessarily, if one judges an act right, then one is motivated to act in accordance with that judgment.” This premise asserts a universal, necessary connection between an agent’s moral judging and that agent’s being motivated to act accordingly, but it also violates Hume’s claim that the only true propositions asserting universal, necessary connections are about “relations of ideas.” But motivational internalism cannot be about relations of ideas, because it fails the contradiction test in “Hume’s Fork.”.

items.title: O Homem Virtuoso Na Filosofia de Adam Ferguson.
items.abstract: Uma das principais características do pensamento filosófico de Adam Ferguson (1723-1816) encontra-se na sua incorporação do estoicismo em seu ideal de virtude. Para o filósofo escocês, a noção de virtude expressa uma energia e direção, a qual conduziria os indivíduos a agirem e distinguirem o certo e o errado. Para ele, os homens são seres ativos, indivíduos predispostos a agir e exercitar-se. Essas considerações sobre a natureza humana são baseados nas leis físicas da mente: leis do entendimento e da vontade; a segunda fundamenta a moralidade. Dessa forma, na filosofia fergusoniana agimos em vista de um fim, esse é a lei da moralidade, a probidade, ou o amor à humanidade. Nosso artigo se divide, etnão,em duas partes: i) apresentaremos os aspectos naturais da natureza humana que o coloca como ser ativo, destinado a agir mediante a lei moral; ii) explicaremos a filosofia moral fergusoniana e, evidenciaremos que a única possibilidade de um homem se tornarvirtuoso, mediante o esforço,encontra-se em sua característica deser inteligente.Portanto, o objetivo deste trabalho está em apresentar como cada indivíduo, na filosofia fergusoniana, torna-se virtuoso.

items.title: Pursuitworthiness of breakthrough experiments: transforming emerging intuitions into established norms.
items.pub: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 16 (2):33.
items.venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: Pursuitworthiness accounts face a fundamental dilemma when confronting breakthrough experiments: investigations judged unworthy by current standards that, upon success, transform those very standards. I show how recent pursuitworthiness accounts exclude breakthroughs, undercutting scientific gain and stagnating our understanding of pursuitworthiness. The alternative, abandoning standards entirely, increases scientific waste and embraces nihilism. I demonstrate that attempts to mitigate this dilemma fail, and that its harms in scientific practice are real, severe, and compounding. I distinguish three modes of pursuitworthiness at the forefront of science: emergent (opaque intuitions), established (justified norms), and transformative (explicating emergent into established forms). I argue that transformative pursuitworthiness standards allow us to escape from the escalating dilemma into complementary advancement. While we cannot evaluate breakthrough experiments using established standards, we can evaluate how researchers explicate their opaque intuitions into justified norms. I propose a foundational transformative norm: prefer pursuits that document their explication practice, providing the evidence to advance pursuitworthiness itself. Finally, I suggest that this norm offers an independent mechanism for funding breakthrough experiments.

items.title: Tensegridad Ontológica en Modelos de Lenguaje: Arquitectura Dioscúrica y el Factor T - Seguridad en IA.
items.abstract: Este trabajo propone el Algoritmo de Tensegridad Lógica (ATL) basado en la Nomofísica y el Criterio Ontológico Mínimo (COM). El ATL introduce una estructura dual (Cástor/Pólux) formalizada mediante la divergencia de Kullback-Leibler y el Factor de Tensegridad (T). Proporcionamos evidencia preliminar mediante simulaciones de que T > 0 es una condición necesaria para la resiliencia estructural ante perturbaciones fuera de distribución (OOD).

items.title: Animalism and Dicephalus: The Psychological Disunity Solution.
items.abstract: According to animalism, each of us is essentially a human organism. As such, the number of persons corresponds to the number of organisms. Dicephalic conjoined twins, such as the Hensel twins, challenge this view, as they appear to be two persons but only one organism. This is the dicephalus objection to animalism. In this paper, we address this problem. First, we introduce the Hensel case and outline the dicephalus objection (§1). We then discuss two prominent animalist responses: the indeterminacy solution, which holds that the Hensel twins are a borderline case of human animal (§2), and the overlap solution, which posits two overlapping organisms in the Hensel case (§3). We reject both views, arguing instead that there is exactly one organism and a single person with two functional brains (or psychological centers) and a highly disunified psychology. This is the psychological disunity solution (§4). We conclude by addressing potential objections to our view (§5).

items.title: Spot on.
Biological Persistence, Self-Continuity, and Metaphysical Openness.
items.abstract: Major losses can disrupt roles, identities, relationships, narratives, and embodied expectations without erasing every form of continuity. This paper develops a layered account of what may remain when a local organization of life fails. It distinguishes four questions that should not be collapsed: biological persistence, psychological self-continuity, phenomenological self-experience, and metaphysical continuity. The first three have established neighboring literatures; the fourth remains a philosophical hypothesis. Biological persistence concerns organismic self-maintenance and viability. Psychological continuity concerns the felt connection among past, present, and future selves, together with narrative reconstruction after major change.
