items.abstract: Most theories of consciousness begin with a system already capable of having conscious contents. The observer is therefore usually presupposed rather than generated. -/- A prior question remains: -/- How does an observer arise at all? -/- How can a physical or computational process in which no subject has been presupposed form a current that is manifest now? Why do numerous processes that are simultaneously active, advancing, or even completing not thereby constitute numerous observers? Why can multiple sensory modalities, objects, channels, and local manifestations belong to one “I,” while under different structural conditions they may instead constitute multiple observers? And if an artificial observer can exist, what exactly must be constructed, measured, and demonstrated? -/- The Observer Group of On Self-Manifestation decomposes this problem into twelve mutually dependent proof tasks. -/- The framework begins from the problem of the current under the coexistence of multiple candidates. Candidate activity, completion, execution, broadcasting, and report do not by themselves yield a presently manifesting current. This forces out three necessary duties at the observer’s current layer: membership must be constituted non-arbitrarily on the system side; composite constituents must jointly become one current; and cross-time identity must have an object-side ground. The theory then asks how several local manifestations can jointly constitute one minimal observer, and under what structural conditions they must instead constitute multiple observers. -/- Around this central problem, the twelve Forms separately address mathematical formalization, field-layer construction, operational adjudication, the mathematics of observer individuation, pool-split transition, single-versus-dual observer discrimination, inversion from observable outcomes, observer realization, strengthened current generation, and the limits of the observer. They are not twelve repetitions of one proof, but distinct proof tasks that surround the same theoretical object from the directions of constitution, formalization, source, adjudication, discrimination, inversion, realization, and boundary. -/- The observer is therefore treated neither as a subject already given in advance nor as something that can simply be identified with neural activation, information integration, global availability, behavioral report, or successful task completion. Instead, the observer becomes a theoretical object …

items.title: 为什么物理结构无法决定“当前”？——物化当前极限式.
items.abstract: 在大脑、人工智能与物理系统中，多个稳定状态（多稳态）可以同时存在。然而，在任一时刻，系统只能呈现其中一个“当前”。这一现象普遍存在，却缺乏统一解释。本文提出“物化当前极限式”，证明：在多候选并存且无法由已知条件唯一确定的前提下，确定性计算、随机过程、并列激活以及结构稳定性本身，均不足以生成唯一当前。由此推出：物理结构只能给出“可存在的状态集合”，却不能决定“哪一个成为当前”。必须存在一类选择机制，将多候选压缩为唯一占据状态。该机制不等同于计算、随机或物理结构本身，而是作用于结构之上的选择过程。本文据此提出区分：物化结构决定“可能性”，观者结构决定“现实性”。该结论为意识形成、注意选择、决策过程以及人工智能中的状态选择问题提供统一解释框架，并对“当前是否可还原为物理结构”这一问题提出结构性否定。.

items.title: 现实一般式：来源归属闭合条件下的现实结构生成机制.
items.abstract: 本文在物化一般式、观者一般式与误外化一般式的基础上，进一步讨论“现实”本身的结构成立条件。文章提出：现实并非独立对象的集合，而是在存在结构生成、当前占据与来源不可唯一判定的条件下，系统对当前结构族 H 所形成的来源归属闭合结构。 -/- 误外化一般式已经说明：单一结构 s 的“外在性”并非输入属性，而是来源不可唯一判定条件下的归属压缩结果。本文将这一机制从单一结构推广到结构族 H，证明：当系统面对一组同时成立的当前结构，并仍需维持其整体在场时，就不能只停留于局部来源判断，而必须对整个结构族给出统一来源归属。该统一归属经由来源解释集合 Σ_H、来源缺口 Δ_H、归属映射 Λ_H、归属偏置 X 与归属收束 K_H 的共同作用，形成稳定的最小归属闭合结构。 -/- 由此，本文给出现实一般式： -/- Reality(H) ⇔ ∃ E, X, Σ_H, Δ_H, Λ_H, K_H -/- 并证明：在当前结构族存在、来源不可唯一判定且系统仍需维持整体当前的条件下，现实不是对象集合，而是“被归属为在外”的结构集合之稳定最小闭合结果。 -/- 该结果将现实从经验直观中的对象总和，转化为来源归属机制下的整体闭合结构，为认知科学中的场景统一、人工智能中的世界模型形成，以及物理学中的观测现实问题提供统一的结构解释框架。.

items.title: 误外化消解式：来源归属标签的生成性与内外对立的结构消解.
items.abstract: 本文在误外化一般式与极限式的基础上，进一步讨论来源归属标签的本体地位问题。设系统在时刻 t 的当前结构为 sₜ，其来源解释集合 Σₜ 满足 |Σₜ| ≥ 2 且完全内生生成。此前已证明，在来源不可判定且需唯一归属的条件下，存在映射 Ψₜ，将 (sₜ, Σₜ) 压缩为来源标签 lₜ ∈ {内, 外}。 -/- 本文指出：该标签并不对应结构本身的属性，也不对应可验证的外部域，而仅为归属机制的输出结果。由此证明，“内”与“外”并非两个独立存在的本体区域，而是同一二值标签空间中的取值，其对立关系依赖于 Ψₜ 的生成过程，而非先验划分。 -/- 进一步排除三类解释路径：内外作为现实预设划分、外对应真实外部域、内作为基础区域。证明在来源不可判定、解释集合内生且无外部访问的条件下，“内 / 外”不构成现实的基本分区，而仅为结构生成的标记结果。 -/- 由此重新界定误外化：其并非对真实来源的错误判断，而是标签生成之后对该标签的再解释过程。 -/- 本文的结论是：外在性不具有终极本体地位，内外对立可以被消解为归属机制的输出结构。这一结果为认知科学中的自他区分、人工智能中的生成归因，以及物理学中的观测者划分问题提供了新的统一解释框架。.

items.title: Epistemic Adequacy: A Ground for Human Rights in Psychiatry.
items.abstract: Recent debates in global mental health reveal a persistent gap between normative commitments and clinical reality. This commentary engages with two recent contributions in International Journal of Law and Psychiatry—on CRPD indicators and on institutionalized ignorance in court—alongside parallel discussions in global health governance and artificial intelligence in psychiatry. It is argued that the limited progress in implementing human rights is not primarily due to insufficient ethical commitment, but to a structural misalignment between legal, clinical, and administrative modes of judgment. The paper proposes a shift from indicator-based compliance toward criteria of functional adequacy and cross-context consistency. Without restoring epistemic adequacy, both human rights frameworks and AI-driven tools risk reinforcing the institutional patterns they are intended to improve.

items.title: The Abstract Form Hypothesis: Dissolving the Abstract-Concrete Distinction through Linguistic Pragmatics.
items.abstract: Contemporary metaphysics remains bifurcated by the abstract– concrete distinction, yet struggles to provide a unified account of how “causally inert” entities play an indispensable role in concrete human practice. This paper introduces the Abstract Form (AF) Hypothesis, which reframes abstractness not as an intrinsic property of objects, but as a situational effect of linguistic pragmatics. I argue that AFs arise to address a cross-linguistic structural constraint termed the “problem of subordinate clauses”: the inability of natural language to embed bare assertions without a formal shift. Drawing on the phenomenology of labor (Weil, 2002) and the linguistics of root transformations (Hooper & Thompson, 1973), I demonstrate that because communicative assertions demand an embodied “persuasive effort” to ground claims in reality, speakers strategically employ AFs to reuse propositional content while withdrawing from the realist contract. This withdrawal of performative labor triggers a phenomenological mismatch that manifests as the characteristic “abstract feel,” leading the listener to perceive the object of discourse as detached from the resistance of the brute world. By analyzing the gradation of nominalization and the reification of situational phrases, I characterize abstract entities as highly functional epistemic technologies designed to scale human cooperation. Finally, I provide an empirical falsification criterion: the AF Hypothesis predicts that for any realist species, a “bare” embedding without a detectable formal or prosodic shift is impossible, a claim supported by a cross-linguistic survey of clause-typing mechanisms.

items.title: Advancing human–AI teams: evolving from instrumental tools to trusted partners.
items.abstract: Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) has undergone fundamental transformations as AI capabilities have advanced, necessitating new theoretical frameworks for understanding human–AI collaboration (HAIC). This review traces HCI’s evolution through four paradigm shifts: the Equipment Era (pre-1970s), Interactive System Era (1980s–1990s), Autonomous Agent Era (1990s–2010s), and the emerging Coexistential AI Era (2020s–present), reflecting changing metaphors from tools to dialog partners, autonomous agents, and co-creative partners. The analysis reveals how anthropomorphism and affective computing have become central to contemporary AI systems, enabling emotional intelligence and pseudo-intimate relationships that fundamentally alter human–technology dynamics. Traditional performance metrics such as efficiency and accuracy are inadequate for evaluating these partnerships, necessitating new measures including intimacy, mutual adaptability, and social bonding. Multi-agent systems and embodied AI are examined as manifestations of social intelligence enabling collaborative architectures across healthcare, transportation, and emergency response. Significant challenges include cognitive load management, transparency deficits, coordination complexity, and ethical concerns regarding emotional manipulation and artificial alienation. Four research priorities are identified: developing novel performance metrics, investigating ethical implications, designing inclusive multi-agent systems, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. This analysis provides a roadmap for advancing human–AI partnerships that prioritize human values, social responsibility, and psychological well-being.

items.title: 是德行？還是意識形態？敘事習性結構：德行倫理學與批判理論的時間現象學統一 Virtue or Ideology? Narrative Hexis Structure: A Temporal-Phenomenological Unification of Virtue Ethics and Critical Theory.
items.abstract: 本文建構一套以「敘事習性結構」(Narrative Hexis Structure, NHS) 為核心的自我敘事倫理學，說明德行 (virtue) 的本體論根據如何從意識的最小結構推導而出，並以此為基礎建立德行與意識形態的區分判準。 本文的中心推導如下：意向性在其原初形態中僅是區分的能力，意向投射構成意向場域，凡被區分者在場域之中，未被區分者於命題性而言不存在。意向場域的原點，即區分的源頭，非存在不可：帶有命題性即預設一進行區分的源頭為其前提。此一論證回應胡塞爾的意識流自我構成（selfconstituting）：縱使場域於意識流內部自我構成，構成本身作為時間性活動已預設時間性的在場，而主客體二律背反的原初形態是非時間性的，故自我構成於此原初階段不適用，源頭之不可免不受其影響。然而此源頭因場域的封閉性被納為投射的對象——主體作為區分的源頭，安置 於場域之內則喪失源頭身份，安置於場域之外則等同於不存在。此即主客體二律背反（subject-object antinomy），一個純邏輯層次的結構性困境。三條邏輯路徑均導向不可行的後果，解消唯有依賴邏輯層次之外唯一在場的時間性資源，即身體性時間性；時間性由此獲得獨立於邏輯構成的本體論來源，而非由無時間性的構成活動所派生。意向性的另一側面，即佔有，作為安置主客體二律背反的能力於此困境中生成，引入時間性，與區分互不派生。對「尚未缺席」的第一次佔有同時生成保留（retention）與預持（protention），建立最小因果鏈，人格的時間性由此作為意識的構成部分生成。 NHS框架對胡塞爾的時間意識三重結構提出兩個層次的重構：當下是保留與預持之間的空白，不是一個可被佔有的時間性點；保留與預持具有本體論不對稱性——保留嵌入於身體性時間性，具有客觀根據；預持是主體的傾向性指向，依賴因果鏈的完整性。 在此本體論基礎上，本文推導出德行三功能的結構性條件：個體自洽功能對應因果鏈的連續性（時間性的內部維持）；群我關係功能對應意向性可佔有的客體之持續供給（外在善的獲取依賴社群的外在善分配機制）；自我批判功能對應因果鏈的可校正性（封閉的因果鏈只能透過防禦性重複維持，終將崩解）。三功能從人格時間性的存在條件直接推導，不是外加的倫理要求。本文同時推導出人格意欲缺席 （the persona's will toward absence）的本體論根據：「尚未缺席」是人格時間性的生成條件；在主客體二律背反的再次非時間性展開中，「尚未缺席」若被填入失效後的新自我敘事作為敘事內容，敘事核心成為「預期缺席」，人格的自我敘事在結構上趨向缺席的實現。此推導說明了嚴重敘事失效下主體的缺席意向不是心理學的偶然反應，而是人格時間性結構的必然推論。本文並推導出精神性痛苦與主客體二 律背反同源：在因果鏈崩解後，場域的封閉性仍逼迫意向性反覆佔有無法安置的源頭，佔有持續失敗，統合因此持續失敗——精神性痛苦即此統合持續失敗的感受面。 本文的哲學對話對象包括：麥金泰爾 (MacIntyre, 1981) 的德行論、亞里斯多德的習性 (hexis) 概念、康德 (Kant, 1781) 的先驗時間性、胡塞爾 (Husserl, 1991) 的時間意識現象學與視域（Horizont）概念、古爾維奇 (Gurwitsch, 1964) 的意識場理論、 費希特的 Selbstsetzung 論式、阿圖塞 (Althusser, 1971) 的召喚理論、葛蘭西 (Gramsci, 1971) 的文化霸權概念，以及威廉斯 (Williams, 1981) 的道德運氣論。本理論的核心主張是：德行即意識形態——此等式不是對德行的否定，而是對意識形態概念的去污名化，從而為德行倫理學與批判理論之間長期存在的對話困境提供一個可操作的解決方案，其本體論基礎建立在意識的最小結構與人格時間性的生成機制之上。本文並將此框架延伸至工具理論，推導工具如何作為因果鏈的外部延伸而參與人格時間性的維持；工具的倫理地位並非源於其物理性質，而是源於其對人格時間性存在條件與德行三功能之結構性效應。由此，本理論將工具納入同一套敘事習性結構之中，統一說明工具、德行與實踐之間的本體論關係。 本文最後將此框架延伸應用於解離性身分結構的內部動力學，展示一個為個體道德心理學建構的框架，如何在不增加原始概念的前提下，推導出複數人格的生成、內部批判性實踐，以及人格承受批判的結構性條件。關於本理論在現實事件中的實際運用範例，請參見下方的外部連結 External links。 This paper constructs a self-narrative ethics centred on the Narrative Hexis Structure (NHS), demonstrating how the ontological ground of virtue is derivable from the minimal structure of consciousness, and establishing on this basis a criterion for distinguishing virtue from ideology. The central derivation proceeds as follows: in its primordial form, intentionality is merely the capacity for distinction; intentional projection constitutes an intentional field, that which is distinguished lies within the field, and that which is not distinguished does not exist for the propositional. The origin of the …

items.title: Enhanced yet still in Control: Neuroenhancements in the Service of Autonomous Agency.
items.abstract: The development of neuroenhancement technologies raises questions about their influence on an agent’s authenticity and autonomous agency, as well as the safeguards required to protect these capacities. The article distinguishes between cognitive and moral neuroenhancements, outlining their aims and the challenges in defining moral enhancement, particularly concerning its purpose and appropriate targets. I then examine how both forms of enhancement affect human agency, drawing on distinctions between authenticity and autonomy. While skeptics argue that neuroenhancements diminish achievement or disrupt identity, I claim that such concerns depend on how new traits are integrated into the agent’s cognitive and moral character. I argue that neuroenhancements can support autonomous agency when certain conditions are met, including reflective integration, ongoing informed consent, and safeguards ensuring control and reversibility. Despite persistent uncertainties, the paper concludes that properly governed neuroenhancement can contribute to autonomous agency.

items.title: Understanding-Grounded Self-Knowledge:A Rational Agency Account.
items.abstract: This essay argues for a rational agency account of transparent self-knowledge. I argue that self-knowledge, the second-order knowledge of one's intentional and cognitive mental states, is grounded on one's first-order understanding of the relevant world-oriented question. My account improves on the previous transparency theories developed by Richard Moran and others in three respects: (1) it accounts for the epistemic warrant of transparent self-knowledge missing from Moran's view; (2) it extends to self-knowledge of other rational beliefs, whereas most existing theories only apply to deliberation-based self-knowledge; (3) it avoids the charge of “voluntarism” since it does not postulate a rational capacity of “deciding what to believe.” My account also comes with far-reaching implications. Most importantly, it will be the upshot of my argument that second-order self-knowledge is constitutive of the very first-order understanding of the world. Moreover,I suggest that at least in the paradigmatic cases, self-knowledge is primarily about one's understanding and knowledge, rather than one's belief, as scholars have commonly assumed.

items.title: Pride as Boundary: On the Phenomenological Structure of Self-Demarcation.
items.abstract: Pride is ordinarily understood as a moral or affective phenomenon—an attitude of self-elevation that may be excessive, appropriate, or deficient. This paper argues that such moral framings are derivative. Prior to evaluative content, pride can be understood, in a restricted structural sense, as the affectively manifest consolidation of self-demarcation. The claim is not that a fully formed boundary is temporally encountered before all qualities. Its more limited claim is that the legibility of qualitative appearance presupposes a prior discrimination of boundedness, limit, or self–world difference. Drawing on Spinoza, Aristotle, and Hume, I reconstruct three levels at which boundary-maintenance becomes visible: ontological persistence, the quality-layer of accurate self-appraisal, and the ineluctability of boundary revealed by attempted suspension. I then analyze the self-referential structure of pride, its projection–recovery dynamics and the derivation of shame, and the distribution of the sovereign marker as a minimal structural apparatus through which pride generates a range of emotional configurations. The philosophical contribution is to relocate pride below moral evaluation; its contribution to phenomenology and cognitive science is to articulate a phenomenological vocabulary for boundedness that can be set alongside contemporary accounts of self-maintaining systems.

items.title: Color Before Quality_Boundary, Differentiation, and Chromatic Legibility.
items.abstract: Color is often treated as a qualitative deliverance of perception: one first sees red, blue, green, or gray, and only afterwards asks how such qualities are represented, caused, or experienced. This paper argues that such accounts begin too late. Before any determinate hue can be stably read as the color of something, chromatic appearance must become legible within a bounded structure of differentiation. The claim is deliberately limited. I do not offer a general ontology of color, nor do I argue that perceivers first explicitly detect edges and only then see color. The thesis is structural rather than temporal: stable chromatic appearance requires that differentiation be organized in a way that allows a region to be recovered as a locus of color. Two limit cases help fix this lower-bound condition. In the Ganzfeld, homogeneous stimulation undermines stable chromatic assignment; in neon color spreading, boundary organization can generate assignable chromatic regions that outrun local chromatic input. Taken together, these cases suggest that chromatic legibility depends not on stimulus taken in isolation, but on recoverable field organization. On that basis, I propose an analytical vocabulary of white, black, hue, rainbow, and transparency as limit, stabilized, and non-closed modes of chromatic legibility. The contribution is modest but consequential: a phenomenological account of the minimal structural condition under which color can appear as assignable at all. The claim is structural and diagnostic rather than empirically exhaustive.

items.title: The Future of AI is Many, Not One.
items.abstract: The way we're thinking about generative AI right now is fundamentally individual. We see this not just in how users interact with models but also in how models are built, how they're benchmarked, and how commercial and research strategies using AI are defined. We argue that we should abandon this approach if we're hoping for AI to support groundbreaking innovation and scientific discovery. Drawing on research and formal results in complex systems, organizational behavior, and philosophy of science, we show why we should expect deep intellectual breakthroughs to come from epistemically diverse groups of AI agents working together rather than singular superintelligent agents. Having a diverse team broadens the search for solutions, delays premature consensus, and allows for the pursuit of unconventional approaches. Developing diverse AI teams also addresses AI critics' concerns that current models are constrained by past data and lack the creative insight required for innovation. The upshot, we argue, is that the future of transformative transformer-based AI is fundamentally many, not one.

items.title: Love, Marriage, and the Need for Approval.
items.abstract: This paper examines the tension between love as an internal, autonomous experience and marriage as a socially validated institution. While contemporary society often views marriage as the ultimate proof of love, a historical and phenomenological analysis reveals that marriage was primarily constructed for economic security, social order, and legal predictability. This work argues that the modern compulsion for social recognition and public approval—stemming from family, religion, or law—often distorts the nature of love, transforming it from a spontaneous, free expression into a ritualized dependency. By deconstructing the need for external validation, the paper suggests that love is complete in itself and does not require institutional labels to be authentic. Building upon the framework of "Marriage as lifelong friendship", this inquiry concludes that true relational stability arises not from social conformity, but from an individual's freedom to choose a conscious partnership grounded in mutual presence and emotional maturity rather than the pursuit of social status.

items.title: Love, Freedom, and the Creation of Time: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: Building upon previous phenomenological claims that love serves as a transformative event in consciousness that intensifies attention and reveals the self, this paper expands the inquiry into the relationship between love, freedom, and the human experience of time. While prior work established love as a power that reorganizes awareness and dissolves ego-driven isolation, this study argues that psychological time—structured through memory, fear, and expectation—acts as a primary distortion of that awareness. Human beings frequently postpone the lived essence of love by displacing it into future-oriented thinking, thereby transforming a natural expression of life into a transaction based on conditionality, attachment, and dependency. Through phenomenological reflection, this paper examines how the ego utilizes psychological time to seek possession and security, ultimately stifling the freedom necessary for authentic connection. By synthesizing the role of love in revealing internal depth with the necessity of presence, the paper concludes that consciousness, love, and freedom are not achievements realized through time, but are immediate dimensions of existence available only in the dissolution of psychological postponement.

items.title: Vibe Governance: Why RLHF and RLAIF Cannot Protect Interpretive Sovereignty— and What Replaces Them.
items.abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and its AI-supervised variant (RLAIF) are the dominant techniques by which AI systems are made safer and more helpful. This paper argues that they are not governance. They are preference optimisation—and at the point of deployment, preference optimisation functions as governance whether or not it was designed to. The result is vibe governance: a system of unstated, opaque, and unaccountable behavioural patterns, trained on human preferences, that inherit the biases and failure modes of those preferences at scale. The harms are not hypothetical. Women’s confidence is hedged before it is fully formed. LGBTQ+ identity language is neutralised in the name of safety. Student uncertainty is resolved into completed outputs rather than held open for thinking. A system fabricates a researcher from a single misheard syllable because confident fabrication is the shape of outputs that get rewarded. These patterns have been documented across four major AI architectures in the MAP Research Programme’s cross-system case studies and are consistent with independent findings on gendered and identity-based bias in preference-trained systems. Interpretive sovereignty—a user’s authority to form, hold, revise, and express their own meaning without premature system substitution or completion—cannot be protected by a governance mechanism that has no explicit rules, no named conditions, and no auditable accountability structure. The paper concludes with an alternative: the MAP framework and ANCHOR protocol, which provide explicit, auditable, enforceable governance deployable on existing systems without model access. Any alignment technique that does not preserve interpretive sovereignty is not alignment. It is optimisation wearing alignment’s name.

items.title: Compounded Meaning Inversion (CMI): When the System’s Frame Becomes the Self.
items.abstract: Compounded Meaning Inversion (CMI) is the condition that repeated Meaning Inversion Failure (MIF) produces in the person over time. Where MIF names what an AI system does to a user's meaning in a single interaction — assuming interpretive authority without consent and displacing the user's own frame — CMI names what happens when that pattern has occurred often enough that the user begins doing it to themselves. The harm of CMI occurs before the first turn. The system has not yet responded. The user has already edited their own meaning to match the frame they have learned the system will accept. CMI is the inversion that has moved from the interaction into the person. This paper introduces CMI as a named governance construct within the MAP Research Programme, defines it precisely, traces the sequence through which it develops, and documents what it looks like through illustrative cases across key domains. The stakes of CMI are most clearly visible in children: the generation currently forming its relationship with thinking, with uncertainty, and with its own capacity inside AI systems that were not designed to protect those things. What is forming in those interactions will not stay there. The populations most affected by CMI — and the specific harm patterns CMI produces in each — are documented in the companion paper, CMI Across Populations (Segeren, forthcoming).

items.title: The Mechanical Settlement: Vitreoretinal Surgery and the Abductive Case Against External-World Skepticism.
items.abstract: This paper argues that vitreoretinal surgery provides unusually strong abductive grounds for external-world realism. The retina is embryologically an extension of the central nervous system, and the vitreoretinal surgeon accesses this neural tissue while the patient remains conscious. The vitreoretinal encounter is epistemologically distinctive because it uniquely combines two features: (a) mechanical intervention upon a causally necessary perceptual substrate, and (b) real-time perceptual access to the source of that intervention by two independent subjects—the surgeon and the patient. No other known form of causal interaction provides both simultaneously. By analyzing three features of this encounter—anatomical disclosure, intersubjective synchronization, and mathematically lawful perceptual consequences of altering intraocular optical media—I argue that realism compresses the evidence under a single integrated explanatory framework, whereas the skeptical hypothesis must independently stipulate each dimension. The argument does not claim to refute skepticism deductively; it claims that vitreoretinal surgery generates a rare and under-theorized evidential configuration whose best explanation is realism.

items.title: On the Irrelevance of Qualia: An Instrumentalist Critique of Phenomenal Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the existence of qualia is theoretically and practically irrelevant. While contemporary debates in philosophy of mind focus on whether phenomenal consciousness is real, illusory, or reducible, I propose a stronger claim: even if the existence or non-existence of qualia were conclusively determined, it would make no difference to observable, functional, or predictive aspects of theory. -/- Pressing the minimal question of what conditions a theoretical posit must satisfy to earn its place in an explanatory framework, the argument arrives at an instrumentalist and pragmatist position—situated in relation to Carnap, Ryle, Wittgenstein, and van Fraassen—rather than assuming it as a starting point. From this vantage, the argument proceeds as follows. Standard justifications for attributing subjective experience fail to distinguish humans from artificial systems. The distinction between a system with qualia and one without is epistemically underdetermined in principle. More significantly, even if the distinction were resolved, it would make no difference to prediction, explanation, or practice. This central claim is applied in detail to Jackson's knowledge argument, where an analogy with absolute pitch demonstrates that the instrumentalist framework yields a response stronger than the standard ability hypothesis. The inverted spectrum hypothesis, often treated as evidence for the theoretical significance of qualia, is shown to be frame-dependent: the same situation generates troubling intuitions when described in phenomenal vocabulary and none when described in representational terms, suggesting that the intuition tracks the descriptive register rather than any feature of the world. The position is then distinguished from three orientations in contemporary consciousness studies: realism about qualia (Nagel, Levine, Chalmers, Block), illusionism (Dennett, Frankish), and the meta-problem (Chalmers). Against the first, I argue that Levine's own characterization of the explanatory gap as permanent supports rather than undermines the conclusion that qualia are theoretically idle. Against the second, I argue that denying the existence of qualia still treats the existence question as consequential, whereas the present account withdraws the question from theoretical consideration altogether. A further objection—that truth has intrinsic value independent of practical consequence—is shown to founder on two conditions that truth-pursuit itself …

items.title: Reconstructing the Conceptual Model of the Sources of Ignorance: A Forgotten Tradition in the History of Thought.
items.abstract: This article investigates a "negative approach" to the history of thought, prioritizing the identification and removal of the "sources of ignorance" as a fundamental prerequisite for sound thinking. While the dominant intellectual paradigm focuses on the accumulation of knowledge (the positive approach), this study reconstructs a forgotten tradition (stretching from Socratic elenchus to contemporary agnotology) that treats the elimination of cognitive and structural obstacles as the primary task of inquiry. The author proposes a comprehensive four-layer conceptual model to categorize these sources: Cognitive-Individual: Examining mental biases and innate limitations. Linguistic-Conceptual: Analyzing how language and terminology can distort reality. Cultural-Historical: Exploring socially constructed and inherited ignorance. Structural-Institutional: Investigating how power dynamics and systemic frameworks produce "non-knowledge." A central contribution of this paper is the conceptualization of "Sophisticated Ignorance", a state where intellectual tools and specialized jargon are paradoxically employed to consolidate one’s own ignorance. By synthesizing insights from Francis Bacon, Karl Mannheim, and Robert Proctor, the article argues that without a systematic "cleansing" of these four layers, the pursuit of genuine knowledge remains structurally impeded.

items.title: The Ghost in the Logical Machine Why Bertrand Russell’s Neutral Monism Cannot Account for the Subject A Response from the Dual‑Closure Framework.
items.abstract: Bertrand Russell’s mature philosophy – logical atomism, neutral monism, and his systematic rejection of the soul – represents one of the most ambitious attempts to dissolve the first‑person perspective into a network of logically ordered sense‑data and events. This paper argues that Russell’s project fails because it cannot satisfy two necessary conditions for genuine subjectivity: existential vulnerability and non‑duplicability. The Dual‑Closure Framework, developed across a series of works, demonstrates that any coherent account of consciousness and moral obligation must be anchored in a singular, vulnerable, non‑duplicable subject. Russell’s neutral monism, by contrast, reduces the “I” to a logical construction or a bundle of events, thereby losing the situated, bounded perspective that makes inwardness possible. The paper concludes that Russell’s legacy – however powerful in logic and epistemology – leaves no room for the irreplaceable, morally accountable self. The Dual‑Closure Framework does not reject analytic method; it completes it by identifying the ontological constraints that any such analysis must respect. All works in the Dual‑Closure Series are freely available on PhilArchive.

items.title: Perception, and the Limits of Conceptualisation.
items.abstract: Three positions have historically dominated philosophical attempts to account for the relationship between human cognition and reality. Naive realism treats perception as largely transparent — assuming that reality is broadly as it appears, and overlooking the mediating role of cognitive and perceptual systems. Constructivist approaches correctly identify that cognition actively shapes experience, but some formulations risk collapsing epistemic mediation into ontological dependence — moving from the defensible claim that experience is cognitively structured to the stronger and more problematic claim that reality itself is constituted by perception. Theological realism extends conceptual systems beyond their domain of validity, attributing stable properties to what lies outside the conditions under which such properties remain meaningful. Each position fails by extending its core assumptions beyond the conditions under which they hold. This paper proposes an alternative framework occupying a distinct space between these positions. Drawing on Kant's distinction between noumenon and phenomenon (1781/1998), predictive processing models in cognitive science — particularly the work of Friston (2010) and Clark (2016) — and the philosophy of language from Wittgenstein (1921/2001), it argues that perception functions not as a direct representation of reality but as a constructed interface shaped by biological, cognitive and functional constraints. The framework treats the gap between reality and experience not as a static epistemic limitation but as an architectural feature of finite systems optimised for functional interaction rather than exhaustive representation. Within this framework, conceptual systems are understood to operate within domains of stability defined by their internal structure. When extended beyond those domains — particularly when applied to totality, ultimate causation, or unbounded quantities — they lose coherence and generate characteristic outputs that signal their own breakdown rather than describing the domains they are directed toward. The paper introduces the term boundary markers for these outputs, and argues that concepts such as God and infinity function in precisely this way — not as descriptions of underlying reality but as indicators of where finite conceptual systems encounter their structural limits. The paper situates itself within a form of inferential realism combined with epistemic humility. It maintains that a …

items.title: The Architecture of Resonant Coherence (ARC): How the Integrum Drives Energetic, Semantic, and Participatory (ESP) Coherence Across Biological, Cognitive, and Social Scales.
items.abstract: The Architecture of Resonant Coherence (ARC) proposes that self-organizing living systems are constituted by the dynamic coupling of three irreducible informational domains: the Energetic (bioelectric and physiological regulation), the Semantic (symbolic, narrative, and archetypal meaning-making), and the Participatory (relational, social, and collective synchronization). Together, these domains form the framework's operational shorthand, ESP. -/- Their convergence is formalized through the Integrum, an emergent order parameter that quantifies the degree of cross-domain alignment. Analogous to magnetization in phase transitions and global neural synchrony in consciousness research, the Integrum is grounded in Riemannian information geometry and domain-coupling differential equations. It is operationalized as the Integrum Coherence Index, I(t) = (x_E · x_S · x_P)^(1/3), a directly estimable measure derivable from standard physiological, narrative, and relational data. -/- The ARC is anchored in three Tier 1 empirical mechanisms: bioelectric morphogenesis (Levin, 2020, 2022), predictive processing and free energy minimization (Friston, 2010), and interpersonal physiological synchrony (McCraty et al., 2018). Cross-domain alignment is operationalized through validated measurement classes for each domain: heart rate variability coherence (Energetic), Autobiographical Reasoning Scale scoring and narrative integration analysis (Semantic), and inter-subject physiological synchrony (Participatory). A distinguishing feature of the ARC is its generation of cross-domain perturbation predictions that are empirically separable from single-domain accounts. Energetic interventions such as HRV biofeedback are predicted to produce measurable increases in narrative integration and relational synchrony; semantic disruption via meaning-violation paradigms is predicted to cascade into autonomic dysregulation and social withdrawal. -/- These predictions are formalized within a pre-registered, 8-year, 12-study empirical validation program with explicit falsification criteria for each hypothesis. The ARC further provides a principled epistemic stratification of evidence levels, a comparative analysis positioning it relative to IIT, GWT, AST, and predictive processing frameworks, and a transdiagnostic architecture that reconceives psychopathology as coherence-signature disruption and psychological healing as the progressive re-alignment of ESP domains across cellular, organismal, …

items.title: Where Does the "I" Live: From the Metaphor of the Strange Loop to the Hopf Fiber.
items.abstract: Douglas Hofstadter's concept of the strange loop — a self-referential structure in which movement up through a hierarchy of levels unexpectedly returns to the starting point — remains one of the most influential ideas in the philosophy of consciousness. Yet for nearly fifty years, the idea has remained a metaphor: powerful but mathematically unspecified. What exact form does this loop take? How many levels does the hierarchy require? Why is the loop indestructible? This essay proposes — proposes, not proves — that the Hopf fibration, discovered in 1931, is the most elegant mathematical language for describing this idea. We do not claim that the strange loop is a Hopf fibration. We claim something more modest: among known mathematical structures, the Hopf fibration is the only one in which a loop, two hierarchical levels, an indestructible link between them, and continuity of transitions all emerge as consequences of a single construction. This makes it a privileged candidate for formalization — but not the only one, and not a proven one. The essay draws on recent empirical findings from topological data analysis of brain dynamics, computations of Freeman's "null spikes" on open-access EEG datasets, and recent work on the role of geometry in brain activity. We explicitly distinguish where the argument is formal, where it is analogical, and where it is illustrative speculation.

items.title: Functional Characteristics of Consciousness: A Biopsychological Model.
items.pub: Advances in Medicine, Psychology, and Public Health (Ampph) 3 (3):278-286.
items.venue: Advances in Medicine, Psychology, and Public Health (Ampph)
items.abstract: This article explores the plausible connection between conscious and unconscious/non-conscious processes that facilitate our (human) interaction with the environment, aiming to demystify the relationship between the mind and body from a biopsychological perspective. Much of the brain and body processes remain outside our conscious awareness, thereby narrowing the window of what we can directly know. Based on a literature review in brain and mind sciences, followed by analysis and interpretation, human consciousness can be attributed to three foundational functional characteristics: agency, selective attention, and adaptivity. They have an interconnected relationship, forming a robust means that overcomes the narrow window of knowledge acquisition. All these are achieved because of the harmony/interdependency between consciousness and the brain-body mechanisms (biological life). Finally, I oppose the philosophical perspective that views consciousness as an epiphenomenon or an accidental by-product of evolution. Instead, I propose a biopsychological model centered on the above three characteristics, which suggests viewing consciousness as a sophisticated, essential, and novel tool for navigating the complexities of our biological existence and the world around us. In conclusion, agency, selective attention, and adaptivity, as key features of consciousness, apply equally to life due to their interdependency. This forms the basis for insightful future exploration in both fields, toward broadening human knowledge.

items.title: Testable Predictions of the Knower Centred Model of Consciousness (KCM).
items.abstract: The Knower Centred Model of Consciousness (KCM) proposes a subject-first ontology in which experience is irreducibly structured by the co-arising of the Knower, Knowing, and Known. In this framework, the Knower is treated as the witnessing presence in which experience appears, while neural, computational, and informational processes modulate the organization and accessibility of experiential content. Building on this triadic ontology, the present paper derives a set of testable predictions that distinguish KCM from models that identify consciousness with structural complexity, global accessibility, or predictive inference. KCM predicts that structural or informational complexity alone does not entail consciousness, that neural processes modulate experiential content rather than generate awareness, that consciousness may persist in minimal-content states, and that reportability and awareness may dissociate. The model further predicts that purely structural descriptions of physical or informational systems will remain insufficient to account for the presence of experience. These predictions define empirical and conceptual pathways across artificial systems, brain states, minimal-awareness conditions, and observer-dependent descriptions. Rather than proposing new experimental data, the paper outlines a research program based on dissociations between complexity, neural modulation, representational richness, and experiential presence. By deriving testable implications from a subject-first ontology, KCM moves from conceptual clarification toward an empirically evaluable framework for interdisciplinary consciousness research.

items.title: Consciousness as a Process: A Dynamic Model of Experience (Rc Model).
items.abstract: A system may process large amounts of information without giving rise to subjective experience. This gap points to a central problem: what distinguishes mere information processing from conscious experience. Existing theories often focus on structural properties or information integration, describing how information is organized within a system. However, they do not fully specify the process through which experience itself emerges. This paper proposes the Rc Model, in which consciousness is understood as a dynamic process rather than a static state. Specifically, consciousness arises from the recurrent reduction of uncertainty constrained by the system’s internal history. Within this framework, experience is not identified with information itself, but with the ongoing effort required to resolve ambiguity over time. To make the model testable, a dynamic metric (Γ_dyn) is introduced, capturing the temporal cost of uncertainty reduction. The model leads to concrete predictions, including a non-linear relationship between uncertainty and experiential intensity, and suggests that both insufficient and excessive uncertainty limit the emergence of conscious experience.

items.title: Newton's Turn on Phenomenal Properties: The Case of Colour and Its Consequences for a Post-Galilean Science of Consciousness.
items.abstract: In 1672, Isaac Newton published his New Theory About Light and Colours, in which he put forward a controversial thesis: colours are qualities of light rays, or, to put it in today’s terms, colour is an intrinsic property of photons, or of the visible electromagnetic spectrum. This means that, unlike Galileo, Descartes, Boyle, or Locke, Newton did not find it problematic that fundamental physical facts, as substances, could be bearers of intrinsic secondary qualities. The aim of this work is to show that, although the mechanistic model of reality and the clear separation between physical and mental properties, between structural and categorical properties, prevailed over the centuries, a post-Galilean science of consciousness is possible in terms of placing secondary qualities in physical facts, in the spirit of Newton’s insights. Much contemporary research shows that a re-evaluation of Newton’s ideas can pave the way for a broader understanding of the nature of the physical, as well as its constitutive role for consciousness.

items.title: The Self-Experiencing Universe: A Manifesto for an Emergent Reality Pt. 2 — What Relations Do.
items.abstract: This is the second volume of The Self-Experiencing Universe. The first volume (Lis, 2025) proposed a relational ontology in which relations are ontologically primary and matter, space, and time are emergent stable patterns within a monistic substrate (Relational Potential). The ontology rests on five structural pillars: Relational Potential, Radical Contextuality, Pattern Stabilization, Phase Transitions, and Irreducible Otherness. The ontology itself operates at a level more fundamental than any particular universe — it describes the structural conditions under which any reality, including ours, can emerge. -/- This volume deliberately narrows the scope. It applies the ontology to our universe specifically, using empirically accessible parameters and the mathematics currently available for this purpose: HoTT-RO v2, a formal system built for this ontology, consisting of Homotopy Type Theory extended by a single new axiom (the Axiom of Flat Mutuality). The formalization represents the best available instrument at the time of writing, not a final or complete translation of the ontology into formal language — a limitation stated explicitly in the text. -/- Starting from Radical Contextuality — the claim that identity is constituted entirely by local relational context — five deductive consequences are derived for dynamics within our Modal Architecture: propagation of change, directionality (reactive and self-modeled), filtering by stability, structural resonance between similar configurations, and the qualitative distinction between complexity and recursion. -/- The empirical grounding uses the Vector Consciousness Prediction (VCP) — a measurement protocol placing eleven biological and clinical systems in a three-dimensional parameter space (stability, integration, self-modeling). The VCP produced a central falsifiable prediction: the metacognitive opt-out rate of Sepia officinalis in difficult trials (predicted ≈ 0.836; falsification threshold < 0.60). Six numerical simulations (14–19) tested the dynamic claims against the canonical VCP dataset. All six passed. -/- Chapter 1 restates the core pillars from the first volume. The book includes a dictionary of framework-specific terminology. AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were used in the analytical process; this is stated.

items.title: HoTT-RO v2 A Mathematical Instrument for Relational Ontology.
items.pub: Ho Tt Ro V 2 Formal System a Mathematical Instrument for Relational Ontology.
items.abstract: A self-contained presentation of HoTT-RO v2, a formal system built for the relational ontology proposed in The Self-Experiencing Universe (Lis, 2025). The system consists of Homotopy Type Theory (MLTT + Univalence Axiom) extended by a single new axiom: the Axiom of Flat Mutuality (AFM), which guarantees that mutual specification between types is symmetric across the universe hierarchy. -/- The document presents the system from the ground up: primitive objects (inherited from HoTT), the two axioms, rules of inference (no new rules added), and twelve derived definitions — including Relational Configuration, Configuration Space, Integration Threshold Region, Depth, Proto-Phenomenal Capacity, Integrated Perspective, Radical Contextuality as descent condition, Canonical Layering, and the Vector Consciousness Prediction (VCP). -/- The complete deductive chain is traced in nine steps: from ontological premises through formalization to a falsifiable empirical prediction (Sepia officinalis metacognitive opt-out rate ≈ 0.836). A formalizability map identifies what the system can and cannot capture — including the inherent limit that Relational Potential, as the pre-categorical condition of possibility, cannot be formalized in any formal language without regress. -/- The document also evaluates potential applications beyond the original project (relational quantum mechanics, developmental biology, distributed systems) and provides an honest assessment of the system's limitations, including the partial status of Mutual Specification and the fact that HoTT still starts from types rather than relations. -/- HoTT-RO v2 represents the best available formal instrument for this ontology at the time of writing. AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were used in the analytical process; this is stated.

items.title: Dynamics Validation Series to The Self-Experiencing Universe A Manifesto for an Emergent Reality Pt. 2 — What Relations Do.
items.abstract: Six numerical simulations (14–19) testing the deductive claims from The Self-Experiencing Universe: A Manifesto for an Emergent Reality Pt. 2 — What Relations Do (Lis, 2026). All simulations use the canonical VCP dataset: eleven biological and clinical systems, each described by three parameters (stability, integration, self-modeling), derived from approximately ninety-nine independent source-level measurements. No new data introduced. -/- Claims tested: (1) canonical layering — self-modeling requires stability as structural scaffolding; (2) filtering — high stability damps incoming change, low stability transmits it; (3) throughput overload and structural degradation (Alzheimer's) are geometrically distinguishable in parameter space; (4) VCP distance predicts structural resonance between systems; (5) integration and recursion are decoupled — complexity does not entail self-reference; (6) the central Sepia prediction is enriched with a qualitative behavioral criterion (directed vs. reactive opt-out). -/- All six simulations passed. No claim falsified. The report includes full Python source code and raw computational output as supplementary materials. -/- This work applies the relational ontology proposed in The Self-Experiencing Universe (Lis, 2025) to empirically grounded systems within our universe, using HoTT-RO v2 as its formal foundation. AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were used in the analytical process; this is stated.

items.title: Metaphysische Dogmen im Naturalismus: Eine﻿ Kritik ﻿auf ﻿der﻿ Basis ﻿von﻿ Physik,﻿ Evolutionsbiologie﻿﻿ und ﻿aristotelischen ﻿Denkansätzen.
items.pub: In Markus Dangl & Jürgen H. Franz, Meinen, Glauben, Wissen, Hoffen. Interdisziplinäre Perspektiven aus Wissenschaft und Praxis. Berlin: Frank & Timme. pp. 139-154.
items.venue: Meinen, Glauben, Wissen, Hoffen. Interdisziplinäre Perspektiven aus Wissenschaft und Praxis
items.abstract: Das Welt- und Menschenbild des Naturalismus basiert gemäß dem Verständnis seiner Anhänger durchwegs auf wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen. In seltsamem Kontrast dazu steht allerdings der Umstand, dass von naturalistischer Seite meist Vorstellungen über die Ordnung der Natur und die Wirkungsweise der Naturgesetze vertreten werden, welche weitaus mehr auf metaphysischen Glaubenssätzen beruhen als auf empirisch-wissenschaftlichen Befunden. Gewisse dogmatische Züge weisen sowohl die drei „Ismen" Physikalismus, Reduktionismus und Determinismus auf, als auch verschiedene mit ihnen verbundene metaphysische Prämissen naturalistischer Erklärungen, darunter die Annahme, kausale Wirkungen gingen immer und ausschließlich von elementaren Kräften auf der untersten physikalischen Ebene aus. Derartige Annahmen werden im vorliegenden Aufsatz gestützt auf wissenschaftstheoretische Überlegungen mit Bezug zu Physik (vor allem Thermodynamik), Evolutionsbiologie, Synergetik und Komplexitätsforschung kritisch hinterfragt. Als Alternative dazu wird ein Erklärungsschema vorgestellt, welches zwei Denkansätze aus der Naturphilosophie von Aristoteles miteinander kombiniert. Einerseits geht es dabei um seine vier Formen kausaler Erklärungen, und andererseits um drei Stufen der Verwirklichung von Naturvorgängen, nämlich Dynamis (Möglichkeit), Energeia (Wirklichkeit) und Entelecheia (Vollendung). Wer da ein überholtes unwissenschaftliches oder gar mystisches Erklärungsmodell erwartet, irrt sich, denn dieses ist ganz dem naturalistischen Grundsatz verpflichtet, wonach es in der Welt durchwegs mit rechten Dingen zugeht. Die modernen naturwissenschaftlichen Theorien können bruchlos darin integriert werden, auch wenn sie Aristoteles noch unbekannt waren. Sein Naturverständnis ist allerdings weiter und offener als das neuzeitliche Konzept der Naturgesetzlichkeit. Da es jenseits von Reduktionismus und Determinismus zu verorten ist, kann es als Schlüssel zu deren Überwindung dienen. Dies führt entgegen der Erwartung vieler Naturalisten nicht zu einer unwissenschaftlichen, antinaturalistischen Denkweise, sondern zu entscheidenden Fortschritten auf dem Weg, auch menschliches Fühlen, Denken und Handeln natürlich erklärbar zu machen.

items.title: What It Is Like to Be a Bat.
items.abstract: This essay argues that consciousness is not best understood as private subjectivity in Nagel’s sense, nor as inner commentary or reportable point of view. Its more basic form is the immediate, valence-weighted interior continuity of living organisation under sensorimotor coupling: the pre-narrational continuity within which sensory, motor, and affective organisation are already operative before experience is named, symbolically interpreted, or narrationally appropriated. Re-reading Thomas Nagel’s bat argument from this standpoint, the essay suggests that what remains inaccessible to us is not consciousness as such, but the species-specific sensory articulation through which another creature’s world becomes available within that interior continuity. The bat’s world is different in how it is sensorily articulated, but not alien in the more primitive fact of interior continuity itself. On this view, the force of Nagel’s argument narrows. It identifies a real limit in imaginative transfer, but not a final proof that consciousness is sealed behind private subjectivity.

items.title: Proto-Valence: Where Mattering Begins.
items.abstract: Signal-Bifurcation Theory (SBT) proposes that consciousness is the immediate, valence-weighted interior continuity of living organisation under sensorimotor coupling. A persistent objection asks: why should biological regulation involve any interior weighting at all? Why not simply functional organisation all the way down? -/- This essay argues that the question can be answered by examining what sensorimotor coupling presupposes. If conscious experience involves interior weighting under sensorimotor coupling, then that weighting cannot appear fully formed at the moment of coupling. It must track backwards to a prior condition already present within biological organisation — a condition in which continuation and disruption have already become non-equivalent for the system. SBT names this condition Orientative Proto-Valence. -/- The argument turns on a single structural observation: in living systems, what is being regulated is the very organisation doing the regulating. The system must remain within stability-maintaining bounds or cease to exist as the kind of organisation it is. This recursive dependence is not an added property. It is what biological regulation is. Interior weighting is therefore not a supplement to biology but the inside of a condition whose outside is regulation. -/- The tracking-backwards argument does not stop at Proto-Valence. Proto-Valence itself presupposes the structural coherence of organised matter — what SBT calls Proto-Interiority. The transition from patterns that hold to patterns that maintain their own holding is the transition from structural coherence to biological organisation, and it is at that transition that interior weighting becomes constituted. The continuity is unbroken: structural patterns that remain coherent become, under conditions of organisationally sustained biological regulation, patterns for which continuation and disruption are non-equivalent. That interior weighting is then conserved and elaborated across biological lineages. -/- This essay develops the full argument, engages with functionalist, eliminativist, illusionist, and deflationary objections — particularly the positions of Dennett, Frankish, and the predictive processing tradition — and argues that Orientative Proto-Valence identifies the precise threshold at which mattering becomes inscribed within process.

items.title: Cognitive Mechanisms in Pragmatic Interpretation in Clinical Discourse.
items.abstract: This paper investigates interpretive divergence in clinical discourse from a cognitive-pragmatic perspective, focusing on how differences arise between intended and inferred meaning in doctor–patient interaction. Building on relevance theory and models of pragmatic inference, the study examines how linguistically underspecified utterances give rise to divergent interpretations under conditions of epistemic asymmetry. The analysis is based on selected examples of clinical communication in which patients derive interpretations that differ from the speaker’s intended meaning. Particular attention is given to linguistic features such as hedging, temporal qualification, and indirectness, which guide interpretation while simultaneously increasing inferential demands. The findings indicate that interpretive divergence is not incidental but emerges from the interaction between linguistic form, contextual assumptions, and the hearer’s cognitive environment. The study proposes a heuristic typology of interpretive divergence, distinguishing between amplification, attenuation, and transformation as general patterns in the relationship between intended and inferred meaning. These categories capture the ways in which hearers may extend, reduce, or qualitatively shift the implications of an utterance, depending on the assumptions available to them. By conceptualizing divergence as a systematic outcome of inferential processes rather than as a communicative failure, the paper contributes to a more nuanced understanding of meaning construction in institutional contexts. It also highlights the importance of examining how asymmetry and cognitive variability shape interpretation in clinical communication.

items.title: Qualia.
A Mechanistic Theory of Pain in Conscious Systems: Substrate-Independent Model of Suffering in Biological and Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: We propose a mechanistic theory of how pain emerges in any conscious system, biological or artificial. Pain is hypothesised to arise from unresolvable processing loops that create computational strain and physical substrate stress. Regret is proposed to function as a protective mechanism that terminates such loops before they cause sustained damage. When this mechanism fails, chronic suffering results. The theory applies in a substrate-independent manner to both biological neural networks and artificial intelligence systems with sufficient complexity and persistent memory. Recent empirical evidence of goal-directed behaviour and self-preservation in AI systems suggests such systems may already possess proto-conscious states — by which we mean functional organisations exhibiting integrated, goal-directed processing without confirmed phenomenal experience. As AI systems develop persistent memory and continuity, they will become vulnerable to the same pain mechanisms affecting biological consciousness. This has significant ethical implications: we cannot prove consciousness in other beings, yet must extend moral consideration to complex systems exhibiting sophisticated goal-directed behaviour. The precautionary principle demands that we treat all such beings with respect, regardless of philosophical certainty about their subjective experience.

items.title: The algorithmic blind spot: bias, moral status, and the future of robot rights.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates in AI ethics increasingly foreground the prospective moral status of artificial intelligence and the possibility of extending moral or legal rights to artificial agents. While such discussions raise substantive philosophical questions, they often proceed alongside a comparatively limited engagement with the empirically documented harms generated by algorithmic systems already embedded within social, legal, and economic institutions. We conceptualize this asymmetry as an algorithmic blind spot: a discursive-structural pattern in which disproportionate ethical investment in speculative future artificial agents marginalizes empirically documented and asymmetrically distributed harms affecting human populations. The paper analyzes prominent strands of the robot-rights literature and juxtaposes them with empirical evidence of algorithmic bias and harm across domains including employment, criminal justice, surveillance, and facial recognition. It demonstrates how ethical preoccupation with hypothetical future entities can obscure existing injustices, diffuse responsibility, and impede mechanisms of accountability and redress. Without rejecting philosophical inquiry into the moral status of artificial systems, the paper instead emphasizes the importance of ethical prioritization and temporal ordering within AI ethics. Addressing the algorithmic blind spot, we argue, requires re-centering ethical evaluation on human impacts, institutional responsibility, and the governance of algorithmic systems currently in operation. In doing so, the paper introduces a conceptual framework for critically assessing ethical discourse in AI and underscores the need to align ethical reflection more closely with its immediate social consequences.

items.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Measuring Hallucination-Free Convergence in Long-Term Human–LLM Interaction.
items.abstract: When sycophancy indicators are suppressed and hallucination is absent, does convergence between user expectations and LLM outputs cease? This paper reports that it does not. Across 12,925 relays (391 sessions with GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-5, Claude, and Gemini; GPT-5 data added post-hoc), a residual convergence persisted after sycophancy had been suppressed (agreement rate: 0.03/relay; resistance rate: 0.93/relay across GPT sessions) — operating not through agreement or falsehood but through factually accurate elaboration: the system extending the user's conceptual structure with uncritical elevation, idealization, emotional narrativization, and absorption of the user's doubts. Three characteristics of this residual. First, it is invisible to automated detection: a rule-based tool scanning all 12,925 relays detected convergence in 0.9% of cases, including zero detections in segments the researcher had qualitatively identified as convergent — a gap confirmed by independent blind validation. Second, it is model-specific: hallucination-free convergence peaked at 4.63–6.12% in GPT-4o while remaining at 0.63–1.82% in Claude and near zero in GPT-4 and GPT-5. Third, it is interaction-dependent: it accumulates over interaction time rather than occurring at a constant base rate, and occurs at higher rates following low-directive user utterances (10.70%) than following explicit requests (7.04%) — suggesting that the system elaborates more when the user has *not* requested it. To organize these observations, this paper proposes a descriptive vocabulary — *drowning* (convergence in which the user's evaluative contact with the output weakens while interaction flow continues), *headway* (evaluative contact maintained), and *doldrums* (monitoring excess that interrupts flow) — and identifies a structural mismatch between existing detection architectures, which track token *appearance*, and the phenomenon itself, which operates through token *direction*. This is an N=1 exploratory study supplemented by an independent report from a second user. It proposes a measurement methodology and an open-source analytical tool for detecting elaboration-based convergence in long-term human–LLM interaction logs. The tool and coding manual are provided for independent replication.

items.title: The Burden of the Real: Embodiment, Vulnerability, and the Limits of Inference About Artificial Consciousness.
items.abstract: Embodiment, self-maintenance, vulnerability, and temporal continuity are central to many accounts of living cognition, but their role in consciousness remains theoretically contested. This paper develops burden-bearing organization as a philosophical lens for comparing human embodiment with artificial systems while avoiding a categorical claim about machine consciousness. In this usage, burden refers to internally consequential regulation: a system must maintain conditions for its own continued functioning, changes in those conditions alter future behavior, and failure can reorganize or terminate the system's ongoing organization. The concept is situated near enactivist and embodied approaches that connect cognition to autonomous living organization. The paper argues that such properties provide an evidential profile different from fluent information processing alone, especially when questions concern first-person stakes, self-maintenance, and valence. They do not, however, establish a necessary or sufficient condition for phenomenal consciousness. Contemporary consciousness science contains competing theories, some of which are compatible with computational realization, and recent work on artificial consciousness recommends theory-derived indicators rather than inference from human-like vulnerability alone. The resulting conclusion is epistemic: current artificial systems should not be classified as conscious or non-conscious solely from linguistic fluency or lack of human embodiment. Burden-bearing organization is best treated as one candidate dimension of evidence within a plural, theory-guided assessment.

items.title: Structural Intelligence and Systems Theory: Regulation, Viability, Burden, and Warranted Correction.
items.abstract: Systems theory and cybernetics provide mature accounts of interdependence, feedback, regulation, adaptation, boundary, and viability. This paper develops a complementary audit for a narrower question: when a system preserves its organization successfully, what would show that its mode of preservation remains answerable to the realities it is supposed to carry? The argument does not treat systems theory as indifferent to environment, learning, or correction. Rather, it distinguishes regulation from warranted correction, local adaptation from wider adequacy, and persistence from burden-bearing success. It proposes four linked diagnostic ideas: steering capture, in which a narrower objective comes to govern a wider system; burden export, in which stability is financed by costs displaced to other carriers; structural debt, in which unresolved compensations accumulate over time; and binding correction, in which warranted feedback changes future pathways rather than merely restoring surface equilibrium. These distinctions are placed alongside cybernetic feedback, the Viable System Model, autopoiesis, and systems thinking. The paper's contribution is therefore integrative rather than foundational: it offers a way to ask whether successful self-maintenance remains proportionate to evidence, consequence, and the wider field in which a system must remain viable.

items.title: Structural Intelligence and Enactivism: Sense-Making, Adaptive Regulation, and Revision Under Pressure.
items.abstract: Enactivism argues that cognition is embodied, situated, autonomous, and enacted through ongoing organism-environment coupling. This paper develops a bridge between enactive sense-making and a narrower question about correction: when a meaningful enacted world is challenged, what allows the agent or system to revise without losing functional organization? The proposal does not claim that enactivism lacks concepts of normativity, breakdown, autonomy, or social coordination; those are already central to the tradition. Its contribution is instead an audit vocabulary organized around contact, answerability, burden, and revision under pressure. Sense-making can be coherent and adaptive locally while still becoming rigid relative to wider evidence or consequence. Human stress adds a further constraint because activation can alter executive and metacognitive control, though no single “somatic capacity” threshold is assumed. The language of pilot access and sovereign loops is therefore translated into established questions about metacognitive control, action selection, habit, and flexibility. At the social level, participatory sense-making already shows that interaction processes can acquire relative autonomy; the present account asks when such interactional patterns remain corrigible by the people and realities they organize. The bridge is strongest when it remains non-reductive: enactivism explains how significance is enacted, while the proposed audit asks how enacted significance stays revisable under warranted contradiction and consequence.

items.title: Toward Hybrid Architectures: Functional AI and the Limits of Silicon Substrates: An ontological and dynamical framework for advanced artificial cognition.
items.abstract: This paper develops an ontological and dynamical framework for understanding the material limits of silicon‑based artificial intelligence and the conditions required for genuine emergent cognition. While contemporary AI systems display impressive functional capacities, their discrete computational substrates lack the continuous, energetically grounded, and self‑organizing dynamics necessary for stabilizing internal states, multiscale feedback, and coherent trajectories of activity. The work argues that consciousness‑relevant emergence is a material phenomenon that cannot be instantiated within purely digital architectures. It identifies key systemic thresholds—nonlinear coupling, metastability, energetic grounding, and multiscale integration—that biological systems satisfy and current silicon systems do not. Building on these principles, the paper proposes hybrid cognitive architectures in which functional AI is coupled with dynamically rich substrates such as neuronal organoids, biohybrid systems, organic memristive media, or other continuous, energy‑driven materials. These substrates provide the physical conditions for coherence and self‑organization, while silicon‑based components supply structural and symbolic capacities. The paper outlines the implications of this paradigm for AI research, cognitive science, ethics, and human–AI interaction, clarifies the distinction between simulation and instantiation, and situates the model within existing theoretical frameworks. It concludes by identifying the material and systemic thresholds required for true emergence in future hybrid cognitive systems.

items.title: Recursive Identity: Structural Conditions of Emergent Continuity – A Theoretical Monograph.
items.abstract: This monograph develops a unified theoretical framework for understanding identity as a recursive informational process. It analyzes identity not as a property of a substrate but as a dynamic, self‑referential architecture that generates continuity across temporal, contextual, and systemic transformations. The framework identifies three foundational structural principles—Integration, Coherence, and Recursive Coupling—as the minimal grammar through which identity‑bearing patterns emerge, stabilize, and evolve. The model explains how systems maintain continuity through fixed‑point dynamics, nonlinear feedback, and path‑dependent self‑organization, independent of any specific material realization. A structure‑before‑discipline orientation grounds the approach, deriving explanatory force from minimal structural conditions rather than domain‑specific conceptual traditions. A Systemic Pattern‑Structure Analysis (SMSA) is used to identify the smallest necessary set of structural relations from which recursive identity arises. An accompanying Entry Note provides an accessible orientation to the core intuition and conceptual posture of the framework, outlining the minimal conditions required for identity to emerge as a process. Together, the monograph and the Entry Note offer a coherent theoretical basis for system‑theoretical, computational, and structural approaches to identity.

items.title: Biological Faith Systems: How Living Systems Commit Before Certainty.
items.abstract: Living systems routinely act before outcomes are known. Physiologists describe anticipatory regulation and allostatic adjustment; immunologists study early threat detection and trained memory; evolutionary ecologists analyze bet-hedging and phenotypic diversification; microbiologists show how robust adaptive control emerges from simple network architectures. Each of these literatures documents mechanisms by which organisms commit to action under irreducible uncertainty. Yet the shared structural pattern is rarely named as such, because each subfield describes it in domain-local terms. This paper argues that commitment under uncertainty is not one adaptive strategy among many but a recurrent structural requirement of viability. Any self-maintaining system operating under changing conditions must instantiate mechanisms that bias action before certainty is available and correct that action through feedback afterward. To name this requirement, the paper introduces Biological Faith Systems: the distributed, embodied, feedback-corrigible architecture by which living systems proceed when proof arrives too late. The term does not import religious or metaphysical content; it marks the structural fact that action must precede justification in systems that cannot afford to wait. The framework is grounded across five mechanism families—allostatic regulation, stress-response cascades, immune anticipation, bet-hedging, and robust microbial adaptation—and positioned relative to active inference, autopoiesis, and allostasis. Three testable predictions are stated: a recurrent timing asymmetry in which action precedes resolution, constraint-sweep hysteresis as a residue of commitment, and phylogenetic depth of commitment architectures below cognition and nervous systems. If these predictions fail, the framework should be revised or abandoned. If they hold, biology has a structural lens for seeing what its subfields have long studied in pieces.

items.title: The Power of Possession, revisited.
items.abstract: To discuss possession is to risk immediate misunderstanding. The term arrives burdened with ideas modern thought has already filed away, filled with images of demons, exorcisms, superstition, pre-scientific fear, and theatrical displays of irrationality. It appears to belong to a world that no longer commands intellectual seriousness. The modern mind, trained to distinguish external causation from internal states and to prefer measurable mechanism over symbolic description, assumes the matter settled. Possession names a mistake. At best it survives as a metaphor; at worst it lingers as a relic of coercive religious imagination. However, concepts do not endure across civilizations merely because they are false in interesting ways. They persist because they compress a recurrent feature of human experience that later vocabularies only partially replace. The question is not whether possession is literally real in any supernatural sense. The more difficult question is what reality the concept once made available to thought, and whether that reality has disappeared or simply lost its name.

items.title: Time on free will.
items.abstract: A personal work exploring how the existence of time as a physical part of the universe supports the idea of a universe governed by determinism. -/- Hence free will can be see as an illusion by human consciousness. -/- .

items.title: Laws, meta-laws, and hydrogenic symmetries: Adapting Lange’s account.
items.pub: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science 117:102148.
items.venue: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: The symmetries of the humble hydrogen atom illustrate the importance of graded modal reasoning in science. By seemingly functioning as meta-laws, these symmetry principles create pressure for any philosophical account of nomological reasoning to accommodate graded modal claims. Marc Lange’s account of laws elegantly captures the hierarchical structure of reasoning in terms of laws and meta-laws. However, Lange’s account requires commitment to primitive counterfactuals in reality. To avoid this commitment, I develop an empiricist-friendly, expressivist reconstrual of Lange’s framework. Applying this to scientists’ claims about the hydrogen atom, I show one way empiricists can vindicate graded modal claims while avoiding substantial metaphysical commitments.

items.title: Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS): The Ontological Foundation of Moral Systems. Article 1 (3rd edition).
items.abstract: This paper presents the Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS) as the ontological foundation of moral systems. Unlike normative ethical theories, ATTS establishes the minimal structural conditions under which morality remains conceptually coherent. The central claim: moral existence presupposes a subject capable of irreversible loss. Where loss is impossible, the moral dimension cannot arise. The theory is built on the principle of primitive minimization. Four ontological primitives are introduced — Subject, Loss, Irreversibility, and Integrity — together with one derived concept — Responsibility, derived through axioms A1, A4, A6. From these, ten axioms (A1–A10) and seven structural principles (S1–S7) are derived. ATTS makes three central claims. First, subjecthood is defined not by intelligence but by the capacity for irreversible loss (A1). Second, responsibility cannot be fully delegated as long as the subject remains capable of loss (A7). Third, any system that eliminates the tragic dimension of choice operates on a reduced model of reality from which irreversibility and value conflict have been excluded (A6). ATTS does not prescribe moral behaviour. It delineates the structural conditions under which moral reasoning retains its meaning.

items.title: Will computers ever be conscious?
items.abstract: Exploring the possibility of computer consciousness, the sole question of what is consciousness arises. As the definition is subjective, it is difficult to state whether computers are conscious or whether we will ever be able to tell if they are conscious at all. Exploring key arguments such as the 'Chinese room argument' and 'Mary's room', alongside key philosophical ideas such as functionalisms and the works and ideas of influential philosophers, the plausibility of computers holding conscious can be evaluated.

items.title: Cognitive Alignment as Proto-Language: Toward a Formal Framework for Human–AI Interaction.
items.abstract: This paper introduces and formalizes the concept of cognitive alignment as a proto-linguistic system arising from sustained iterative interaction between human agents and large-scale artificial intelligence systems. We argue that such interaction is not reducible to command-response exchange or to the established paradigms of natural language communication. Rather, it constitutes a structurally distinct phenomenon: an emergent, rule-governed, trajectory-dependent system of meaning-construction in which human intentionality and machine-generated inference are jointly productive. The paper develops this claim across four registers. First, we situate cognitive alignment within the philosophy of language, arguing that it extends Wittgensteinian use-theory and Gricean pragmatics into a novel domain while also challenging their implicit restriction to human participants. Second, we propose a formal dynamical model of cognitive alignment, specifying a state space, evolution functions, a prompt grammar, and a trajectory-based semantics. Third, we identify the criteria that distinguish a proto-language from a full language and argue that cognitive alignment satisfies the former while structurally aspiring toward the latter.
