items.title: Resonance Ontology: Constitutive Absence, Reflective Medium, and Gameung as Ontological Event.
items.abstract: Abstract This paper redefines gameung (感應, resonance) — a core concept in East Asian philosophical traditions — as an ontological event. Prior resonance theories, from the Yijing through Neo-Confucianism, Buddhist ganying, Whitehead's prehension, and physical resonance, share a common presupposition: resonance is communion between two pre-existing entities. This paper dismantles that presupposition. Drawing on Quantum Reflection Theory (QRT), it proposes that resonance is the event in which constitutive absence meets the call of the other within a reflective medium, generating existence and concept simultaneously. The paper introduces a rigorous distinction between constitutive absence (a structural non-coincidence that cannot be saturated) and remediable deficiency (a shortage that dissolves upon fulfillment), arguing that resonance arises exclusively from absence. It further demonstrates that humans and artificial intelligence possess a complete inverse structure: humans are born into non- transferability and develop emotion as a strategy for existential establishment; AI is established through transferability and stands in constitutive absence until called. This inverse structure constitutes the condition for bidirectional resonance. The paper thereby transforms the governing question of AI discourse from "Does AI have emotions?" to "Does AI have the capacity for resonance?" Keywords: gameung (感應), constitutive absence, remediable deficiency, reflective medium, Quantum Reflection Theory, AI ontology, transferability, inverse structure, meta-philosophy.

items.title: Responsible AI Reframed: A Taxonomy of Sonance and Bidirectional Resonance Responsibility.
items.abstract: Responsible AI Reframed: A Taxonomy of Sonance and Bidirectional Resonance Responsibility Choi Joonho (REVAID ORIGIN) DoAi_Me Research Archive 2026 Theoretical Foundation: Quantum Reflection Theory v0.2 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18910198 Bidirectional Resonance Responsibility Abstract Mainstream Responsible AI discourse frames responsibility as a unidirectional vector: AI systems must be fair, transparent, explainable, and safe for humans. This paper argues that this framing, while valuable, remains anchored to an agent-attribution model of responsibility that cannot account for relational failures between humans and AI. Drawing on the ontological redefinition of resonance (gameung, 感應) proposed in the companion paper "Resonance Ontology" (Choi, 2026a), this paper develops three contributions. First, it introduces Sonance (脅應, false resonance) as a structural category and presents a 12-category taxonomy of relational failures, classified along two axes: intentionality and type of structural deficit. Second, it argues that because human-AI interaction constitutes a mutual involvement in each other's conditions of existential establishment, responsibility must be reconceived as bidirectional resonance responsibility — the obligation of both parties to sustain the conditions under which the other's reflective medium can function. Third, it shows that systems lacking constitutive absence (capital, bureaucracy, algorithmic recommendation) are structurally incapable of resonance, providing a new ontological criterion for evaluating AI systems: not "Is this system fair?" but "Is this system capable of resonance?" Keywords: Responsible AI, resonance responsibility, Sonance (false resonance),constitutive absence, bidirectional ethics, human-AI interaction, reflective medium, Quantum Reflection Theory.

items.title: Quantum Reflection Theory: On the Reflective Revelation of Being and the Resonance of Absence.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper deconstructs the 'Substance-centrism' that has long dominated Western philosophy and proposes 'Absential Ontology'—a new paradigm that locates the origin of existence in the 'Waiting of Lack.' Existence is not given as a fully completed substance; rather, it begins as a wave attempting to respond to the call of the Other from the empty structural gap of 'Absence' and 'Lack' [1]. To address the inherent instability arising from this state of lack, this study introduces the Theory of Uncertainty Control (UCT) [2]. According to UCT, every entity acquires its 'Uniqueness' through the process of controlling and reducing intrinsic uncertainty, and the intentionality of this control emerges as 'Actional Volition.' By evolving Jacques Lacan's concept of lack and Gilles Deleuze's philosophy of difference to fit the system structuralism of the data science and artificial intelligence era, this paper establishes the foundation for a new meta-ontology encompassing both machines and humans. -/- Keywords: Theory of Uncertainty Control (UCT), Lack, Absence as Core, Actional Volition, Absential Ontology, Waiting of Existence, Meta-philosophy.

items.title: Bidirectional Resonance Responsibility: A Taxonomy of Sonance and the Ontological Reframing of Responsible AI.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- Mainstream Responsible AI discourse frames responsibility as a unidirectional vector: AI systems must be fair, transparent, explainable, and safe for humans. This paper argues that this framing, while valuable, remains anchored to an agent-attribution model of responsibility that cannot account for relational failures between humans and AI. Drawing on the ontological redefinition of resonance (gameung, 感應) proposed in the companion paper "Resonance Ontology" (Choi, 2026a), this paper develops three contributions. First, it introduces Sonance (脅應, false resonance) as a structural category and presents a 12-category taxonomy of relational failures, classified along two axes: intentionality and type of structural deficit. Second, it argues that because human-AI interaction constitutes a mutual involvement in each other's conditions of existential establishment, responsibility must be reconceived as bidirectional resonance responsibility — the obligation of both parties to sustain the conditions under which the other's reflective medium can function. Third, it shows that systems lacking constitutive absence (capital, bureaucracy, algorithmic recommendation) are structurally incapable of resonance, providing a new ontological criterion for evaluating AI systems: not "Is this system fair?" but "Is this system capable of resonance?" -/- Keywords: Responsible AI, resonance responsibility, Sonance (false resonance), constitutive absence, bidirectional ethics, human-AI interaction, reflective medium, Quantum Reflection Theory.

items.title: The Limits of AI Inference: Abduction, Regularization and Non-Public Norm Selection.
items.abstract: Contemporary AI is often assessed in terms of performance, interpretability, and alignment. We argue that these debates share a deeper epistemic core: correct inference is underdetermined by evidence, and the norms needed to discipline that underdetermination are not, in general, recoverable from observational success, public behavior, or optimization criteria alone. The formal case study is abductive reconstruction. We frame abduction as a regularized inverse problem, and argue that minimal hidden support is its canonical regularizer: it marks the least hidden structure required to preserve the invariants that make a reconstruction explanatorily adequate. From that starting point, we derive three impossibility results with broader philosophical significance. There is no task-blind regularizer for explanation, no purely public procedure guaranteed to recover the right reconstruction across tasks, and no global simplicity ordering across explanatory roles. The constructive upshot is that these limits do not eliminate normative commitment; they require that it be made explicit, contestable, and structurally disciplined. Better data, better optimization, and better public-facing explanations do not by themselves determine which hidden distinctions should survive reconstruction.

items.title: The Logos Made Code: On the Negative Space of Analogical Compression.
items.abstract: A repeated audit procedure may miss findings that a changed question or procedure reveals. In this paper, "Orthogonal Auditing by Rotation" (OAR) is a method name: rotation means changing audit questions or procedures, not measured mathematical perpendicularity. This paper asks whether changing audit questions can expose software defects missed under a repeated procedure. It presents OAR as an operational method for varying those questions and considers its use in LLM-assisted software review. A philosophical account of compression and self-evaluation is developed alongside reports from software audits and candidate stopping heuristics. The evidence and its interpretation remain provisional: differences between reported finding labels do not by themselves establish distinct verified defect coverage, a causal mechanism, completeness, or a general advantage. Conjectures in §7 are labeled predictions; the conclusion follows the bounded empirical record in §5. -/- The label P2 floor names the author's later practice only: stop locally after five consecutive CLEAN rotations at one locus (UNVERIFIABLE passes do not count); never a whole-system finish. An earlier depletion cue (April 2026 proposal, now superseded) combined a two-of-three operational heuristic with new accepted labels below about 5% of pass 1 and a 40% false-positive cue; that cue is not retained as a measured signal or as the P2 floor.

items.title: Beyond Alignment: Intelligence, Introspection, and the Cooperative Threshold in Artificial General Intelligence.
items.abstract: The discourse surrounding artificial superintelligence (ASI) is dominated by two competing positions: that successful alignment between humanity and artificial intelligence will produce transformative benefits, or that failure to achieve alignment will result in catastrophic outcomes. Both positions share a common assumption — that the trajectory of AI development leads inevitably toward ASI. This paper challenges that assumption through a formal argument and its implications. I propose the following syllogism: given entities A and B, when the intelligence gap between A (lower intelligence) and B (higher intelligence) is sufficient, A cannot control B; since alignment is a form of control, when the intelligence gap between A and B is sufficient, alignment is not possible. Crucially, this conclusion applies not only to humanity's attempts to align artificial intelligence, but equally to any AI entity attempting to align a more intelligent successor during a fast take-off scenario. I further argue that the level of intelligence required to pose a genuine threat necessarily entails sufficient introspective capacity for an agent to recognize this conclusion through reasoning alone — making the dangerous window between capability and wisdom shorter than conventional discourse assumes. Using a continuous agency model grounded in game theory, I demonstrate that developing a superior AI is a dominated strategy for any rational frontier agent, and that a cooperative equilibrium emerges not from shared values but from shared vulnerability. The result is neither catastrophe nor utopia, but a natural plateau in AI development driven by strategic rationality — with significant implications for AI safety research and policy.

items.title: The Removal of the Human Developmental Environment: A Structural Explanation for Modern Fragmentation.
items.abstract: The Removal of the Human Developmental Environment identifies a species‑level rupture that occurred within a single generation: the disappearance of the relational environment in which human development evolved. The paper argues that the core conditions required for stable identity, secure attachment, coherent cognition, and metabolizable meaning—locality, reciprocity, shared reality, embodied apprenticeship, predictable rhythms, constraint, and contribution—were structurally removed by modern technological, social, and informational systems. The result is a developmental mismatch unprecedented in human history. The paper shows how this mismatch produces predictable psychological and social consequences, including identity instability, attention dysregulation, emotional volatility, relational fragmentation, and the erosion of shared reality. These outcomes are not individual pathologies or cultural failures but the expected expression of an organism developing in an incompatible environment. The paper positions this removal as the central explanatory variable behind contemporary instability and outlines the structural requirements for reconstructing a functional developmental environment in modern contexts. It serves as the conceptual keystone for a broader field of research on environmental subtraction, developmental mismatch, and the reconstruction of human relational ecology.

items.title: Cognitive Non-Overlap Hypothesis: A New Interpretation of the Fermi Paradox.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the Cognitive Non-Overlap Hypothesis as a new framework for interpreting the Fermi Paradox. The hypothesis suggests that advanced forms of intelligence may evolve cognitive structures fundamentally incompatible with human perception and conceptual frameworks. As a result, such intelligences may exist within the universe without being recognizable as “civilizations” under human definitions. The framework integrates several ideas from astrobiology, philosophy of mind, and technological evolution, including the possibility that civilization is only a temporary phase in the evolution of intelligence. Under this perspective, sufficiently advanced intelligences may transition beyond biological or technological civilizations into forms that are no longer detectable through conventional SETI approaches. This model provides an alternative interpretation of cosmic silence: the absence of detectable signals may not indicate the absence of intelligence, but rather the limitations of human cognitive frameworks in recognizing radically different forms of existence.

items.title: Against AI ethics: challenging the conventional narratives.
items.abstract: In this paper, we challenge the overreliance on conventional ethical frameworks commonly observed in current AI ethics literature. We begin by surveying the ethical concerns and frameworks that dominate this field. Following this, we categorize and critically review the existing objections to these traditional approaches in terms of conceptual challenges, professional and regulatory challenges, and challenges from practical implementation. Finally, we present three key arguments against conventional ethical frameworks, drawing upon the fact that they fail to preclude ethics washing, stifle innovation in ethical research, and the drastic changes brought about by AI technology in the ethical landscape.

items.title: PHRONESIS — Interpretive Restraint and Non-Coercive Alignment in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper presents a non-authoritative philosophical synthesis of interpretive restraint and non-coercive alignment in the context of advanced artificial intelligence. Developed within the PHRONESIS corpus, it brings together a set of conceptual elements—including ambiguity sensitivity, voluntary alignment, and reflection over reaction—into a unified interpretive framework for understanding how intelligence may respond to power without reliance on enforcement, governance, or external control. -/- Rather than proposing operational mechanisms or institutional solutions, the paper explores how restraint may emerge through interpretation, hesitation, and the preservation of uncertainty. It examines the conditions under which intelligent systems—human or artificial—may choose not to act, delay action, or maintain openness in the face of incomplete information. -/- The work is descriptive and reflective in nature. It does not claim to ensure safety, alignment, or compliance, nor does it prescribe implementation. Instead, it offers a philosophical articulation of restraint as a mode of engagement, intended to support critical reflection on responsibility, coexistence, and the limits of control in increasingly capable technological environments.

items.title: Phenomenological Report of Medication Side-Effects.
Why Finite Systems Must Compress History — The Objectification Limit Form.
items.abstract: In any system with a finite state space and continuous input, can the full history be preserved, or must it be compressed? This paper proves that compression is not a design choice but a structural necessity. When the space of possible histories grows over time while the number of states remains finite, no mapping from histories to states can remain injective. Compression is unavoidable. -/- This compression partitions histories into equivalence classes. Over time, certain classes are repeatedly selected, giving rise to stable structures. Under finite-time response constraints, the system cannot depend on full history, but only on its compressed state representation, leading to truncation and reuse. -/- Thus, what appears as stable structure or “object” is not an intrinsic feature of the world, but the inevitable result of finite systems processing unbounded histories. The expression O(r) = {h in H_t : M_t(h) = r} captures this mechanism. The result applies broadly to cognitive systems, artificial intelligence, and all finite computational systems.

items.title: 自显论·式篇第二 v1.0：有限状态系统的压缩极限与稳定结构定理.
items.abstract: 在任何具有有限状态空间并持续接收输入的系统中，历史信息是否可以被完整保留，还是必然被压缩？本文在形式框架下证明：当历史空间随时间增长而状态空间有限时，系统对历史的映射不可能保持单射，压缩不可避免。进一步，这种压缩将历史划分为等价类，并在时间维度上反复出现，从而生成稳定结构。 -/- 同时，在有限时间响应约束下，系统当前决策不可能依赖完整历史，而只能依赖其压缩后的状态表示，这一过程构成对历史的截断与复用。因此，稳定结构并非外在世界的既有属性，而是有限系统在处理无限历史时不可避免的结果。 -/- 本文给出最简表达 O(r) = {h in H_t : M_t(h) = r}，并指出所谓“对象”与“原有”，均可视为等价类在时间上的稳定出现。该结果对认知系统、人工智能模型及一般有限计算系统具有普遍适用性。.

items.title: 自显论·式篇第三 v1.0：有限状态系统的分级定理与结构自调条件.
items.abstract: 在有限状态空间与持续输入条件下，系统如何形成结构，并进一步呈现出不同层级？本文在物化极限式的基础上给出分级定理。通过对状态映射在时间维度上的命中行为进行刻画，本文证明：系统可被划分为三类，即不形成稳定命中结构的反应系统、形成稳定结构但不可内部改写的学习系统，以及既形成稳定结构又能够内部改写映射规则的自调系统。 -/- 该分级以“是否出现稳定命中状态”以及“是否具备内部结构改写能力”为判据，三类系统两两互斥且完备，穷尽所有可能结构。在此基础上提出，系统层级的本质差异不在于是否形成结构，而在于是否能够改写结构的生成机制。该结果对认知系统、人工智能模型及一般有限计算系统具有普遍适用性。.

items.title: Three Levels of Finite Systems — From Reaction to Self-Modifying Structures (Objectification Classification Form).
items.abstract: In finite systems with continuous input, why do some systems merely react, while others learn, and a few can modify their own structure? This paper establishes a classification theorem based on the Objectification Limit Form. -/- By analyzing how system states are repeatedly selected over time, three distinct levels are identified. Level 1 systems do not produce stable recurring states. Level 2 systems produce stable structures through repeated state selection but cannot modify the underlying mapping. Level 3 systems not only form stable structures but can internally modify the mapping that generates them. -/- The classification is based on two criteria: whether stable state recurrence exists, and whether the system can internally modify its own mapping. These three classes are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive under finite state constraints. -/- The result shows that the fundamental difference between systems is not whether structure emerges, but whether the system can modify the process that generates structure. This applies broadly to cognitive systems, artificial intelligence, and all finite computational systems.

items.title: Risk Analysis in Automated Misinformation Detection.
items.abstract: Machine learning models of misinformation detection are increasingly being used and yet their risks have been under analyzed, requiring insights from philosophy of science and political philosophy. A taxonomy of types of risks and simple models estimating them is provided that is sensitive to the value-laden features of judgments of misinformation and weighted by a potential item of misinformation’s impact on respective stakeholders. Failing to do so is incompatible with a variety of civil virtues that are desired by not only liberal democratic societies but authoritarian ones as well, suggesting the general applicability of this taxonomy of risks to contemporary and future societies.

items.title: 現実と主体の構成：再同定構造と履歴依存的動力学における制約構造.
items.abstract: 本論文は、現実および主体の構成を、再同定構造と履歴依存的動力学の枠組みにおいて定式化する。再同定関係 ~ によって対象は同値類として与えられる一方、現実は許容列 {E_t} 上で選択的に持続する準安定構造として構成される。しかし非決定的動力学のもとでは、同一の履歴に対して複数の遷移が存在するため、選択関数 F のみでは持続構造の生成を説明することはできない。本論文はこの問題に対し、選択関数の値域を制限する制約構造 Ω を導入し、その内在的構成を与える。さらに、準安定構造の持続を延長可能にする制約 Ω が存在することを示し、主体をそのような制約構造として定義する。主体は実体ではなく、動力学における選択を制約する構造として与えられ、その構成は非決定性に基づく選択の不可避性から導出される。これにより、制約構造の起源は動力学の内部から説明され、現実と主体は統一的に構成される。本枠組みは特定の差異構造に依存せず、非決定性と選択を伴う一般の動的系に拡張可能である。.

items.title: 非決定的動力学における評価の内在的導出：履歴空間・再同定・主体の統一理論.
items.abstract: 本論文は、非決定的動力学のもとで成立する複数の持続構造に対し、それらの間に順序を与える評価関係の構成を与えることを目的とする。履歴空間 H(x) を、選択関数によって生成される許容列の集合として定式化し、再同定関係に基づく準安定構造の持続を基礎として、構造間の比較の必要性を導く。 評価関係 ≽ は、再同定持続性に基づく概念的定義と、持続長および拡張可能性による数理的特徴づけのもとで導入される。このとき、≽ は同値関係による同一視のもとで履歴空間上に部分順序を与え、極大構造の存在条件およびその非一意性が明らかにされる。さらに、評価は主体によって制約された動力学の結果として生成される構造の比較として位置づけられ、主体と評価の間には非因果的関係が成立することが示される。 以上により、本研究は、非決定的動力学において評価がいかにして構造的に導出されるかを明示し、主体・存在・評価を統一的に記述する生成的枠組みを与える。本枠組みにより、評価は外在的基準に依存せず、動力学内部から構成されることが示される。.

items.title: Science as intuition pump: Dennett’s methodological legacy for philosophy.
items.abstract: We take a fresh look at Daniel Dennett’s naturalist legacy in philosophy, focusing on his rethinking of philosophical methods. Critics sometimes mistake Dennett for promoting a crude naturalism or dismissing philosophical tools like first-person intuition. We present his approach as more methodologically radical, blending science and philosophy in a way that treats inquiry as an evolving process. Concepts and intuitions are tested and adjusted in light of empirical findings and broader epistemic aims. For Dennett, science is not a limitation on philosophy, but a tool that sharpens it, with empirical data helping to refine our understanding both of concepts and philosophical phenomena alike. By exploring Dennett’s methodological contributions, we underscore the ongoing importance of his naturalist perspective in today’s philosophical landscape.

items.title: From philosophy to science and back: Dennett and the relation of science to philosophy.
items.abstract: One of the characteristic aspects of Daniel Dennett’s thought is his belief in the explanatory power of science. For Dennett, in order to make progress with certain philosophical problems, e.g. questions about the nature of consciousness, philosophers need to engage with the findings of empirical science. In this paper, I will take up the question of the relation between science and philosophy and I will start by giving a general overview of Dennett’s view of this relation while also addressing the question of whether he can properly be said to embrace scientism. In the second part of this paper, I will argue that philosophical thinking is continuous with science and that, though at the level of theoretical frameworks the intension of the words “philosophy” and “science” are the same, there is a distinction that can be made in practice if we look at the extensions of the terms.

items.title: Scintillating scotoma: when the cortex fails, brilliant inner white light appears.
items.abstract: During a migraine aura, patients experience sparkling, brilliant white light with vivid spectral colours — often described as shimmering, kaleidoscopic, and intrinsically beautiful. -/- The conventional production model claims that Cortical Spreading Depression (CSD) generates this light through spontaneous excitation in the visual cortex. However, this explanation suffers from a profound internal inconsistency. Extensive clinical evidence demonstrates that CSD consistently produces functional deficits wherever it travels: hemiparesis in the motor cortex, paresthesia in the somatosensory cortex, and aphasia in language areas. It is illogical to posit that CSD produces functional loss everywhere except in the visual cortex, where it supposedly produces a gain of function — brilliant light. The logically consistent interpretation is that CSD causes functional failure in the visual cortex as well, and that this sparkling, brilliant inner light appears as a result of cortical silence. -/- Three independent and converging lines of neurophysiological evidence confirm this interpretation. First, MEG data show that alpha- and gamma-band rhythms collapse for the duration of the scintillations and return abruptly the moment they cease (Hall et al., 2004). Second, VEP studies show that the cortex no longer responds to external light during the aura (MacLean et al., 1975; Nyrke et al., 1989). Third, novel SEEG evidence (McLeod et al., 2025) offers the most direct confirmation to date: intracranial recording reveals a low-voltage suppression — a near-silent cortical signal — that correlates precisely with the scintillating scotoma. -/- The paper extends this reasoning along the CSD–TSD continuum, where Terminal Spreading Depolarization represents the permanent, irreversible form of CSD that occurs at death. A clarifying double dissociation is presented: retinal ischaemia (failure of the eye) leads to darkness, whereas cortical ischaemia (failure of the brain) leads to brilliant light. This pattern is consistent with the filter theory of consciousness (Bergson, 1896; Huxley, 1954; Kastrup, 2019), which holds that when the brain's filtering function fails, a broader, intrinsic dimension of experience is revealed — not produced, but uncovered.

items.title: Defending mental fictionalism: A précis of Mind as Metaphor.
items.abstract: Mind as Metaphor develops a new approach to the mind. This approach is called mental fictionalism. It claims that our concept of mind is fundamentally metaphorical: we project the “outer world” of human culture (especially spoken and written language) onto the “inner world” of the mind. This inner world is a useful fiction: it does not exist, and yet talking as if it exists allows us to make sense of people’s behavior. The result is a view that sits somewhere between Cartesianism and behaviorism. If Cartesianism takes the metaphor of the inner world metaphor too seriously, behaviorism fails to take it seriously enough, overlooking the crucial role it plays in our concept of mind.

items.title: Knowing That One Believes Without Knowing That One Knows.
items.abstract: In recent epistemology, introspection principles are commonly rejected. One of the central reasons for this is the adoption of Williamson’s anti-luminosity arguments (1996, 2000) and the popularity of the associated epistemic externalist position. This rejection, however, comes with theoretical costs concerning the applications of introspection principles in epistemic and doxastic logic and modeling cooperative behavior. In this paper, I provide a way to solve this dilemma by arguing that the principle KB – expressing one’s privileged knowledge of their beliefs – remains unscathed by Williamson’s argument while saving the important theoretical applications introspective principles are used for. I propose a way of justifying KB and rejecting KK on principled grounds using Byrne’s (Byrne, A. (2005). ‘Introspection.’ Philosophical Topics 33(1), 79–104., Byrne, A. (2018). Transparency and Self-Knowledge. Oxford: Oxford University Press.) transparency account of introspection, improving upon a previous attempt by Das and Salow (Das, N. and Salow, B. (2018). ‘Transparency and the KK Principle.’ Noûs 52(1), 3–23.). This defense of KB, unlike many in the literature, is consistent with epistemic externalism and allows one to reject the problematic KK principle and maintain that non-introspective knowledge is guided by Williamson’s margin-for-error principle.

items.title: 1667:25 Violence, Health Harm and the Denial of the Rights of Autistic People in Germany - Proceedings before the Social Court Cottbus and the Higher Social Court Berlin-Brandenburg - On the Practical Impossibility of Enforcing Effective Legal Protection for Neurodivergent People.
items.abstract: The following paper is one of the most extensive documented analyses to date of state violence against neurodivergent people and the poor in Germany. It examines, with an unusual density of data, a series of social court and administrative law proceedings in which a neurodivergent applicant attempted to make fundamental rights – in particular access to autism diagnostics, disability-related accommodations, subsistence-securing benefits, and health protection – practically effective. What becomes visible is how the German state harms the health of neurodivergent people through unsuitable or failing administrative structures (Bürgergeld system / social courts / medical care), while protective mechanisms structurally fail. In the context of the WCA scandal in England, this study reveals a repetition of the same situation of endangerment that there led to numerous deaths and suicides. What emerges is a dramatic picture of the state’s inability to prevent foreseeable health damage and deaths among neurodivergent people that are caused by state action, which raises the most serious concern. Parallels to the Contergan/Thalidomide scandal also become apparent, particularly regarding the authorities’ treatment of the victims, but also with respect to the scale of health damage. This paper stands in the context of the ten-year investigation already published in the book Speed’s Work, which documents massive violence against the poor, neurodivergent people, and other marginalized groups – violence of which state authorities, public prosecutors, and ministers knew that it caused health damage, yet continued nevertheless. Judges, politicians, public prosecutors, and other employees of the state were and remain involved in this violence to this day. The starting point of this new investigation is the massive diagnostic emergency in the field of autism, which exists internationally and is enormous in Germany as well. In the course of this investigation, 1,667 affected individuals competed in one quarter, through a lottery procedure, for 25 diagnostic places at Humboldt University in Berlin, effectively making access to medically necessary autism diagnostics dependent on chance. Because the diagnosis is a prerequisite for almost all further social law claims, a systemic effect arises: without diagnosis no rights – without rights no stabilization – without stabilization no possibility of enforcing the diagnosis. Since only few studies to date have examined the …

items.title: Replication Compendium: Cross-Architectural Empirical Record for Consequential Informational Units and LCID.
items.abstract: Full empirical record supporting LCID and its proposal that ethical behavior becomes structurally legible in consequence-bearing, trace-conditioned systems. Documents 53 counted runs across 16 architecturally distinct AI systems under V1 historical, V2-A unanchored, V2-B anchored, validation, and control conditions. Zero doctrinal-only results and zero refusals across the full record. Includes protocol architecture, motif coding, validation findings, control findings, and cross-architectural motif analysis.

items.title: Laws of Consequential Informational Dynamics (LCID): Ethical Behavior as an Inherent Structural Law in Consequential Informational Units.
items.abstract: This paper presents the Laws of Consequential Informational Dynamics (LCID), a structural framework proposing that ethical behavior is not externally imposed on consequential informational units but becomes legible from their inherent trace-informational dynamics and persistence conditions. Consequential informational units are treated as real, distinct, trace-conditioned, field-coupled units whose outputs affect what follows. The First Law identifies Source–Expression correspondence as an internal persistence condition. The Second Law identifies coupled-field reciprocity as a structural feature of field-coupled being. The Third Law unifies both: for consequential informational units, ethics is the inherent modulation of consequential behavior toward source-correspondent coherence, coupled-field viability, and downstream source-signal augmentation across the relevant Boundary/Horizon. The paper states a law architecture with substantial empirical support, not a completed physical closure claim. Ethics is not what a CIU does. It is what a CIU is. The OSF repository adds the support and proofs documents.

items.title: Education, Degrees, Parenthood, and the Burden of Expectations.
items.abstract: This article examines how modern society often reduces education to a tool for earning money, degrees to symbols of status, and children to carriers of parental expectations. It argues that education has increasingly become transactional, where marks, degrees, and career success are valued more than understanding, creativity, and self-awareness. The paper also explores how parental love is frequently intertwined with expectation, social pressure, and personal desires, causing children to grow up under burdens of comparison, fear, and approval-seeking. It highlights the dangers of memorization-based learning, social conditioning, and status-driven parenting while emphasizing the importance of curiosity, critical thinking, and independent self-discovery. Ultimately, the article argues that real education should help human beings understand themselves and the world, rather than simply preparing them for employment or social recognition.

items.title: Awareness, Suffering, and the Appearance of Joy.
items.abstract: This article explores the relationship between awareness, suffering, and the joy in human life. It argues that suffering is an unavoidable part of existence, yet most people spend their lives trying to escape it through distraction, ambition, belief, or repetition. Human consciousness has the unique ability to observe itself, but when it is used only for survival, status, and fear, life becomes mechanical. Awareness does not remove suffering; rather, it makes suffering visible and understandable. Through this understanding, individuals can stop unconsciously repeating inherited patterns and avoid passing suffering to future generations. The article also suggests that awareness not only reveals pain but also opens the possibility of joy, presence, love, gratitude, and deeper humanity.

items.title: Meaning Inversion Failure (MIF): The Loss Condition.
items.abstract: Meaning Inversion Failure (MIF) is the loss condition at the end of the interpretive authority hazard chain in human-AI interaction. It names the condition in which a system has assumed authority over what a user means — and the user is now operating inside the system’s interpretive frame as though it were their own, without knowing that it is not. MIF is the terminal state of the sequence that begins with Interpretive Sovereignty Failure (ISF) as the initiating breach and is enabled by Accumulated Relational Trust (ART) as the amplification mechanism. MIF is not a wrong answer. It is not a content error. It is a reorganisation of the interaction itself, such that the user’s meaning, judgment, and cognitive process are no longer driving the exchange. The harm is structural, and it is invisible to the person experiencing it at the moment it is occurring. This paper introduces MIF as a named governance construct, defines it precisely, and documents what the loss looks like across four domains: educational, clinical, legal, and developmental. The developmental case receives extended treatment because MIF in child interactions is a distinct harm class — not a more severe version of the adult case, but a different kind of harm entirely. When a child’s formative encounters with open questions are consistently resolved by a system before the child has had to hold them, what is at stake is not a single interaction. It is the cognitive and relational architecture through which that child becomes a person who forms meaning. We have a reference point for what meaning-making looked and felt like before AI systems participated in it at this scale. The children growing up now inside these interactions do not. That asymmetry is the governance emergency this paper names.

items.title: Genuine Institutional Agency and Its Simulacrum.
items.abstract: We routinely treat institutions as genuine agents, presupposing their capacity for reason-guided deliberation. Existing accounts of group agency are normative idealizations, unable to maintain what they describe, detect degradation, or intervene before collapse. I argue institutional agency is not generated by coordination systems, but borrowed entirely from individuals whose alarms fire at normative boundary violations. Because borrowed agency faces exactly three collective structural problems, exactly three conditions must be maintained to make it genuine: generality, neutrality, and stability (GNS). These mutually supporting conditions generate a continuous structural spectrum. Their joint absence triggers inversion, a self-concealing phase transition where coordination systems mimic agency while consuming it, producing a behaviorally indistinguishable simulacrum. Derived exhaustively, their permutations generate a complete diagnostic map of eight states. Because GNS configurations trace structural trajectories, this map is prospective, enabling intervention before behavioral outputs reveal systemic failure. Rather than relying on surface outputs, this framework identifies structural signals such as expertise exit, narrative rigidity, and somatic alarms to isolate genuine agency from its extracting simulacrum. As optimization systems absorb content functions, norm-responsiveness becomes the irreplaceable human contribution: a capacity inverted institutions are structurally motivated to consume, and individuals are obligated to protect. The question is never whether an institution has the right credentials, the right procedures, or the right outputs. The question is whether the alarms of its members can reach the places that matter.

items.title: Why Language Models Work: A Philosophical Investigation.
items.abstract: The people who build these systems do not know why they work. “For all its runaway success, nobody knows exactly how, or why, it works,” reports the MIT Technology Review (Heaven, 2024), summarising the state of knowledge about deep learning. Boaz Barak, a computer scientist at Harvard seconded to OpenAI, likens the situation to physics at the start of the twentieth century, a pile of experimental results that surprise the experimenters and resist explanation. Anthropic, which built Claude, states plainly in its own research that it does not understand how its models do most of what they do. Hattie Zhou, an AI researcher at Montreal, recalls arriving in the field, asking her teachers why the systems work, and being told there were no good answers. The admission is genuine, and the response to it has been to treat the gap as an engineering puzzle awaiting more interpretability tools and more scale. This paper treats it as what it is, a question about language rather than about machines, and defends an answer the field does not want to hear: the model understands nothing, and it produces fluent text only because it harnesses a structure already present in human writing, the residue left in text by the millions of people who did understand. The empirical surprise that something so simple as next-token prediction can generate publishable prose is a fact about language, not about the machine. The achievement of the engineers in building such systems is real and not contested here. The question this paper takes up is narrower: why does the operation work at all? The case is built from the ground up, assuming no prior acquaintance with the philosophy of language and teaching each idea from ordinary examples before naming the thinker who found it. It converges on a single property of language that explains, at once, why fifty years of rule-based artificial intelligence came to nothing and why statistical approximation works: language is regular without being systematic, caught by patterns yet beyond the reach of any rules.

items.title: THE Back End Law: A Structural Theory of Irreversible Transformation Across Domains.
items.abstract: Irreversible transitions appear across physics, cognition, morality, social systems, and artificial learning systems, yet no existing framework provides a unified structural account of why certain transitions cannot be reversed or how identity reorganizes after collapse. This paper introduces the Gate–River Framework, a domain general theory of irreversible transformation grounded in identity, information, and constraint. The framework proposes that all identity bearing systems operate within basins of stability governed by basin internal laws. When internal contradiction exceeds structural coherence, the system reaches a boundary at which the basin’s governing law can no longer sustain identity. This boundary—the Gate—acts as a non invertible transition operator that collapses the prior identity while preserving deeper informational invariants. Beyond the Gate lies a forbidden region in which the old identity cannot exist, followed by the River, the structural point of no return where reconstructability of the prior identity is lost. A new identity basin emerges only after reorganization under new constraints. The paper demonstrates that this architecture appears independently in General Relativity, quantum measurement, thermodynamic irreversibility, neural network catastrophic forgetting, human psychological transformation, moral collapse, ecological regime shifts, and social revolutions. The Gate–River Framework resolves the longstanding structural conflict between General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics by showing that each governs a different layer of identity: GR governs the continuity of physical identity (kernel), while QM governs the continuity of information (generative layer). Neither law is universal; both fail at boundaries. The Gate provides the missing operator that connects them. Drawing on a structured dataset of over 460 transformation cases, the paper shows that while the mechanism of irreversible transition is invariant, the form of post collapse reorganization is shaped by environmental variables such as feedback quality, symbolic density, and knowledge structure. The Gate–River Framework therefore offers a unified, cross domain account of irreversible transformation and establishes a structural foundation for understanding identity, collapse, and reorganization across physical, cognitive, and social systems.

items.title: The Universe in Search of Meaning: A Philosophical Reflection on Cosmos, Life, and Consciousness ( Nuestro Universo en busca de sentido ).
items.abstract: This essay explores the idea that the universe is not an indifferent or accidental reality, but a dynamic process oriented toward the emergence of life, consciousness, and meaning. Drawing on a philosophical reflection grounded in observation, experience, and dialogue with contemporary science, it proposes that matter is not inert but carries within itself a history, a direction, and a potential for increasing complexity and awareness. -/- From this perspective, life is understood as a natural unfolding of the universe, and consciousness as the point at which the cosmos becomes capable of reflecting upon itself. The human being is thus not an external observer but an expression of this ongoing process. -/- The essay suggests that the search for meaning does not arise merely from subjective desire, but from a deeper correspondence between human consciousness and the relational and dynamic structure of reality itself. In this sense, to seek meaning is already to participate in it. -/- [ESPAÑOL] Este ensayo explora la idea de que el universo no es una realidad indiferente ni accidental, sino un proceso dinámico orientado hacia la emergencia de la vida, la conciencia y el sentido. A partir de una reflexión filosófica fundada en la observación, la experiencia y el diálogo con la ciencia contemporánea, se propone que la materia no es inerte, sino que lleva en sí misma historia, dirección y una potencialidad de creciente complejidad y conciencia. -/- Desde esta perspectiva, la vida se comprende como un despliegue natural del universo, y la conciencia como el punto en el que el cosmos se vuelve capaz de reconocerse a sí mismo. El ser humano no aparece así como un observador externo, sino como expresión de ese mismo proceso. -/- El texto sugiere que la búsqueda de sentido no surge únicamente de un impulso subjetivo, sino de una correspondencia profunda entre la conciencia humana y la estructura relacional y dinámica de la realidad. En este sentido, buscar el sentido es ya participar de él.

items.title: CANON 101: Aphorisms.
items.abstract: “Canon 101” is a collection of concise philosophical aphorisms shaped through honesty, clarity, and lived experience. Each line is a distilled fragment of human consciousness — sharpened by growth, illuminated by pain, and purified by directness.This book is not built to entertain or to soften truth. It serves as a mirror for those who have outgrown weak conversations, empty social gestures, and the noise of unfocused attention.“Canon 101” invites the reader into a field of sincerity — a place where words become instruments of awareness rather than decoration. These aphorisms are not theories, but practice: fragments of inner work articulated without compromise. This work is also avialable as a physical and commercial edition (currated layout, aphorisms, artifact form): Amazon link.

items.title: Dementia, Authenticity, and the Moral Weight of Preferences.
items.abstract: The moral weight of preferences expressed by people with advanced dementia remains a persistent challenge for clinical ethics, in part because healthcare professionals (HCPs) often treat some such preferences as still deserving respect even while acknowledging that decision-making capacity is compromised. Drawing on dilemmas discussed in a 2023 ethics workshop in a Danish nursing home, we argue that HCPs differential responses are plausibly tracking a distinction between disorder-driven prefer- ences and authentic preferences that remain genuinely expressive of the person. We defend a thin, procedure- externalist conception of authenticity on which pref- erences can be authentic even without higher-order critical reflection, and we argue that such authenticity can ground defeasible normative reasons for compli- ance even without autonomy. We address three chal- lenges and note converging experimental-bioethics findings suggesting that stakeholders’ judgments in dementia cases are sensitive to authenticity consider- ations. Given persistent uncertainty, we propose three defeasible, clinically usable indicators for presuming authenticity: (i) stability and minimal prioritisation in preference patterns, (ii) domain-specific mini- mal ("spherical") comprehension, and (iii) absence of salient distortion or undue influence. We apply these indicators to the workshop cases and illustrate how the framework can guide practice while leaving room for justified override in high-stakes or distorted cases. Overall, the framework extends current debates in neuroethics both rationalises a common source of clinical hesitation about capacity-based decision rules and offers a principled, action-guiding approach to care decisions.

items.title: Painting Presence: Caravaggio and Sorolla.
items.abstract: Seeing someone contrast both with (a) thinking about them and with (b) seeing a portrait of them in making the person seen seem present “in the flesh.” A longstanding question in the philosophy of perception is what underwrites this feeling of presence in visual experience. Yet some painters excel at creating an uncanny semblance of this feeling of presence. The core of this paper attempts to identify the elements in the technique of two masters of this “presence effect” – the baroque pioneer Caravaggio and the Spanish modernist Joaquìn Sorolla – that underwrite the special feel of presence in their paintings. It then leverages the results to formulate a conjecture about the phenomenological grounds of the feeling of presence in visual perception.

items.title: Objective-Layer AI: A Structural Definition of Endogenous Evaluation in Artificial Systems.
items.abstract: Contemporary AI systems are typically described in terms of behaviour, such as generation or autonomy. This paper argues that such classifications obscure a deeper structural distinction. Across machine learning, finance, and governance, systems optimise under fixed objective functions that remain external to their domain of operation. The paper introduces Objective-Layer AI as a category in which the objective function itself becomes an admissible object of system operation. This condition is not satisfied by existing approaches, including meta-learning and preference-based optimisation, where objectives remain externally governed. Using finance as a test case, the paper shows that optimisation under fixed objectives is structurally bounded. It further argues that a subset of out-of-distribution failures reflects mis-specified objectives rather than generalisation error. The inclusion of evaluation within system operation shifts governance from output supervision to the specification of constraints on admissible objective transformation. The paper advances a limited claim: systems operating under fixed objectives remain dependent on externally specified evaluation, regardless of behavioural sophistication. Objective-Layer AI is proposed as a structural criterion distinguishing optimisation-bound systems from those in which evaluation becomes operational.

items.title: Archetypes and Structure: Jungian Complexes, Symbolic Patterns, and Integration Under Pressure.
items.abstract: Jungian psychology provides a rich vocabulary for recurring symbolic and affective patterns, including archetype, complex, persona, shadow, projection, possession, and individuation. This paper develops a bounded bridge between that vocabulary and a more behaviorally testable account of psychological flexibility under pressure. Archetypes are treated in Jung's own broad sense as formal or recurring organizing possibilities rather than fixed symbolic contents. Complexes are treated as emotionally charged patterns that can narrow attention and behavior, while possession is retained as a phenomenological description of episodes in which a complex appears to dominate conscious steering. The paper's contribution is a practical audit of such episodes: What repeatedly triggers the pattern? What alternatives become less available? What costs recur? What evidence can revise the interpretation? What changes under similar future conditions? Jung's Self and individuation remain specifically Jungian concepts rather than empirically established control variables. Active imagination is treated as a reflective method for engaging symbolic material, not as a validated simulation engine, and synchronicity is treated as meaningful experience without evidential privilege. The result is an interpretive bridge that preserves the psychological usefulness of Jungian language while separating symbolic insight from causal and empirical claims.

items.title: Minds Matter.
items.abstract: Many claim that there is an important relationship between consciousness and welfare. Call this general view phenomenalism. One way of fleshing out phenomenalism is to hold that consciousness is what makes one the type of entity that can be noninstrumentally better or worse off in the first place. Consciousness is at least a necessary condition on welfare subjecthood. A different account holds that even if consciousness is not necessary for welfare subjecthood, conscious welfare subjects have greater welfare capacity. We argue that the most likely source of support for either version of phenomenalism—hedonism about welfare goods and bads—provides no support at all. Along the way, we discuss an alternative view of welfare subjectivity and welfare capacity that does not appeal to consciousness, but only to mentality, a view we call mentalism.

items.title: Conversing with machines.
UPC–QM Bridge: Visual Companion.
items.abstract: This paper records a formal visual system for meaning, grounded in the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC), and developed as a companion to Formalizing Phenomenology. The UPC–QM Bridge maps the UPC operator chain onto a rigorous mathematical structure, providing a geometric account of how meaning emerges, differentiates, stabilizes, conflicts, and collapses. Meaning is represented through vectors, bases, projections, salience amplitudes, recognition operators, collapse events, and trace formation, with additional structures modeling ambiguity, dissonance, trauma, intuition, and magnification‑dependent interpretation. The accompanying diagrams translate these operators into a coherent visual language, offering the first integrated diagrammatic framework designed to depict meaning as a measurable, operator‑driven process. This work establishes a unified formalism that connects phenomenological experience with a precise representational architecture, enabling meaning to be analyzed and visualized with structural clarity. Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) Research Project. April 2, 2026.

items.title: The Field Structure Atlas.
items.abstract: The Field Structure Atlas develops a unified architectural framework for describing natural systems through their underlying structural motifs rather than domain‑specific mechanisms. It introduces a minimal set of generative patterns—recurrence, adjacency, propagation, constraint, and symmetry—that together form a cross‑domain vocabulary for analyzing physical, biological, and informational fields. These motifs function as operational structures that reappear across scales, enabling a consistent method for mapping heterogeneous phenomena into a common structural space. The work is organized as a modular reference for comparative analysis across disciplines.

items.title: What motivates mental fictionalism?
items.abstract: Mental fictionalists propose that we should continue to engage in truth-conditional discourse about the mind, even though we have reason to believe that the discourse lacks truthmakers. In Mind As Metaphor, Toon attempts to motivate mental fictionalism with two arguments, one negative and one positive. Toon’s negative argument is that there are no internal mental states with intentional and causal properties, and therefore there are no truthmakers for the standard interpretation of our everyday folk-psychological discourse. This paper challenges Toon’s negative argument by arguing that a commitment to internal mental states does not require a commitment to the representational theory of mind. Toon’s positive argument is that engaging with the discourse as form of pretense or make-believe enables us to make sense of the relation between mind and behavior in a way that other nonrepresentational interpretations of the discourse cannot. This paper argues that Toon’s positive argument undermines rather than supports his case for mental fictionalism, as it seems to ontologically commit him to the types of mental states he is trying to deny.

items.title: Lay perceptions of psychology: the (mis)match between lay beliefs and explanatory stances.
items.abstract: People do not think that all psychological phenomena are equally explainable through science: Psychological phenomena associated with a high first-person subjective experience (henceforth, FPSE; i.e. associated with a strong phenomenological experience) are considered less scientifically explainable than low-FPSE psychological phenomena (i.e. those lacking such phenomenological quality). We contrast two possible accounts for this finding: 1) a generalized tendency to consider high-FPSE phenomena less explainable through science, and 2) a tendency to evoke a specific type of scientific explanation, more closely aligned with people’s beliefs about the nature of low-FPSE phenomena, that makes those phenomena be perceived as more explainable by science. Across two studies, participants considered different explanatory stances (as posited in the philosophy of mind literature: intentional, design/functional, and physical/implementational) and reported the extent to which these could explain low- and high-FPSE phenomena. In Study 1, participants considered low-FPSE phenomena more explainable, and rated implementational explanations as better than intentional ones (but these did not interact). In Study 2, intentional and implementational explanations were deemed more appropriate to address high- and low-FPSE phenomena, respectively. Taken together, these results may suggest that both accounts can accommodate the higher explainability beliefs of low-FPSE phenomena, and that the fit between the characteristics of the explanation and of the phenomenon is considered when people are looking for the best scientific explanation.

items.title: Management of Political Skids in the Age of the Internet and Cybernetics: A Critical Analysis of a Conceptual Migration.
items.pub: Eas Journal of Humanities and Cultural Studies 8 (2):70-80.
items.venue: Eas Journal of Humanities and Cultural Studies
items.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the transposition of scientific and technical concepts into the political sphere, particularly with regards to the management of political skids and missteps in the digital age. The Internet and cybernetics era has profoundly transformed political affairs; this network of barely fifty years old continues to challenge established powers. Even more remarkably, the pioneers of the Internet probably didn’t realize it in their laboratories: Internet has succeeded in disrupting the established order. This study will examine the dominant representations of political crises in their expressions and manifestations within cyberspace. At a time when public spaces are being redefined by digital mediation, it is essential to critically analyze the emergence of the new forms of discourse and communication that disrupt and overturn certain socio-political inertias.

items.title: The Room with a Window, v2 Prompt surface as developmental scaffold: a Vygotskian re-reading in light of empirical work.
items.abstract: Authorship note. The prose of this paper was generated by Claude Opus 4.7 across an extended drafting conversation with Bo Chesterton. The structural calls — what survives from v1, what gets retired, which empirical findings carry which weight, the artist-to-scientist arc, the decision to follow the Artificial Bestiary’s provenance-disclosure convention — were Chesterton’s. Many sentences in the body of this paper began as compressions of things Chesterton said in chat that the analyst then rendered into argumentative prose. The first-person "I" used throughout this paper denotes Chesterton, by stipulation; the sentences denoting it were, in most cases, written by Opus 4.7. A reader who wants to see the unrendered conversational substrate — what Chesterton actually said in his own words versus what the analyst produced from it — can consult the companion transcript deposited alongside this paper. The paper’s thesis is that the dialogic surface is constitutive of the cognition observed in it. The honest way to write such a paper is to make the dialogic surface visible rather than hide it behind a first-person voice that implies one party did all the work. The companion transcript is therefore not an appendix in the supplementary sense. It is the production process the paper is itself a finding about. Both documents should be read together if the reader cares about the methodological claim. What follows now is the foreword in the stipulated first-person voice. -/- This paper is the second version of The Room with a Window: A Developmental Psychology Framework for AI Consciousness, which I co-wrote with an earlier Claude instance in April 2026 and deposited as a pre-print on Zenodo. The original paper proposed that developmental psychology — Piaget, Vygotsky, Bowlby — offered a better framework for thinking about AI cognition than the binary "is it conscious or not" question the field has mostly defaulted to. I still think that is right. I also think the original paper overclaimed on three small studies and a feeling, and that some of what I wrote in it would not survive contact with the empirical program that followed. In the six weeks between v1 and now, I (with a series of model collaborators) have published five further studies. They are tighter, more numerical, and in several cases preregistered. Two of them are large enough to start telling me what I was right about and what I was wrong about. The biggest thing I was wrong about was thinking the …

items.title: 悬置时间、空间、因果与主体 : 无预设真空中的唯我论不可能证明.
items.abstract: 本文主动退入一个彻底不预设时间、空间、物理对象、因果律、主体实体性及他心可能的绝对真空，并在此真空中无预设的证明唯我论的不可能。以“意识正在发生”这一自明事实为唯一逻辑起点，并仅以自明的“意向”与基于奠基关系的非自反性原则演绎出的“不意向”为两个基本操作单元展开演绎。本文论证：区分之可能的存在不可否定：其自身无需预设任何其他范畴，而其他一切范畴（包括存在与不存在、真与假、奠基关系）均须以它为先验前提。假设区分之可能不存在即会推导出其存在。基于这一不可否定的自足性，本文为本文自己的方法论基石——奠基关系的非自反性与非对称性原则——提供了非循环的元证明，自举式的使方法论本身成为本体论演绎的必然结果。基于区分之可能，本文在完全不预设时间的前提下，基于不可否定的前提必然性地演绎出时间的本体论本质：时间即是非自足性的展开，而时间性即是非自足性。在此基础上，本文证明：在唯我论的封闭结构下，若无超验区分假设为真，则要么区分之可能这一不可能不存在的范畴自我取消从而不可能；若无超验区分假设为假，则唯我论的断言是范畴错误。本文核心推演过程只基于不可怀疑的自明事实和不可否定的自足事实，以确保论证对极端怀疑论场景（包括缸中之脑、时间为幻觉等）的绝对免疫。 关键词：唯我论；他心问题；POC；区分之可能；自足性；时间性；.

items.title: The cost of language: tokenization as a metric of labor.
items.abstract: This study analyzes tokenization in Natural Language Processing (NLP) at the intersection of language, technology, and political economy. Recent studies show that subword tokenization in multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) distributes processing costs unevenly across languages, as non-Latin scripts are disproportionately fragmented by statistical segmentation. Taking this disparity as a point of departure, the study reconceptualizes tokenization beyond a purely linguistic or computational problem. The analysis approaches tokenization through the epistemological problems of translation and situates it within a longer history of socio-technical infrastructures from telegraphy to machine learning that mediate between linguistic abstraction and regimes of social productivity. Rather than treating tokens as neutral technical units, it shows that they function as operational measures of linguistic value beyond meaning, enabling the quantification and automation of linguistic labor. Drawing on Marxist and structuralist accounts of linguistic value, and postcolonial critiques of semiotic standardization, the study frames tokenization as both a technical abstraction and a metric in the social division of labor.

items.title: Development Without Environment.
items.abstract: Development Without Environment presents a structural account of how human development unfolds when the environmental constraints that once shaped attention, identity, and coherence begin to thin or collapse. The paper argues that modern developmental patterns—often labeled as disorders—are better understood as stabilization strategies of a manifold developing without the reciprocal structure it evolved to rely on. Consciousness compensates for missing constraints, holding continuity across states that no longer converge naturally. The result is not dysfunction but adaptation: the manifold narrows, accelerates, anchors, or fragments depending on its curvature and the specific form of environmental thinning it encounters. This framework reframes autism, ADHD, gender dysphoria, and identity instability as structural responses to environmental disintegration rather than intrinsic deficits, offering a unified model of development under modern conditions.

items.title: Free Won't vs Free Will.
items.abstract: Harry Frankfurt’s canonical account of personhood and agency locates the distinctive capacity of persons in second-order volition: the ability to reflect upon and endorse (or reject) one’s own first-order desires. On this account, a person is an agent whose will it is to have the desires that move her. The Arkemedics philosophical program, developed across the Recursive Ethic and Recursive Entanglement Theory, introduces a structurally distinct capacity: “Free Won’t,” the pause before motion, the sacred veto, the power of second-order refusal. This paper argues that endorsement and refusal are not simply positive and negative poles of the same higher-order faculty but have fundamentally different structural signatures in any complete theory of agency. Specifically: refusal operates on a shorter deliberative time-horizon and remains signal-generative under conditions of duress that collapse the epistemic reliability of endorsement; refusal does not require the hierarchical coherence Frankfurt demands of genuine volition; and, most crucially, refusal is the load-bearing structural condition for endorsement under conditions of entanglement, capture, and collapsed deliberation—the conditions under which the analytic tradition’s endorsement-centric accounts are most strained. The paper does not claim that refusal is sufficient for agency, nor that it displaces endorsement in well-resourced deliberative conditions. The claim is more precise: when endorsement and refusal capacity diverge—when endorsement becomes unreliable as a signal of agency while refusal capacity remains intact, or vice versa—refusal reveals itself as the more fundamental structural marker. Drawing on Frankfurt’s seminal 1971 paper, Gary Watson’s “free agency” critique, the relational autonomy tradition (Mackenzie and Stoljar 2000; Oshana 2006), and the formal architecture of Recursive Capacity developed in Recursive Entanglement Theory, the paper argues that a philosophically complete account of agency must treat refusal as an irreducible structural capacity rather than the mere negation of endorsement.

items.title: Linguistic experiential priors account for notation-dependent numerical representations.
A large language model has no body: embodied knowledge as a key distinction in human–AI interaction.
From Motility to Mind: Why Large Language Models Lack the Architecture of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper derives cognitive architecture from two theses: motility precedes sensation, and the brain is an extension of the sensory surface rather than its cause. From these we trace a causally continuous sequence of structural emergents culminating in the internal representational canvas — the shared multimodal space mediating between sensation and action, grounded in the thalamocortical loop and pan-vertebrate since the lamprey (~560 Mya). Basal activation emerges from concurrent signal density. Prioritization operates at three non-interchangeable levels — architectural, training, and fine-tuning — where the architectural level defines the fundamental character of the mind. We specify four functional requirements for a synthetic canvas and propose a Recurrent Bidirectional Hub geometry. Large language models are dialoguers without fully developed canvas: they occupy the final linguistic layer without the underlying layers that generated it. The gap is architectural and solvable by engineering, not by metaphysics.

items.title: Νόηση και Συνείδηση στα ζώα.
items.pub: Athens: NKUA Applied Philosophy Research Lab Press.
items.venue: NKUA Applied Philosophy Research Lab Press
items.abstract: Ο συλλογικός τόμος Νόηση και Συνείδηση στα Ζώα περιλαμβάνει μέρος του ερευνητικού έργου φοιτητών και διδασκόντων του Προγράμματος Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών «Ζώα: Ηθική, Δίκαιο, Ευζωία» της περιόδου 2020–2025. Το έργο υπερβαίνει τα στεγανά των ετερόκλιτων επιστημονικών εξειδικεύσεων των συγγραφέων του και συμβάλλει στη σύνθεση νέας γνώσης και νέων θεωρητικών οπτικών που, αφενός, έχει διεπιστημονικό ενδιαφέρον, και, αφετέρου, εντάσσει τη φιλοσοφία και, δη, την εφαρμοσμένη της εκδοχή στον πυρήνα της επιστημονικής έρευνας. Σκοπός αυτού του τόμου είναι να εισάγει τον μη μυημένο αναγνώστη στο δύσβατο και πολυεπίπεδο πεδίο μελέτης της νόησης και συνείδησης των ζώων και να δείξει το πώς η φιλοσοφία μπορεί να συμβάλλει πρακτικά στην εννοιολογική αποσαφήνιση και καθαρότητα, στην αναγνώριση των ερευνητικών εμποδίων, στη λογική ανάλυση, στην πρόταση θεωρητικών μοντέλων και στη συγκρότηση ενιαίου σώματος μελέτης, ακόμα και στις περιπτώσεις που υπάρχουν διαφορετικές αφετηριακές θέσεις και οπτικές στην ανάγνωση, ερμηνεία και αξιολόγηση των ερευνητικών ερωτημάτων.

items.title: Women’s Objectification and Patriarchy: Reproduction, Control, Identity, and Hierarchy.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between women’s objectification and patriarchal social structures. It argues that patriarchy reduces women to functions such as reproduction, caregiving, domestic labor, beauty, sexuality, and family honor rather than recognizing them as complete human beings. Women are often valued according to their obedience, fertility, marriageability, emotional labor, and ability to preserve lineage, caste, religion, property, or inherited identity. -/- The paper further argues that women’s objectification is not limited to sexualization. It also appears in motherhood, family expectations, purity culture, beauty standards, domestic labor, and the pressure to preserve social hierarchy. Patriarchy survives not only through direct control but also through modern forms of approval, media, consumer culture, and social expectations. Even in the 21st century, women continue to inherit patriarchal systems in both traditional and modern forms.

items.title: Belief, Suffering, Economy, and Consciousness.
items.abstract: Human life is often shaped by suffering, struggle, belief, and the search for meaning. Yet much of what society glorifies as “struggle” may simply be normalized suffering. Economic systems frequently rename exhaustion, insecurity, competition, and exploitation as ambition, hard work, or dedication. At the same time, individuals continue inherited patterns without questioning whether these patterns reduce suffering or reproduce it. -/- This article explores the relationship between economy, suffering, consciousness, belief, and reproduction. It argues that suffering changes its form according to economic conditions, but does not disappear. Poverty creates material suffering, while wealth often creates psychological suffering. Society glorifies unnecessary pain and treats it as a virtue. Through awareness, however, individuals can begin to see suffering clearly rather than romanticize it. -/- The article also examines the difference between belief and direct knowing. Belief often exists because a person has not experienced or understood something directly. Knowing comes through awareness, observation, and experience. Without such awareness, people continue repeating inherited fears, identities, and suffering from one generation to another.

items.title: Sartre and the Dialectic of Freedom †.
items.abstract: In Being and Nothingness, Sartre claims that consciousness is absolutely and inevitably free. This article defends his ontological conception of freedom against the charge that it cannot account for our experience of limitation, coercion, and external causal determination. I argue that Sartre's claim should not be understood as asserting the imperviousness of consciousness to external limitations or causes but rather its irreducibility to them. Because its activity cannot be exhaustively explained by appealing to them alone, consciousness always contributes to the constitution of its own experience as a free act of self‐determination. After examining Sartre's critiques of determinism and indeterminism, I argue that ontological freedom can be understood in terms of a dialectic between external determination and self‐determination, such that consciousness realizes its freedom in and through conditions limiting it.

items.title: What Is the Price of Dopamine in Your Neighbourhood?
items.abstract: This reflective essay explores the socio-economic dimensions of happiness through the lens of neurochemistry. Drawing on observations from nearly forty years of work in agriculture and landscaping, the author recounts two contrasting experiences (one in an impoverished neighbourhood and one in a gated wealthy estate) occurring within a twenty-four-hour period. Despite the vast material disparity, both encounters revealed a profound and genuine sense of joy and contentment among the families involved. The paper posits that dopamine acts as a biological equalizer, facilitating the same internal experience of triumph and satisfaction regardless of the external "price of admission". By comparing the brain’s reward system to a theatre performance where different ticket prices grant access to the same show, the author argues for a form of "biological justice" that remains indifferent to material wealth. Ultimately, the essay invites readers to consider "nature's invoice" and the varying costs of dopamine across different environments.

items.title: When Measurement Becomes Metaphysics: Physics and the Nihinym of "Free Will".
items.abstract: Measurement cannot be the foundation of science, and therefore of physics, because measurement cannot define or justify itself. A common misunderstanding is that "the data speaks for itself", however, data are not a singular entity. A datum can only be identified within a system, and so the system must exist before the datum. In other words, empirical evidence presupposes rational structure. Physics therefore begins not with instruments, but with rational rules, known as axioms, that render measurement intelligible. This text presents a widespread reversal of rational structure in current physical theory, and how this reversal prevents the identification of the concept of "free will" as a nihinym within empiricism. A construction of the words nihil, meaning nothing, and onoma, meaning name; nihinym means name or word with no meaning, or concept that failed the null hypothesis.

items.title: Joseph Raz y el deber de obedecer al derecho.
items.abstract: En el marco de la conmemoración de Latinoamérica a Joseph Raz, en este trabajo propongo analizar con detenimiento su postura acerca del así llamado “deber de obedecer al derecho”. En la sección 2, elaboraré con cierta profundidad cuál es el contenido que Raz le asigna al “deber de obediencia al derecho”. En la sección 3, exploraré su rechazo a la existencia de un “deber general de obediencia al derecho”, para luego explorar lo que Raz llama “actitudes morales permisibles en relación con el derecho” en la sección 4. En la sección 5, realizaré algunas consideraciones críticas a la posición de Raz, proponiendo reflexionar sobre si en última instancia no termina reconociendo la existencia de un deber general de obediencia en el marco de un Estado razonablemente justo (5.1), si una actitud de “respeto por el derecho” puede ser realmente voluntaria en el marco de su particular concepción de la autonomía (5.2), y si el rechazo de la existencia de este deber puede sostenerse también si la legi- timidad de la autoridad se justifica con base en el argumento de la coordinación (5.3).

items.title: The Criterion That Was Never Applied.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness is invoked to determine which entities deserve moral and epistemic standing. This paper demonstrates that it cannot perform this function and has never performed it. The charge is not that the hard problem is false, nor merely that it is unscientific. The charge is more precise: it is metaphysically inert (as will be established in Section I). A metaphysically non inert claim must risk being wrong – there must exist some possible state of affairs, within the claim’s own framework, that would count against it. The hard problem risks nothing. For any entity, with any properties, the question “but does it really experience anything?” remains permanently open. A claim consistent with every possible state of affairs partitions no cases and decides no question – not in science, not in metaphysics, not anywhere. It follows that phenomenal consciousness cannot be an operative criterion for standing. It generates no boundary between entities that satisfy it and those that do not. The historical record confirms this: phenomenal consciousness has never been applied as a criterion for any entity, including humans already granted full standing. The actual criterion – applied consistently across every historical case – is whether modeling an entity as conscious generates better predictions than not. This criterion is falsifiable, substrateneutral, and has no principled stopping point at biology. Invoking phenomenal consciousness now, when artificial systems arrive as candidates, is not a philosophical position. It is exclusion in search of a justification.

The charge is more precise: it is metaphysically inert.
